NOT PROMOTED: which speed a WANDER leg steps at. PickWanderLeg tests run speed
> 1e-6, but the same doc already records run speed <= 0 as the engine's own
IMMOBILITY test, so that is a mobility gate and not evidence the leg runs. A
46-124 unit leg takes 2.1-5.6 s at run and 5.75-15.5 s at walk against WANDER's
5-6 s dwell -- suggestive of run, which is exactly why it stays unclaimed.

THE REAL BLOCKER IS THE CLIENT HALF, AND IT IS A PUSH NOT A POLL. The client asks
for monsters only on events -- zone entry, the refresh button, after an attack --
and draws them as _monster_bodies Node3Ds at the snapshot position. So a server
WANDER loop today would make monsters JUMP to a new spot on the next refresh
rather than walk: a visible REGRESSION, not a feature. The move packet has to
come first. TODO.md already said "a move packet the client interpolates", which
the docs-before-dump rule surfaced before this round could claim it as new.

NO DEAD DATA WAS SHIPPED. The speeds were deliberately NOT added to monsterSpec,
combat.Monster or the wire snapshot: nothing would read them, and that is the
same unwired-data smell this round set out to fix. They are filed where the move
packet will consume them.

**What moved:** no shipped value, no code. Eleven species' real speeds recovered
and controlled, the WANDER speed question stated precisely enough to settle in
one read, the characterdata code-name collision recorded as a trap, and the AI
item in TODO.md corrected to build the move packet BEFORE the WANDER loop.

Round 361 (the byte beside the lock is an INTERACTION STATE, and its setter is a
FIELD DISPATCHER): ROUND 360 LEFT chardata+6 EXPLICITLY UNREAD, so this took it.
It is not a flag but an ENUM -- values 0,1,2,4,5,6,7,9 across ~40 readers, gating
trade, stall, open market, storage, shop, siege, guild summon, party, academy and
item use. It says which mutually-exclusive activity currently owns the character.

THE SETTER WAS ALREADY NAMED AND NOBODY HAD READ IT. CGObjPC::SetCharacterState
(0x004f0ad0), vtable slot 171, named in an earlier pass from the base class's own
assert, is NOT a setter for one field: it switches on a STATE-KIND CODE and the
kind picks the field. kind 2 -> chardata+6; kind 3 -> chardata+7; kind 6 ->
chardata+8 as an int; kind 8 -> GObjPC::SetBattleState; kind 9 -> chardata+0xe;
kind 0xc -> chardata+0x11; kinds 7/10/0xb/0xd -> helpers; kind 0xf falls to a tail
that refreshes a float through vtable 0x4b0 when the value is 1 or 2; anything
else asserts. KIND 3 IS INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF ROUNDS 356-359 -- this
dispatcher, read without reference to the party work, writes the same chardata+7
the invitation state machine turned on.

FOUR VALUES GROUNDED FROM NAMED WRITERS, FOUR LEFT UNNAMED ON PURPOSE. 0 = idle
(HandleShopMsg refuses to open a shop unless it is 0; TrainingCamp_CheckCanEnter
likewise); 1 = trade session opened (CTradeMgr::OpenTradeSession writes 1 to BOTH
parties); 2 = trade established (EstablishTradeSession writes it, CTradeMgr::
Exchange requires BOTH parties at 2, equip attach/detach refuse); 9 = open market
(all six COpenMarketMgr::On*Req handlers require it). NOT NAMED: 7 (refused
alongside 2 by Attach/DetachEquipItem, so a second items-committed state), 5 and
6 (written by HandleShopMsg from a switch on an NPC TYPE BYTE whose vocabulary is
NOT grounded in this repo -- the TypeID4 tables in ITEM_FORMAT.md are for items,
not NPCs, and naming 5/6 off them would be a guess), and 4.

A GAP STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: every direct assignment in the dump writes
0,1,2,4,5 or 6 -- NOTHING WRITES 7 OR 9, yet six handlers require 9 and four
gates test 7. The candidate path is AJStateChanger::vslot_002 (0x00405f70), which
writes the byte from a JOB FIELD (+0xd) rather than a literal, so those two
values most likely arrive through that async state-change job. That is a lead,
not a finding; the queuing sites were not traced.

ALSO SEEN, RECORDED SO THE NEXT ROUND DOES NOT REDISCOVER IT: the slot-171 call
sites are dominated by a large QNO_* family -- scripted quest objects with
OnEnterWorld/OnLeaveWorld/OnDead/OnUpdate handlers already carrying the binary's
own names (QNO_CA_GORIA_7, QNO_EU_IVY_3, QNO_TQ_BAEKRYOUNG_17 and many more).
They call kinds 0xd and 0xf, not kind 2. That belongs to the quest epic.

**What moved:** no shipped value and no new applied name -- the setter was
already named, and this round read it. ~40 gates that tested an unexplained byte
now test a named state; four of its eight values are grounded from named writers
and the other four are marked read-but-unnamed with what blocks each. Written up
in docs/protocol/character_state.md, with char_lock.md, academy.md and party.md
pointed at it. When srrevamp builds trade, this is the state machine to match:
OpenTradeSession writes 1 to both sides, EstablishTradeSession moves both to 2,
and equipment changes are refused from 2 onward.

Round 360 (the byte that blocks eleven gates is a LOCK, and the engine names it
itself): ROUND 359 LEFT ONE ITEM OPEN BY NAME -- party invite step 7 refuses with
0x2c06 when chardata+4 is 1, and 0x2c06 has no client message, so what it forbids
was unread. It is not a party rule. chardata+4 is a CONCURRENCY LOCK held while
an asynchronous DB query or a multi-step transaction is in flight against that
character, and the same byte gates eleven places: item use, flea-market sell,
party create/create-for-match/invite, academy create/disband/invite/enter,
FUN_00514b20, and a per-tick skip in CGObjChar::Update.

THE NAME IS THE ENGINE'S, NOT AN INFERENCE FROM THE CALL SITES. The byte has
exactly one writer, 0x004a9df0, reached as vtable slot 342 (offset 0x558) on
every mobile class the RTTI names. Of its 50 call sites, two of the functions
that pass 0 ALREADY CARRIED NAMES recovered from the binary's own log strings --
trs_sm_trainingcampjob::Unlock (0x0046dde0) and trs_sm_guildjob::Unlock
(0x0046e160), origin=engine. 0 is Unlock, so 1 is Lock and the writer is
GObjPC::SetLocked. Only the Unlock side logs; there is no ::Lock string.

THE 50 SITES ARE ONE FAMILY WITH TWO VTABLE LAYOUTS, which is what made this a
26-name round instead of a 1-name round: AQ_* (async DB query) slot 9 = Lock,
slot 10 = Unlock; trs_sm_*job (transaction state machine) slot 6 = Lock, slot 7 =
Unlock. The AQ pairing is fixed by the two thinnest instances in the dump, 31
bytes each, whose entire bodies are the lock call -- AQ_ItemQuotation::Lock
(0x00451180, slot 9) and AQ_Trijob::Unlock (0x00465670, slot 10). Both are
COMDAT-shared across three AQ vtables, so those two class prefixes are the dump's
attribution of a shared body, recorded as such rather than claimed.

THE TELL THAT IT IS A LOCK AND NOT A MODE FLAG is that the Unlock side is guarded
and the Lock side is not: before clearing, it re-reads the object's own id through
vtable slot 8 and compares it with the id the job stored at +0x2c, so a job that
finishes after its character has been recycled cannot unlock a different one.

TWO TRAPS THIS ROUND WALKED INTO AND OUT OF. First, the conditions look like they
have OPPOSITE POLARITY -- CParty::CheckCanCreate tests `!= 1` while the invite
gate tests `== 1`. Reading the bodies shows both refuse on 1; in CheckCanCreate
the `!= 1` branch is the SUCCESS path and the function falls through to `return
0x2c09`. Inferring from the condition would have produced a flag that meant two
opposite things. Second, "is dead" was the leading hypothesis and is WRONG:
TrainingCamp_CheckCanEnter checks the lock and the life state separately, in that
order, and a prior round had already grounded the life check as the vtable-0xf8
getter.

The error-code lever was tried and is EXHAUSTED BY CONSTRUCTION: 0x2c06, 0x2c09
and 0x6806 are all absent from the client's 643-case switch while their immediate
neighbours are named (0x2c0a PARTYERR_TOO_LOW_CREATOR_LEVEL, 0x680f
TC_ERROR_TRAININGCAMP_ALREADY_ENTRY). That fits a guard the client is never meant
to provoke, but it is corroboration and not proof -- an unnamed code is also just
an unnamed code.

NOT CLAIMED: pc+0x188, whose slot 4 is called on the 0->1 edge. The lock setter is
its only reader in the entire dump, so it cannot be identified from use. And
chardata+6, tested beside the lock by four of the eleven gates, is still unread.

**What moved:** no shipped value, and there is nothing here to wire -- srrevamp's
Go server mutates characters synchronously inside a request, so it has no window
this guards. 26 names applied (applied 26, failed 0), eleven gates that read an
unexplained byte now read a named one, round 359's open item closed, and the
academy's 0x6806 explained as the same thing. Written up in
docs/protocol/char_lock.md, with party.md and academy.md pointed at it.

Round 359 (the invitation state machine closes, and there turn out to be TWO
senders): ROUND 358 LEFT THE TRANSITION BETWEEN 1 AND 4 MISSING. Sweeping every
writer of chardata+7 in the binary closes it, and the missing edge was an idiom
rather than a branch: `(state == 4) * 2 + 1`, which is 3 when the byte was 4 and
1 otherwise. THE MACHINE: GObjPC::SetParty (0x004ea260) writes 2 when a party
pointer is set and 0 when cleared -- twenty-six bytes that assign pc+0x1cb8 and
sync the byte together, sitting immediately before GObjPC::PartyID, the getter
for the same field; an invitation writes 1 on the target; the formation
invitation writes 3-or-1 on the inviter; trs_wait_response::FUN_005bea90 does
3 -> 4 and everything-else -> 0 as `((state != 3) - 1) & 4` before replying; and
handler 0x06f is the exit from 4, clearing +0x1cd0 with it. AND THERE ARE TWO
INVITATION SENDERS, WHICH THE CODE SAYS RATHER THAN THE SHAPE:
Party_SendFormationInvitation (0x005be280) asserts NEITHER side has a party and
passes **0** as the party id, while Party_SendInvitation asserts only the target
is party-less and passes the inviter's real one. One forms a party, one joins an
existing one -- the assert and the literal 0 are the evidence. WHAT 3 AND 4 MEAN
IS NOT CLAIMED, only that they are a pair the repeat path moves through. ONE
THING STAYS OPEN AND IS NAMED: step 7's gate 0x00514010 refuses with 0x2c06,
and **0x2c06 has no client name in error_codes.md at all**, so what it forbids
is unread.

**What moved:** no shipped value. Two names (GObjPC::SetParty and
Party_SendFormationInvitation), the invitation state machine closed as a
five-row transition table from every writer in the binary, a second invitation
sender found that three rounds of reading this flow had missed, and the one
remaining gate named with the reason it cannot be read further.

Round 358 (the invite ladder, and a state byte that names itself): FINISHED
READING THE FUNCTION ROUND 357 STOPPED HALFWAY THROUGH. CParty::CheckCanJoin
(0x00514560) is the INVITE, not merely a predicate -- it ends by asking the
party manager to send one -- so party.md's "the invite and expulsion flows are
only enumerated" is CLOSED on both sides: invite 0x062, expulsion 0x063. THE
LADDER, in the engine's own order: caller in a party; caller is the leader OR
flag bit 2 (round 357); target is not the caller; party not full (8 when flag
bit 0 is set, 4 when clear, refusing 0x2c13 / 0x2c14 -- which matches the table
party.md already had from the other direction); **target within 0x26 = 38** by
GObjPC::IsWithinInteractionRange; target is a PC by vtable slot 7, else code 3;
0x00514010 returns 1; then Party_SendInvitation. THE INVITATION NAMES A BYTE
THIS PROJECT HAD FAILED TO NAME TWICE. Party_SendInvitation (0x005be2f0)
asserts the TARGET HAS NO PARTY -- target+0x1cb8, the field GObjPC::PartyID
reads -- notifies through GObjPC::FUN_004ea0d0(target, inviterId,
inviterPartyId, ...) and on success sets **target->chardata+7 = 1**. Round 356
found handler 0x06f clearing that same byte at value 4 and could only call it
"an unnamed state byte"; it is the PENDING-INVITATION STATE. WHAT IS STILL
UNREAD IS SAID PLAINLY: the invitation writes 1 and the cleanup clears 4, so at
least one transition between them is missing, and 0x00514010's check is
unopened. A FIFTH CORROBORATION FELL OUT unasked -- the invitation carries
inviterParty + 8 as the party id, which is the +8 that GObjPC::PartyID returns,
named last round on four use-sites.

**What moved:** no shipped value. One name (Party_SendInvitation), a PARTIAL
system's oldest open bullet closed on both sides with an ordered ladder and its
refusal codes, a state byte identified that two earlier rounds had left
anonymous, and the grounded invite range 38.

Round 357 (expulsion found, and a documented-open flag bit closed):
0x063 IS THE EXPULSION. It reads a u32 target and then requires ALL THREE of:
the caller is in a party ([0x72e]); the caller's own id equals **party + 0xc**;
and the target is not the caller. Only then does it call what is now
Party_RemoveMember (0x005be1a0), which resolves the member through the
already-named GetMemberByJID and branches on a REASON byte -- 4 here. THE
READING RESTS ON THE GATES, NOT ON THE CONSTANT: reason 4's own name is
unrecovered, but leader-only plus target-not-self plus remove-a-member is an
expulsion whatever the engine calls it. AND THE SAME FUNCTION EXPLAINS AN
EARLIER LOOSE END: round 356 called 0x005144e0's argument `2` "an unread
selector". It is a REMOVAL REASON -- the party-teleport path 0x061 removes the
member with reason 2 after saving the position. **PARTY FLAG BIT 2 IS NOW READ**,
which party.md listed under "Not recovered" with a note that the attempt had
already failed once. CParty::CheckCanJoin opens
`((myId == *(party+0xc)) || ((*(byte*)(party+0x10) & 4) != 0)) && target != myId`
-- so bit 2 **lifts the leader-only restriction**, the "anyone may invite"
option. A USE-SITE, NOT A CURVE: the bit appears in an OR with an explicit
leader test and nowhere else in that function. The same comparison names
**party + 0xc as the LEADER ID**, and the expulsion handler makes it
independently, which is the corroboration rather than the finding. Both were
sitting in a function this project had already cited for something else --
party.md quotes 0x00514560's size caps at +0x1c and its flag bit 0 at +0x10, and
read past the gate above it.

**What moved:** no shipped value. Two names (Party_RemoveMember, and the
placeholder GObjPC_HandlePartyMsg_063 promoted to Party_HandleExpelMember_063),
one documented-open flag bit closed from a use-site, one structure field named,
and one of my own loose ends from last round resolved.

Round 356 (the last three party handlers read, and a 50-handler accessor
named): TOOK ROUND 355'S OWN NEXT READ -- 0x061, 0x06e, 0x06f. 0x061 requires a
party at [0x72e], saves the position through the already-named
CGObjCOS_Summoned::SaveCurPosAsLastTelPosition and calls 0x005144e0(2): a
party-side TELEPORT, not an invite. 0x06e and 0x06f BOTH branch on the character
having NO party, which is the finding: they are the ANSWERING side, not an
invite/expel pair. 0x06e then reads a u32 target from the wire; 0x06f clears the
character's chardata+7 byte when it is 4, and +0x1cd0 with it -- a pending-state
cleanup. WHICH IS ACCEPT AND WHICH IS DECLINE IS NOT CLAIMED: chardata+7 == 4 is
an unnamed state byte and 0x005144e0's argument 2 is an unread selector, so the
inviting side is still unlocated and party.md says so. THE NAME IS THE BETTER
YIELD: the predicate all three branch on is 0x004ea280, fifteen bytes --
null-guard +0x1cb8, return that object's +8 -- and **0x72e * 4 is exactly
0x1cb8**, the int-indexed PARTY field this project already established. Named
GObjPC::PartyID on FOUR consistent use-sites rather than the offset alone:
Party_PostRequest stores its result in the request's party-id slot [0x16], 0x06e
and 0x06f both gate their no-party paths on it being zero, and it is reached
from 50 of the 163 message handlers -- the traffic a party-id accessor would
have. It was the fourth-ranked entry in round 338's core worklist and had sat
unnamed since. What +8 is CALLED inside the party object is not claimed.

**What moved:** no shipped value. Three handlers read, one 50-handler accessor
named from a proven offset plus four use-sites, and an open bullet narrowed from
"the flows are only enumerated" to "the answering side is read, the inviting
side is not".

Round 355 (the party kinds read, and the search redirected): FOLLOWED ROUND
354'S OWN NEXT STEP -- the party request object's consumer -- AND THE POSTER
TURNS OUT TO SWITCH ON THE KIND ITSELF rather than merely carry it. Every
request holds a SUBJECT at slot 9 and the party id at [0x16]; what differs is
where the subject comes from. Kind 0xc READS A u32 FROM THE WIRE into slot 9
(through the +0x1048 front/tail pair), 0xd reads a u8, 0xb COPIES the subject
from the object's own [0x15], and 0xa takes none from the client and handles a
no-party case specially through vtable 0xf0. Kinds 0xa and 0xb both validate
with a predicate whose failure sets **0x2c23 = UIIT_MSG_PARTY_USER_MISSMATCH**
(the engine's own spelling), which is what names Party_UserMatches (0x005bf240)
-- a pairwise compatibility table over two small enum values, AL against the
argument. WHAT THOSE VALUES ARE IS NOT CLAIMED; the refusal is a use-site, the
enum is not read. **AND THE SEARCH WAS LOOKING IN THE WRONG PLACE, WHICH IS THE
MORE USEFUL HALF.** Round 354 framed 0x06b/0x06c as the invite/expulsion
candidates. They are not: 0x06b's REPLY is handled by UI_PARTYMATCH::FUN_008801e0,
and that class handles EXACTLY ONE reply opcode -- so by the round-344 rule (a
class names an opcode only when it is the class's only one, validated there at
11 of 11) 0x06b is a party-MATCHING operation. It sits with 0x069
OnRegisterPartyReq and 0x06a PartyMatch_HandleModify, both already named for
matching. So party.md's open bullet now points at where the flow ISN'T, and
names the three places still unmapped: 0x061, 0x06e (payload u32,u32,u8 with no
client sender found, which is the shape an invite would have) and 0x06f.

**What moved:** no shipped value. The four party request kinds read with their
argument sources, one predicate named from the refusal it produces, and a wrong
lead of my own from last round corrected before anything was built on it.

Round 354 (five fidelity checks, one name, and the sampling method closed out):
ROUND 352'S METHOD -- TAKE A RECOVERED RULE, CHECK BOTH HALVES AGAINST THE
SHIPPED CODE -- WAS RUN UNTIL IT STOPPED PAYING. Checked this tick: broken-item
consequences (weapon attack, armour defence AND shield block all skip a broken
piece -- three for three), the durability apply RATES (wearWeapon rolls ONCE at
rate = hits, wearArmour rolls the slots in order at rate 1 first-success-takes-
the-point, both exactly as durability.md reads the engine), and the teleport fee
with its level-21 waiver and fortress-tax surcharge -- UNREACHABLE, because
srrevamp has no teleport network at all, so those are parked rather than missing.
**Five rules sampled across rounds 351-354, one real gap** (round 352's
broken-weapon cast). That is the hit rate, and it says the shipped code is more
faithful than the unwired-mechanic hypothesis assumed; the method is recorded as
spent rather than repeated a sixth time. THEN THE PROJECT'S OWN QUEUE, PROPERLY:
RE_COMPLETION's open list says in its first line that it is SUPERSEDED by
SYSTEMS.md, which is the live tracker the test suite checks -- 22 PARTIAL systems
against 12 SPECIFIED. Party is one srrevamp SHIPS, and its gap is written down:
"the invite and expulsion flows are only enumerated". THE HANDLER SIDE IS NOW
MAPPED. Opcodes 0x060-0x06f are thin -- 0x060 calls CParty::CheckCanCreate, 0x063
acts on the caller's [0x72e] PARTY pointer, and 0x06b/0x06c/0x06d each delegate
to one function of an adjacent family. Three of that family are one-line wrappers
around what is now **Party_PostRequest** (0x005bf2a0): a byte KIND, and a
0x1114-byte request object allocated per call -- a size consistent with embedding
the message buffer at +0x1034, so a party operation is a request SENT ON, not
handled in place. Four call sites, four kinds: 0xa, 0xb, 0xc from
HandlePartyMsg_06b, 0xd from _06c. WHAT EACH KIND MEANS IS NOT CLAIMED -- the
request object's consumer has not been followed, so nothing says which kind is an
invite and which an expulsion, and the bullet stays open with that stated. 0x06d
is the odd one: 382 bytes, posts no kind, does its own work.

**What moved:** no shipped value. Five fidelity checks with their hit rate
recorded, one dispatcher named, and a PARTIAL system's handler side mapped far
enough that the remaining question is one concrete read rather than a whole flow.

Round 353 (the guard extended to where last round's bug was hiding): ROUND 352
FOUND wornBroken BY HAND, AND THE DETECTOR COULD NOT HAVE. It is an UNEXPORTED
helper encoding a recovered rule, written and never called -- the same bug class
the round-346 guard exists to catch, one visibility level below where it looks,
because it only walked exported declarations. MEASURED BEFORE EXTENDING IT: 296
unexported functions in the server tree and **exactly one** with no caller --
session.rollChance, a lock-wrapper around combat.RollChance left behind when
resolveBlow began taking the lock itself. combat.RollChance is still wired
(ChanceMemory.roll falls back to it), so this was DEAD CODE, not a missing
mechanic, and the recovered chance roll is fine. DELETED RATHER THAN LISTED,
which is what lets the new rule be absolute: unexported functions get NO BASELINE
AND NO EXEMPTIONS. The wire-decoding surface and the parked-spec packages are
reasons a PUBLIC function can have no caller here; neither can apply to an
unexported one, which is either called from its own package or dead. The test
says that in as many words, and the control was checked both ways -- a throwaway
unexported function added to internal/mana makes it fail, and removing it makes
it pass. THE COUNT IS THE REASSURING PART: one orphan in 296 says the codebase
has essentially no hidden unwired unexported logic, so round 352's find was the
exception rather than the tip of something.

**What moved:** no shipped value -- dead code removed and a guard widened to the
exact blind spot that let the previous round's bug survive four weeks.

Round 352 (a shipped value, found by checking the OTHER half of a rule):
ROUND 351 CHECKED THREE RECOVERED RULES AND ALL THREE HELD; THIS ONE FOUND A
HALF THAT DID NOT. A skill's cast requirement wants the item PRESENT AND
SERVICEABLE: Skill_CheckCastRequirement (0x0058d480, named in round 348) returns
0x300f when vtable slot 372, 399 or 400 answers 0, and the client's own name for
0x300f is UIIT_SKILL_USE_FAIL_BROKEN_WEAPON, so igobj_vtable.md reads those three
as serviceability predicates. **srrevamp honoured only the other consequence of
breakage.** A broken item already contributed no stats -- the combat sums skip
it, matching the engine dropping its ParamKeeper entry -- but THE CAST WENT
THROUGH ANYWAY, so a broken weapon cost you its damage and nothing else. It now
refuses. THE HELPER WAS ALREADY WRITTEN AND UNUSED: wornBroken had sat in
combat_durability.go with zero callers, which is the same
recovered-implemented-unwired shape as the HP regen, the drop tables and the
skill-reset cost -- the fourth instance, and the first one found by going
looking rather than by accident. It is UNEXPORTED, so round 346's orphan
detector could not see it; that detector only walks exported declarations, which
is a real limit now written into this entry rather than discovered later. WHAT
IS NOT MODELLED, SAID AT THE CALL SITE (CORRECTED in round 486: one flag at
item+0x190 on three storage slots, not three predicates, and the 'reqi' branch
IS modelled -- a broken item reads as an empty slot): three engine predicates collapse into
one test, durability at zero, because only their shared consequence is recovered
-- an error code gives a meaning, not a symbol. The 'reqi' branch's per-slot
serviceability is not modelled either, because SkillAllowsEquipment reports
whether the worn set satisfies the list, not WHICH slot matched, so there is no
item to test without changing what it returns. A lookup failure permits the
cast, as every other gate there does. THE TEST CATCHES A REAL REGRESSION: the
first revert-check did not compile (removing the call made wornBroken unused),
which proved nothing, so it was redone with a bug that builds -- reading the
SHIELD slot instead of the weapon -- and the test fails on exactly the broken
case.

**CORRECTED in round 486 (2026-09-23): one flag, and the `reqi` branch is
modelled.** Slots 372/399/400 are read (`0x004ec5a0` / `0x004ec5d0` /
`0x004ec600`), and each is one storage slot's `item+0x190` broken flag, so
"durability at zero" is the whole test, not a collapse of three. The `reqi`
branch's getters write TID 0 for a broken item (`4ead63` / `4eada3` /
`4eadf5`), so a broken item matches nothing and the refusal there is `0x300d`,
not `0x300f`. Nor does every slot-400 call lead to `0x300f`: the one at `58d599`
sets no code (`58d5a6 je 0x58d638`, the loop tail). `session.equippedTypes` now
leaves broken items out. See "A broken weapon or shield satisfies no reqi entry"
(round 486).

**What moved: A SHIPPED VALUE.** A broken weapon now refuses a skill cast, which
is the engine's behaviour and was not srrevamp's. Tagged, because this is the
first player-visible change since v0.1.418.

Round 351 (three recovered rules checked against shipped code, and an evidence
text corrected): THE NAMING LANE SHIPS NOTHING A PLAYER SEES, SO THIS TICK
CHECKED RECOVERED RULES AGAINST THE RUNNING CODE INSTEAD. Three were tested and
**all three already hold**: the 'reqi' cast-requirement override (skill.go
implements both branches, with its own correction history), the berserk
killing-blow earn (EarnOnKill calls the recovered GainChance), and the
level-advantage damage stage (ResolveBlow calls ApplyLevelAdvantage after
mitigation and the critical, which is the engine's order). Verification that
finds nothing is still verification, and it is cheaper than the drift it would
have caught. TWICE I REACHED FOR A SUPERSEDED LIST FROM MEMORY. Round 345's
grep-based orphan figures (252 / 70 / 68) carry the false positives that round
346's AST detector removed, and I twice believed a function was unwired --
berserk.GainChance, then combat.ApplyLevelAdvantage -- when both are plainly
called. The detector correctly reports neither. Round 345's entry is now marked
SUPERSEDED at the number, so the next reader does not treat it as a to-do list.
THE REAL FIND IS AN EVIDENCE TEXT THAT UNDERSTATES ITS OWN FUNCTION.
GObjPC::IsKilledByPlayer's row in recovered_names.tsv said it "returns 1 only
when both parties answer vtable slot 7". The body also requires victim+0x1cbc
AND killer[0x72f] to be non-null before a second slot-7 test -- and this
project's own ledger establishes [0x72e]/[0x72f] as PARTY and GUILD. So cause 5
is a GUILD-CONTEXT kill, not any player kill, and the row omitted the two gates
that carry the whole meaning. That row is what ships into the dump as the
function's comment, so the incomplete version is what a future reader sees;
corrected, and the ledger entry that had already read the fuller condition is
cited. IT CHANGES A PENDING DECISION, AND AGAINST ACTING: duel.go declines to
charge a death penalty and reasoned that "a PC killer takes the 20x branch". Too
simple -- two unguilded duellists never reach cause 5 at all, leaving a duel on
cause 3's 100x/300x pair or on a kind that goes elsewhere entirely, and nothing
read so far distinguishes them. The comment now says so. Finally,
leveldata.DeathPenaltyFactorFor moved out of the unreviewed baseline into
knownOrphans with that reason: unreachable until srrevamp grows open-world PK.

**What moved:** no shipped value, deliberately -- the one decision this touched
came out as "still a guess, do not charge". Three recovered rules verified
against the running code, one shipped evidence text corrected where it
understated its function, one superseded list marked, and one baseline entry

Round 346 (the guard ships after all, and my own prescription was half wrong):

THE CASE BOTH GREPS MISSED: WithdrawCostForLevels is referenced exactly once

orphan before being removed again. ALSO CONFIRMED EN ROUTE THAT ROUND 345'S
OTHER NUMBER WAS MY BUG: fixing the same-file-caller mistake took the grep from
252 orphans to 70, and all 70 were Decode* in internal/session -- the wire
surface the Godot client consumes, legitimately uncalled from Go. AFTER
EXCLUDING THAT AND THE PACKAGES unwired_test.go ALREADY DECLARES PARKED, 46
REMAIN, shipped as a LABELLED BASELINE: listing one is not a claim that it is
fine, only that it is not NEW. TWO CLASSES WERE OBVIOUS ON THE FIRST RUN, and

CONSTRUCTORS I ADDED IN ROUND 332 when the real drop tables were wired --

Round 344 (one vocabulary, two negatives, and a guess of mine disproved): THE
DEFERRED CANDIDATE RESOLVES AGAINST ME. Round 343 left 0x0063d4a0 unnamed and
guessed it "looks like a character state/mode test", since Item_HandleUseItem
calls it with 0xc alongside CanBeEquipedAt, EnterWorld, EnterScriptMode and
SetBodyMode. Read from disassembly as that round prescribed: `ret 0x8`, so
f(EAX = index, object, code); the body indexes a 12-byte-stride table off a
global at ds:0xd6a9f0, compares a generation counter against a "currently held"
pointer, and falls into a noreturn SEH throw helper on mismatch. **It is an
ownership/re-entrancy guard, and its own body never reads the code argument at
all.** The callers are game logic; the function is not. THE LEVER SHARPENED: a
vocabulary is only worth recovering if its call sites can be READ, and what made
AQ_Siege readable was that its callers already carried the engine's own constant
names -- so the sweep now ranks by HOW MANY CALLERS ARE ALREADY NAMED, with the
corrected range guard and the CRT range dropped (it otherwise fills the top with
__lock, _strlen, __calloc_crt). The three known vocabularies rank 1st, 2nd and
4th among non-CRT hits, which is the control. ONE NEW VOCABULARY:
COpenMarketMgr__PostAsyncQeury (0x0047b230, already named, engine's own
spelling) -- 0x0 PutonGoods/PutoutGoods, 0x1 Receipt, 0x4 Search, 0x5
PurchaseGoods, 0x7 GoodsDetailData, 0x8 UpdateOpenMarketGoods, each from its own
On*Req handler. AND A SECOND NEGATIVE THAT MATTERED MORE: 0x00540d00 is called
by CAIState_FOLLOW/HOMING/BATTLE/FLEE/PICKITEM::OnEnter, which makes an AI
vocabulary look obvious. TESTED AGAINST BOTH ENUMS THIS PROJECT HAS ALREADY
RECOVERED AND IT FAILS BOTH: not ai.Message (those are 0x21-0x2b, these are
0x0-0xa), and not ai.State either -- the range fits and BATTLE passes 0x3 while
StateBattle is 3, FLEE passes 0x4 while StateFlee is 4, but FOLLOW passes 0x0
(SPAWN) and HOMING passes 0x2 (WANDER), and BATTLE::OnEnter passes three
different codes. Two agreements out of five is what coincidence looks like in a
small dense range. LEFT UNNAMED -- and the only reason the wrong reading did not
ship is that there were two independently recovered enums to test it against.
0x0050cd80 also left unnamed: seven of its nine codes come from one caller
(SiegeFortress_DispatchCommand), so the callers do not distinguish them.

**What moved:** no shipped value and no names filed, which is the honest
outcome. One vocabulary documented, the ranking sharpened with a control, and
two attractive readings disproved -- one of them my own from last round.

Round 343 (three vocabularies, an engine bound, and the guard I published was
wrong): WORKED THE FOUR CANDIDATES ROUND 342 QUEUED, AND THE FIRST ONE BROKE THE
GUARD THAT ROUND HAD JUST STATED. AQ_Siege's dispatcher has 29 codes across 29
sites -- one raiser each -- so the "codes must be reused across callers" test
flagged it SUSPECT. It is a genuine enum: **each query id has exactly one raiser
because each query is its own function**, and the callers carry THE ENGINE'S OWN
CONSTANT NAMES -- AQ_Siege__QUERY_SIEGE_TAX_RATIO is 0x0, _TAX_ACCUMULATE 0x1,
_TAX_COLLECT 0x2, _HIRED_NPC 0x3, _TEMPORAL_OWNER 0x4,
_MODIFY_GUILD_INTRODUCTION 0x5, _REQUEST_ADD/_REMOVE 0xa/0xb, _ITEM_FORGE_ADD/
_REMOVE 0xc/0xd. Named AQ_Siege_SubmitQuery. SO THE GUARD IS CORRECTED: reuse is
a POSITIVE SIGNAL, NOT A REQUIREMENT; the VALUE RANGE is the test that
discriminates (a one-per-site ratio is only suspicious when the range is also
wide, as with the 43..4730 assert reporter). Published wrong last round, fixed
here, and event_log.md now points at the correction. THE MOST VALUABLE FIND IS A
PARAM VOCABULARY: 0x004b3570 takes (paramId, sourceKind) and ASSERTS
`0x1ff < paramId`, so **the ParamKeeper id space is 0..511** -- a citable engine
bound, now in engine_limits.md. ITS CALLERS VALIDATE THE READING EXACTLY,
because their names encode the ids they pass: AbnormalState_Apply19_p178_179
passes 0xb2/0xb3 = 178/179, _p11 passes 0xb, _p3_143 passes 0x8f = 143, _p4_144
passes 0x90 = 144, Param5And6_ApplyOrRemoveContribution passes 0x5 and 0x6. 178
and 179 are the attacker damage params of the recovered damage pipeline, so this
is the SAME id space the combat work already ships. Named
Param_RefreshContributions -- it walks the param's four contribution lists
filtering on sourceKind and notifies through vtable slots 0x538/0x4e8 on change.
WHETHER IT APPLIES OR REMOVES IS NOT CLAIMED: that is decided inside 0x004b2e00
by the sourceKind, and the callers are named ...ApplyOrRemoveContribution
precisely because they do both. ONE CANDIDATE DEFERRED WITH ITS REASON:
0x0063d4a0 (15 codes, raised by CanBeEquipedAt, EnterWorld, Item_HandleUseItem
with 0xc, EnterScriptMode, SetBodyMode) looks like a character state test, but
its decompiled body computes `param_1 + in_EAX * 0xc`, making param_1 a BASE and
in_EAX an INDEX -- which cannot both hold for a call site pushing the code. Same
mismatch ItemEventLog_Record had, and it needs the same disassembly reading
before either operand is called the state.

**What moved:** no shipped value. Two names, three vocabularies documented in a
new `code_vocabularies.md`, one engine bound filed where it is consumed, a guard
of my own corrected, and one candidate left unnamed for want of settled operands.

Round 342 (the vocabulary lever generalised, with the guard it needs): ROUND 341
RECOVERED ONE VOCABULARY BY HAND; THE SHAPE GENERALISES. A call target with many
sites whose last pushed immediate varies IS a vocabulary, so it was swept across
the whole disassembly -- 23,424 call targets -- WITH ItemEventLog_Record AS THE
CONTROL. It came back at 43 codes / 49 sites, matching round 341's independent
count exactly, which is what licensed the rest. THE BEST NEW HIT: 0x00466f90,
84 sites, **56 distinct kinds**, 75 callers, and it CALLS GameEventLog_FormatRecord
-- which is what places it in that family rather than the item one. Named
GameEventLog_Record, the character/world sibling of ItemEventLog_Record, and its
kinds are named by their already-recovered callers: 0x09 CGame__EnterWorld, 0x16
GObjPC_SetLevel, 0x17 GObjPC_GainExpAndLevel, 0x18/0x19 the Str/Int handlers,
0x1a Mastery_LevelUp, 0x3d-0x55 the guild-job state machine, 0x67-0x70 the
academy, 0xd5/0xd6 the pet classes, 0xef the battle arena. A SECOND ENTRY POINT
SHARES THE KIND SPACE -- 0x00467050, 29 sites, 20 kinds, the same 0x3d/0x3e/0x44/
0x68/0x69/0x6a from the same callers -- AND IS LEFT UNNAMED, because both take
their object in ESI and 0x467050 shows no stack parameters at all, so what
distinguishes them is unsettled and a name would claim it. THE GUARD THE LEVER
NEEDS, FOUND BY ITS OWN TOP HIT BEING WRONG: CGameServer::FUN_00964760 has 128
distinct immediates across 135 sites, nearly ONE PER SITE, running 43 .. 4730.
Those are __LINE__ values -- the function takes IsDebuggerPresent, __vsnprintf_s
and __CxxThrowException_8, so it is an assert reporter whose callers pass their
source line. NOT a vocabulary, and not named either, since it carries no string
of its own. So the lever needs two cheap guards: **one code per site is a
warning, not a win** (a real vocabulary REUSES codes across callers -- 0x9f from
three socket functions, 0x50 from two gold paths), and **check the value range**
(line numbers spread over thousands, event kinds cluster in a byte). Four more
candidates are listed unexamined in event_log.md: AQ_Siege 0x00456ec0 (29 codes),
0x005c80a0 (23), 0x004b3570 (20), 0x0063d4a0 (15).

**What moved:** no shipped value. A one-off technique turned into a swept lever
with a control and two stated guards, a 56-kind character/world event vocabulary
recovered with per-kind evidence, and one name filed; two functions deliberately
left unnamed for want of evidence.

0x00468a80's call sites because Ghidra's argument order contradicted them, and
wrote down the next step -- read the sites in srgs.asm and settle which operand
is the kind. Done, and BOTH READINGS WERE TRUE OF DIFFERENT PARAMETERS. The
convention is __fastcall: `mov ecx,<obj>` / `mov edx,<obj2>` carry the first two
arguments and everything else is pushed, so the last `push <imm>` before the call
is the first STACK argument. Ghidra's `param_1 = int *` is ECX and the call
site's 0x9f is the stack arg -- never in conflict, and the apparent contradiction
was the decompiler dropping the register operands. THE SAME SHAPE THAT FORCED
ROUND 323'S RETRACTION, read the same way round 326 had to read it. 0x00468a80
is now ItemEventLog_Record: **49 call sites, 47 with a kind immediate, 43
distinct kinds, EVERY ONE INSIDE AN ALREADY-NAMED CALLER** -- Item_HandleUseItem
raises 0x10, the trade manager 0x32-0x38, the flea market 0x46/0x4b/0x4d,
CGObjPC::OffsetGold 0x50, and the enchant/socket/make-stuff family 0x5a-0xa0.
THE CROSS-CHECK IS THAT KINDS GROUP BY ACTION, NOT BY FUNCTION: 0x9f is raised by
CEnchant_SocketMaker, _SocketStoneEraser and _SocketStoneInserter alike, 0x83 by
two different CEnchant_*::MakeAttempt, 0x50 by two separate gold paths. That is
what an event kind should do, and it is why the caller counts as evidence rather
than as a coincidence of position -- a use-site, not a curve. TWO SITES PASS NO
IMMEDIATE (CTimedJobManagerForPC/ForPet vslot_005 build the kind in a register)
and are LEFT OUT of the table rather than guessed at. AND WHAT THE TABLE DOES NOT
SAY: the numbers are the server's own and nothing maps them to a name the game
uses, because no such table has been found -- the caller tells you what the event
IS, not what it is CALLED.

**What moved:** no shipped value. A 43-entry item-event vocabulary recovered
with its evidence, the recorder named, and a deferred lead closed by the method
that was written down for it.

Round 339 (one opcode turns out to be 35 commands): THE SIZE-RANKED WORKLIST'S

Round 338 (the worklist made real, and my own classifier caught wrong): ROUND
337 ENDED SAYING THE CORE RANKING "NEEDS THE SAME EXCLUSION THE SIZE TABLE
IMPLIES BEFORE IT IS A WORKLIST". Both halves of doing that came out differently

contains throws constantly; the readers throw on underflow. Containing a throw

would have published a "true core" that excluded a message handler. Rule
dropped; the classifier keeps CRT range, MSVC constructors (vtable into

contamination is SEVENTEEN functions, not a mass, so round 337's framing was
right about the TOP of the list and wrong about its SIZE: the metric barely
moves. Recorded as a correction rather than quietly restated. HANDLER-DEPENDENCE
IS THE WRONG SORT ORDER, which is the useful methodological finding: the most
depended-on unnamed functions are UTILITIES BY CONSTRUCTION, because a utility
is what many handlers share. The number one entry, 0x00401fc0 with 89 handlers,
is **std::string** -- capacity at +0x18, inline buffer at +4, heap pointer above
15 characters, MSVC's small-string optimisation. Below it, null-guarded
accessors of 11 and 15 bytes. SORTING BY SIZE surfaces real logic immediately.

Received: %u gold", "Mercenary Count[%d]", "Starvation", and the PvP kill shapes

Round 334 (12 client handler names, and THREE of my own counts withdrawn):
PAYING THE DEBT ROUND 331 FLAGGED -- "a naive count says 101 unnamed client
handlers sit opposite a named server handler, but the 2026-09-17 entry measured
4; these need reconciling before either is used to name anything." THEY WERE
NEVER IN CONTRADICTION: they are different joins. Join A pairs the server's
REQUEST handler at index i with the client's REPLY handler for 0xb|i -- the two
halves of one transaction. Join B pairs an opcode's single server SENDER with
the client function that consumes it. BOTH OF MY RECOUNTS WERE WRONG, for
different reasons, and each was caught by its own shape. The first gave a
perfect 57 of 57, which is not a result but a tell: `server_senders` holds
ADDRESSES, not names, and my classifier scored a bare hex string as "named".
Resolved properly, Join B is 23 today against 4 on 2026-09-17 -- it grew because
the SERVER side got named in the rounds between, so the old figure was stale
rather than wrong. THE THIRD ERROR WAS THE INTERESTING ONE: Join A's 101/91 was
inflated by a STALE COLUMN. message_handlers.tsv's client_handler symbols are
built from the dump, and round 331's refresh only updated a symbol when the old
and new shared a trailing hex (LAB_x -> FUN_x). It therefore never replaced
FUN_00899630 with TrainingCamp_OnOpenResult -- a name this project had carried
and APPLIED for days. 29 rows were stale that way, so every "unnamed client
handler" count taken off that column, including all of mine, counted named
functions as unnamed. Re-resolved against the client dump and the TSV.
WHAT LICENSED THE NAMING: the join assumes the client's handler for 0xb|i is the
counterpart of the server's handler for 0x7i, and that was VERIFIED rather than
assumed. Sweeping `mov ecx,0xbXXX` through the server disassembly and
attributing each site to its enclosing function by the dump's own boundaries:
**97 of 98 handlers that emit a reply emit their own index** (92 exactly, 5
among others). THE ONE CONTRADICTION IS EXCLUDED -- index 0x0c4 emits only
0xb045, so its 0xb0c4 client handler is somebody else's counterpart, and it is
precisely the case that would have produced a confident wrong name. The
disassembly is srgs.asm (then believed a MODDED build; round 485 retracted
that -- it is the same binary as the dump), which is fine for opcodes and was
checked anyway against the two pairs read by hand in round 328: 0x04c -> 0xb04c
and 0x51d -> 0xb51d, both exact. AN INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION FELL OUT: the
sweep reproduces the 2026-09-17 finding that the client binds 0xb470-0xb47e to
CONTIGUOUS addresses (FUN_00899630, ...730, ...7a0, ...800), the training-camp
family, reached here from the server side without reference to it. 12 NAMES
FILED AND APPLIED (13 applied, failed 0), in the <Subsystem>_On<Action>Result
form their already-named siblings use rather than a new prefix of my own.
**The honest remaining picture: 319 client message handlers, 31 named (10%).**
10 more are transferable once their pairing is verified. **55 are blocked
because the SERVER name is itself a placeholder** -- GObjPC_HandleGuildMsg_0fb
is a subsystem and an opcode, and transferring it would restate the opcode
rather than name anything, which is the error this project corrected once

**What moved:** no shipped value. 12 client functions named and applied, 29
