a mastery: 1 SP from the no-table fallback. This round checked both against
the instructions first. Both readings were wrong, so the server now follows the
function.

	59c611  cmp ecx,eax ; jle 0x59c622    <- current + requested <= GetLevel(), else 0x3804
	59c625  mov cl,[eax+0x20]             <- the mastery's current level
	59c628  test cl,cl ; jne 0x59c638     <- level 0? ...
	59c62c  mov cl,0x1
	59c62e  call 0x5a8bf0                 <- ... set the level to 1 ...
	59c633  jmp 0x59c6d8                  <- ... and skip the loop AND the SP check
	59c64e  cmp esi,0x78 ; jg 0x59c687    <- the cost loop's bound: out to the SP check
	59c669  call 0x411130                 <- RefLevel_GetEntry(esi) = rows[esi-1]
	59c66e  mov ecx,[eax+0x10]            <- leveldata column 2
	59c67c  add [esp+0x14],ecx            <- cost += it
	59c687  ...                           <- the SP check starts here
	59c694  cmp eax,[ecx+0x80] ; jbe      <- cost <= skill points, else 0x3802
	59c6b3  add cl,0x1 ... 59c6cb  mov [eax+0x20],cl   <- the raise
	59c793  test esi,esi ; jle            <- spend only a positive cost

Those addresses are the on-disk exe. The Ghidra dump has the same structure:
`if (bVar2 == 0) { FUN_005a8bf0(); } else { ... do { if (0x78 < (int)uVar4)
break; ...`. Round 483 showed the two are one build.

**(a) `0x78` bounds the loop. It is not a refusal.** `jg 0x59c687` lands on the
skill-point check. The raise at `0x59c6b3`-`0x59c6cb` comes after that check.
No error code goes with `0x78`. All five codes are set elsewhere: `0x3801` at
`0x59c55a`, `0x3805` at `0x59c5cc`, `0x3804` at `0x59c615`, `0x3802` at
`0x59c69c`, and `0x3803` at `0x59c727`, when `GObjPC::FUN_004e7350` fails after
the raise. So a raise from
level 120 still sums row 120's column 2. `0x78 < 120` is false. A raise from
121 or higher sums nothing, costs 0, and still happens.

**(b) The first point is free.** `FUN_005a8bf0` is the mastery record's level
setter: `cmp cl,[eax+0x20] ; je` and then `mov [eax+0x20],cl` under the same
dirty-flag guard as the inline raise at `0x59c6b3`. The call passes cl = 1. The
path jumps to `0x59c6d8`, past the cost loop and past the `0x3802` check. The
cost at `[esp+0x14]` keeps the 0 written at `0x59c51d`, and the spend at
`0x59c793` is skipped. It also fits the table. `RefLevel_GetEntry` indexes
`rows[level-1]`, so level 0 has no row to read.

**(c) What caps a single mastery.** Only `0x3804`. Its comparand is vtable
`+0x124`, `IGObj::GetLevel` (slot 73, recovered in earlier rounds). The raise
is refused when `current + requested > characterLevel`. Nothing else caps one
mastery.

**What moved.**
- `skill.go`: `MasteryLevelCap` is removed. `MasteryCostLevelCeiling = 120`
  names what the `0x78` really does.
- `masteryUpCost` returns 0 for level 0 and for any level above 120, whatever
  the level table holds. Levels 1-120 are unchanged: the table's column 2, or
  the disclosed `level+1` without a table.
- `RaiseMasteryHandler` passes the character's level as the store's cap. Its
  checks keep the engine's order: total (`0x3805`), then character level
  (`0x3804`), then points (`0x3802`). A cost of 0 passes the points check, as
  the engine's level-0 path does by skipping it.
- `leveldata.go`: the comments that called 120 "the single-mastery cap" now say
  what it is. A mastery above 120, which escapes the mastery-lag EXP penalty, is
  now reachable by a character above level 120.
- Client: `hud_panels.gd` no longer greys LEVEL UP with "Not enough skill
  points" for a raise that costs none: a mastery at 0, or one above
  `MASTERY_COST_LEVEL_CEILING := 120`.
- Docs: the 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-16 entries are annotated where they call 120
  a cap. `SYSTEMS.md` anchors the row on `MasteryCostLevelCeiling`.
  `GROUNDING_AUDIT.md` and `LEVELING.md` note the two free cases.

**Still not modelled.** The engine's first check, `FUN_0059d6f0`, looks the
mastery up in the character's own list and refuses a missing one with
`0x3801`. srrevamp does not check mastery ids. A client could therefore take a
free first point in an id that is no real mastery. Before this round that cost
1 SP. Each such point still counts against the 330 total.

The visible change: a new character with 0 SP can take its first point in a
mastery. A character above level 120 can raise a mastery past 120, and each
raise from 121 up is free.

**Tests.**
- `session.TestMasteryUpCostFirstPointIsFree`: `masteryUpCost(0)` is 0 with no
  table, and 0 with a table that has a level-0 row of 7. Level 1 still costs
  its table value or the fallback.
- `session.TestMasteryCostLoopStopsSummingAt120` pins
  `MasteryCostLevelCeiling = 120`. With a table carrying 119/120/121/140 at
  5000/6000/7000/9000, costs are 5000, 6000, 0 and 0. With no table, costs are
  120, 121, 0 and 0.
- `session.TestRaiseMasteryFirstPointFreeAndNoCapAt120` drives the handler over
  the wire:
  - A level-1 character with 0 SP raises Bicheon 0 -> 1 and has 0 SP left. The
    next raise is `mastery at level cap`.
  - A level-122 character at Bicheon 120 with 6000 SP raises to 121 and has 0
    left. It raises to 122 with 0 SP. Then it is refused `mastery at level cap`.
- The old `TestMasteryLevelCap` pinned the wrong reading and is replaced. The
  seed helpers in `masterycap_test.go` and `learngate_test.go` now pass
  `seedMasteryCap = 255`, the byte's maximum.

Negative case: with only `skill.go` reverted, plus a test-only shim that
defines the new constant, all three new tests failed:
- `masteryUpCost(0) = 1`, and `= 7` with the level-0 row.
- `masteryUpCost(121) = 122`, and `= 7000` with the table.
- The handler answered `not enough skill points` for the free first raise.

A second run skipped the first-raise half. There, 120 -> 121 was refused
`mastery at level cap`. The existing tests run beside them in the negative case,
`TestRaiseMasteryTotalCapIsFlatForChina` and
`TestMasteryUpCostUsesTheLevelTable`, passed against the old code. They also
pass against the new code. `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green.
On the render box, `client/tools/remote_godot.sh tests` ran 77 suites with 0
failing, and `check` compiled 239 scripts and 5 scenes (`ALL LOAD`). The client
grey-out change was not rendered, so it is read from the code only.

## Batch-1 review follow-ups: a party of one, the receiver's +0x1cd8, and ONE server build (round 485)

The five rounds above each passed an adversarial review. The reviewers' non-blocking notes held
three real corrections and a handful of stale sentences; this round lands them.

**1. There is one server build, not two.** The 2026-09-18 entry "Two server builds: the dump is
authoritative, srgs.asm is a mod" is RETRACTED in place. Its evidence was a search for `imul`
immediates in the death-penalty block that found three and no `0x14`; the on-disk exe computes the
player branch's ×20 as `0x4e6aa2 lea esi,[esi+esi*4]; add esi,esi; add esi,esi`. All four branches
(×100 at `0x4e6a77`, ×20, ×300 at `0x4e6ad2`, ×100 at `0x4e6aff`) are there, in `srv.asm` and
`srgs.asm` alike (both are disassemblies of md5 `864ffd0d2b76…`, which is also the Blitzkrieq copy).
Consequence for method: `srv.asm` is valid for values, not only structure; a constant that looks
absent from asm must be searched for in its strength-reduced forms (lea/shl/add) before absence is
claimed. The follow-up ".rdata shared across both builds" entry and the round-328 aside calling
`srgs.asm` "the MODDED build" carry superseded notes.

**2. The gap bonus needs a second party member.** Round 480 paid it to a party of one because the
engine's gate (`0x410018`) tests the party pointer, not a count. That is a correct reading of the
gate and a wrong model of the world: the engine only creates a party when an invite is accepted,
with two member records at once (`trs_wait_response::FUN_005be4f0`, party.md round 271), so the
pointer never meets a party of one through creation. srrevamp's `handlePartyCreate` makes a party
of just the leader, which turned "create party" into a solo EXP bonus. `session.killExpFor` now
gates on `inPartyWithOthers` (two or more members). What the engine does when a party of two drops
to one is **unread** — the party lives in another server process — and that case follows the same
reading, disclosed in the code. The party EXP-share multiplier (`applyPartyExpBonus`) is unaffected:
its `(members-1)` term is already zero for one.

**3. The `+0x1cd8` factor in the kill reward is the receiver's mastery-lag scale.**
`Formula_MonsterExpReward` loads `fld [edi+0x1cd8]` at `0x410660` and then `mov esi,edi` hands
the same object to `Formula_ExpScaleByLevelDiff` as its receiver, so EDI is the PC being paid.
`GObjPC_RecalcLevelDiffExpScale` is the float's only writer (`leveldata.MasteryExpScale`), and the
session already applies it (`applyMasteryExpScale`). The `KillExp` doc comment still called it an
unmodelled "premium/event rate written only by CTJ_PremiumKeeper's neighbours", the kill-EXP row of
GROUNDING_AUDIT.md said `victim[0x1cd8]`, and the Ghidra plate for `0x004105d0` in
ApplyKnownNames.java said `target[0x1cd8]`; all three are corrected. No value changes.

**Smaller fixes.** Two dated Open bullets about `[0x72e]`/the tier bonus are marked closed/superseded
(round 480 shipped it). Round 482's `0x18b6` condition said "bit `2`" for a `& 2` test; it now says
mask `2` (bit 1). A leveldata comment that read "0x78 being exactly the 0x78 in Mastery_LevelUp"
now names the coincidence it meant (the recompute's `ref > 0x78` cut-off). `MemStore.Create`'s
membership-before-uniqueness order (round 481) had no test that could tell the orders apart; a
guilded founder re-creating their own taken name now must get `ErrAlreadyInGuild`, and a guildless
character asking for it `ErrNameTaken`.

**Tests.** `session.TestKillExpPartyGapBonus` now expects 327 (no bonus) for a party of one and for
a party dropped back to one, 432 for both members of a party of two. Negative case run: with
`killExpFor` put back on `inParty`, both one-member cases fail with 432. `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...`
is green.

Behaviour change: a player alone in a party they created no longer earns the level-gap EXP bonus;
parties of two or more are unchanged from round 480.

## A broken weapon or shield satisfies no reqi entry: the engine's TID getters read it as an empty slot (0x300d) (round 486)

A skill with a `reqi` list (1,094 real skills) was cast with a broken item in the
required slot. `session.equippedTypes` fed every worn item into
`combat.SkillAllowsEquipment`, whatever its durability, so a broken staff still
satisfied a staff skill. The engine refuses it. This round reads why, and with
which code.

**The reading.** `Skill_CheckCastRequirement` (`0x0058d480`) reads the worn types
up front when the list is non-empty:

	58d4c9  call 0x4ead80        <- the shield's TID into [esp+0x14]
	58d4d4  call 0x4ead40        <- the weapon's TID into [esp+0x38] (Equip_GetWeaponTID)
	58d57e  call 0x4eadc0        <- an armour part's TID, index = the entry's value
	58d5c8  call 0x4eadc0        <- the same, in the value-0 part scan

All three getters test the item's `+0x190` before they read its TID, and write 0
if it is set:

	4ead63  cmp DWORD PTR [eax+0x190],0x0 ; jne 0x4ead58 -> mov WORD PTR [edi],0x0
	4eada3  cmp DWORD PTR [eax+0x190],0x0 ; jne 0x4ead98 -> mov WORD PTR [edi],0x0
	4eadf5  cmp DWORD PTR [esi+0x190],0x0 ; jne 0x4eae0b -> mov WORD PTR [edi],0x0

`+0x190` is the flag `GItemEquip::SetBrokenFlag` (`0x00495980`) stores.
`GItemEquip::AddDurability` passes it `new < 1` (the call at `496e1b`) and
`CGItemEquip::Create` passes `durability == 0`. So a broken item's TID is 0, the
same as an empty slot's. A weapon or shield entry compares `TID >> 11` against
its value (`58d513`, `58d542`), and every shipped value is non-zero, so nothing
matches. The walk ends at `58d689`: `[esp+0x1c]` is still 0, and `58d695`
returns **`0x300d`**, `UIIT_SKILL_USE_FAIL_WRONGWEAPON`.

**The earlier `0x300f` reading was wrong for this branch.** The first plan for
this item applied `0x300f` (`UIIT_SKILL_USE_FAIL_BROKEN_WEAPON`) here, and its
implementer aborted it. A vtable call follows each match: `+0x5d0` at `58d527`
(weapon), `+0x63c` at `58d556` (shield), and `+0x640` twice, at `58d599` for an
armour entry with a Value and at `58d5de` in the value-0 part scan. Only three of
the four can set `0x300f`:

	58d533  je 0x58d607                  <- +0x5d0 answered 0
	58d562  je 0x58d607                  <- +0x63c answered 0
	58d5eb  je 0x58d605                  <- the scan's +0x640 answered 0;
	58d605  xor edi,edi                     58d605 clears the match flag and
	58d607  mov [esp+0x1c],0x300f           falls into 58d607

A failed `+0x640` at `58d599` sets no code: `58d5a4 test eax,eax ; 58d5a6 je
0x58d638` jumps straight to the loop tail, the same as no match. And none of the
four can answer 0 after a match on a shipped record. They are CGObjPC's slots
372/399/400 (`0x004ec5a0` / `0x004ec5d0` / `0x004ec600`, table `0x00af59fc`),
and each answers `item == 0 || item+0x190 == 0` on the same storage slot the
getter just read (`4ec5bb` / `4ec5eb` / `4ec631`). For a shipped skill,
`0x300f` comes only from the weapon-byte branch (`58d719`: `+0x5d0`, then
`58d72a mov [esp+0x20],0x300f`), and `weaponIsBroken` already models that.

**What moved.**
- `session.equippedTypes` skips a worn item when `durability.IsBroken` is true.
  The skip comes before the reference lookup, because an empty slot has no row to
  read either. Untracked (-1) is not broken and stays in. The refusal is the
  existing "wrong equipment for this skill".
- `combat.SkillAllowsEquipment` / `Satisfied` are unchanged. Their stale "NOT
  MODELLED: srrevamp has no per-instance durability" comment is replaced with the
  reading above.
- `skill.go`'s weapon-byte comment said "three predicates collapsed into one". It
  now says one flag on three storage slots.
- Names filed in `docs/protocol/recovered_names.tsv`:
  `Equip_GetShieldTID` (`0x004ead80`), `Equip_GetArmourPartTID` (`0x004eadc0`,
  indexing `DAT_00c63f44` = `0x80000000,0,2,1,4,3,5`, the helm/shoulder/mail/
  pants/gauntlet/boots storage slots for TypeID4 1-6),
  `CGObjPC::IsWeaponServiceable` (`0x004ec5a0`) and
  `CGObjPC::IsShieldServiceable` (`0x004ec5d0`). `0x004ec600` is renamed from
  `UseItem` to `CGObjPC::IsEquipPartServiceable`. `UseItem` was a slot-400
  propagation from `CGObjCOS_Pet`, and the body is a per-part broken-flag test.
  These are descriptive names; the game's own are not recovered. They are filed
  only: ApplyRecoveredNames was not run on the RE box.
- `GROUNDING_AUDIT.md`'s broken-weapon section and `igobj_vtable.md`'s "What
  this does NOT recover" are corrected to match.

**Flagged, not corrected.** The same propagation put `UseItem` on
`CGObjNPCNPC` `0x004c9310`, `CGObjSiegeObject` `0x004ccca0` and
`CGObjSiegeStruct` `0x004ced10`. Two of those are one accessor: `0x004ccca0` is
`mov eax,[ecx+0x34] ; test ; jne ; ret ; mov eax,[eax+0x20] ; ret`, and
`0x004ced10` is the same without the null guard, `mov eax,[ecx+0x34] ; mov
eax,[eax+0x20] ; ret`. So those two plausibly are one virtual. `0x004c9310`
looks key 2 up in the `+0x1c78` interaction set through the find helper
`0x431790` and may then call `0x488650`. Different bodies alone would not
separate these from `0x004ec600`, because overrides of one virtual differ by
design. The stack cleanup does separate two of them. `0x004ec600` pops one
argument (`ret 0x4`), and so does `0x004c9310`, but the two siege bodies pop none
(`ret`). A virtual has one signature, so the siege classes' slot 400 is not the
virtual CGObjPC's slot 400 is. For `0x004c9310` the cleanup settles nothing.
The three rows are left as they are until someone reads them. **Round 490:** the
cleanup does settle the propagation that named all three. It linked these
classes' tables and inferred "a differing slot is two overrides of one virtual";
slot 400 has overrides of two arities among them, so for slot 400 that premise is
false, and every name it carried there -- including `0x004c9310`'s -- is
unsupported rather than merely unconfirmed. The three rows are marked SUSPECT in
recovered_names.tsv pending an audit of slot propagation past the shared base's
table.

**Engine details NOT modelled.** They are disclosed in
`combat.CastRequirement.Satisfied` and are not checked against any record:
1. An armour entry with Value 0 scans parts 1..6 in order (`58d5c0`) and stops
   at the first part not of the Kind. The answer depends on the first part, not
   on any part.
2. An ALL-of list with all five entries filled and matching falls out of the loop
   with the match flag cleared (`58d649`) and returns `0x300d` (`58d681` ->
   `58d695`).
3. A weapon or shield entry with Value 0 matches an EMPTY slot in the engine
   (`TID >> 11 == 0`). No shipped record has one.
4. An armour entry with a Value compares TypeID4 only, never the Kind. No shipped
   record has one.

Separately, in the weapon-byte branch the engine calls `+0x5d0` whatever the type
match said. A broken weapon of the wrong kind is therefore `0x300f` in the engine
and "wrong weapon" here. Both refuse.

**Tests.** `session.TestReqiBrokenWeaponSatisfiesNothing` drives
`equippedTypes` + `combat.SkillAllowsEquipment` over the memory stores:
- a staff (6/15) at `durability.Broken` on a `[{6,15}]` any-of skill is refused;
- the same staff at durability 1 and at Untracked (-1) is allowed;
- a broken buckler on `[{4,1}]` is refused, and the same buckler at 5 is allowed;
- `[{6,15},{4,1}]` with a whole staff and a broken buckler is allowed any-of and
  refused all-of.

Negative case: with `skill.go` and `attacktype.go` stashed, the new test failed
three ways: the broken staff was allowed, the broken buckler was allowed, and
the all-of list was allowed. It passes with them restored.
`go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green.

Behaviour change: a skill that requires a specific weapon or shield kind through
`reqi` is refused with "wrong equipment for this skill" when the only matching
item is broken. Before this round the cast went through.

## Guild founder must be alive, level >= 20, and hold >= 500,000 gold; founding deducts 500,000 (FUN_00514b20 + GObjPC::FUN_004e4140) (round 487)

Until this round, any character could found a guild for free. The engine refuses
a founder who is dead, below level 20 or carrying less than 500,000 gold, and it
charges the 500,000.

**The check.** `CGuildManager::HandleCreateGuild` (`0x00514ce0`) calls
`FUN_00514b20` first, before the name-length test that round 481 wired. The
function is seven tests. `in_EAX` is the founder's `GObjPC`. Steps 2-4 are the new
rules, re-read from `/var/tmp/decomp_server` this round:

	cVar2 = (**(code **)(*in_EAX + 0xf8))();    if (cVar2 != '\x01') return 0x4c07;
	bVar3 = (**(code **)(*in_EAX + 0x124))();   if (bVar3 < 0x14)    return 0x4c0a;
	iVar1 = *(int *)(in_EAX[0xd] + 0x7c);
	if ((iVar1 < 1) && ((iVar1 < 0 || (*(uint *)(in_EAX[0xd] + 0x78) < 500000)))) return 0x4c0c;

Vtable `+0xf8` is `IGObj::GetLifeState` and `+0x124` is `IGObj::GetLevel`
(`igobj_vtable.md`). The client names the codes (`error_codes.md`, "The table", rows `0x4c07`,
`0x4c0a` and `0x4c0c`; this cited lines 569-571, which round 518's additions above the table
shifted):
`GUILDERR_IM_DEAD`, `GUILDERR_TOO_LOW_CREATOR_LEVEL` and
`GUILDERR_NOT_ENOUGH_GOLD`. The gold is the 64-bit pair at `+0x78/+0x7c` of the
`+0x34` object, the same place `CGuild::CheckLevelUpCost` (`0x005c6240`) reads
it. The remaining steps are the character lock (`0x4c09`), `GetJobState != 4`
(`0x4c57`), a pending `FindTimedJob(2,1)` (`0x4c3c`) and already-in-a-guild
(`0x4c17`). The last of these was already enforced; the other three have nothing
in srrevamp to test.

**The deduction.** This item's first plan said founding costs nothing, and
batch 1's implementer aborted it. The cost is real. It is taken on the create
job's reply, not in the check. `FUN_005c5f90` sends job 0
(`SendOlappedGuildJobReqToSM(pc, 0, 0)`). Case 0 of
`trs_sm_guildjob::FUN_005c8990` is `trs_sm_guildjob::FUN_005c8bf0`, which reads
the gold, calls `GObjPC::FUN_004e4140`, logs `"Gold: %I64d ==> %I64d"` (event
`0x3d`) and sends `0xb0f0`, the create response. `srv.asm` shows
`FUN_004e4140`'s argument pushes: `4e414e push 0xffffffff` / `4e4150 push
0xfff85ee0` form the int64 -500,000, and `4e4157 call edx` goes through vtable
`+0x16c`, which is `IGObj::OffsetGold`. `FUN_005c8bf0` is its only caller (`5c8c39
call 0x4e4140`). `FUN_005d0e00` also holds a 500,000, but it is a different
number with a different purpose: only `FUN_005c7900` calls it, after refusing a
guild below level 4 (`0x4c52`).

**What moved.**
- `guild.go`: `MinCreatorLevel` (20), `CreateGoldRequired` (500,000),
  `ErrCreatorDead`, `ErrCreatorLevelTooLow`, `ErrNotEnoughGold`, and
  `CheckCreator(alive, level, gold)` in the engine's order. The comments quote
  the ladder and the deduction.
- `session.handleGuildCreate`: after `resolveCharacterID`, `chars.GetByID`, then
  `guild.CheckCreator(HP > 0, Level, Gold)` before `guilds.Create`. HP > 0 stands
  in for `GetLifeState == 1`, since srrevamp stores no life state. After `Create`
  succeeds, `chars.DeductGold(CreateGoldRequired)`. If the deduction fails, the
  handler calls `guilds.Leave` for the founder, which disbands a one-member
  guild in both stores, and replies with the not-enough-gold message. This
  rollback is srrevamp's own handling, because the engine's `OffsetGold` has no
  refusal path. It is disclosed in the code and in `guild.md`, together with its
  one window (a character joining by id before the rollback runs gets the
  leadership instead).
- `guildErrorMessage` has three new cases, in our own wording: `cannot found a
  guild while dead`, `a guild founder must be at least level 20` and `founding a
  guild requires 500000 gold`.
- Client: `World3D._on_guild_create_result` re-requests the character's stats
  after a successful create, the same way a shop buy refreshes the purse. The
  server pushes no gold update for either.
- `docs/protocol/guild.md` has a new section, "Founding a guild — `FUN_00514b20`
  (round 487)", with the eight-step table and what srrevamp enforces. The Opcodes
  note now names `FUN_005c8bf0` as the success-path sender of `0xb0f0`.
  `SYSTEMS.md`'s Guild row anchors on `CheckCreator` and `CreateGoldRequired`.

**Tests.**
- `guild.TestCheckCreator` pins 20 and 500,000 and checks eight cases:
  (true,20,500000) nil, (true,19,500000) level, (true,20,499999) gold,
  (true,99,1<<40) nil, (false,1,0) dead, (false,99,1<<40) dead, (true,19,0) level
  and (true,20,-1) gold.
- `session.TestGuildCreateRequiresLevelAndGold` sends `OpGuildCreate` through
  `LoginHandler` + `GuildHandler` over memory stores:
  - A fresh level-1 character with 1,000 gold gets the level message.
  - At level 20 it gets the gold message.
  - At 499,999 gold it gets the gold message.
  - At 500,000 it founds the guild and is left with 0.
  - A level-19 character with 500,000 gets the level message.
  - A level-20 character with 500,000 at 0 HP gets the dead message.
  - A founder with 1,234,567 is left with 734,567.
  - Every refusal leaves the character guildless and its gold untouched.
- `session.TestGuildCreateRollsBackWhenGoldCannotBeTaken` wraps the character
  store in a test-only type whose `DeductGold` fails. The founder ends
  guildless, with its gold untouched, gets the not-enough-gold reply, and the
  name is free again.
- `TestGuildFullFlow`, `TestGuildInfoFlow` and
  `TestGuildCreateRejectsBadNameLength` now qualify their founder first
  (`qualifyFounder`: level 20 and +500,000 gold).

Negative cases:
- With `session/guild.go` stashed, both new session tests fail. The level-1
  founder gets guild 1, and the rollback test's founder also gets guild 1.
- With only the `DeductGold` call mutated out, the 500,000 founder keeps 500,000.
- With `guild.go` also stashed, the tests do not compile.

`go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green. On the render box,
`client/tools/remote_godot.sh check` loaded 239 scripts and 5 scenes ("ALL
LOAD"), and `remote_godot.sh tests` ran 77 suites with 0 failing.

Behaviour change: a character below level 20, a dead character, or one carrying
less than 500,000 gold can no longer found a guild, and the guild tab shows the
reason. Founding a guild now costs 500,000 gold.

## GM-spawned monsters carry their BC radius and attack fields; ApproachBand at exactly 10 adds no reach (round 488)

Two defects in the attack-distance rule's inputs, split out of the
attack-approach-band plan's step 0.

**GM `/spawn` monsters had no BCRadius.** `cmd/server.gmSpecies` built the
`combat.Species` the GM console's `/spawn` hands `Hub.SpawnSpecies` without
`BCRadius`, `AttackReuseMs` or `AttackRange`. `maintainMonster`'s roster spawn
set all three. A GM-spawned Mangyang therefore had BCRadius 0 instead of 6
(characterdata col 50, round 247). `combat.ApproachBand`'s base was 4 + 0 instead
of 4 + 6, so its reach was 6 units shorter than a roster Mangyang's. Its attack
cadence and range were also unknown (0) instead of skilldata cols 14/21
(round 254: 3000 ms, 10).

Both paths now call one helper, `combatSpeciesOf(spec)`, so they cannot drift
again. It defaults a zero BCRadius to `combat.PlayerBCRadius` (4), as the
roster spawn always did. `gm.Species` keeps Zone/MaxHP/Defense/Attack/Gold/X/Z as
before.

**At exactly 10 the reach gets no range either.** Re-read this session from the
dump, `CGCharAutoCommandActor::Tick_Attack` (`0x004ad8e0`), phase 0:

	if (fVar2 < _DAT_00b45dc0 == (fVar2 == _DAT_00b45dc0)) {        // r > 4
	  if ((fVar2 <= _DAT_00b46010) || (_DAT_00b45b44 <= fVar2)) {   // r >= 10
	    if (_DAT_00b45b44 < fVar2) {                                  // r > 10
	      +0x14 = 0.7 * r + +0x14;
	      +0x18 = r + +0x18;
	    }
	  } else { +0x14 = (r - 2) + +0x14; +0x18 = r + +0x18; }
	} else { +0x14 = r + +0x14; +0x18 = r + +0x18; }

Phase 3 has the same shape: `if (fVar2 <= _DAT_00b45b44) goto LAB_004ae04f`
skips both stores. The skill tick, `Tick_UseSkill` (`0x004ae590`), has the same
single `if (_DAT_00b45b44 < fVar1)` around both adds. `0xb45b44` is `00002041`
= 10.0f. So at r == 10 the action carries the bare BC sum in both `+0x14` (stop)
and `+0x18` (reach). `ApproachBand`'s `default:` case set only `stop = base` and
left `reach = base + 10`. It now sets `reach = base` too, and the rule comment in
`reach.go` states g(r) for the reach.

**Tests.**
- `cmd/server.TestGMSpawnCarriesBCRadius` checks every `gmSpecies()[i]`:
  - `BCRadius` equals `monsterSpecs[i].BCRadius`, or `PlayerBCRadius` when that
    is 0.
  - `AttackReuseMs` and `AttackRange` equal the spec's.
  - Mangyang's BCRadius is 6.
- `combat.TestApproachBand`'s "exactly ten" row now wants reach 4 + 6 (was
  4 + 6 + 10).

Negative cases: with `cmd/server/main.go` and `internal/combat/reach.go`
stashed, `TestGMSpawnCarriesBCRadius` failed for all eleven species
("GM spawn BCRadius = 0, want 6", "attack reuse/range = 0/0, want 3000/10") and
`TestApproachBand` failed with "exactly ten: got stop 10 reach 20, want 10 / 10".
With them restored both pass. `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green.

Behaviour change: a monster spawned with GM `/spawn` can be hit from as far away
as a roster spawn of the same species. For a Mangyang that is 6 units further than
before. A GM-spawned monster also counterattacks no faster than its attack skill's
ReuseDelay (`Hub.CounterattackReady` reads `AttackReuseMs`; 0 imposed no cadence).
A skill or weapon with range exactly 10 no longer gets +10 reach. In the roster,
Mangyang's and Stone Ghost's attack skills have Range 10, but nothing in the
server reads `Monster.AttackRange` yet, so their behaviour does not change.

## Carry CanUse (itemdata col 24) and refuse using a non-usable item (Item_HandleUseItem 0x183e) (round 489)

**The engine refuses to use an item whose CanUse bit is clear, and srrevamp did
not.** `Item_HandleUseItem` (`0x00510980`), re-read this session, fetches the
item, passes the state check (`0x1889`), then:

	iVar5 = (**(code **)(*piVar6 + 0xe0))();
	if (iVar5 == 0) {
	  uStack_e8 = 0x183e;
	}
	else {
	  puVar7 = (ushort *)CGObj::GetTID();
	  if (*puVar7 == auStack_ec[0]) { ... ItemCooldowns::IsReady ... 0x185b ...

`0xe0` is vtable slot 56, `IGObj::CanUse` (`docs/protocol/igobj_vtable.md`).
`0x183e` is `UIIT_MSG_STRGERR_CANNOT_BE_USED` (`docs/protocol/error_codes.md`).
The seven `CGItem*` vtables were found by scanning `SR_GameServer.exe` for the
dword `0x00483ee0` and naming each hit's vtable through its RTTI locator. All
seven hold `CGObj::CanUse` (`0x00483ee0`) at slot 56, and `CanTrade`/`CanSell` at
49/50 confirm the base. `CGObj::CanUse` returns `refobj+0x8c >> 8 & 1`, and
`RefObjCommon_ExtractData` (`0x006a3090`) sets bit 8 as `-(cVar1 != 0) & 0x100`.

**The column is 24.** This is round 460's anchoring in
`item_capability_flags.md`, re-measured over the combined itemdata (21,552 item rows):

- Column 24 holds `0` (19,970 rows), `1` (1,369) and `129` (213).
- It is non-zero on **99 of 99** HP/MP potion rows (TypeID 3/3/1). It is zero on
  every equipment row except the 28 cash-shop avatars (3/1/14). It is zero on
  every elixir (3/3/10) and every alchemy material or stone (3/3/11).
- The mall inventory and warehouse expansions (24365/24366) read 1, so this gate
  does not block the warehouse item.
- **Column 23**, where the file's older read-count table put `CanUse`, reads 0
  on all 25 HP potions. It cannot be the bit a potion is used through. That table
  now carries a note saying it is superseded from column 18 on.

**Change.**
- `export-refdata` gains `fCanUse = 24`. It emits record index 68 through a new
  `nonZero` helper: `"1"` for any non-zero number, the parser's `c != 0`, so 129
  arrives as usable. `nonZero` is defined once for the later flag columns to
  reuse.
- `refdata` item CSV column 68 `CanUse`, a strict suffix.
  `ItemCSVColumnCount` is now 69. `Item.CanUse` is the last field.
- Permission default: the loader sets `CanUse = true` unless column 68 is
  present, and `items.can_use` is `BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE`. An export or
  import older than this column leaves every item usable, the same rule as
  `CanTrade`/`CanSell`/`CanDrop`. A hand-built `refdata.Item{}` forbids use; say
  `CanUse: true`.
- `session.UseItemHandler` refuses `"that item cannot be used"` right after the
  item lookup, before the restores-nothing check and the reuse delay. This is the
  engine's order. No item is consumed and nothing is healed.

**Why it mattered.** A non-usable row's Param block can still read as restore
amounts. 7001 (`ITEM_ETC_ARCHEMY_ATTRSTONE_MD_11`, column 24 = 0) exports
RestoreHP 11 from column 118. Before this round, right-clicking such an item
passed the "restores nothing" check, healed the player and ate the item.

**Tests.**
- `export-refdata.TestItemRecordReadsCanUseFromColumn24` sets columns 23/24/25
  to 1/0/1, then 0/1/0, then 0/129/0. It checks `record[68]` against "0", "1"
  and "1", and checks that `LoadItemsCSV` agrees. The column is written as the
  literal 24, not `fCanUse`. The existing round trip checks the width against
  `ItemCSVColumnCount`.
- `refdata.TestCanUseDefaultsToUsable`: a 68-column row loads usable, a
  trailing "0" forbids use, and a trailing "1" permits it.
- `refdata.TestCanUseFalseSurvivesSQL`: `Item{ID: 987656, CanUse: false}`
  reads back false from both `GetItem` and `ListAll`. `fillStruct` sets every
  bool true and the schema default is true, so the full-field audit alone
  cannot see a lost false.
- `session.TestUseItemRefusesAnItemWhoseCanUseIsClear` starts the character
  50 HP down. An item with CanUse clear and non-zero (illustrative) restore
  amounts is refused with the exact reason, keeps its 5, and heals nothing. A
  potion (RestoreHP 120, CanUse set) restores HP and leaves 4.

Negative cases:
- **All production files stashed:** every new test fails to build, because the
  field does not exist.
- **Each file stashed alone, the field kept:**
  - `useitem.go` stashed: the handler test fails. The item was used ("RestoredHP:
    19 ... Remaining:4"), was consumed ("4 left, want 5") and healed
    ("HP 150 -> 169").
  - `csv.go` stashed: `TestCanUseDefaultsToUsable` fails, and the export test
    fails on its two usable cases.
  - `main.go` stashed: the export test panics on `record[68]` ("index out of
    range [68] with length 68").
  - `sqlstore.go` stashed: `TestEveryItemFieldSurvivesSQL` fails ("1 of 69
    Item fields did not survive").
- Restored: all pass, and `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green.

**Deploy note.** srrevamp-01's `items` table gains `can_use DEFAULT TRUE` on
the next server start, so nothing is refused there until `export-refdata` and
`import-refdata` are re-run against the player's own itemdata. Batch that
re-export with the other exporter items in this series (CanPick is next, record
index 69).

**Found and not fixed: the `CanDrop` column.** `fCanDrop` is 19, but round 460's
table puts `CanDrop` at 20 and the `& 0x80`/`& 0x40` field at 19. Round 460's
header also claimed the code read 20. Bit 0 of the two columns disagrees on
7,997 of 21,552 rows. Nothing in the server reads `CanDrop`, so no behaviour
depends on it yet. `item_capability_flags.md`'s header now records the
disagreement instead of the wrong claim.

## Batch-2 review follow-ups: slot 400 is not one virtual, and six stale claims (round 490)

Rounds 486-489 each passed review; this round lands the reviewers' non-blocking notes, each
re-checked against the dump or `srv.asm` before it was written down.

**Slot 400's propagated names are unsupported.** Round 486 renamed CGObjPC's slot 400
(`0x004ec600`) from a propagated `UseItem` to `IsEquipPartServiceable`, and flagged the three
other classes the same propagation had named. The decisive fact is arity: `CGObjCOS::UseItem`
`0x004d57b0`, CGObjNPCNPC's `0x004c9310` and CGObjPC's `0x004ec600` all end in `ret 0x4`
(`4d5ac2`, `4c9380`, `4ec60b`), while CGObjSiegeObject `0x004ccca0` and CGObjSiegeStruct
`0x004ced10` end in plain `ret`. One virtual has one signature, so slot 400 is not one virtual
across the tables the propagation linked, and its premise -- "vtables sharing eight or more
identical slots share an inherited table, so a differing slot is two overrides of one virtual" --
is false at slot 400. The likely mechanism: classes that share a base's table each APPEND their own
virtuals past its end, and an index past the shared prefix names different functions in each. The
three rows are marked SUSPECT in recovered_names.tsv (not renamed: nothing yet names what they do),
and the obvious next step is an audit of every propagated name whose slot lies past the linked
classes' shared prefix.

**`0x300f` is reachable from three calls, not every serviceability call.** error_codes.md and
GROUNDING_AUDIT.md said the reqi walk returns `0x300f` when slot `0x5d0`, `0x63c` or `0x640`
answers 0. The Valued-armour `+0x640` call at `58d599` does not: `58d5a6 je 0x58d638` goes to the
loop tail with no store. Only `58d527` (`je 58d607`), `58d556` (`je 58d607`) and the Value-0 scan's
`58d5de` (`je 58d605`, falling into `58d607`) reach the `0x300f` store. Both docs now say so.

**`CanUse` is not the first check.** Round 489's comments called it "the engine's first question
about the item". `Item_HandleUseItem` checks, in order: the slot range, an empty slot (`0x1809`),
the rental expiry (`FUN_00492680` -> `0x183d`), the user's life state (`0x1889`: a state other
than 1 passes only when it is 2 and the item answers `FUN_004929c0` with a TID class `& 0xf800 ==
0x3000`; state 2 is DEAD -- round 413 had already closed that, and round 491 confirmed it
independently from the resurrection scroll's `0x1887`), then `CanUse` (`0x183e`), then the TID match. Three comments reworded; `CGObj::CanUse`'s leading `IsItem` call is noted.

**Round 488's exactly-10 reach change alters no player's reach.** A census on the RE box: skilldata
column 21 is exactly 10 on 2,080 rows, every one `MSKILL_` (monster) or `PSKILL_` (pet); itemdata
column 94 is never 10 (it takes 0/6/18/100/150/180). `ApproachBand` is called only for the player's
swing and skill (`session/keepup.go`), so the change is latent. SYSTEMS.md's damage-pipeline row
said the reach rule was "data wired, behaviour not yet"; the reach half is live and only the
server-side walk to the stop distance is unbuilt, which it now says.

**Guild founding is paid on the success reply only**, now with the evidence in guild.md:
`FUN_005c8990` (the dispatcher whose case 0 deducts) has one caller, `trs_sm_guildjob::vslot_002`;
`vslot_003` and `OnTimeout` go to `trs_wait_response::FUN_005cc8d0`, whose case 0 is
`FUN_005ccb50`, which logs event `0x3e` and reads no gold.

**Smaller.** The guild package comment no longer calls the system "entirely own design; no real
guild data to RE". `equippedTypes`' comment on SetBrokenFlag's three exemptions no longer says all
three "need not" matter while naming one as a gap: two cannot arise, vslot 284 is an unread,
disclosed gap. item_capability_flags.md's header no longer lists `CanDrop` at column 20 as settled.
SYSTEMS.md's capability row anchors `CanUse`. TODO.md no longer calls `0x4ad8e0`
`ActionTick_UseSkill` (round 256 named it `Tick_Attack`). Round 352's entry and round 486's flagged
paragraph carry pointers to their corrections.

**Found by round 489's review, queued as its own item:** the exporter emits itemdata column 118
(Param1) as `RestoreHP` for every item, so a `CanUse` item that is not a potion -- a return scroll,
a cure item, a mall storage expansion, a cash avatar -- still "heals" and is consumed. That is the
first item of the next batch.

Docs and comments only; no behaviour changes. `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green.

## Only recovery items restore HP/MP: a CanUse item of another kind no longer heals from its Param1 (round 491)

**The bug (round 489's review).** `export-refdata` emits itemdata columns 118/120/122/124
(Param1..4) as `RestoreHP`/`RestoreHPPct`/`RestoreMP`/`RestoreMPPct` for every row, and
`UseItemHandler` healed whenever any of them was positive. So any `CanUse` item healed from its
Param1 and was eaten: a return scroll (61, Param1 30000), the bag expansion (24365, 32), a pet HP
potion (2143, 360).

**The engine's dispatch, read before anything was changed.**

- **Which class.** The object factory `FUN_00489de0` builds a `CGItemExpendable` for TypeID1 3 /
  TypeID2 3 (`param_1 >> 2 & 7 == 3`, `param_1 >> 5 & 3 == 3`), through `GObjPC::FUN_0049a840`
  (`0x489ec9`). That function is only the pooled-allocator wrapper: it takes a block from
  `FUN_004a0da0` (refilled by `CChunkAllocatorST__AllocItemBlock`) and calls its first slot. The
  expendable vtable `0x00aeb2b4` is stored by the neighbouring `FUN_0049a8e0` (`0x49a918`, after
  a call to `0x48f750`: the constructor shape) and `FUN_0049a940` (`0x49a965`, before a call to
  `0x48f800`: the destructor shape).
  Equipment (TypeID2 1) and pet summoners / capsules / storage (TypeID2 2) are other classes.
- **Which use.** `Item_HandleUseItem` (`0x00510980`) performs the use through `(*item + 0x4c8)`,
  slot 306, which in the expendable vtable (entry `0xaeb77c`) is `CGItemExpendable::DoJob`
  (`0x0049aca0`). DoJob switches on TypeID3 (`TID >> 7 & 0xf`):
  - **1**: TypeID4 4/5/6/7/9 go to slot 327 (`0x0049d240`), 10 to slot 330 (`0x0049cc80`), and
    every other TypeID4 to slot 308 (`0x0049b710`).
  - **2**: TypeID4 7 goes to slot 327, and every other TypeID4 to slot 308.
  - **3**: slot 307 (`0x0049b9f0`), the scrolls.
  - **6**: TypeID4 2 goes to slot 329. Any other TypeID4 is refused with `0x186b` unless the
    byte at `owner+0x30`, `+0x11` is 1; when it is, the item is consumed with no effect here.
  - **9 and 0xf**: consumed, with no effect here.
  - **0xc**: three helpers.
  - **0xd**: TypeID4 12 goes to slot 328, and every other TypeID4 to slot 309 (`UseByKind`,
    `0x0049c2b0`).
- **Where HP/MP is restored.** Slot 308 under TypeID3 1 sends TypeID4 8 to
  `GObjPC::AddHwanCount` (`0x49b89a cmp al,0x8`). Any other TypeID4 calls `GObjPC::FUN_0049aa70`,
  then applies the amounts to the owner PC (`0x49b90c..0x49b946`). Under TypeID3 2, slot 308 hands
  Param1..3 to the status manager at `pc+0xd30` (`FUN_004a56c0`): a cure, with no pool write.
  Slot 327 handles the other TypeID4s:
  - 4, 5 and 7 read a target id from the packet and apply their amounts to that PET, whose owner
    must be the user (`piVar7[0x736] == owner`).
  - 6 revives a pet (`COS_SubmitAsyncQuery(5, ...)`).
  - 9 feeds a pet.

  Slot 330 is the siege-structure repair (war period only).
- **Which Param fields.** `FUN_0049aa70` reads Param1 `+0x2a0` as HP, Param2 `+0x2c0` as HP%
  (of `GetMaxHP`, slot `0x110`), Param3 `+0x2e0` as MP and Param4 `+0x300` as MP% (of
  `GetMaxMP`, `0x114`). The exporter's 118/120/122/124 mapping is therefore RIGHT for the
  recovery kinds, and the exporter is unchanged apart from a comment.
- **Direct pool writes checked.** The 27 call sites of `ApplyHPMPDelta` (`0x4a86a0`) were each
  mapped to their function. The item paths among them are `vslot_308`, slot 327 (the pet), the
  potion-queue tick `FUN_0049a5b0`/`FUN_0049a510` (the deferred branch of the same potion), and
  `FUN_0049ff20`. `FUN_0049ff20` is `UseByKind` case 6: the resurrection scroll 3/3/13/6. It
  refuses a user whose life state is not 2 with `0x1887 ONLY_THE_DEAD_CAN_USE_RESURRECT_SCROLL`,
  then calls `GObjPC::Revive` and fills HP/MP. As a side result this independently confirms
  round 413's "life-state 2 closed -- it is DEAD" (round 490 wrongly called it unread): which is why `Item_HandleUseItem` lets state 2 through only for
  TypeID4 6 (`& 0xf800 == 0x3000`).

So, among the DIRECT pool writes an item use makes, a use restores the user's own HP/MP only for
**3/3/1/x with x outside {4,5,6,7,8,9,10}**. The resurrection kind also writes the pool, but only
as part of a revival srrevamp does not model.

**Not traced: pool writes made by a skill an item casts.** `UseByKind`'s cases 1..3 (TypeID4 1..3
under 3/3/13) read the row's Param1 (`+0x2a0`) as a skill id, look it up through `FUN_0046c1f0` and
apply it with `FUN_0059b8d0`. Whether such a skill (a buff, a heal) writes the user's pool was not
followed, so the census above covers direct item writes only. The gate is unaffected: on those
rows Param1 is a skill id, not a restore amount, and srrevamp models none of those uses.

**The census.** Over the combined itemdata (`allitems.txt` on the RE box, 21,552 rows, 15,333 ids -- 15,334 by a recount in round 495, and the
file glues 10 row pairs, see round 495
with the last occurrence kept, as `export-refdata` keeps it), **588** `CanUse` rows carry a positive
value in columns 118..124. All of them healed before this round.

- **58 still restore.** These are 3/3/1/1 (19 HP potions), 3/3/1/2 (19 MP potions) and 3/3/1/3
  (20 that restore both).
- **530 stop**, by TypeID1/2/3:

| TypeID | Rows | What they are |
|---|---:|---|
| 3/3/13 | 300 | mall tickets, resurrection scrolls, expansions, stat recall, and more |
| 3/3/3 | 88 | return, reverse-return and fortress scrolls |
| 3/3/12 | 46 | guild items, teleport holes |
| 3/1/14 | 26 | cash avatars (equipment) |
| 3/2/1 | 21 | pet summoner scrolls (not an expendable) |
| 3/3/9 | 20 | quest items |
| 3/3/1 | 14 | pet HP potions (4), berserk potions (8), pet feed (9), fortress repair kits (10) |
| 3/3/2 | 14 | cure pills |
| 3/3/6 | 1 | the shock bomb |

**Change.**

- `session.restoresUserPool(it)` is DoJob's dispatch as a predicate. It requires
  `equipment.TypeItem`/`TypeExpendable`, `recoveryFamily` (TypeID3 1), and a TypeID4 other than
  4/5/6/7/9/10 and `berserkPotionKind` (8). The constants cite their addresses.
- `UseItemHandler` refuses any other kind with the existing `"that cannot be used"`. The check
  sits beside the restores-nothing check, after `CanUse`, so every existing check keeps its order.
  Nothing is consumed and nothing is healed.
- The handler's doc comment says this is srrevamp's DISCLOSED GAP, not an engine refusal. The
  engine uses those items, and srrevamp models none of their effects.
- Comments: `refdata.Item.RestoreHP` and the exporter's `fRestoreHP` now say the columns are
  restore amounts only on the recovery kinds.
- `item_capability_flags.md`'s `CanUse` paragraph now says that `CanUse` alone does not make an
  item a potion, and lists, in order, every refusal `Item_HandleUseItem` sets before the `CanUse`
  check (`pc[0x311]` -> `0x183e`, quest block `0x185f`, interaction `0x1835`, the `+4` state byte
  -> 2, slot range `0x1806`, empty slot `0x1809`, rental `0x183d`, life state `0x1889`). The first
  draft named only the last four, which read as a complete list.

**Found, not fixed: the amount is scaled before it lands.** This is now written into
`useitem.go` as a disclosed gap, and the 2026-09-15 "unmodified heal" section carries a pointer
here.

- **The scaling.** `FUN_0049aa70`'s absolute path (`0x49ab63..0x49ac37`, read from `srv.asm`)
  computes:
  - HP = `Param1 * 1.02^(Level-1) * (1 + GetParam(1)/416)`
  - MP = `Param3 * 1.02^(Level-1) * (1 + GetParam(2)/416)`
- **Where the terms come from.** `Char_GetLevel` is `GetParam(0)`. At the call site (`0x49abb9`) the
  parameter id is pushed (`push 0x1`) and the call goes through vtable `+0x104` to
  `CGObjChar::GetParam` (`0x4aa5c0`), a 20-byte thunk to `ParamKeeper_GetParamChecked` (round 495
  corrected "passes its argument in EAX"). Params 1 and 2 are Str and Int (the `_CHAR` root binds recorded earlier in
  this file: `SetParam(1, charData+0x74)` Strength, `SetParam(2, charData+0x76)` Intellect). 1.02 is the
  double at `.rdata 0xb45ea0`, 416.0 is at `0xb45e98`, and 1.0 is at `0xb45ac0`.
- **The percentages.** The percentage pair is read only when Param1 and Param3 are both zero.
  srrevamp adds both pairs, but none of the 58 recovery rows carries both, so the only live
  difference is the scaling.
- **The 143/144 step is NOT unconditionally a no-op.** The 2026-09-15 section called params 143
  and 144 structurally zero ("neither has a `SetParam` site anywhere"), and a first draft of this
  round repeated it. Round 248 had already recorded writers for both
  (`docs/protocol/status_effects.md` bits 21/22, `recovered_names.tsv` rows `004a5320`/`004a54a0`,
  `param_writers.md`):
  - `AbnormalState_Panic_Apply21` (`0x4a5320`) writes 143: `0x4a5418 mov edi,0x8f`,
    `0x4a541d call 0x4b3510` (`ParamKeeper_SetParam`), from the effect's `+0x34` value.
  - `AbnormalState_Combustion_Apply22` (`0x4a54a0`) writes 144: `0x4a5598 mov edi,0x90`,
    `0x4a559d call 0x4b3510`.
  - `FUN_004a86a0` multiplies the HP amount by `1 - param143/100` and the MP amount by
    `1 - param144/100`: `ParamKeeper_GetParamChecked` (`0x4b3740`), `0x4a86c9 fdiv` by the 100.0
    at `.rdata 0xb45af0`, `fld1`, `fsubrp` (DE E1, `1 - p/100`), `fimul` the amount.

  So the step is a no-op only while the character has neither panic nor combustion on. With one
  on, the engine cuts the potion's HP (MP) by the effect's percentage. srrevamp heals the full
  amount regardless, and `useitem.go` now discloses this as a second gap. The earlier section
  checked the last step and not the one before it, and its writer probe missed the two appliers.
- **Not wired this round.** Wiring the scaling changes every potion's heal amount, so it is its
  own item.

**Tests.**

- **`session.TestUseItemRestoresOnlyForRecoveryKinds`.** The character takes 50 damage and spends
  half its MP first, so a refusal cannot be the "no need" answer. Before each case the test undoes
  whatever an earlier case restored (`reopenRoom`), so each case's stack and HP checks pin its own
  item rather than only the error string. The test then uses four real rows' kinds, ids and
  Param blocks:
  - the return scroll (61, 3/3/3/1, 30000/1)
  - the bag expansion (24365, 3/3/13/17, 32)
  - the pet HP potion (2143, 3/3/1/4, 360)
  - the berserk potion (24993, 3/3/1/8, 5)

  Each is refused with `"that cannot be used"`, keeps its whole stack, and changes neither HP nor
  MP. HP_POTION_01 (4, 3/3/1/1, 120) then heals and leaves 4. MP_POTION_01 (11, 3/3/1/2, 120)
  restores MP and leaves 4.
- **`session.TestRestoresUserPoolFollowsDoJobDispatch`.** It walks TypeID4 0..31 under 3/3/1,
  where only 4..10 are excluded. It also checks the cure pill 3/3/2/6, the resurrection scroll
  3/3/13/6, a cash avatar 3/1/14/1, a pet summoner 3/2/1/2, and a kind-less item; none of them
  restores.
- **`TestUseItemRefusesAnItemWhoseCanUseIsClear`.** Its potion now carries TypeID 3/3/1/1.

**Negative case, run.**

- **Production files stashed** (`useitem.go`, `main.go`, `item.go`): the package fails to build on
  `restoresUserPool`.
- **Dispatch test also cut out, so the behaviour test builds:**
  `TestUseItemRestoresOnlyForRecoveryKinds` FAILS.
  - The return scroll was used, consumed and healed ("RestoredHP:50 Remaining:4", "HP 150 ->
    200").
  - The next three got "no need for that right now" instead of the refusal, because the scroll had
    already healed the character to full. The review pointed out that those three then failed on
    the error string alone, which is why `reopenRoom` was added.
- **Re-run with `reopenRoom`, the gate disabled in place** (`if false && !restoresUserPool(it)`):
  each of the four fails on its own stack and HP checks. The return scroll heals 150 -> 200 and
  leaves 4. The bag expansion heals 150 -> 182 and leaves 0. The pet HP potion heals 150 -> 200
  and leaves 4. The berserk potion heals 150 -> 155 and leaves 4.
- **Restored:** all pass, and `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green.

**Deploy note.** None needed. The gate reads TypeID1..4, which every export has carried since
`ITEM_FORMAT.md` existed, so srrevamp-01's current `items` table already has what it needs.

## An untradeable drop stays reserved to its owner until it decays (GObjPC::FUN_004901c0) (round 492)

**The gap.** `grounditem` released every owned drop 30 s after it fell: `OwnerAt` answered 0 and
`ReleaseOwnerships` cleared the owner and told the zone. The engine does that only for an item
that can be traded.

**The grounding, read this round.**

- `CGItem::Update` (`0x0048f9b0`) accumulates `+0x158` and, once it reaches the 30.0 at
  `.rdata 0xb45e58` (`00 00 00 00 00 00 3e 40`), calls the release: `48fa0b mov eax,esi;
  48fa0d call 0x4901c0`.
- `GObjPC::FUN_004901c0` (`0x004901c0`, 78 bytes) opens with `4901c5 mov edx,[eax+0xc4]`,
  `4901cd call edx`, `4901cf test eax,eax`, `4901d1 je 0x49020c`. Only when that call answers
  non-zero and `+0x150` is non-zero does it clear `+0x150` (`4901e2`) and send `0x304D`. On zero it
  returns with the owner intact, and `Update` asks again on every later tick with the same answer.
- `+0xc4` is slot 49. All seven vtables that carry `CGItem::Update` at slot 211 (`0xae9384`,
  `0xae9934`, `0xae9e5c`, `0xaea394`, `0xaea9ec`, `0xaeb2b4`, `0xaeb824`, found by scanning
  `.rdata` for the pointer) hold `0x00483d50` at slot 49: `CGObj::CanTrade`, which answers 0
  unless `CGObj::IsItem` (slot 18, `0x00482d80`, the same in all seven) says yes, then the ref
  row's flags word `+0x8c & 1`, itemdata column 16 (`item_capability_flags.md`, "The bit map").
- The release has one more caller, `0x4e98b7`, in a job handler that asserts `+0x150 == -1` and
  picks between it and `FUN_004901b0` on `[ebp+0x118]`. srrevamp has no such reservation, so
  only the 30 s path is wired. No name is given to `FUN_004901c0`.
- **Which items this is.** Measured over `/var/tmp/tables/itemdata_all.utf8.txt` on the RE box
  (851 `ITEM_QNO_` rows, 607 distinct ids, no id with differing values): 598 ids (833 rows) carry
  `CanTrade = 0`, 9 ids (18 rows: `ITEM_QNO_RM_ARCHEMY_1..8`, `ITEM_QNO_RM_MEETROC_6_01`) carry 1,
  and all carry DecayTime 180000. The plan for this round said "832 of 851"; the 833rd is the row
  whose first field carries the file's byte-order mark. Gold (ids 1..3) and HP/MP potions (4..12)
  carry `CanTrade = 1` and DecayTime 10000, so they are unchanged. **Recount (round 501):** the
  file glues ten row pairs (round 495), and one glued second half is `ITEM_QNO_SD_NO_053_1`
  (24748, 3/3/9, `CanTrade = 0`, DecayTime 180000). With the glued lines split the figures here
  and below are 852 rows and 608 ids, 599 bound ids (834 rows), 755 3/3/9 rows and 737 bound 3/3/9
  rows (540 ids); the 18 tradeable rows and the 97 non-3/3/9 bound rows are unchanged.
- **Who else may pick one: not the party, for most of them (corrected in review).** The plan said
  `PickCheck` needed no change because "a party member is still allowed". The dump says otherwise.
  In `GObjPC::CheckCanPickUp` (`0x004a9050`) a non-owner reaches `0x4a930d` (player path: after
  `IGObj::IsPC`, slot 7, at `0x4a93f4` and `jmp 0x4a930d` at `0x4a9405`) before the party test at
  `0x4a9360`. There the item's TID (`CGObj::GetTID`, `0x00485c90`) goes to `FUN_0042fdc0`, which
  answers 1 only for bit 1 clear, `& 0x1c == 0xc`, `& 0x60 == 0x60`, `& 0x780 == 0x480`, which is
  TypeID 3/3/9 (`damage_pipeline.md`, "The TID layout"). For such an item the codename is compared
  with `CompareStringA(0x400, 0, codename, 0x13, "ITEM_QNO_RM_ARCHEMY", 0x13)` (`.rdata 0xaebf58`,
  `0x4a9342`). Anything but `CSTR_EQUAL` stores `0x1812` at `0x4a934d`, so the party test never
  runs. Measured over the same file: 754 of the 851 `ITEM_QNO_` rows are 3/3/9, and 736 of the
  833 bound rows (539 of the 598 ids). All 18 tradeable rows are 3/3/9 too; the 16 `ARCHEMY` rows
  pass the name compare, `MEETROC_6_01` does not. So a bound quest item is, in the engine, the
  OWNER's alone for most rows, not the owner's party's. The same read shows that an owner id that
  resolves to no object (`FUN_00485dc0 == 0`, `0x4a93d1`) gives result 1 and false.

**Change.**

- `grounditem.Item.Bound`, set at `Drop` when the hub's new trade lookup
  (`Hub.SetTradeLookup(func(itemID) (canTrade, known bool))`) knows the item and says it cannot be
  traded. A nil lookup or an unknown item is not bound, so a deployment without reference data
  does not lock its drops.
- `Item.OwnerAt` returns the owner of a bound item regardless of time. `ReleaseOwnerships` skips
  bound items, so `RunGroundItemSweep` never sends `OpGroundItemOwnerReleased` (the real `0x304D`)
  for one, and `snapshotOf` keeps naming the owner to a player who arrives later. `PickCheck` was
  unchanged by this round: a stranger is refused `0x1812`, and the owner may pick.
  - **The party divergence -- CLOSED in round 497.** After this round `PickCheck` still asked the
    caller's party rule for every item, so a sharing party member could pick a bound TypeID 3/3/9
    item that the engine refuses them. The divergence predated this round for the 30 s window,
    and binding made it last the item's whole DecayTime. Modelling it needed the item's TID and
    codename in the hub. Round 497 supplied both: `grounditem.OwnerOnlyPick` models the exclusion
    from the item's TypeIDs and the new `refdata.Item.CodeName`.
  - **The absent owner -- still open.** The outcome for an owner id that resolves to no object is
    not modelled. It is recorded in `ground_items.md`, step 3, and in `PickCheck`'s doc comment.
- `cmd/server` wires the lookup through `groundTradeLookup(ctx, refItems)` to
  `refItems.GetItem(...).CanTrade`; an error or a nil row answers unknown. The SQL column already
  defaults to TRUE and the CSV parser to true for an export without column 16, so an older table
  binds nothing. **Renamed in round 497**, when one lookup took over all of a drop's rules:
  `groundTradeLookup` is now `groundDropRules`, `Hub.SetTradeLookup` is `Hub.SetRulesLookup`
  (`DropRules.Bound` carries this round's answer), and `TestGroundTradeLookupAdapter` below is
  `TestGroundDropRulesAdapter`.
- Docs: `ground_items.md` "The ownership window" carries the gate with its addresses and the
  measurement; its stale "not recovered" bullet about the lifetime (read in round 227) now says
  so. Its "Picking up" step 3, which had left out the same exclusion, now spells out the whole
  ownership branch (the absent owner, `IsPC`, the 3/3/9 exclusion, the party test) and the
  divergence. `item_capability_flags.md`'s enforcement table lists this use of `CanTrade`.

**Tests.**

- `grounditem.TestBoundDropStaysReservedPastWindow`, on a fake clock. The lookup says 500 is
  untradeable, 4 tradeable, and anything else unknown; all three are dropped for character 7.
  Item 500 stands for a bound item OUTSIDE TypeID 3/3/9 (one of the 97 such `ITEM_QNO_` rows,
  e.g. `ITEM_QNO_CH_EUROPE_1_02`, 3/3/13), the class for which the engine's party rule really
  applies. At +31 s `ReleaseOwnerships` returns only the potion and the unknown item; the bound
  item's `OwnerAt` is 7, both on the returned copy and on the item still on the ground; a
  stranger (9) is refused `ErrNotOwner`; a sharing party member (8) and the owner get 0; a
  stranger picks the released potion. At +60 s a second release is empty and the owner is still
  7. No assertion covers a 3/3/9 item's party member, because srrevamp does not model that
  refusal. (Round 497 models it; `TestQuestItemIsOwnerOnlyEvenForParty` is that assertion.)
- `cmd/server.TestGroundTradeLookupAdapter`: the adapter passes a row's `CanTrade` through as
  known, and answers (true, false) for a missing row and for a failed lookup. Inverting
  `return it.CanTrade, true` fails it. It does not cover the `SetTradeLookup` call itself.
- `grounditem.TestNoTradeLookupReleasesEverything`: with no lookup, both drops are released at
  30 s and a stranger may pick.
- `session.TestGroundItemSnapshotKeepsBoundOwner`: `snapshotOf` a bound item at +31 s names 7; its
  unbound twin names 0.

**Negative case, run.**

- Production files stashed (`grounditem.go`, `main.go`): both test packages fail to build on
  `Bound` / `SetTradeLookup`.
- Field and API kept, both gates removed in place (`OwnerAt`'s and `ReleaseOwnerships`'s):
  `TestBoundDropStaysReservedPastWindow` FAILS with the bound item among the released three, and
  `TestGroundItemSnapshotKeepsBoundOwner` FAILS with "owner 0, want 7".
- Only `OwnerAt`'s gate removed: the grounditem test FAILS at "bound OwnerAt(31 s) = 0, want 7".
- Restored: all pass, and `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green.

**Deploy note.** None needed: `items.can_trade` (`NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE`) has been in the schema
since commit `2ff7d69`, so srrevamp-01's table already answers the lookup. The own-design fallback
loot (`combat.LootTables`) drops gold and potions, which are tradeable; a drop is bound only where
operator-supplied real drop tables (`session.realDrops`) roll a quest item.

## Carry CanPick (itemdata col 21), refuse picking a CanPick=0 item, and not-found answers 3 (round 493)

**The gap.** `grounditem.PickCheck` refused only on range, busy and owner. It answered `0x1839`
for an id that was no longer on the ground, and `ground_items.md` step 1 read `IGObj::CanPick` as
"a ground item says yes". Both were wrong: `CanPick` is a per-row bit, and the engine answers a
gone drop with a different code.

**The grounding, read this round.**

- `GObjPC::CheckCanPickUp` (dump `0x004a9050`) opens `*param_2 = 3`. It returns false with the 3
  standing when `FUN_00485d90` finds no object or `IGObj::IsItem` (`+0x48`, slot 18) says no. Next
  comes `(**(code **)(*item + 0xd4))()`: slot 53, `IGObj::CanPick` (`igobj_vtable.md`). A zero sets
  `0x1839` and returns. After that come the quest-item check (slot 46,
  `IGObj::IsQuest_n_EventItem` -> `0x1874`), the range (4), the life state (3), busy `+0x14c`
  (`0x1813`) and then the owner. `error_emitters.tsv` names the codes of the `0x004a9050` row:
  `0x1839=UIIT_MSG_STRGERR_CANNOT_BE_PICKED`, `0x1874=..._AT_QUEST_ACHIEVE_CONDITION`.
- `CGObj::CanPick` (dump `0x00483e50`): `IsItem`, then `*(ref + 0x8c) >> 5 & 1`. It sits at slot 53
  in all seven `CGItem*` vtables. They are the ones holding `CGItem::Update` at slot 211:
  `0xae9384`, `0xae9934`, `0xae9e5c`, `0xaea394`, `0xaea9ec`, `0xaeb2b4`, `0xaeb824`. Each was read
  from `SR_GameServer.exe`, and slot 18 is `0x00482d80` in all seven.
- The column. `RefObjCommon_ExtractData` (`0x006a3090`) keeps its own column counter at
  `[stream+0x28]`, bumped once per column. From the disassembly:
  - CanTrade's byte goes to `esp+0x11` (column 16) and CanSell's to `esp+0x26` (17).
  - Column 18 is consumed but not stored: `0x6a33f0` advances the cursor with no load, and `0x6a33f6`
    bumps the counter.
  - `esp+0x12` is column 19 and `esp+0x13` is 20.
  - At `0x6a3455` the counter is bumped for column 21, and `0x6a3464 mov [esp+0x23],dl` stores its
    byte.
  - `0x6a3588..0x6a3590` (`mov al,[esp+0x23]; neg al; sbb eax,eax; and eax,0x20`) makes it bit 5.
  - Counting on, `bl` lands on column 24 (bit 8), round 489's grounded `CanUse`, so the two anchor
    each other.
  This is round 460's data-anchored table. The older read-count table put `CanPick` at 20 because it
  missed the column-18 skip; `item_capability_flags.md` now says so beside that table.
- The data. Over `/var/tmp/tables/itemdata_all.utf8.txt` on the RE box, column 21 is 0/1 only and 0
  on **309 of 21,552 rows** (210 of 15,334 ids, last occurrence kept; "15,333" until round 495's
  recount). The zeros:
  - all 54 starter `_DEF` ids (84 rows);
  - 34 `ITEM_FORT_*` ids;
  - `_RARE_ACTIVE_STARTER` and `_SUPER` gear;
  - guard COS items;
  - a scatter of mall and event items.
  Gold (ids 1..3) and the HP/MP potions (4..6, 11..13) read 1, so the own-design fallback loot is
  unaffected. The neighbours have other shapes: column 20 is 0/1/3 and column 22 is 0/1 with 7,591 (7,590 until round 495's recount)
  zeros.

**Change.**

- `export-refdata`: `fCanPick = 21`, emitted at record index 69 through `nonZero`, after round
  489's `CanUse` at 68. `refdata`: CSV column 69 `CanPick`, a strict suffix, so
  `ItemCSVColumnCount` is 70. `Item.CanPick` defaults to TRUE in the loader and in `items.can_pick`
  (`BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE`). It is carried through ImportItems, GetItem and ListAll.
- `grounditem`:
  - New `ErrNotThere = 3`. `ErrCannotPick`'s comment now says what it is: `CanPick` answered 0.
  - New `Hub.SetPickLookup(func(itemID) bool)`. `Drop` resolves it once into the unexported
    `Item.noPick`, so no lookup runs under the hub lock at pick time. A nil lookup means everything
    is pickable.
  - `PickCheck` now follows the engine's order:
    1. a missing id answers `ErrNotThere`;
    2. `noPick` answers `ErrCannotPick` to everyone, the owner included;
    3. then the range;
    4. then busy, moved after the range to match the engine;
    5. then the owner.
  - The quest-condition refusal (`0x1874`) is not modelled, and neither is the life-state 3. Both
    are stated in `PickCheck`'s comment.
- `cmd/server`: `ground.SetPickLookup(groundPickLookup(ctx, refItems))`. An error or a missing row
  answers true.
- `session`: the handler's own failures that the engine has no code for still answer `0x1839`. The
  `PickUpResult` comment says so.
- Client: `GroundItemsNet.ERR_NOT_THERE := 3`. `World3D._pick_up_refusal_line` maps 3 to "That drop
  is no longer there." (with the playtest-2026-09-20 note) and `0x1839` to "That item cannot be
  picked up." This has to ship in the same release as the server change. Without it, a duplicate
  pick, which now answers 3, would print "code 0x3".
- Docs: `ground_items.md` step 1 (the object test, the per-row bit, column 21 with its addresses and
  the measurement, the quest-condition refusal), step 2 (life state and busy after the range),
  srrevamp's order, and the protocol section's code list. `item_capability_flags.md`: `CanPick` in
  the enforcement table, and the read-to-column note beside the read-number table. `SYSTEMS.md`:
  `CanPick` added to the capability-flags row's anchors.

**Tests.**

- `grounditem.TestCanPickClearRefusesBeforeRangeBusyAndOwner`: the lookup refuses item 99.
  - The owner (7) standing on it gets `0x1839`.
  - A stranger (8) 500 units away also gets `0x1839`, not `ErrTooFar` or `ErrNotOwner`.
  - A repeat still gets `0x1839`, not `ErrBusy`.
  - The pickable item beside it gets 0.
  - A hub with no lookup gives 0 for item 99.
- `grounditem.TestRangeIsTestedBeforeBusy`: while character 7's pick is in flight, a second picker 50
  away gets 4 and one in reach gets `0x1813`.
- `grounditem.TestBusyFlag` and `session.TestGroundDropAndPickUpFlow` now expect `ErrNotThere` (3)
  after `Remove`. They got `0x1839` before. The session flow also sends a duplicate `OpPickUp` for
  the potion it just took, and the answer must be 3 on the wire.
- `export-refdata.TestCanPickReadsColumn21`: columns 19..22 set to 128/0/1/0 give `rec[69] == "1"`,
  and 255/3/0/1 give `"0"`. Each record is round-tripped through `LoadItemsCSV`. Reading column 20
  or 22 fails it.
- `refdata.TestCanPickDefaultsToPickable`: a 69-column row loads pickable, and "0"/"1" at 69 are
  obeyed. `refdata.TestCanPickFalseSurvivesSQL` sends a clear bit through ImportItems, GetItem and
  ListAll, and checks `CanUse` beside it.
- `cmd/server.TestGroundPickLookupAdapter`: the row's value passes through. A missing row or a
  failed lookup answers true.
- Client: `ground_items_test.gd` decodes a code-3 result as `ERR_NOT_THERE`. `remote_godot.sh
  tests` ran 77 suites with 0 failing, and `remote_godot.sh check` loaded 239 scripts.

**Negative case, run.**

- All seven production files stashed: every touched test package fails to build (`ErrNotThere`,
  `SetPickLookup`, `CanPick`, `groundPickLookup` undefined).
- Behavioural mutations, each run and then restored:
  - the not-found path answering `ErrCannotPick` again fails `TestBusyFlag` and the session flow
    ("code 0x1839, want ErrNotThere");
  - dropping the `noPick` gate fails the CanPick test ("owner ... code 0x0");
  - moving busy back before the range fails `TestRangeIsTestedBeforeBusy`
    ("code 0x1813, want ErrTooFar");
  - `fCanPick = 20` or `22` fails the exporter test;
  - dropping index 69 fails the exporter round-trip test ("69 fields, want 70");
  - ignoring column 69 in the loader fails the CSV test;
  - writing `true` in place of `CanPick` fails the SQL test;
  - inverting the adapter fails its test.
- `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green.

**Deploy note.** srrevamp-01's `items.can_pick` takes `DEFAULT TRUE` until export-refdata and
import-refdata are re-run, so nothing is refused there until then. Batch the re-run with the other
exporter items. The client change must ship in the same release as the server.

## Fix the exporter's CanDrop column: 20 (with the CanTrade coupling), not 19 (round 494)

Round 489 recorded, and did not fix, that `export-refdata` read `CanDrop` from itemdata column 19
while round 460's table in `item_capability_flags.md` puts it at 20. This round checks the binary
and moves it.

**Grounding.** `RefObjCommon_ExtractData` (`0x006a3090`), read in both the Ghidra dump and
`srv.asm`. The parser keeps its own column counter at `[stream+0x28]` and bumps it once per column:

- Column 16 goes to `esp+0x11` (`CanTrade`, bit 0) and column 17 to `esp+0x26` (`CanSell`, bit 1).
- Column 18 is consumed without a load: `0x6a33f0 add [edi+0x1c],ebx` advances the cursor and
  `0x6a33f6 add [edi+0x28],ebx` bumps the counter. The dump shows the same bare pair between
  `local_9e` and `local_b2`.
- Column 19 goes to `esp+0x12` (`0x6a341e`, `local_b2`). It is tested only `& 0x80` (`0x6a3516`)
  and `& 0x40` (`0x6a352f`), for flags bits 12 and 13. The engine names neither bit and they are not
  exported.
- Column 20 goes to `esp+0x13` (`0x6a3441`, `local_b1`). It is folded at `0x6a3540..0x6a3552` as
  `((b & 2) << 9 | b & 1) << 4`: `b & 1` is bit 4, the bit `CGObj::CanDrop` (`0x00483de0`) reads,
  and `b & 2` is the unnamed bit 14.
- The coupling runs just before the word is built: `0x6a34e6 cmp [esp+0x11],0`, `0x6a34f0 cmp
  [esp+0x13],1`, `0x6a34f7 mov [esp+0x13],0`. In the dump: `if (local_b3 == 0 && local_b1 == 1)
  local_b1 = 0`. The test is equality with 1, so a byte of 3 keeps bit 0.

The same count already placed `CanPick` at 21 (round 493) and `CanUse` at 24 (round 489). The data
agrees with the shapes. Over `/var/tmp/tables/itemdata_all.utf8.txt` on the RE box, column 19 holds
255/128/223/192/159/1/0, a packed byte, and column 20 holds only 0/1/3.

**Change.**

- `export-refdata`: `fCanDrop = 20`, with the column walk (16, 17, 18 consumed, 19 packed, 20) and
  its addresses in the comment.
- The `dropBit` closure is replaced by `canDrop(trade, drop string) string`. A value that is not a
  number counts as 0. When `CanTrade` is 0 and the byte is exactly 1, it becomes 0. The result is
  `d & 1`.
- Record index 43 is `canDrop(get(fCanTrade), get(fCanDrop))`. The CSV width does not change.
- `refdata.Item`'s comment now says columns 16, 17 and 20, and says that column 19 is the
  255/128/223/192 byte.

**The class argument never chose between 19 and 20.** The comment and the doc called the class
check decisive: bound starter (`_A_DEF`) and quest (`ITEM_QNO_`) rows, free ordinary swords. It
confirms `CanTrade`. For `CanDrop`, over the same combined itemdata:

| class | rows | droppable by column 19 | droppable by column 20 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `_A_DEF` | 81 | 0 | 0 |
| `ITEM_QNO_` | 851 | 37 | 0 |
| non-rare `ITEM_CH_SWORD_` | 89 | 83 | 82 |
| `ITEM_MALL_` | 750 | 727 | 10 |

The only large difference is the cash-shop rows. "Cash-shop items are droppable" was an expectation
and was never measured, so it cannot decide the column. The binary's column counter decides it.

**Census.** These are rows of the combined itemdata that `itemRecord` accepts: 21,552 rows, with 9
short rows skipped. **Round 495:** the combined file (`/var/tmp/tables/itemdata_all.utf8.txt`)
glues 10 row pairs into single lines where a source file ended without a newline (e.g. line 837 is
`ITEM_CH_M_CLOTHES_10_AA_B` + `ITEM_CH_M_CLOTHES_10_AA_C`; confirmed: 10 lines of 319+ fields), so
every census on it silently loses 10 rows. The round-494 reviewer re-ran this one on the individual
files: 21,562 rows, **8,003** flip 1 -> 0, none 0 -> 1, 18,931 droppable before and 10,928 after.
The figures below are the concatenated-file ones.

- `CanDrop` goes from 1 to 0 on **7,998** rows and from 0 to 1 on none. Before the change 18,923
  rows were droppable; after it, 10,925.
- **Rare equipment:** 6,791 of the 7,527 rows (code name containing `_RARE`, TypeID 3/1) are not
  droppable by column 20. 5,861 of them flip from 1 to 0, because column 19 holds 255 on them.
  The other 930 were already 0: 792 hold 128 and 138 hold 0.
- **The coupling fires on 7 rows.** These are the rows with `CanTrade` 0 and column 20 exactly 1:
  `ITEM_ETC_ARENA_COIN` (two rows), `ITEM_SANTA_BOX`, `ITEM_MALL_GACHA_CARD`,
