## Client walks to the retail stop distance before swinging or casting (Tick_Attack phase 1) (round 519)

A click on a monster out of reach sent the attack at once, and the server answered "too far
away" (`session.firstSwingInReach`, and `skillInReach` for a cast). In retail the server walks
the attacker into reach. srrevamp's server does not move players, so the client now does the
walk and sends the attack when it arrives in reach. The walk aims at the stop distance, but the
attack goes out on the first frame in reach, usually before the walk gets to `stop` (below). A
cast of a skill that needs no target, or targets the ground, is sent at once with no walk, as the
engine's skill tick does.

**Grounding** (read-only, `/var/tmp/decomp_server`):

- **The band and the test are the server's, re-read.** `CGCharAutoCommandActor::Tick_Attack`
  (`0x004ad8e0`) phase 0 puts `stop` at action `+0x14` and `reach` at `+0x18`. The branches are
  the same as `combat.ApproachBand`. `r <= 4` adds `r` to both. `4 < r < 10` adds `r - 2` to
  stop and `r` to reach. For `r > 10`, stop gets `0.7 r` and reach gets `r`. At exactly 10 one
  `if (10 < r)` guards both adds (round 488). Phase 1 calls
  `Action_IsTargetWithinReach(actor, ftol(reach))` (`0x004ad4a0`). That function returns
  `iVar3 <= param_2 + 2`, where `iVar3` is the truncated distance. On failure it calls
  `GObjPC::MoveTowardObject(target, ROUND(+0x14))` (`0x004b0350`), which stores the target at
  `+8` and the stop at `+0xc`. The client mirrors `server/internal/combat/reach.go` and
  `session/keepup.go` as they are now (`int(d) <= int(reach) + 2`, reach at 10 fixed).
- **When the blow goes out.** Phase 1 returns 1 without changing phase, so it runs again on the
  next tick and re-tests the reach while the walk goes on. The `pc+0x1bfc` check stops the walk
  from being restarted. On the first tick in reach, `FUN_004ad780` calls `FUN_004b03f0`. That
  sets the heading through the mover's slot `0x4b0` and calls `FUN_004b0450`, which zeroes the
  `+8` target that MoveTowardObject stored. Then gate `0x81` runs and phase 2 posts the blow. So
  the engine fires on the first tick in reach, before the walk reaches `stop`. **This departs
  from the plan.** The plan said to walk all the way to `stop` and then send ("a bow user stops
  at about 70% of the 180 range"). The client does what the tick does: it aims the walk at
  `stop` and sends on the first frame in reach. The plan's arrival send is kept as a backstop.
  It cannot fire in practice. The per-frame test fires once the distance drops below reach + 3
  (reach is a whole number). The arrival branch needs the player within
  `MOVE_TARGET_STOP_DISTANCE` (about 2.4) of the point, which is at most stop + 2.4, and stop is
  never beyond reach. Not
  read: whether the retail body keeps moving after `FUN_004b0450` drops the follow target.
  srrevamp's client stops, because of the next point.
- **The skill tick walks only for a skill that needs a target** (fixed in review, before
  push; the first cut walked for every cast). `Tick_UseSkill` (`0x004ae590`) phase 0, read in
  `/var/tmp/srv.asm`: `0x4ae73b` loads `Target_Required` (`+0x94`), `0x4ae743 je 0x4aecfd` when it
  is 0, and `0x4ae749`-`0x4ae753` (`cmp al,1 ; jne ; cmp [edi+0x96],al ; je 0x4aecfd`) when it is
  1 and `TargetType_Land` (`+0x96`) is 1. `0x4aecfd` is `mov eax,2 ; call 0x4ac9e0`, phase 2,
  past the band and the reach test. `docs/protocol/auto_command.md`, "The skill tick", phase 0,
  says the same. The columns follow `CRefSkill::CopyFixedColumns`' order
  (`docs/protocol/skill_fields.md`): Range `+0x92` is column 21, `+0x94` column 22 (the exporter's
  `skTargetRequired`), `+0x96` column 24. Measured on the box's skilldata tables (read-only, 2,185
  China board rows over 258 skills): column 22 is 0 on 831 rows and 1 on 1,354, and never varies
  within a skill; 115 of the 264 level-1 rows are 0 (`SKILL_CH_SWORD_SHIELD_D_01`,
  `SKILL_CH_COLD_SHIELD_A_01`, `SKILL_CH_WATER_SELFHEAL_E_01`, ...); column 24 is 1 only on the 19
  `SKILL_CH_LIGHTNING_GYEONGGONG_B/D` rows. Rows whose `Basic_Activity` (`+0x65`) is not 2 never
  reach that test (`0x4ae6e6 cmp [edi+0x65],2 ; jne 0x4ae9dc`); all 256 such board rows
  carry `Target_Required` 0, so `skill_tick_approaches` gives them no walk either way (worded as
  in `combat.gd` in round 527; this said "so the one test covers them", which the jump above
  contradicts). **Corrected in round 523:** this said
  such rows "leave phase 0 earlier still". `0x4ae9dc` is `mov eax,1 ; pop ; ... ; ret 8`, and the
  decompile reads `if (+0x65 != 2) return 1;`: the tick returns and STAYS in phase 0. The server agrees for the
  non-damaging rows: `session/skill.go`'s `noCombat || zeroDmg` return comes before
  `skillInReach`, so a self heal or a shield was accepted at any distance before this round and
  still is. The damaging `Target_Required` 0 rows are a server departure, filed below.
- **Range per level.** Column 21 is constant within a China skill except for four:
  `SKILL_CH_BOW_SPECIAL_A..D` (bases 467-470) rise 2 a level, 204->214, 218->228, 228->238 and
  240->244. **Corrected in round 523:** this said "within a skill"; one Europe skill varies too,
  `SKILL_EU_WARRIOR_FRENZYA_TOUNT_SPRINT_A` (group 540, ids 8479-8499), 80->240 by level.
  `SkillDataReader` keeps only `SKILL_CH_` rows. The server measures a cast with that level's row (`session/skill.go`, `ref.Range`),
  so the client keys the range by the level's own id.
- **Nothing moves between the walk and the request.** `handleMove` (`session/world.go`) calls
  `keepUp.Cancel` on every OpMove. So `_flush_position` sends the final position before the
  attack, and `_last_sent_pos` then matches, so the physics tick's send gate stays quiet.
- **The data.** BCRadius is characterdata column 50, re-checked on the box's extracted tables
  (read-only). `CHAR_CH_MAN_FIGHTER`/`WOMAN_FIGHTER` read 4, `MOB_CH_MANGNYANG` 6,
  `MOB_CH_GYO` 10 and `MOB_CH_YEOHA` 11, matching the roster in `cmd/server`. 13,291 rows carry
  a numeric column 50 under 13,291 distinct code names. That is why a code-name key is safe.
  The "second MOB_CH_MANGNYANG" in `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md` is `MOB_CH_STRONG_MANGNYANG`
  (id 9383), a different code (found, not changed; that doc was corrected in round 523). The weapon Range is itemdata column 94:
  `ITEM_CH_SWORD_01_A_DEF` 6, `SPEAR` 18, `BOW` 180, the exporter's `fRange`. A skill's Range is
  skilldata column 21 (`SkillDataReader.S_RANGE`, the exporter's `skRange`).

**Change.**

- `client/scripts/net/combat.gd` adds the rule as statics with their citations:
  `PLAYER_BC_RADIUS` 4, `REACH_SLACK` 2 and the band constants. It adds `approach_band` (a
  `Vector2(stop, reach)`), `effective_range`, `in_reach` and `approach_point` (the point `stop`
  short of the target on the line back to the walker; a walker already that close stays put).
- `client/scripts/npc/npc_table_reader.gd` adds `COL_BC_RADIUS` 50 and
  `parse_bc_radius_by_code`, modelled on `parse_speeds_by_code`. It skips short and non-numeric
  rows rather than reading them as 0.
- `client/scripts/npc/item_table_reader.gd` adds `COL_RANGE` 94 and `Item.attack_range`. The
  tooltip comment that called attack distance "not among these columns" is corrected.
- `client/scripts/npc/skill_data_reader.gd` adds `S_TARGET_REQUIRED` 22 and `S_TARGET_LAND` 24
  and keeps three per-level arrays on `BaseSkill`: `level_range`, `level_target_required` and
  `level_target_land`.
- `client/scripts/net/combat.gd` adds `skill_tick_approaches(target_required, target_land)`,
  the phase-0 test above.
- `client/scripts/ui/hud/hud_panels.gd` maps every level's unique skill id to that level's
  Range and to whether the skill tick walks for it, when the catalog loads. `skill_reach(id)`
  loads the catalog on first use and gives `{}` for an unknown id.
- `client/scripts/World3D.gd`:
  - `_load_character_assets` fills `_bc_radius_by_code` for every row.
  - `_attack_monster(monster_id, skill_id := 0, basic_code := "")` is now called by
    `_try_attack_monster`, `_on_attack_pressed`, `_qa_attack_nearest` and `_cast_skill`.
  - `_attack_band` builds the band from the gender body row's radius (falling back to 4), the
    species' radius from `MonsterSnapshot.code_name`, and the skill's or weapon's range.
  - `_equipped_weapon_range` mirrors keepup's `equippedWeaponRange`: 0 unarmed, and 0 when the
    weapon slot's durability is 0 (`durability.IsBroken`).
  - A skill the skill tick casts without a band (`skill_tick_approaches` false) is sent at once
    from where the player stands, and the log says so.
  - With the band unknown (no species row, a skill not in the catalog, no archive), the request
    goes out at once and the log says why.
  - In reach, `_release_pending_attack` stops the player, flushes the position and sends.
    Otherwise `_pending_attack` is stored and `_move_target` is aimed at `approach_point`.
  - The `_has_move_target` branch of `_physics_process` runs `_step_pending_attack` every frame,
    before the send gate. It re-aims at the target's latest snapshot and releases on the first
    frame in reach.
  - The cast animation, the battle stance and `_pending_skill_hit_code` moved into
    `_send_attack`, so they play when the request goes out.
  - `_pending_attack` is cleared by typing, WASD, void recovery, a new ground walk or pick-up
    walk, another monster, a zone change, and the target dying or leaving the list.
    `_drop_pending_attack` also ends the walk, for a click that acts from where the player
    stands: an NPC's talk window, or a pick-up within `PICK_RANGE`. A zone change and the
    target's death use it too.
- `SRREVAMP_QA_ATTACK_GOTO` still teleports. It now records the teleport's OpMove as sent, so the
  attack finds itself in reach and sends with no second, identical OpMove.

## Record correction: NPC_SD_GUILD_AGENT/2/3 register no interaction id (round 520)

Round 455's interaction-id table gave id 0xc to `NPC_SD_GUILD_AGENT*`, and round 458 repeated it
("specialty goods"). Both were wrong. No codename test in the server registers any interaction id
on the three guild agents. Nothing a player sees changes: the client already offered them no
Guild line (round 458), and nothing in srrevamp acts on 0xc. The fix is to the record, so that
no later talk-menu or specialty-goods change gives 0xc to them.

**Grounding** (read-only on the RE box: `/var/tmp/decomp_server`, `/var/tmp/srv.asm`, the exe's
`.rdata` and `/var/tmp/tables`; `CGObjNPCNPC::Create` is at `0x4c6350` and is 5,561 bytes long):

- **The agents' chain.** `0x4c6d6b`-`0x4c6ddb` runs four `strstr` tests (`FUN_009dddc0`). They
  use `.rdata` `0xaeedd8` `NPC_SD_THIEF_AGENT_CHANGER`, `0xaeedf4` `NPC_SD_GUILD_AGENT`, `0xaeee08`
  `NPC_SD_GUILD_AGENT2` and `0xaeee1c` `NPC_SD_GUILD_AGENT3`, read with `objdump -s`. A hit jumps
  to `0x4c6ddd`: `cmp esi,1 ; jne 0x4c6dfd`, then `call [edx+0x318]` with `(4, 0xff, 0.0f, 0)`.
  - `+0x318` is slot 198, `IGObj::SetBodyMode` (`docs/protocol/igobj_vtable.md`, the table).
  - 4 is `BODYMODE_BERSERKER` (`character_state.md`, "The body-mode enum").
  - `esi` is the byte at `CMainProcess` (`DAT_00d6a8dc`) `+0x42404`, loaded at `0x4c6494`. No
    instruction writes `esi` between there and `0x4c6ddd`.
  - The decompiler agrees: `bVar2 == 1` guards `(*piVar11 + 0x318)(4,0xff,0,0)`, and the branch
    has no `+0x164` call.
  - Not read: what the byte means, and why an agent is put in that body mode.
- **Where 0xc really is.** The next chain tests nine literals, `0xaeee30` `NPC_CH_SPECIAL2`
  through `0xaeeec0` `NPC_SD_M_AREA_SPECIAL3`. A hit jumps to `0x4c6f31`,
  `mov eax,[edx+0x164] ; push 0xc`. **Corrected in round 523:** `0x4c6f31` is `mov edx,[ebx]`;
  the slot load is at `0x4c6f33` and the `push 0xc` at `0x4c6f39`.
- **Three censuses over the whole function** (`0x4c6350` to the `ret` at `0x4c7906`):
  - two `push 0xc`: the SPECIAL chain's, and `0x4c6ae1`, `NPC_TD_THIEF_BUY`, followed by 0xd;
  - two loads of slot `0x318`: `0x4c6de6` (the agents) and `0x4c774b`. At `0x4c774b`,
    `NPC_CH_GACHA_MACHINE` or `NPC_CH_GACHA_OPERATOR` (`_stricmp`, `0x9ddf4e`) gets the same
    call, on the branch where the `+0x42404` byte is not 0;
  - every string the function pushes, 116 distinct `.rdata` addresses read out of the exe, tested
    as a substring of each agent's codename. The only matches are the agents' own literals.
- **The data-driven paths.** Two registrations in `Create` do not test the codename:
  - the reference record's `+0x90` set (round 454; ids 7 and 9 from the teleport tables, id 8
    from a loader whose table is unattributed);
  - 0x11, a lookup keyed by `IGObj::GetRefObjID` (slot 1).

  The agents' object ids are 26826, 26827, 26829 and 26830 (characterdata). They were looked
  for in all 82 files under `/var/tmp/tables`, which is not the whole textdata set. They occur
  only in their own characterdata rows, in `npcpos.txt` and as numbers in `skilldata_30000.txt`
  rows. None is in a teleport table. The control, gate 2094, is found in `teleportdata` and
  `teleportbuilding`. The claim is therefore exact for the codename paths. For the data paths it
  holds against the tables extracted on the box.

**Change** (comments and docs only; no logic):

- `client/scripts/npc/npc_service_reader.gd`: the second `GUILD_PATTERNS` bullet now says no
  codename test gives the agents an id. It gives the chain, the slot and the gate.
- `client/scripts/npc/npc_service_reader_test.gd`: the agents' check now reads "gets no
  interaction id by codename, so offers no Guild". The repair check's comment on its negative
  list no longer calls the agent 0xc.
- `docs/protocol/character_state.md`, "The interaction-id vocabulary, from the NPCs themselves":
  - The 0xc row lists `NPC_TD_THIEF_BUY` and the nine SPECIAL literals, and says the guild agents
    are not on it. The plan named seven of the nine; `NPC_SD_M_AREA_SPECIAL2` and `_SPECIAL3` are
    in the same chain, so they are listed too.
  - A new "none (by codename)" row lists the thief agent changer and the three guild agents,
    with the `SetBodyMode` call and its gate.
  - A new subsection, "One misattribution, corrected (round 520)", follows "Why this is trusted".
    It gives the evidence above.
- `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`, round 458: an inline correction under "It invented three".

**Departs from the plan.** The plan's no-id row also listed `NPC_CH_GACHA_MACHINE`. It is left
out, because that could not be confirmed. When the `+0x42404` byte is 0, `0x4c77c2` registers
0x11 on any NPC for which `FUN_004ccb70` (a map on `DAT_00d6aa14 + 0x110`) finds an entry. That
map's table was not identified. The player's `gachanpcmap.txt` has a single row, `1 9251 1 2`,
and 9251 is the gacha machine. That is a candidate, not a finding. The same read disputes the
0x11 row, which put the id "beside 0x28", and the 0x12 row, which is gated on the same byte
(`0x4c76d6 cmp [esp+0x14],0 ; je 0x4c7788`). Both rows now point at the new subsection and are
otherwise unchanged; they need their own round. srrevamp uses neither id.

**Tests.**

- New doc probe: `TestInteractionTableAgentsRegisterNoID` in
  `server/internal/systems/interaction_table_test.go`, which reads `character_state.md` at run
  time. The `| **0xc** |` row must not contain `GUILD_AGENT` and must contain
  `NPC_TD_THIEF_BUY`, `NPC_CH_SPECIAL2` and `NPC_SD_M_AREA_SPECIAL`. Some table row must carry
  both `NPC_SD_GUILD_AGENT` and `SetBodyMode`.
- **Negative case proven.** With `character_state.md` and `npc_service_reader.gd` stashed, the
  probe failed four ways: the row names the agents, it lacks `NPC_CH_SPECIAL2`, it lacks
  `NPC_SD_M_AREA_SPECIAL`, and no row records `SetBodyMode`. With the files restored, it passes.
- `npc_service_reader_test.gd` on the render box: 70 ok and ALL PASS, the same 70 as at BASE
  (only a message changed). `client/tools/remote_godot.sh tests` ran 80 suites, 0 failing.
  `client/tools/remote_godot.sh check` checked 246 scripts and 5 scenes: ALL LOAD.

## Guild NPC menu by membership: Create (no guild) opens a name prompt, Leave (member); master keeps the placeholder (round 521)

A guild NPC's talk box offered one "Guild" line to everyone, and choosing it said "Guild is not
available yet.". The real client picks the guild lines by two tests that are taken to be the
player's guild state: "in a guild" and "is the master". What each test means is inferred, not
read from its writer (see the grounding below). srrevamp now does the same for the two lines it
has a server for. At `NPC_CH_GENARAL_SP`, a player with no guild sees the archive's "Create a new
guild". That line asks for a name and founds the guild, subject to the server's level 20,
500,000 gold and 2-12 byte name gates (rounds 481 and 487). A member sees "Leave guild.", which
asks Leave / Cancel before it sends. A master keeps the placeholder. This also covers the guild
half of the talk-menu-labels item.

**Grounding** (read-only on the RE box: `/var/tmp/decomp_client`, `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm`, and
`.rdata` with `objdump -s` on `/opt/sro-files/client/sro_client.exe`). The full write-up is in
`docs/protocol/character_state.md`, "The guild NPC's lines (round 521)".

- **`FUN_00700440`'s id 0xf block** (row 15 of the talk-menu table). The lookup is at `0x70105e`
  and the membership test at `0x70107e`-`0x70108b`.
  - `FUN_009870e0()` is 0 (`0x701096`, `0x70109d` `je 0x701165`): item 0x12 alone
    (`0x701165`-`0x70116c`).
  - Otherwise `FUN_00989ce0(name)` is 0 (`0x7010c4`, `0x7010f6`, `0x7010ff` `je 0x70112a`): item
    0x1c (`0x70112a`).
  - Otherwise items 0x17, 0x14, 0x18 and 0x1b.
  - Both member branches then get 0x19 or 0x1a, 0x1d and 0x43. So a master is never offered 0x1c.
- **The tokens.** In `FUN_006fcd60`, item 0x12 takes index byte `0x0e` (`0x6fd394`+0x12). Its
  jump-table entry, at `0x6fd310`, is `0x6fd076` `push 0xdad440`. Item 0x1c takes index byte
  `0x17`. Its entry, at `0x6fd334`, is `0x6fd0bc` `push 0xdad2ec`. `.rdata 0xdad440` is
  `UIIT_CTL_GUILD_CREATE` and `0xdad2ec` is `UIIT_CTL_GUILD_SECESSION`. The decompiled switch
  agrees: case 0x12 and case 0x1c name the same two strings. The player's
  `textuisystem.txt` (`/var/tmp/tables/textuisystem.txt`) reads "Create a new guild" and
  "Leave guild." in both of its layouts. Those are the fallback labels.
- **The two tests are inferred, not read from their writers.**
  - `FUN_009870e0` is the byte at `+4` of the `+0x148` block (`FUN_009870d0`) of the object at
    `0xeeebd8`. Its zero branch offers only creation, so it is taken as "in a guild".
  - `FUN_00989ce0` compares the block's `+0x34` string with its argument and answers true on
    equal (`0x989cec` `add eax,0x34`; `0x989d05` `call 0x47ec20`; `0x989d0e` `sete al`). The
    argument is `FUN_009d6580`'s copy of `[0xeef5ec]+0x84c` (`0x7010a3`-`0x7010ae`). It is taken
    as "the player is the master" for three reasons:
    - `UI_GUILD::FUN_005b5150` finds the player's member record with the same string
      (`FUN_009960a0` walks a list comparing names);
    - on the same test, that function shows `..._UNION_CHAT_GRANT` rather than `..._CONFIRM`;
    - the true branch is the one with `GUILD_BREAK` and `MASTERLEAVE`.

  (The plan said the string was at `+0x148+0x44`. The decompiler hides the `add eax,0x34`, and
  the instruction listing shows `+0x34`.)
- **The leave line's click** (found in review). `CIF_NPCTalk::FUN_007020c0` dispatches a chosen
  item through the index bytes at `0x703d2c` and the jump table at `0x703c6c`
  (`0x702143`-`0x70214a`). Item 0x1c takes index byte `0x12` (`0x703d48`), and entry `0x703cb4`
  is `0x702ba9`. That case tests `FUN_009870e0` again and opens a window of kind 0x14
  (`0x702bf9` `push 0x14`; `0x702c0e` `call 0x6ec5d0`, a centred `0x134` x `0x94` gwnd built at
  `0x6ec689`-`0x6ec6e2`), and the block holds no call to `Net_SendRequestPacket`. Item 0x1d's
  case (`0x702c1f`) sends its request at once (`0x702c31` `push 0x7046`; `call 0x841780`,
  `Net_SendRequestPacket`). What the kind 0x14 window shows was not read, so srrevamp's Leave /
  Cancel prompt is its own design.
- **The server** registers id 0xf on the seven `GUILD_PATTERNS` (`CGObjNPCNPC::Create`, rounds 455
  and 458). The create gates are in `guild.CheckCreator` and the stores' `Create` (rounds 481 and
  487). The name cap is `guild.MaxNameLength`, 12, from the engine's `len - 2u < 0xb`
  (`docs/protocol/guild.md`, the "name length" row).

**Change.**
- `client/scripts/npc/npc_service_reader.gd`:
  - New constants `GUILD_CREATE_STRID` and `GUILD_SECESSION_STRID`, each cited as above.
  - `services_for(code, shop_npcs, guild_id := -1, guild_master := false, _player_job_kind := 0)`.
    The last argument is reserved for the job-guild talk entries and is not read yet. A
    two-argument call still gives a guild NPC the placeholder.
  - `guild_services(guild_id, is_master)`:
    - -1 gives `guild`;
    - 0 gives `guild_create` ("Create a new guild", `GUILD_CREATE_STRID`);
    - a member gives `guild_leave` ("Leave guild.", `GUILD_SECESSION_STRID`);
    - a master gives `guild`.
- `client/scripts/World3D.gd`:
  - New `_guild_id` (-1 until a guild reply arrives) and `_guild_master`.
  - `_on_guild_result` (info, join and create) records the id on success. The player is the
    master when the member with `current_character_name` holds `ROLE_LEADER`, which mirrors
    `FUN_00989ce0`'s name test.
  - `_on_guild_leave_result` sets 0/false on success and logs "Left the guild.". On a refusal
    it logs the reason and asks for the guild again (`NetClient.guild_info`), so the info reply
    corrects a stale state (the server's "not in a guild").
  - `_on_guild_create_result` logs "Guild %s founded." or the server's refusal.
  - `_npc_services` passes the state.
  - `_on_npc_service_selected`: `guild_create` opens the name prompt and `guild_leave` opens the
    leave prompt. Both need a server connection.
  - After each guild reply, `_refresh_open_talk_menu` rebuilds the talk menu in place if it is
    open (`HudPanels.refresh_npc_talk`).
  - `guild_create_requested` is connected to `_on_guild_create_requested`, which calls
    `NetClient.create_guild`. `guild_leave_requested` is connected to `_on_guild_leave_requested`,
    which calls `NetClient.leave_guild`.
  - The movement gate is now `_is_typing()`: the chat's line, or any focused `LineEdit` or
    `TextEdit` (`HudPanels.is_typing`). `_physics_process` reads the move keys from the raw key
    state (`Input.get_axis`), which a focused line does not consume. Before this, a name such as
    "Swords" typed into the prompt walked the character on S, W and D, and the arrow keys moved it
    too. The old gate asked only the chat line.
- `client/scripts/ui/hud/hud_panels.gd`:
  - New signal `guild_create_requested(guild_name)` and `open_guild_name_prompt(npc_name)`, a
    panel on the talk window laid out like `_open_gold_dialog`.
    - Its heading is `_resolve_ui(GUILD_CREATE_STRID, ...)`.
    - Its `LineEdit` has `max_length` = `GUILD_NAME_MAX` = 12, the server's limit (not a claimed
      client limit).
    - Create or Enter emits the trimmed name and an empty name sends nothing.
    - It prints `GUILDPROMPT <npc>: name prompt opened`.
    - The prompt is this project's own design. The real client's guild-creation window was not
      read.
  - New signal `guild_leave_requested` and `open_guild_leave_prompt(npc_name)`: the leave
    line's text (`GUILD_SECESSION_STRID`), then Leave and Cancel. Only Leave emits the signal.
    It prints `GUILDPROMPT <npc>: leave prompt opened`. It is this project's own design (see the
    leave line's click above). The two prompts share `_talk_prompt`, `_talk_prompt_buttons` and
    `_show_talk_prompt`, and only one is up at a time (`TALK_PROMPTS`).
  - New `is_open(panel_id)` and `is_typing()` (the viewport's focus owner is a `LineEdit` or
    `TextEdit`).
  - `open_npc_talk` is a new conversation, so it always drops a prompt. A click on another NPC
    while the name prompt is up no longer leaves a create line over that NPC's talk box. The new
    `refresh_npc_talk` rebuilds an open talk box's lines without `open()`. It keeps the prompt and
    does not raise the talk box above a window opened from it, such as the store after Buy. The
    lines are drawn by `_fill_npc_talk`, split out of `open_npc_talk`.

**Not modelled, and disclosed** (`character_state.md` and `TODO.md`): the master's items 0x17,
0x14, 0x18 and 0x1b, and items 0x19/0x1a, 0x1d and 0x43, which member and master both get.
srrevamp has no server for them, so a member sees one guild line where the real client shows
four.

**One known mismatch, left for its own round: "Buy" at a guild NPC.** The server registers id 1
beside 0xf on all seven guild patterns (`CGObjNPCNPC::Create`, `0x4c6a4f`: `push 0xf`, then
`push 0x1`, each through `+0x164`). With 0xf present, the client emits item 1 (the store lines)

`character_state.md` records the mismatch under "The guild NPC's lines (round 521)".

  `refshopgroup.txt` names `NPC_CH_GENARAL_SP` as running `GROUP_STORE_CH_GUILD`
  (`/var/tmp/tables/refshopgroup.txt`). Because `_on_guild_result` rebuilds an open talk menu,
  the reply may arrive before or after `QA_TALK` opens it. No running client has printed those
  lines yet.
- **Not measured either: a real key press into the prompt.** (m) measures the two things the
  walking bug turned on: the viewport's focus owner and the value of `World3D._is_typing()`. No
  key event was sent through `Input.get_axis`, and nobody has typed into the prompt in a running
  client.
- `cd server && go build ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green. No server file changed.
  `SYSTEMS.md`'s Guild row does not describe the talk menu, so it needed no edit.

## Two review notes on rounds 519 and 521: a cast ends the attack walk, and a click on the world takes the keyboard back (round 522)

Two non-blocking review notes described bugs a player would meet, so they were fixed before
the release rather than batched with the record corrections. This round's own review then found
that the click half leaned on a false premise, and that is fixed here too.

**A cast pressed on the way to a monster ends the walk (round 519's review).** Clicking a
monster out of reach stores `_pending_attack` and walks toward it (`World3D._attack_monster`).
A second attack replaced the pending one with a bare `_pending_attack = {}`. On the two paths
that send at once -- a skill the skill tick casts with no walk (Target_Required 0 or a land
target, `CombatNet.skill_tick_approaches`) and an attack whose band cannot be computed -- the old
walk kept going: the character walked to the old stop point and stood by the monster doing
nothing. `_attack_monster` now calls `_drop_pending_attack()` first, which ends the walk only when
an attack was pending, so a ground walk with no attack is left alone and a walk the new attack
needs is re-aimed by `_step_pending_attack`. Both send-at-once paths now also call
`_flush_position()` before the request, as `_release_pending_attack` does: after a dropped walk
the player has usually moved past `MIN_SEND_DISTANCE` since the last send, and the physics send
gate would otherwise emit one more OpMove within `MIN_SEND_INTERVAL` (0.05 s, about three physics
frames), which cancels the keep-up the attack just started (`world.go` handleMove). **Not tested by the suite**: `_attack_monster` needs a
running world. Round 522's review read every caller (`_cast_skill`, `_try_attack_monster`,
`_on_attack_pressed`, `_qa_attack_nearest` including `QA_ATTACK_GOTO`): whenever
`_pending_attack` is set, the walk in progress is that attack's own.

**A line left focused no longer keeps movement dead (round 521's review).** Round 521 widened
the movement gate from the chat line to any focused `LineEdit` or `TextEdit`
(`HudPanels.is_typing`), so typing a guild name no longer walked the character. The review found
the other side of that. In Godot 4.2 a click on a `SpinBox`'s arrows grabs its inner `LineEdit`'s
focus, and a click on empty world does not release focus. So after touching the options panel's
chat-font spinner, WASD, click-to-move and the attack walk stayed dead while the panel was open,
because the gate clears `_has_move_target` and `_pending_attack` every frame.
- `World3D._unhandled_input` now starts with `take_focus_back`, which releases the viewport's
  focus owner on a LEFT button press that reaches it. Not on the right button (a drag orbits the
  camera), the wheel (zoom) or the middle button (a quickslot): none of those should end a
  message being typed. The click carries on to the handlers below.
- The options panel's chat-font spinner hands the focus back once its value is set
  (`debug_panel.gd` `_on_chat_font_changed`), so a step with its arrows leaves nothing focused.
- A `SpinBox`'s line still counts as typing while it has the focus. The first draft of this
  round excluded it; the review measured that keys pressed then go into the spinner and not to
  quickslots or berserk, so letting W also walk would split one key press two ways. A line not
  visible in the tree does not count (Godot already releases a hidden control's focus; the check
  is only a guard).

**Which clicks reach `_unhandled_input` (this round's review).** The first draft said a click
there "landed on the world, not on a control". False: in Godot 4.2 a press is marked handled only
when a STOP control is on its chain, and several HUD surfaces are PASS or IGNORE all the way up.
**Measured** on the render box by the review, with the real HUD built from Media.pk2: a left or
right click on the chat's scrollback or frame reached `_unhandled_input`, and so did a click on a
hotbar slot (which also fired its quickslot); with the chat line focused, the draft's
`take_focus_back` then took that focus away mid-message. **Read from the code, not measured**:
the release of such a click runs `_dispatch_left_click` -> `_try_set_move_target`, which walks
the character to the ground behind the chat (that walk predates this round) and, for a slot,
clears `_pending_attack` -- replacing round 519's approach walk for a skill just clicked on a
distant target.
- `HudChat` is now `MOUSE_FILTER_STOP`, as `HudWindow` has been since the 2026-09-20 playtest
  (its comment has the reasoning: Godot hit-tests the deepest control first, so the input line
  and the mode button still get their clicks).
- The hotbar slots (`HudUnderbar`, `GDR_TMPQS_*`) are now STOP. A middle press on a slot is
  handled there (`activate_key(0)`, the middle-button quickslot binding), since STOP now keeps it
  from `World3D._unhandled_input`.
- Still passing clicks to the world, measured by the re-review (press and release both reach
  `_unhandled_input`, and `take_focus_back` ends a message being typed): the player-info block,
  the minimap's map (every node IGNORE, `hud_minimap.gd`), the target window (every node IGNORE,
  `hud_target.gd`) and the hotbar's body away from its slots and buttons. Recorded in
  `docs/TODO.md`, not fixed here.
- A side effect of STOP, as every `HudWindow` and the F3 panel already have it: a right-drag that
  starts on the world stops orbiting while the cursor is over the chat (Godot 4.2 sends a drag
  that began on no control to the control under the cursor, and STOP consumes it). Measured by
  the re-review; not fixed here.

`npc_service_reader_test.gd` check (n), in the running tree beside check (m):
- the spinner's inner line really holds the focus (the probe), and counts as typing;
- a focused visible `LineEdit` is typing;
- a key press, the wheel, the right and middle buttons, and a left release do not take the focus
  back; a left press does (NEGATIVE: there was no `take_focus_back`), and the gate then reads no
  typing;
- `HudChat.new().setup()` leaves the chat `MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` (NEGATIVE: with `hud_chat.gd`
  reverted it FAILS, "filter 1", measured).
The hotbar's STOP and the spinner's release are not driven by the suite (they need the built
underbar and a world). Render box: `remote_godot.sh tests` 80 suites, 0 failing; `check` ALL
LOAD. No real click or key has been sent through a running client.

Also landed from round 521's review: `FRONTEND_CHECKLIST.md`'s talk-dialogue item no longer says
the guild line only reports that it is unavailable, and `TODO.md`'s attack-distance item carries
its releases.

Found, not caused here: `hud_window_test.gd` prints `SCRIPT ERROR: Compile Error: Identifier not
found: NetClient` and still reports ALL PASS, and the suite loop does not flag it. It prints the
same at `dbbedc4` (round 517), so it predates this round.

## Batch-10 review follow-ups (rounds 519-521): skill range wording, the phase-0 return, the interaction-id record, the guild-state limits (round 523)

The reviewers' non-blocking notes on rounds 519-521, each re-checked against the dumps, the asm
and the box's extracted tables (all read-only) before it was written. Comments and docs only, plus
one doc probe. Nothing a player sees changes.

**Round 519: skill range, the phase-0 return, BCRadius, the Mangyang row.**

- **Range per level is constant for China skills only.** Every skilldata row with a non-zero
  mastery (col 34) was grouped by GroupID (col 2). Range (col 21) varies in five groups. (GroupID
  0 was left out, as it is no skill: its two rows are the ungrouped event skills
  `SKILL_EVENT_GHOST_AMULET` 32099, Range 45, and `SKILL_EVENT_GHOST_TRAP` 32100, Range 0, both
  mastery 1. Round 527 added this note after re-running the grouping.) Four are
  `SKILL_CH_BOW_SPECIAL_A..D` (467-470), as round 519 said. The fifth is
  `SKILL_EU_WARRIOR_FRENZYA_TOUNT_SPRINT_A` (group 540, ids 8479-8499, mastery 513), which rises
  80 -> 240 over 21 levels. Without the mastery filter, groups 1064-1066 and 1073 vary as well.
  That is only because four `SKILL_VSROEDITORCOM_VISUAL_*` rows (46351-46353, 46360; mastery 0,
  Range 0) share their GroupIDs. `SkillDataReader.parse_skills` keeps only `SKILL_CH_` rows, so
  it never sees the Europe skill. `skill_data_reader.gd`'s comments now say "China", name the EU
  row, and point at that filter. Round 519's bullet has an inline correction.
- **A `Basic_Activity` other than 2 stays in phase 0.** `/var/tmp/srv.asm`: `0x4ae6e6 cmp
  byte [edi+0x65],2 ; 0x4ae6ea jne 0x4ae9dc`. `0x4ae9dc` is `mov eax,1 ; pop edi ; pop esi ; pop
  ebx ; mov esp,ebp ; pop ebp ; ret 8`. The `call 0x4ac9e0` at `0x4ae9d7`, which sets the next
  phase, sits before the jump target. `Tick_UseSkill` in `/var/tmp/decomp_server` reads
  `if (*(char *)(iVar6 + 0x65) != '\x02') { return 1; }`. So the tick returns and stays in phase
  0. It does not "leave phase 0 earlier". This was fixed in `combat.gd`, in round 519's bullet
  (inline) and in `TODO.md`'s filed-departure line. `TODO.md` already said as much further down.
  The count still holds when re-counted: 2,185 China board rows over 258 skills, and 256 with
  Activity != 2 (174 with 1, 82 with 0). Every one has `Target_Required` 0.
- **The player's BCRadius: the client reads a row, the server a constant.** All 52 `CHAR_*` rows
  read 4, re-counted over the six characterdata data files. `World3D._attack_band` reads the
  gender body row, and its comment now says that `keepUpInReach`/`skillInReach`
  (`session/keepup.go`) pass the constant `combat.PlayerBCRadius` instead. The two agree only
  because the rows do. `combat.gd`'s `PLAYER_BC_RADIUS` comment says the same.
- **`monster_ai.md`'s "second `MOB_CH_MANGNYANG`"** is `MOB_CH_STRONG_MANGNYANG` (RefObjID 9383,
  `characterdata_10000.txt`, level 90, 676,983 HP, speeds 8/22, BCRadius 6). The doc's "code
  names are not unique" was wrong too: 13,291 rows carry 13,291 distinct names. A suffix match on
  `MANGNYANG` also finds `MOB_EVE_STRONG_TQ_MANGNYANG` (26927, `characterdata_30000.txt`). The
  paragraph is corrected, keeping the control's lesson, and the round-362 entry above has an
  inline note. The client reads seven characterdata files; the seventh, `characterdata.txt`, only
  lists file names.
- **The debug panel's Skills-tab "Use"** (`World3D._on_skill_use_pressed`) still calls
  `NetClient.use_skill` at once, with no approach walk. This is now in `TODO.md`'s "Attack
  distance" list. It is a developer panel. The hotbar goes through `_cast_skill` ->
  `_attack_monster`.

**Round 520: the interaction-id record** (`character_state.md`, "The interaction-id vocabulary,
from the NPCs themselves"). A census of every `mov eax,[edx+0x164]` in `CGObjNPCNPC::Create`
(`0x4c6350`-`0x4c7906`, `/var/tmp/srv.asm`) was paired with its push and the call before it:

- **32 call sites.** 31 follow a codename test: `strstr` (`FUN_009dddc0`) for all but 0x28, whose
  test is `CompareStringA` (import `0xad90b8`, `0x4c76bd`, flags `0x10001`) against `.rdata
  0xaef3f8` `NPC_SIEGE_DUNGEON_TELEPORT`. The 32nd, 0x11 at `0x4c77c2`, follows none. It is
  reached when `[esp+0x14]` (the `+0x42404` byte, stored at `0x4c64a9`) is 0 (`0x4c76d6`), and
  when `FUN_004ccb70` (`0x4c77ac`) returns an entry whose first byte is not 0.
- **31 sites push a literal beside the call.** The one at `0x4c75f9` has no push of its own.
  `0x4c75d1 push 0x21` follows a hit on `.rdata 0xaebf6c` `NPC_BATTLE_ARENA_MANAGER` and jumps to
  `0x4c75f7`. `0x4c75f5 push 0x22` follows a hit on `0xaef394` `NPC_BATTLE_ARENA_EXCHANGER` and
  falls into it. The decompile shows the same thing as `uVar6 = 0x21` / `0x22`, then
  `goto LAB_004c75f7`. **This departs from the plan**, which called the id "computed". It is two
  literals sharing one call, so the table's "computed" row became rows 0x21 and 0x22. What the
  two ids do was not read.
- **The paragraph before the table** said "thirty-two times with literal ids, each behind a
  comparison against the NPC's own CodeName". It is now qualified with the two points above.
- **The 0x11 row** now says what the subsection says: no codename, the map lookup, the byte, and
  not the siege-dungeon block (that block ends at 0x28's call, `0x4c76d4`). The 0x12 row keeps
  its byte-0 condition. The subsection is now "Two misattributions, corrected (rounds 520 and
  523)". It opens by naming both, and the 0x11 paragraph is headed as the second rather than as
  "not changed here".
- **`0x4c6f31`** is `mov edx,[ebx]`. The slot load is at `0x4c6f33` and `push 0xc` at `0x4c6f39`.
  Eight `jne 0x4c6f31` reach it, and the ninth test falls through to it on a hit
  (`0x4c6f2f je 0x4c6f3f` on a miss). Fixed in the subsection, with an inline note in round 520's
  entry.
- **`npc_service_reader.gd`'s `GUILD_PATTERNS` comment** now names both 0xc registrations: the
  SPECIAL chain (`0x4c6f39`) and `NPC_TD_THIEF_BUY` (`0x4c6ae1`, followed by 0xd). It also points
  at the renamed subsection.

**Round 521: the guild state can go stale.** srrevamp's server sends no guild broadcasts. Every
`sess.Send` in `session/guild.go` answers the requester, and no other guild opcode exists. When
the master leaves, `guild.Store.Leave` (`MemStore` by join order, `SQLStore` by `joined_at`)
promotes the longest-standing member, and that member's client is not told. That client keeps
`_guild_master` false and its guild NPC still offers "Leave guild.", until the next `guild_info`
reply (world entry, or opening the guild window). The server does not refuse a leader's leave,
so only a refused leave asks again. This is disclosed in `World3D`'s `_guild_id`/`_guild_master`
comment, in `character_state.md`'s "The guild NPC's lines (round 521)" and in `TODO.md`'s NPC-talk
item. Behaviour is unchanged.

**Tests.**

- New doc probe `TestInteractionTable0x11AndArenaRows` in

  0x21 and 0x22 must name their arena NPC and `0x4c75f9`, and no `| computed |` row may be left.
- **Negative case proven.** With `character_state.md` stashed (BASE), the probe failed four
  ways: the 0x11 row still in the siege block, both arena rows missing, and the "computed" row

- Render box: `client/tools/remote_godot.sh tests` ran 80 suites, 0 failing.
  `client/tools/remote_godot.sh check` checked 246 scripts and 5 scenes: ALL LOAD. Only comments

## A guild NPC's store line only for a player in a guild (FUN_00700440: item 1 with 0x0f needs FUN_009870e0) (round 524)

Round 521 found, and left open, that a guildless player at a guild NPC got "Buy" in srrevamp
where the real client shows no store line. This round closes it. It is a client change: at a
guild NPC, `NpcServiceReader.services_for` leaves the shop service out when the player is known
to have no guild.

**Grounding, re-read for this round** (all read-only on the render box).

- **Server.** `/var/tmp/srv.asm`: in `CGObjNPCNPC::Create`, the seven `strstr` tests on the
  guild literals (`.rdata 0xaeec34` `NPC_CH_GENARAL_SP` through `0xaeec9c`
  `NPC_SD_T_AREA_GUILD2`, read with `objdump -s` on `SR_GameServer.exe`) each branch to
  `0x4c6a4f`. There, `0x4c6a57` `push 0xf` and `0x4c6a65` `push 0x1` each go through
  `[edx+0x164]` (`AddAvailableInteraction`). So every guild NPC holds ids 0xf and 1.
- **Client, `FUN_00700440`** (`/var/tmp/sro_client.asm`). Id 1 is looked up at `0x700982`, and
  `0x7009af` `je 0x700b10` skips item 1 when it is absent. With id 1 present, 0xf is looked up
  (`0x7009c4`). If 0xf is absent, `0x7009f5` `je 0x700a0e` goes to the keeper branch (id 3 and
  `FUN_00989d20`), which never calls `FUN_009870e0`. If 0xf is present, `0x7009f7`
  `mov ecx,0xeeebd8`, `0x7009fc` `call 0x9870e0`, `0x700a01` `test al,al`: on 0, `0x700a03`
  `je 0x700b10`; otherwise `0x700a09` `jmp 0x700afe`, which is item 1 (`push 0; push 1; push
  ebx; call 0x6fcd60`, then `0x700b0a` `mov ebx,eax`).
- **What the skip covers.** `0x700b10` is where the next row begins: `test esi,esi`, then the id 4
  lookup byte at `0x700b12`. So the jump skips item 1 and nothing else. `ebx` (the running line
  number) is written only after the item-1 call, so a skipped item 1 takes no number, and the
  guild NPC's first line (the create line, row 15) is 1.
- **Item 1 is the store lines.** `FUN_006fcd60`: `0x6fce4d` `movzx ecx,[ebp+0x6fd394]`,
  `0x6fce54` `jmp [ecx*4+0x6fd2d8]`. Index byte `0x6fd394`+1 is `0x01` and entry `0x6fd2d8`[1] is
  `0x6fceb0` (`objdump -s` on `/opt/sro-files/client/sro_client.exe`), which calls `0x6fb630`
  (`0x6fcebc`).
- **`FUN_009870e0`** is `call 0x9870d0; mov al,[eax+4]; ret`, and `FUN_009870d0` is
  `lea eax,[ecx+0x148]; ret`: the byte at `+0x14c` of the object at `0xeeebd8`. That it means "in
  a guild" stays the inference round 521 recorded: its zero branch in the 0xf block offers only
  the create line. No writer was read. One more caller agrees without proving it:
  `FUN_005bec70` calls both on `0xeeebd8` (`0x5bec87` `call 0x9870e0`, `0x5bec96`
  `call 0x9870d0`, each after a `mov ecx,0xeeebd8`) and reads the block's `+5` byte (`0x5beca3`,
  `0x5becb4`) only when `FUN_009870e0` is nonzero (`0x5bec8e` `je 0x5becca`). (Corrected in round
  527: this cited `0x5bec82` and `0x5bec91`, which are the two `mov ecx,0xeeebd8`.)
  `sro_client.asm` has ten `call 0x9870e0` sites in all.
- **The fixture's shape.** `/var/tmp/tables/refshopgroup.txt` has seven `GROUP_STORE_*_GUILD`
  rows, one per guild pattern (`GROUP_STORE_CH_GUILD` / `NPC_CH_GENARAL_SP` through
  `GROUP_STORE_SD_T_GUILD` / `NPC_SD_T_AREA_GUILD2`), which is why srrevamp showed "Buy" there.

**Nothing else srrevamp shows at those seven NPCs depends on the gate.** None of their codenames
holds `WAREHOUSE`, so there is no storage line. The store window's repair buttons follow id 4,
which no guild NPC has (`REPAIR_PATTERNS`, round 514). The guild lines were already gated by the
same byte in round 521.

**Change** (`client/scripts/npc/npc_service_reader.gd`). `services_for` decides first whether the
codename matches a `GUILD_PATTERNS` entry. It adds "Buy" from the shop set unless the NPC is a
guild NPC and `guild_id` is 0. The guild lines use the same flag. Behaviour by guild state:

- `0` (no guild): no "Buy". At `NPC_CH_GENARAL_SP` the menu is "1. Create a new guild",
  "2. End conversation." (it was "1. Buy", "2. Create a new guild", "3. End conversation.").
- `> 0` (a member, or the master): "Buy" stays, ahead of the guild line, since item 1 comes
  before row 15 in `FUN_00700440`.
- `-1` (no guild reply yet), and the two-argument call: unchanged, "Buy" and the "Guild"
  placeholder.

`World3D` already passes `_guild_id` and rebuilds an open talk menu after each guild reply
(round 521), so creating a guild brings "Buy" back, and leaving drops it. No other store changes.
The comments in `services_for` and `guild_services` now describe the gate, not an open mismatch.

**Docs.** `character_state.md`: the round-521 section's "One known mismatch" paragraph is now
"'Buy' at a guild NPC needs a guild (round 524)", with the addresses above. `TODO.md`'s NPC-talk
item and `FRONTEND_CHECKLIST.md`'s talk item say it is done. Round 521's entry above has an
inline note. `SYSTEMS.md` has no row for the talk menu, so it is unchanged.

**Tests** (`client/scripts/npc/npc_service_reader_test.gd`, new check (o)). The shop set is
shaped like the player's `refshopgroup.txt`: the seven guild rows plus `NPC_CH_POTION`, with
the unread id column set to 0.

- **Negative:** with guild 0, each of the seven guild NPCs gives exactly `["guild_create"]`, and
  `talk_menu_lines` at `NPC_CH_GENARAL_SP` reads `1. Create a new guild`, `2. End conversation.`.
- A member at `NPC_CH_GENARAL_SP` (7, false) gives `["shop", "guild_leave"]`. The master at
  `NPC_WC_GUILD` (7, true) gives `["shop", "guild"]`.
- Guild -1, and the two-argument call, give `["shop", "guild"]`.
- `NPC_CH_POTION` with guild 0 still gives `["shop"]`.
- **Negative case proven.** With `npc_service_reader.gd` stashed (BASE), the suite failed 8
  checks: the seven guildless guild NPCs each gave `["shop", "guild_create"]`, and the menu
  started "1. Buy". With the file restored it prints ALL PASS.
- Render box: `client/tools/remote_godot.sh tests` ran 80 suites, 0 failing.
  `client/tools/remote_godot.sh check` checked 246 scripts and 5 scenes: ALL LOAD.
- `cd server && go build ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...`: green.

Not measured on a running real client, and no running srrevamp client has printed the new
`NPCTALK` lines yet.

## Credit guild points (GatheredSP and per-member GP_Donation) from converted skill points, batched at 10 (round 525)

**What was open.** Round 272 found where guild points come from, and `guild.PointAccumulator`
held the batching rule. Nothing called it. srrevamp's guild had no points total and no
per-member share, so kills gave the guild nothing. `SYSTEMS.md`'s Guild row and `TODO.md`'s
"Guild points and levels" item both listed this as the next step.

**Grounding, re-read this round** (`/var/tmp/decomp_server`, `/var/tmp/srv.asm`):

- **`GObjPC::GObjPC_GainExpAndLevel` (`0x004e5250`).** After the 400:1 conversion and the grant
  through vtable `+0x174`, it runs `if (0 < iVar9 && param_1[0x72f] != 0 && (param_1[0x861] +=
  iVar9, 9 < param_1[0x861])) { RequestAddGuildPoints(param_1[0x861]); param_1[0x861] = 0; }`.
  So points are counted only for a guild member, go out as one batch once the count passes 9,
  and the counter is zeroed without checking the request's result.
- **`CGuildManager::RequestAddGuildPoints` (`0x005c62e0`), in asm.** `5c62e3 cmp [esp+0x14],0;
  ja` needs a count above zero. `5c62fe` calls vtable `+0xf8` and `5c6308 cmp al,0x1`, else
  `0x4c07`. `5c6318` reads `[edi+0x1cbc]` (the guild, `pc[0x72f]`), else `0x4c0d`. `5c6335 cmp
  al,0x5; ja` needs guild level 5 or below. Then it sends `0x78f7`.
- **`CGuild::AddPoints` (`0x005c4110`, "CMainProcess::AddPoints" in the dump).** It calls
  `FUN_005d0c90(member)`, and only when that is nonzero does it do `rec+0x3c += d` (dirty bit 8)
  and `member rec+0x40 += d` (dirty bit 4) [corrected in round 534: dirty FLAGS 8 and 4, mask
  values, not bit indices -- `or [eax+0x8],0x8` at `0x5c4148` and `or [eax+0x8],0x4` at
  `0x5c4175`, as round 531 (e) already fixed in the name row and `guild.md`], then broadcast
  `0x38f5` types 5 and 6 through
  `CGuild::BroadcastToLocalMember`.
- **`docs/protocol/db_bind_offsets.tsv`.** `_GUILD GatheredSP 0x3c`, `_GUILDMEMBER GP_Donation
  0x40`, `_GUILDMEMBER Contribution 0x58`. The same file's `_GUILD Lvl 0x38` and
  `_GUILDMEMBER Permission 0x54` match offsets this project already reads off the same record
  pointers (the full-guild predicate `0x005d0fb0` and the permission test `FUN_005d0f80`), so
  the bind offsets and the in-memory offsets are the same record.

**Two record corrections.**

- `guild.md` and `guild.go` said `RequestAddGuildPoints` "requires a PC (`0x4c07`
  otherwise)". Vtable `+0xf8` is `IGObj::GetLifeState` (`docs/protocol/igobj_vtable.md`, slot
  62), so the test is for a **living** character. The dump's own annotation of `0x5c62e0` still
  says "unless a PC". The RE box is read-only here, so it is left as it is.
- Both files called `member+0x40` the member's "contribution". The column is `GP_Donation`, and
  `Contribution` is a separate column at `+0x58`.

**Change.**

- **`guild`**
  - `Guild.GatheredSP` and `Member.GPDonation` are new fields.
  - New `Store.AddPoints(guildID, characterID, points)` credits both totals or neither:
    `ErrGuildNotFound`, then `ErrNotInGuild`. A count of zero or less is a no-op.
  - `MemStore` implements it under its lock. `SQLStore` adds `gathered_sp` / `gp_donation`
    (`BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`), reads both in `Get`, and runs
    `AddPoints` in one transaction. That transaction updates the member row first, then the
    guild row. When no member row matches, it checks whether the guild exists, to tell the two
    errors apart. That order does not rule out a deadlock with a leader's `Leave`, which locks
    the leaver's row, then the guild row, then the new leader's row: an `AddPoints` for the new
    leader at the same moment closes a cycle, and Postgres aborts one side (the batch is logged
    and lost, or the leave fails). Taking the guild row first would cycle on the leaver's row
    instead. The comment on `SQLStore.AddPoints` says so.
  - New `Store.GuildIDOf(characterID)`: membership alone (`pc[0x72f] != 0`), one query in
    `SQLStore`, without the roster `GetByCharacter` loads. `SQLStore.GetByCharacter` now uses
    it.
  - The engine's fields are dwords. srrevamp stores 64-bit, which is its own width, not a claim
    about the engine.
- **`session.NewGuildPointSkills`** (new `guildpoints.go`)
  - A `skill.Store` decorator (`*GuildPointSkills`) that overrides only `AddSkillExp`. After
    the inner store converts points (`gained > 0`) and `GuildIDOf` finds a guild, it books them
    on that character's `PointAccumulator` under a mutex. A batch goes to `AddPoints`.
  - A failed credit is logged and never returned. The inner store's values are returned
    unchanged.
  - The request's life test (`GetLifeState == 1`, else `0x4c07`) uses the founder check's
    stand-in, HP above 0 (the decorator takes the character store for it). A dead earner's
    batch is dropped and the count zeroed, as in the engine.
  - `FlushPending(characterID)` is the logout flush (below): any count above zero goes to the
    guild through the same gates, and the character's accumulator is removed from the map, so
    the map holds only characters who have earned since they last left the world.
    `FlushAllPending` runs it for every character. `GuildPointsDisconnectHandler(hub, gp)` runs
    `FlushPending` for a disconnecting session's character.
  - `AddSkillPoints` passes straight through, so GM `/sp`, learn refunds and the
    no-level-table kill fallback credit nothing. None of them is the conversion.
- **`cmd/server`.** `gpSkills := session.NewGuildPointSkills(skills, guilds, chars)` goes to
  `CombatHandlerWithDrops` and `UseSkillHandlerWithDrops`. Those handlers, and the keep-up swing
  `combatDeps` built inside them, are the only callers of `AddSkillExp` (`combat.go`, the kill
  block). `GuildPointsDisconnectHandler` joins the `OnDisconnect` chain after the duel and trade
  handlers and before `worldDisconnect`, since it finds the character in the world hub. The
  gateway does not run `OnDisconnect` for sessions still open when it stops, so `main` calls
  `FlushAllPending` once `ListenAndServe` returns, with a 30 s bound of srrevamp's own.
- **Wire: a deviation from the plan, which had appended a trailer to `GuildResult`.** That
  would change an existing packet layout. Instead there is a new placeholder pair in
  `session/guild.go`:
  - `OpGuildPoints` (`0x0098`) is a name-only request.
  - `OpGuildPointsResult` (`0x0099`) carries the error string, then guild id `s64`,
    `GatheredSP` `s64`, a `u16` count, and per member a name plus `GPDonation` `s64`.
  - Before claiming the pair, every `Op* uint16` in `server/internal` and every `OP_*` in
    `client/scripts` was listed. `0x0098`/`0x0099` were unused, and `0x00a0` is the next taken
    value. A character in no guild gets the error "not in a guild".
- **Client**
  - `GuildNet.encode_points` / `decode_points_result`, with explicit `int` types.
  - `NetClient.guild_points` and the `guild_points_result` signal.
  - `World3D` asks for points after every successful guild reply for a guild, alongside round
    521's `_guild_id` / `_guild_master` rather than duplicating them. It keeps the roster in
    `_guild_roster` and shows `"… N GP"` on the status line and `"Name [Role] N GP"` in the
    list. A points reply for another guild, or a refusal, changes nothing. Leaving, or changing
    guild, clears the numbers shown.
- **Comment only in `combat.go`.** A note says guild points inherit the disclosed M = 1 for
  kill skill experience.

**Not modelled, and said so where the code is.**

- The level test cannot fail, since srrevamp's guilds have no level.
- There is no `0x38F5` push. The client asks for the points after each successful guild reply
  (world entry, create or join, opening the guild HUD panel), so the numbers shown are as of
  the last reply, **not live** while members earn.
- The shutdown flush is srrevamp's own handling (the engine's clean-shutdown path is unread).
  Pending points are lost only if the process dies without stopping cleanly, or the credit
  fails (logged). *Corrected in round 527:* not "only". On a clean stop, points booked after
  `FlushAllPending` has passed a character are lost at exit too (a count below ten per
  character, or a batch whose credit is still running when `main` returns), and so are the
  points of a conversion or flush whose `GuildIDOf` fails with a database error.

**Review follow-up: the logout flush** (folded into this round's commit). The first version
treated `GainExpAndLevel` as the only user of `pc+0x2184` and recorded "whether the engine
persists `pc+0x2184` is unknown". The dump settles it, re-read for this fix:

- `srv.asm` addresses `+0x2184` at three sites only (a grep for `0x2184]`, every base
  register): `4dea77` in `CGObjPC::vslot_000`, which zeroes it with `ebx` (cleared by `4de9cb
  xor ebx,ebx`, with no write to `ebx` between; the one call there, `4de9e3 call edx`, must
  preserve it under the MSVC convention); `4def96`-`4defc2` in
  `FUN_004def90`; and `4e5625`-`4e5647` in `GainExpAndLevel`.
- `FUN_004def90`: `4def96 cmp [esi+0x2184],ebp; jle` (ebp = 0 from `4def94 xor ebp,ebp`),
  `4def9f cmp [esi+0x1cbc],ebp; je`, `4defb4 push [esi+0x2184]`, `4defbd call 0x5c62e0`,
  `4defc2 mov [esi+0x2184],ebp`. So `if (0 < pc[0x861] && pc[0x72f] != 0) {
  RequestAddGuildPoints(pc[0x861]); pc[0x861] = 0; }`, with no threshold.
- Its one caller is `4df214` in `FUN_004df050`, which has 61 call sites, among them
  `transaction::transaction__OnTimeout` (`0x46c780`, right after "DISCONNECT FROM
  transaction::OnTimeout()"), `CGObjPC::StorageOperation` (`0x50f5c0`, after "posting
  AsyncQuery failed. will be disconnected!!!") and `CMainProcess::FUN_00417a80`, which runs it
  for every PC and is called by `CMainProcess::FUN_00416f80` when the ShardManager link drops
  ("all user connections will be lost (but, data saved)"). Right after the flush,
  `FUN_004df050` calls vtable `+0x1f0` (`IGObj::SetLifeState`) with 3, `GONE`.
- The flush goes through `RequestAddGuildPoints`, so its life test applies. `FUN_004df050`'s
  branch for a PC in state 2 (DEAD) computes the return point and writes the saved position
  (`CGObjPC::FUN_004e08a0`, `FUN_004f9950`/`9920`/`9850`) with no `SetLifeState` among them, so a
  PC dead at logout gets `0x4c07` and loses its count.

So nothing is persisted: the count lives as long as the PC is in the world, and one to nine
pending points reach the guild when it leaves. `guildpoints.go`, `guild.go`, `guild.md`,
`TODO.md` and this entry said otherwise and are corrected, and the flush is built. Three
cheaper review points went in with it: `GuildIDOf` replaces the roster load on every
point-yielding conversion; the life test is applied with the founder check's stand-in rather
than skipped; and the `SQLStore.AddPoints` comment no longer claims its lock order cannot
deadlock with `Leave`.

  `FlushAllPending` as soon as `ListenAndServe` returns. The gateway was read
  (`internal/gateway/gateway.go`):
  - `ListenAndServe` closes the listener on cancel and returns. It keeps no record of its
    `serveConn` goroutines and does not wait for them.
  - `serveConn` checks `ctx` only at the top of its loop. One blocked in `proto.Read` hands its
    next packet to the handler, with the cancelled context, before it notices.
  - The keep-up swings run on their own timers with `context.Background()`
    (`session/keepup.go`, `armKeepUp`).

  So a kill during or after the flush books on an accumulator the flush has already passed, and
  `main` returns without sending it. That is up to nine points per character on a clean stop,
  plus any batch whose credit is still running at exit. A drain would need the gateway to track,
  close and wait for its connections, and the keep-up loops to stop first. That changes the
  gateway's lifecycle, which this item may not do, so the window is disclosed instead:

  bullet, `TODO.md`'s guild item, and an inline correction to round 525's "lost only if" line.

  disclosed in their comments and in `guild.md`. Behaviour is unchanged.

## Guild master levels the guild up: gold + GP cost from the current level, the engine's refusal order, and the member cap by level (FUN_005c63d0 / CheckLevelUpCost 0x5c6240) (round 528)

**What was open.** `guild.MaxLevel`, `guild.LevelUpCost` and `guild.MaxMembersFor` held the
recovered level rules, and nothing called the last two (both were in the orphan baseline).
srrevamp's guilds had no level, so every guild had the level-1 cap of 15 and the guild points
credited since round 525 had nothing to buy. `SYSTEMS.md`'s Guild row and `TODO.md`'s "Guild
points and levels" item both listed this as the next step.

**Grounding, re-read this round** (`/var/tmp/decomp_server`, `/var/tmp/srv.asm`, `objdump` on
`SR_GameServer.exe`; `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm` and `/opt/sro-files/client/sro_client.exe` for the
client).

- **`CGuild::HandleLevelUp` (`0x005c63d0`), in asm.** `5c63e3`-`5c63ed` vtable `+0xf8`, `cmp
  al,0x1`, else `0x4c07`. `5c63fa` `[esi+0x1cbc]`, else `0x4c0d`. `5c641b call 0x5d0f50`
  (`CGuild::IsGuildMaster`), else `0x4c1e`. `5c642f call 0x5d0e80` (`GetLevel`), `5c6434 cmp
  al,0x5; jb`, else `0x4c21`. `5c6445`-`5c644c` pushes the saved level byte to `0x5c6240`. If
  that returns 1, `5c645d`-`5c6466` call `0x5c80a0` with `(pc, 9, 0)`.
- **`CGuild::CheckLevelUpCost` (`0x005c6240`).** A switch on levels 1 to 4 (anything else
  asserts and returns 1). It compares the 64-bit gold at `+0x78/+0x7c` with `&DAT_00ade910 +
  level*8`, else `0x4c31`. It compares `guild+0x3c` (a signed dword) with `&DAT_00ade8ec +
  level*4`, else `0x4c32`.
- **The tables, by `objdump -s`.** `.rdata 0xade8dc`: 15, 20, 25, 35, 50. `0xade8f0`: 5400,
  50400, 135000, 378000. `0xade918`: 3,000,000, 9,000,000, 15,000,000, 21,000,000 as 64-bit
  values with a zero high dword. `0xade910`/`0xade914` hold 3 and 6, the index-0 slot the switch
  never reads.
- **The job's reply, `trs_sm_guildjob::FUN_005c8fd0`** (case 9 of `FUN_005c8990`). It reads
  `CGuild::GetLevel()`, asserts it is 2 to 5, and calls vtable `+0x16c` (`OffsetGold`) with the
  negated 64-bit entry at `0xade918 + (level - 2)*8`, which is the gold for `level - 1`. Then
  `BackupData(0x80, 0)` and `0xb0fa`. So the gold is spent at the checked amount, after the level
  has already changed.
- **The guild points, and why the amount is not readable here.**
  `CGuildMamager__SendOlappedGuildJobReqToSM`'s case 9 stores only the character's id and
  `FUN_004ea580()`, with no amount. `FUN_005c8fd0` writes no guild field. The guild record is
  written by the ShardManager's update: `CMainProcess::FUN_005c9bd0` cases 9/10 go to
  `FUN_005ca4b0`, then `FUN_005c3c90` (a mask byte), then `FUN_005cfc20`. That copies the fields
  the mask names: 1 id `+0x18`, 4 `Lvl` `+0x38`, 8 `GatheredSP` `+0x3c`, `0x20` `+0x94`, `0x40`
  `+0x98` (2 and `0x10` read strings). The mask comes from the ShardManager, which is not in
  the binary.
- **The sibling that tips the decision.** `FUN_005c7900` (mercenary attribute `guild+0x98`,
  refusing `0x4c32` on `guild+0x3c`) sends job `0x2b`. Dispatcher case `0x2b` is `FUN_005cc590`
  (reads guild id, byte, dword), then `FUN_005c5600`, which writes `+0x98` (dirty `0x100`) and
  `+0x3c` (dirty 8).

**The GP decision: spend the checked cost, disclosed.** The plan audit's claim holds: the
guild-point deduction is not in `SR_GameServer.exe`. The evidence leans to a spend, for two
reasons. The ShardManager does send a new `GatheredSP` after the other points-gated guild
purchase. And the gold, checked beside it against the same level's entry, is spent at exactly
the checked amount. So `guild.CheckLevelUp` returns the table's guild points as `gpCost`, and the
stores take it off `GatheredSP`. This is disclosed in `guild.go`, in `guild.md` ("What a level-up
spends (round 528)", and a new "What is not recovered" bullet) and in `SYSTEMS.md` / `TODO.md`.

**The founding level.** The founding write is the ShardManager's.
`trs_sm_guildjob::FUN_005c8bf0` looks the guild up and sets no level. So `guild.FoundingLevel` =
1 is stated as the floor the engine's tables agree on: `CGuild::IsFull` treats 0 as 1 after an
assert, `CheckLevelUpCost` has cases 1 to 4, and `FUN_005c8fd0` asserts a levelled guild is at
least 2. It is not claimed as a read value.

**The client's category, read rather than assumed.** `Guild_OnLevelUpResult` (`0x881bd0`,
registered for `0xb0fa`) reads the code on result 2 and pushes `0x10` (`0x881c53`) into
`FUN_00778190`, which tail-jumps to the dispatcher (`0x7781a5`). The dispatcher reads the
category at `0x7b8b90`. Category `0x10` (`0x7bb378` entry `0x10` = `0x7ba32b`, code -
`0x4c06`, index bytes `0x7bbc80`, targets `0x7bbb78`) gives `0x4c07` `0x7ba359` `push
0xdc1710`, `0x4c1e` `0x7ba3db` `push 0xdc5388`, `0x4c21` `0x7ba3e5` `push 0xdc1378`, `0x4c31`
`0x7ba449` `push 0xdc1018` and `0x4c32` `0x7ba453` `push 0xdc0fc0`. Each pushed UTF-16 string
was decoded, and each matches `error_codes.md`'s row. `0x4c0d`'s index byte is `0x41`, the
default (`0x7b913a`): no message.

**Change.**

- **`guild`**
  - `Guild.Level` (`_GUILD.Lvl`, `+0x38`) and `FoundingLevel`.
  - `CheckLevelUp(alive, inGuild, master, level, gold, gatheredSP)` is the ladder in the
    engine's order, and returns the gold and guild-point cost of the CURRENT level. New sentinel
    errors are `ErrLevelUpDead`, `ErrNotGuildMaster`, `ErrLevelUpFull`, `ErrLevelUpGoldDeficit`
    and `ErrLevelUpGPDeficit`; `ErrNotInGuild` serves for `0x4c0d`. `LevelUpCode(err)` maps each
    to its engine code, and anything else to 0.
  - New `Store.LevelUp(ctx, characterID, alive, gold, pay)`: the ladder, then `pay(goldCost)`,
    then `GatheredSP -= gpCost` and `Level++`, atomically. `MemStore` does this under its lock.
    `SQLStore` does it in one transaction with `FOR UPDATE OF g` on the guild row. It reads the
    result back inside the transaction (`getGuild` now takes a `querier`, the `*sql.DB` or the
    `*sql.Tx`), so a failure after the commit cannot be reported as a failed level-up. Members'
    `GPDonation` is untouched.
  - The `lvl INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` column is added with `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`.
    `Create` writes `FoundingLevel` and `Get` reads `lvl`.
  - Both stores' `Join` refuse at `MaxMembersFor(Level)`, no longer `MaxMembers`. `MaxMembers`
    stays as a new guild's cap.
- **`session`**
  - New placeholder pair `OpGuildLevel` (`0x009A`) and `OpGuildLevelResult` (`0x009B`). Every
    `Op* uint16` in `server/internal` and every `OP_*`/`0x9a`/`0x9b` in `client/scripts` was
    grepped first. `0x0099` is the last guild opcode and `0x00A0` the next taken one. No existing
    layout changed.
  - The request is a name and a 0/1 byte (1 = level up, 0 = report only).
  - The result is the error string and a `u16` engine code, then on success the guild id,
    `Level` u8, `LevelledUp` u8, `MaxMembers` u16, and `NextGold` and `NextGuildPoints` s64
    (0 at level 5).
  - `handleGuildLevel`: a report is `GetByCharacter`. A level-up is `LevelUp` with alive = HP > 0
    (the founder check's stand-in) and a `pay` that calls `DeductGold`.
    `ErrInsufficientGold` from `DeductGold` becomes `ErrLevelUpGoldDeficit`, code `0x4c31`. **Our
    own handling:** if `LevelUp` fails after the gold was taken, the handler refunds it with
    `AddGold` and logs a refund that fails. That is the counterpart of round 487's founding
    rollback.
  - `guildErrorMessage` gains our wording for the five refusals, and for `ErrGuildFull` ("the
    guild is full"), which used to read "operation failed".
- **Comments only.** `guildpoints.go`: the request's level test cannot fail because levels stop
  at 5 (it used to say "guilds have no level"). `guild.go`'s notes on `MaxMembersByLevel`,
  `MaxMembers`, `MaxMembersFor`, `ErrGuildFull`, the permissions scope, and the package comment.
- **Client**
  - `GuildNet.OP_LEVEL`/`OP_LEVEL_RESULT`, `encode_level`, `LevelResult` and
    `decode_level_result`. `NetClient.guild_level(name, level_up)` and the `guild_level_result`
    signal.
  - `ErrorText` gains the five category-`0x10` rows and `guild_level_up_line(code, table,
    fallback)`. The fallback is the server's words, which stand for `0x4c0d`, code 0 and a missing
    key.
  - `World3D` asks for the level with the points after each successful guild reply. It shows
    "level N, M/cap members" on the Guild tab status line.
  - The master sees a new "Level Up Guild (gold, GP)" button, our own dev control, disabled at
    level 5 (`World3D.tscn` gains the hidden `LevelUpButton` node).
  - A refusal carrying a code goes to the tab and to chat through `ErrorText`. A level-up re-reads
    the purse (`_request_world_stats`) and the points.
- **Orphan baseline.** `LevelUpCost` and `MaxMembersFor` now have callers
  (`CheckLevelUp`/`guildLevelResult`, and `Join`/`guildLevelResult`), so both lines leave
  `internal/systems/orphans_test.go`.

**Not modelled, and said so where the code is.** The master's guild NPC line (item `0x17`,
`UIIT_MSG_GUILD_LEVEL_UP`) still shows the "Guild" placeholder. There is no `0x38F5` push of the
new level, so the other members see it on their next guild reply. The guild-point spend is the
stand-in above.

**Docs.**
