## The player-info block, minimap, target window and hotbar body stop clicks reaching the world; a camera orbit keeps orbiting over HUD (round 529)

**What was open.** Round 522's re-review measured four HUD surfaces passing clicks to the world:
the player-info block, the minimap's map, the target window, and the hotbar's body away from its
slots and buttons. The press and the release both reached `World3D._unhandled_input`, where a left
click counts as a click on the world: it walks the character, and `take_focus_back` takes the
keyboard from a focused text line. The same re-review measured a side effect of STOP: a right-drag
orbit that began on the world stopped turning while the cursor was over a STOP control (the chat).
`TODO.md` recorded both, suggesting the orbit be read in `World3D._input`.

**Grounding, re-read this round.**
- **Round 522's measurements** (its RE_COMPLETION entry, "Which clicks reach `_unhandled_input`").
  `World3D.tscn`'s `UI/Control`, the HUD's parent, is `mouse_filter = 2` (IGNORE), so no ancestor
  stops a click.
- **Godot 4.2.2-stable's `scene/main/viewport.cpp`**, read at the tag.
  - `Viewport::push_input` runs `_input`, then `_gui_input_event`, then `_unhandled_input`, and
    stops at the first that marks the event handled.
  - In `_gui_input_event`, a press with no button already held on a control sets
    `gui.mouse_focus = gui_find_control(mpos)`, and returns at once when that is null. The press is marked handled only when `_gui_call_input` reports it
    stopped. That happens at a STOP control on the chain; a PASS control's event bubbles on
    through IGNORE ancestors.
  - A motion goes to `gui.mouse_focus`, or, when that is empty, to `gui_find_control(mpos)` while
    `gui.mouse_in_viewport`. So a right press on no control leaves the drag's motion to whatever
    control the cursor crosses.
  - A release goes to `gui.mouse_focus` when there is one, and otherwise returns unhandled.
  - `_gui_find_control_at_pos` tests the children first, last to first. It returns the node itself
    only when its filter is not IGNORE and the point is inside its own rect. A child outside its
    parent's rect is still tested on its own filter.
- **The real layouts**, dumped on the render box with `tools/dump_layout.gd` from
  `/opt/sro-files/client/Media.pk2` (read, nothing committed).
  - `ifplayerminiinfo.txt`'s `GDR_PMI_PICTURE` is a `CIFStaticWithPictureClip` with no art.
    `UiBuilder` builds it generic, which is PASS.
  - `ifunderbar.txt`'s one generic control is `GDR_QS_INIDCTION` (`CIFWnd`, 285,8 40x40), inside
    the 800x52 body. Everything outside the body is a `CIFStatic` with art (`GDR_DECORATE_1..3`,
    built IGNORE) or a `CIFButton` (menu, community, option; STOP by default).
  - `ifminimap.txt` and the target window's three layouts have no PASS control. Each has only
    buttons, statics and gauges.

**Change.**
- `HudPlayerInfo`, `HudMinimap`, `HudTarget` and `HudUnderbar` set their ROOT to
  `MOUSE_FILTER_STOP`, as `HudWindow` and `HudChat` are. HudWindow's comment has the reasoning:
  children are tested first, so buttons and slots keep their clicks. Each root's rect is exactly
  its drawn body:
  - the player block's `Frame` and the minimap's `MinimapFrame` are placed at 0,0 with the root's
    size;
  - `HudTarget._select` sizes the root to the showing piece;
  - the hotbar's root is the 800x52 rect `BarBackground` is drawn in.
  A PASS child (the portrait, `GDR_QS_INIDCTION`) bubbles to the root and stops there.
- **Where this departs from the plan.** The plan put STOP on the hotbar's `BarBackground` rather
  than the root, to keep the transparent space above the bar clear. The root's rect is that same
  body, and Godot returns a control only inside its own rect, so the root leaves the space above
  the bar just as clear. The root also catches `GDR_QS_INIDCTION`'s bubbled click, which a
  `BarBackground` sibling would not. And `BarBackground` exists only with an archive.
- The hotbar's body fires the middle-button quickslot itself (`HudUnderbar._on_body_gui_input`).
  That binding worked over the body before, through `World3D._unhandled_input`, and the slots
  already fire it themselves (round 522). It is connected once, because World3D runs the bar's
  `setup()` twice (below).
- **The orbit.** `World3D._input` turns the camera when the new static
  `World3D.orbit_motion_applies(event, _camera_orbiting, _camera_view)` says so. The orbit branch
  is gone from `_unhandled_input`, so over the world the motion is applied once, not twice. The
  event is not marked handled, so the control under the cursor still sees it.
  `orbit_motion_applies` also requires the right button in the motion's own `button_mask`. A
  right release can miss `_unhandled_input`: when a left press on a STOP control holds the mouse
  focus, the release goes to that control (measured below). `_camera_orbiting` then stays set with
  no button down, and without the mask check plain motion would turn the camera everywhere.
- The left drag is unchanged. It still sets `_left_dragging` / `_left_steering` in
  `_unhandled_input`. One edge moved: with both buttons held, the one motion that crosses the
  left-drag threshold now also turns the camera. Before, the old `elif` chain skipped the orbit
  for that event.

**Tests.** `npc_service_reader_test.gd` check (o), in the live tree after check (n). It sends real
events through `root.push_input`, with a recorder node whose `_input` and `_unhandled_input`
stand in for World3D's. So "reaches the world" is measured, not read off a filter value. Headless,
the viewport's mouse-enter is sent by hand (`NOTIFICATION_VP_MOUSE_ENTER`). Without it no motion
finds a control, and the pane checks below would fail.
- The probe: a click on no control reaches `_unhandled_input`.
- Each surface, built without an archive, is STOP. A click on it does not reach the world: the
  player block, the minimap's aperture, and the shown target window. A hidden target window
  catches nothing.
- The hotbar, from a synthetic `ifunderbar`-shaped layout (never real data). The body is STOP, and
  a click on it, or on a PASS `CIFWnd` inside it, does not reach the world. A slot and the menu
  button above the bar still take their clicks. The empty space above the bar and the decoration
  beside it still pass a click to the world. A middle press on the body, or on a slot, fires the
  first quickslot once.
- The routing the orbit rests on, over a plain STOP control:
  - over the world, a right drag's motion reaches both handlers;
  - over the STOP control, `_input` sees it and `_unhandled_input` does not;
  - the right release still reaches `_unhandled_input`;
  - with a left press holding the control's focus, it does not.
- `World3D.orbit_motion_applies` is true while orbiting over a control, and false:
  - when not orbiting;
  - with no right button in the mask;
  - in the third-person view;
  - for a button event.
- `World3D._input`, called directly with a stand-in `SpringArm3D`, turns the yaw by `relative.x *
  CAMERA_ORBIT_SENSITIVITY`. `_unhandled_input` then leaves it alone. A left drag still sets
  `_left_steering` and turns nothing.
- **NEGATIVE, measured.** With the five production scripts stashed and shipped, the suite reported
  18 FAILURES, exactly the round's checks: each STOP filter, each click-through, the body's middle
  press, `orbit_motion_applies` and its cases, and the two handler checks. The routing
  measurements passed either way. Restored and shipped: ALL PASS.
- Render box: `client/tools/remote_godot.sh tests` ran 80 suites, 0 failing.
  `client/tools/remote_godot.sh check` checked 246 scripts and 5 scenes: ALL LOAD.
  `cd server && go build ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...`: green.

**Not driven:** a real click or drag in a running client, and the four surfaces built from
Media.pk2. The claim that each root's rect equals its artwork's rect is read from the code, not
measured on a built HUD. A drawn surface's transparent corners inside that rect now take the
click, as a window's do.

**Found, not fixed (read from the code, not measured).** `World3D._try_initialize_pk2_ui` adds
`HudMinimap` and `HudUnderbar` to the tree, and each one's `_ready` runs `setup()` because it has
no children yet. Then World3D calls `setup()` again, which builds a second copy on top of the first.
Filed in `TODO.md`.

## Record: guild-store goods are refused by their guild-point price, not by the store (CheckCurrencyRequirement bit 8: 0x18c4, 0x18c5) (round 530)

**The question.** Round 524 hid a guild NPC's "Buy" line from a guildless player, which is the
client's own rule (`FUN_00700440`). Its implementer noted that srrevamp's server shop handler does
not check the guild, so a client that skips the menu could still buy. Does the real server refuse
that buyer, and with what code? This is a record round. **No code changed**, for the reasons
below. The full reading, with every address, is in `docs/protocol/character_state.md`, "What the
server checks at a guild store (round 530)".

**What the engine does** (read-only on the render box: `/var/tmp/srv.asm`, `/var/tmp/decomp_server`,
`objdump -s` on `SR_GameServer.exe`).

- **Opening the store has no guild test.** `GObjPC_HandleShopMsg_046`'s id-1 arm looks the store
  up (code 3 when there is none) and sends it. Its only codename tests are
  `NPC_SD_MERCHANT_CHANGER` and `NPC_SD_THIEF_AGENT_CHANGER`, which refuse `0x1c26` on a
  byte read through `pc+0x1fb4`. No guild NPC is tested.
- **The buy is `CGObjPC::StorageOperation` op 8** (`FUN_005266a0`, which `FUN_0050ce80` stores at
  `0xcd3b98`). Its own refusals are `0x185f`, 2, `0x1829`, the range/interaction refusals of
  `0x4e72a0`, 3 (the NPC does not offer id 1) and 5 (the store index). None of them reads the
  guild. It then walks the store's access permissions (`0x617a30`) and buys (`0x618fe0`).
- **Access permissions can test the guild, but no data row does.** The list at `+0xb8` of the
  store's reference record holds `_RefAccessPermissionOfShop` rows (`RefShop_InsertFamilyRow`
  case 2, `0x6b4895`/`0x6b48a3`). Each row goes by its `+4` key to one of three handlers. RTTI
  names them, through each vtable's `[-1]` locator:
  - key 0: `SCNothing`, vtable `0xb02a50`;
  - `0x55534c56`, `USLV`: `SCUserLevelLimit`, vtable `0xb02a5c`;
  - `0x47444c56`, `GDLV`: `SCGuildLevelLimit`, vtable `0xb02a68`.

  The keys are registered at `0x61bbaa`-`0x61bbbb`. `SCGuildLevelLimit`'s check (`0x61bb00`)
  answers 2 when `pc+0x1cbc` (the guild) is 0, and otherwise tests `CGuild::GetLevel` against the
  row's range. But `refaccesspermissionofshop.txt` has no rows in any copy here:
  - the server pack's export (`SMC_Independent/SR_GameRefData`) is 2 bytes, `ff fe`, the byte-order
    mark alone;
  - its zlib patch copy inflates to the same two bytes;
  - the client's `Media.pk2` copy prints no row with `dump_text_table.gd`.

  The shard database's `_RefAccessPermissionOfShop` itself was not read.
- **The refusal that applies is the goods' guild-point price.** The buy reaches
  `GObjPC::CheckCurrencyRequirement` (`0x619026` -> `0x617a50`, `0x617e82` -> `0x617950`,
  `0x617997`). After the gold test (bit 1, `0x180f`), the coins, honour points and silk, it tests
  bit 8 (`0x61787d`):
  - no guild (`0x617886` `[esi+0x1cbc]`): `0x18c4` `UIIT_MSG_GUILD_STORE_BUY_LIMIT`;
  - not the master (`0x61789e` `call 0x5d0f50`, `CGuild::IsGuildMaster`): `0x18c4`;
  - the guild's GatheredSP (`[[pc+0x1cbc]+0x4]+0x3c`, `0x6178a7`-`0x6178b0`) below the price's
    `+0x20`: `0x18c5` `UIIT_MSG_GUILD_LACK_GP`.
- **Every guild-store good carries bit 8.** The five `STORE_*_GUILD` stores sell 25 goods, five
  each: the guild and union crest items on tab 1 and `PACKAGE_ITEM_ETC_GUILD_RECALL` on tab 3. The
  two SD guild groups map to `STORE_KT_GUILD`. In `refpricepolicyofitem.txt` each of the five
  packages has a PaymentDevice 1 row and a PaymentDevice 8 row. The client's copy and the server
  pack's export agree.

So a guildless player may open a guild store, and every buy there is refused with `0x18c4` once the
gold test passes. So is a member who is not the master. The master is refused `0x18c5` while the
guild is short of points.

**Why no code.** The plan's code branch keyed the refusal on the store group (`GROUP_STORE_*_GUILD`)
or on the NPC (`GUILD_PATTERNS`). Its test expected a guildless buyer refused and a member served.
The engine keys the refusal on the goods' price policy, and it refuses a plain member too, so that
test would have pinned a rule the engine does not have. srrevamp imports no price policy
(`refdata.Item` has no payment device). `OpShopBuy` names only the item, so a store-keyed test
would also need a new layout, and that is out of scope. srrevamp today charges `shop.Price`, which
is itemdata column 26: 1,000,000 gold for `ITEM_ETC_GUILD_CREST_USER`, the device-1 amount. It
checks no guild and spends no points. The follow-up is filed in `TODO.md`, `guild.md` and `SYSTEMS.md`'s Shops
row: import each good's device-8 amount; after the gold test, refuse `0x18c4` and `0x18c5` in the
engine's order; spend the points. Where the engine spends them was not followed. `0x618930`'s
bit-8 arm copies the amount into the purchase record at `+0xa8`.

**Names filed.** `recovered_names.tsv` gains the five condition-handler methods:
`SCNothing::Check` (`0x61ba30`), `SCUserLevelLimit::IsValid`/`Check` (`0x61ba40`,
`0x61ba70`) and `SCGuildLevelLimit::IsValid`/`Check` (`0x61bad0`, `0x61bb00`). The RTTI above
grounds only the class half of each name. `Check` and `IsValid` are readings of what each vtable
slot's body does, filed with origin `reading`, not names the binary gives (corrected in round 531).

**Probes and their failure modes.** A range grep of `srv.asm` for `0x1cbc` finds no guild read in
the open handler, `StorageOperation`, the op-8 entry, the purchase, or `0x617a50`/`0x617950`. The
same grep finds the three known reads (`0x617886`, `0x6178a7`, `0x61bb28`), so the probe can see
one. It cannot see a callee that reads the guild itself, so the callees on the path were read by
hand. The empty-table reading cannot tell a failed export from an empty table. The client copy
agrees, but it is another export of the same data.

**Tests.** No code and no new test, so there is no negative case to prove. After the doc edits,
`cd server && go build ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green. The doc-driven
`internal/systems` probes read the edited `SYSTEMS.md`, `recovered_names.tsv` and
`character_state.md` at run time. No client file changed, so the client suites were not run. The
render box was used read-only, except for one `remote_godot.sh sync` of the unchanged tree and
three `dump_text_table.gd` runs (the table, a known table, and a misspelt name).

## Batch-12 review follow-ups (rounds 527-530): the Hide UI button, middle-click over HUD, the level-up refund on shutdown, record wording (round 531)

The reviewers' notes on rounds 527-530. Each claim was re-checked before it was written: the client
against Godot 4.2.2's viewport behaviour, measured on the render box, and the archive's
`ifminimap.txt`; the server against `/var/tmp/srv.asm` and `/var/tmp/decomp_server`, read-only.
Three changes a player can notice, one server fix that acts only when a stop interrupts a guild
write, and wording.

**Round 529: two routes the STOP surfaces broke.**

- **(a) The developer Hide UI button could not be clicked.** `World3D.tscn` had `UI/HideUIButton`
  (offsets -84..-8 x 8..40 from the top right) as an EARLIER sibling of `UI/Control`, and the
  minimap (-150..-14 x 10..185, `World3D._try_initialize_pk2_ui`) is a child of `UI/Control`.
  Godot 4.2 hit-tests a later sibling first. Once round 529 made the minimap STOP, the minimap
  took every click on the part of the button it covered: all but a 6-pixel strip down its right
  side and a 2-pixel strip along its top. Measured: at BASE, a click at the button's centre
  pressed nothing (`hud_click_routing_test.gd`, below).
  **Change.** The button is now `UI/Control`'s LATER sibling, the last child of `UI`, so nothing
  in `UI/Control` can cover it. It also moved left of the minimap, to -234..-158 x 8..40. Moving
  it after `UI/Control` alone would have drawn it over the minimap's area name
  (`GDR_MINIMAP_TEXT_AREANAME` at 12,9 104x12, dumped this round from the render box's
  `Media.pk2` with `tools/dump_layout.gd --file=ifminimap`; nothing committed). The position is our
  own, since the button has no authored equivalent. The minimap's STOP body is unchanged. Its
  placement moved, unchanged, into the static `World3D.place_minimap`, so the suite places a
  minimap exactly where the world does. The button shows only with the developer tools
  (`_set_dev_ui_visible(false)` runs when the archive HUD is built; Ctrl+F1).
- **(b) A middle press over the minimap, the player-info block or the target window fired no
  quickslot.** Their STOP roots consumed it before `World3D._unhandled_input`, which fires the
  page's first quickslot. Round 529 gave only the hotbar's body its own handler. **Change.** One
  path: `HudUnderbar.relay_middle_button(surface)` connects a surface's `gui_input` to the handler
  the hotbar's body already used (`_on_body_gui_input`, whose `setup()` connection now goes
  through the relay too). It connects each surface once, however often it is called.
  `World3D._relay_middle_button_to_hotbar` hands it the three surfaces once they all exist, right
  after `_hide_debug_ui_replaced_by_hud` (which builds the target window). A press on a STOP child
  of a surface (the minimap's zoom and map buttons, the target's close button) is consumed by that
  child and fires nothing, as before round 529.

**Round 528: the level-up.**

- **(c) The refund on a stop.** `session.handleGuildLevel` refunded with `chars.AddGold(ctx, ...)`
  on the handler's `ctx`. That is the gateway's context (`gateway.Server.serveConn` hands its own
  `ctx` to the handler), and a server stop cancels it. A stop between the deduction and the guild's
  `UPDATE` fails the `UPDATE` with `context.Canceled`, and a refund on the same `ctx` failed too,
  so the gold was lost. The refund now runs on `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (Go 1.21+; `go.mod`
  says 1.25). Round 487's founding rollback had the same shape: a `DeductGold` failed by the stop,
  then `guilds.Leave(ctx, ...)` on the same `ctx`. It left the guild founded for free, and it gets
  the same fix. Not closed: `main` does not wait for connection goroutines (round 527), so a
  process that exits before the refund returns still loses it. A refund that fails is logged, as
  before. On the server this acts only when a stop lands inside one of those two writes.
- **(d) A commit error is ambiguous.** `SQLStore.LevelUp`'s comment said a failed commit means the
  level was not kept. A connection that drops after Postgres committed reports an error too, and
  then the level WAS kept, so the refund pays back a level the guild kept. The comment, the
  handler's comment and `guild.md` now say so. A `ctx` cancelled before the commit is not
  ambiguous: `database/sql`'s `Tx.Commit` checks the context first and, once it is done, returns
  the context's error (or `ErrTxDone`) at once without sending COMMIT; the rollback runs
  separately, in the `awaitDone` goroutine the transaction started (`DB.beginDC`), which may
  not have run yet when `Commit` returns (read in the Go 1.25 source; reworded in round 534,
  which found the earlier wording claimed the rollback had already happened).
- **(e) Mask values, not bits.** `FUN_005cfc20` tests `& 1`, `& 2`, `& 4`, `& 8`, `& 0x10`,
  `& 0x20`, `& 0x40` (`getfn.sh 005cfc20`). "bit 4 Lvl, bit 8 GatheredSP" named mask values as bit
  indices. Now fixed in `guild.go`'s level-up comment and in `guild.md`'s ShardManager bullet. The
  same misnomer ("dirty bit 8", "dirty bit 4") in `CGuild::AddPoints`'s row and `guild.md`
  (`or [eax+0x8],0x8` at `0x5c4148`, `,0x4` at `0x5c4175`) now reads "flag". Round 528's entry
  already wrote the values bare. Its commit message cannot be changed.
- **(f) `TODO.md`, "Guild points and levels"** was checked before a release. It now says
  v0.1.434, the next tag, which carries rounds 527-531. The points shipped in v0.1.433.
- **(g) The Guild tab after a refusal.** `World3D._on_guild_level_result` replaced the status line
  with the refusal, which hid the guild's summary until the next reply. The refusal now goes after
  the summary (`"<summary> Guild level: <refusal>"`). It stays alone when there is no roster, so
  `error_text_test.gd`'s check is unchanged. The next reply rewrites the line.

**Round 527's reviewer.**

- **(h) The wildcard claim, qualified where it was still bare.** Round 526's Grounding bullet and
  `npc_service_reader_test.gd`'s comment now say the wildcard catches those codenames only when
  read as a substring pattern, the way the server's `strstr` tests match. An anchored
  `NPC_*_MERCHANT` stops at `_CHANGER`.
- **(i) `CGuild::AddPoints` or `CMainProcess::AddPoints`.** The dump names `0x5c4110`
  `CMainProcess::AddPoints` (`getfn.sh 005c4110`). The row keeps `CGuild::AddPoints` and now says
  why:
  - `ApplyRecoveredNames.java` set the row's leaf and kept the owner it found. It keeps any
    existing owner unless a row says `force`.
  - That owner reads as a module attribution. The one caller, `0x5ca585`, is in
    `CMainProcess::HandleGuildPointsChanged`, which is exactly the unanimous-caller case
    `PropagateModules.java` attributes. The applier's comment replaced the plate, so the dump no
    longer shows which pass set it.
  - `CGuild` is the row's reading. EDI is passed as `this` to `FUN_005d0c90` (`0x5c4121` `mov
    ecx,edi`) and to `CGuild::BroadcastToLocalMember` (`0x5c41d7` `mov ecx,edi`, `0x5c41d9` `call
    0x5c4260`). The record it raises is `[EDI+4]`.
  - No `force` was added. The owner is a reading, so the dump stays as it is.
- **(j) `main.go`'s stop-flush comment** said "up to nine per character". It now adds any batch of
  ten or more whose credit is still running when `main` returns, as `FlushAllPending`'s comment
  and `guild.md` already did.

**Round 530's reviewer.**

- **(k) The store-keyed bullet had the logic backwards.** `character_state.md` said keying the
  refusal on the store "would also refuse the guild master". A rule that refuses only a guildless
  buyer at a `STORE_*_GUILD` store would instead SERVE a plain member, whom the engine refuses
  `0x18c4`, and would spend no points. Corrected.
- **(l) PaymentDevice 8 is flag 8, cited.** `RefPricePolicyOfItem_ExtractData` (`0x6a8b80`) reads
  a row's PaymentDevice into `+0x8` and, after skipping PreviousCost (`FUN_006b1a80`), its Cost
  into `+0x14`. That is the column order `refdata_schema.md` records. `ReferenceData::FUN_006a99c0`
  finds the lowest set bit `i` of `+0x8` (`0x6a9a26`-`0x6a9a50`) and calls `0x4b2bd0` with the
  item's price record (`0x6a9a67`). That sets `1 << i` (`0x4b2c2d` `or [ebx],eax`) and stores the
  Cost at `+0x8 + i*8` (`0x4b2c38`/`0x4b2c3c`). So PaymentDevice 8 is flag 8 (`i` = 3) with its
  amount at `+0x20`, which is the `[ebp+0x24]:[ebp+0x20]` the flag-8 arm compares (`0x6178b3`,
  `0x6178bd`). The gold arm reads `+0x8` (`0x6173b2`, `0x6173bc`), so flag 1 is PaymentDevice 1.
  Cited in `character_state.md` and in `guild.md`'s moved paragraph.
- **(m) "It tests gold first"** holds only among the payment flags. `CheckCurrencyRequirement`
  first calls `0x617000` (`0x617383`), which can answer 2 or `0x1893` and then returns at once
  (`0x61738f`). `0x617a50` refuses `0x1806`, `0x1809`, `0x18ab`, `0x1807`, `0x18cf`, 2 and
  `0x1893` before it reaches `0x617950` (read from the dump). Qualified.
- **(n) The RTTI names.** Round 530's "Names filed ... from the RTTI" now says the RTTI grounds only
  the class half. `Check` and `IsValid` are readings of each slot's body, filed as `reading`.
- **(o) `guild.md`.** The round-530 paragraph sat inside "What a level-up spends", just before
  "What the client does with a refusal", which is about the level-up. It moved under its own
  subheading after "What srrevamp does (round 528)": "A third purchase gated on `GatheredSP`: the
  guild store's goods (round 530)".
- **(p) `TODO.md`'s long line** in the NPC-talk item is rewrapped.
- **(q) The follow-up has its own open item** in `TODO.md`, "The guild stores' guild-point
  price". It lists importing the device-8 amounts (`refpricepolicyofitem` through
  `refscrapofpackageitem`), refusing `0x18c4`/`0x18c5` in `shop.Service.Buy` in the engine's
  order, and spending the points. Where the engine spends them was not followed. Before, the
  follow-up was only prose inside a checked item.

**Tests.**

- Server, `internal/session/guild_test.go`:
  - `TestGuildLevelUpRefundSurvivesAStop`: a guild store takes the payment, cancels the gateway's
    context (the stop) and fails its `UPDATE` with the context's error. The character store's gold
    writes honour `ctx`, as `ExecContext` does.
  - `TestGuildCreateRollbackSurvivesAStop`: the same stop right after `Create`, with a `Leave` that
    honours `ctx`.
  - Each carries a probe that the deduction ran on the live context and that the stop really
    cancelled it.
  - NEGATIVE: with `session/guild.go` stashed, both FAIL ("Aria has 0 gold after a level-up the
    stop interrupted"; "Aria is still in a guild after a stop interrupted its founding").
    Restored, both pass.
- Client, the new `client/scripts/ui/hud/hud_click_routing_test.gd`:
  - It instantiates `World3D.tscn` without letting World3D enter the tree, moves its `UI` into the
    live viewport and pushes real events through `Viewport.push_input`. A recorder stands in for
    World3D's `_unhandled_input`.
  - The suite waits one frame and sets the root to 1152x648. A headless root is 64x64, measured.
  - (a) The button comes after `UI/Control`. It is clear of a minimap placed by `place_minimap`,
    it takes a click at its centre, and it still wins that centre over a full-screen STOP control
    added last to `UI/Control`. A hidden button takes nothing.

## The killer's own client plays the monster's death animation: the hold is set when the result arrives, the clip plays at the blow's hit event (round 532)

The player who lands the killing blow now sees the monster play its death animation where it fell,
held on the last frame until the clip ends. Before, it vanished on the list refresh that followed
the result. The killer's target window now closes when the death clip starts; before, nothing
cleared the target on an own kill. Client only. The server is unchanged.

**Grounding, re-read for this round.**

- The killer never receives `OpMonsterDied`. `session/combat.go` `performAttack` sends it only to
  `others`, built with `e.Session.ID() != sess.ID()`. `session/gm.go`'s `/kill` broadcast skips the
  GM the same way.
- `World3D._on_attack_result` skipped the hit reaction on a kill and played nothing instead. It
  ends with a synchronous `NetClient.list_monsters()`. `_sync_monster_bodies` freed every body
  missing from that list unless `_dying_until` held it, and erased `_monster_assembled` with it.
  Only `_on_monster_died` set `_dying_until`.
- Type 4 is the die clip: `BsrReader.AnimationEntry.TYPE_DIE`, and `die` in mangnyang's `default`
  group (`docs/protocol/BSR_FORMAT.md`, the default-group line).
- The hold is the clip's own length, `BanReader` `duration_seconds()`.
- `lands_after` is the swing's `EVENT_HIT`, the delay the handler already used. Its millisecond
  unit is inferred from the numbers (BSR_FORMAT.md, "Events and walk points"). That is unchanged.
- No new constant, no stand-in, and no packet or opcode change.

**Wired.**

- New `client/scripts/world/monster_bodies.gd` (`MonsterBodies`). `should_free(id, live_ids,
  dying_until, now)` is the rule `_sync_monster_bodies` used inline, now called from there.
  `hold_for_kill(dying_until, id, now, lands_after, die_seconds)` sets the hold to
  `now + lands_after + die_seconds`, keeps any later hold, and sets nothing when `die_seconds` is 0.
- `World3D._monster_action_seconds(monster_id, action_type)` does `_play_monster_action`'s lookup
  without playing. It returns 0 wherever `_play_once` would play nothing: no assembled body, no
  skeleton, no clip, or one of a single frame.
- `_on_attack_result`, when the result says the monster died, calls `hold_for_kill` before the
  deferred blow is scheduled and before its trailing list request. The deferred blow then calls
  `_begin_monster_death` instead of skipping.
- `_begin_monster_death` is `_on_monster_died`'s old body:
  - it clears the target if it is this monster, and drops a walk toward it;
  - it plays `TYPE_DIE`, held on the last frame;
  - it resets the hold from the clip's real start, and sets a timer that asks for the list when
    the clip ends;
  - when nothing played but a kill hold is set, it lifts the hold and asks for the list.
  `_on_monster_died` calls it, then asks for the list as before.
- Log lines: `monster N killed by own blow t=T, clip starts in L`, `monster N dies, holding S t=`,
  `monster N body removed t=R`, and `t=` on the existing `attack hit` line.

**Disclosed residuals**, in the code at `hold_for_kill` and in WORLD_ISSUES round 532:

- A keep-up swing sends its result from the keep-up goroutine (`session/keepup.go`
  `autoAttack.loop`). `OpMonsterList` is answered on the session reader, so a list reply can
  overtake a keep-up kill's result and free the body before any hold exists. This is the usual
  kill path: the `OpAttack` handler swings once and then calls `armKeepUp` ("One click is the whole
  fight"). Every kill past the first swing comes from that goroutine. The window is narrow,
  though. A list request has to be handled on the reader between the kill's `ApplyDamage` (which
  deletes the id) and the goroutine's `sess.Send` of the result.
- A GM `/kill` still vanishes on the GM's own screen.

**Other residuals found in review**, recorded in WORLD_ISSUES round 532 and not changed here:

- `_try_attack_monster`, the real click picker, does not skip `_dying_until` ids. A click on the
  killer's corpse can therefore open a target window on a dead monster, and nothing closes it.
  Other players' corpses already behaved this way.
- The hold is kept on `_idle_anim_time`, which the physics step advances, while the end-of-clip
  timer counts process time. If physics lags, the corpse can hold its last frame until an
  unrelated list refresh. The `_on_monster_died` path already had this.
- A late blow from an earlier swing can replace the held die clip. It then holds its own last
  frame, because the die entry has no resume. This predates the round.

**Tests.**

- New `client/scripts/world/monster_bodies_test.gd`, with fixture numbers (a 0.651 s hit event, a
  1.4 s clip):
  - a live id is never freed;
  - an id with no hold is freed;
  - after `hold_for_kill(d, 7, 10.0, 0.651, 1.4)`, the body is kept at 11.9 and freed at 12.052;
  - `die_seconds` 0 sets no hold;
  - a later existing hold is kept;
  - a clip-start hold written over the predicted one is honoured.
- NEGATIVE: a list 5 ms after the kill result (t = 10.005) that omits 7 must not free it. With
  `hold_for_kill` still the no-op of the refactor step, which mirrors the old killer path, the
  suite reported 2 FAILURES, this one among them. Implemented: ALL PASS.
- `client/tools/remote_godot.sh tests`: 82 suites, 0 failing. `remote_godot.sh check`: 249 scripts
  and 5 scenes, ALL LOAD. `cd server && go build ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...`: green,
  re-run after the doc edits.
- Not run: the live `qa_shot.sh` timing (`SRREVAMP_QA_ATTACK_FAST=1 SRREVAMP_QA_ATTACK_NAME=Mangyang
  SRREVAMP_QA_ATTACK_GOTO=1 qa_shot.sh --server <host:port> --attack --frames 900`). This round
  used the render box only through `remote_godot.sh`. The box does have an executable server at
  the script's default `SERVER_BIN` (`/opt/srrevamp-server/srrevamp-server`, 15,276,922 bytes).
  But it is a 2026-09-19 build, older than this tree, so the check should run against a server
  built from this tree, passed as `--server <host:port>`. The assertion it should meet is in
  WORLD_ISSUES round 532.
- Not covered headlessly: the World3D wiring. Nothing headless checks that `hold_for_kill` runs
  before the trailing `list_monsters()`, that `_monster_action_seconds` matches
  `_play_monster_action`, or `_begin_monster_death`'s branch for a clip that did not play. The
  test covers `MonsterBodies` only, so this round's tag waits for the live check.

**Docs.** WORLD_ISSUES round 532 was added. Round 208's "the die animation comes from the list
sync" now carries a dated correction. `docs/SYSTEMS.md` has no row for the client's death
animation, so it is unchanged.

## Client: decode and draw server-driven monster moves (0x007C push and 0x007F motion list) with the engine's mover and both of its clamps, the walk/run clip, a measured facing and throttled height (round 533)

The client can now draw a monster the server moves. Nothing is visible in normal play: no server
sends either message until the monster AI (a later change, behind a default-off flag) is switched
on. With `SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_MOVE`, a monster walks at its speed in its walk clip, faces its path, and
is no longer teleported back by list refreshes. An attack that the approach walk released and the
server refused as too far away now walks again, up to a cap. Client only; the server is unchanged,
and no existing opcode or layout changed.

**Grounding, re-read for this round.**

- The mover is `CGObjMoverByDest::FUN_0048bff0` (SR_GameServer.exe, re-read with `getfn.sh` on the
  RE box). It returns the owner's unit direction (+0x24/+0x2c) times
  min(|speed(+0x174) x dt|, cap). The cap is .rdata `0xb45ea8`, whose bytes `00 00 20 43` were
  read out of the PE: 160.0f.
- Its caller `CGObjMoverByDest::vslot_003` (`0x48c4e0`) computes dest - position with
  `FUN_00430ad0` (`call` at `0x48c5a9`; the body is `(dest + region offset) - pos`, y = 0). It
  compares the two lengths (`fcompp` at `0x48c622`, `test ah,0x41 ; jne 0x48c63f`), and when the
  step is longer it copies dest - position over it (`0x48c62b..0x48c63c`). That is the
  no-overshoot clamp. The 0.01f component zeroing (`0xb45df8`) is not modelled.
- The clips are type 1 walk and 7 run in a model's `default` group (`bsr_reader.gd`;
  `docs/protocol/BSR_FORMAT.md`, mangnyang's group). Mode 0/1 -> walk/run is an inference:
  `AITactics_Handler_110` (`0x5489b0`) picks 0 or 1 (read), and the `0x704f` byte is
  `(mode == 1) + 2` (`0x54184d..0x541859`, read).
- The facing was measured: `client/tools/probe_monster_front.gd` on the box's archives. The control
  `CHAR_CH_MAN_FIGHTER` reads -Z, and all seven roster models read -Z (the table is in
  `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`).
- 0x007C..0x007F were used by no non-test file under `server/internal/session`,
  `server/internal/proto` or `client/scripts/net` (grep).

**Wired.**

- `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`, "srrevamp's own monster protocol (placeholders)":
  - `OpMonsterMoved 0x007c` (s→zone, 29 bytes: s64 id, f32 x/z, f32 dest_x/dest_z, f32 speed, u8
    mode) and `OpMonsterMotionList 0x007f` (s→requester after a list: u16 n + 21-byte entries);
  - the fixtures;
  - the stop push (the leg's speed, or the species' walk speed; mode unchanged; no re-facing;
    stand clip).
- `CombatNet`:
  - `OP_MONSTER_MOVED` and `OP_MONSTER_MOTION_LIST`, `MonsterMoved`, `MotionEntry`;
  - `decode_monster_moved` (null under 29 bytes) and `decode_monster_motion_list` (keeps whole
    entries before a truncated tail);
  - the approach helpers `approach_releases`, `approach_aim` and `should_rewalk`, with
    `REFUSED_TOO_FAR` and `APPROACH_RETRY_CAP` 3 (srrevamp's own).
- `NetClient` has the signals `monster_moved` and `monster_motion_list`, with their `_dispatch`
  cases. The unhandled-opcode warning now fires once per opcode per connection
  (`_should_warn_unhandled`, cleared in `connect_to_server`).
- New `client/scripts/world/monster_motion.gd` (`MonsterMotion`, pure):
  - `step`, the engine's two clamps;
  - `begin`, which starts from the drawn position and resyncs past `RESYNC_DISTANCE` 32; a speed of
    0 places the body at once;
  - `reconcile`, `gait_type` / `state_gait`, `turns_to_face`, `front_of` / `FRONT_BY_MODEL`,
    `facing_yaw`, `gait_clip` (stand = the assembler's idle), `swap_loop` (a one-shot's resume
    slot, never a second loop; a death hold untouched) and `needs_height`
    (`HEIGHT_RESOLVE_STEP` 2).
  - srrevamp's own constants: `MAX_HEIGHT_RESOLVES_PER_FRAME` 32, `UNKNOWN_MOVE_PULL_SECONDS` 5,
    `REAIM_EPSILON` 0.5.
- `World3D`:
  - `_monster_motion`;
  - `_on_monster_moved`: an unknown id pulls the list at most once in 5 s, and a dying body
    ignores the move;
  - `_on_monster_motion_list`: re-aims past `REAIM_EPSILON`; unlisted bodies finish their leg;
  - `_apply_monster_leg`, `_set_monster_gait`, `_stop_monster_motion`;
  - `_step_monster_bodies`, called first in `_physics_process`. It steps each body, writes its x/z
    into `_monster_snapshots`, throttles the height rays and stands the body on arrival.
  - `_spawn_or_update_monster` places an existing body through `reconcile`, resolves y at the placed
    x/z and writes both back.
  - A leg is dropped in `_begin_monster_death`, in the free path of `_sync_monster_bodies`, in
    `_on_change_zone_result`, and at a kill result, next to `hold_for_kill`.
  - Bodies carry their model path as `meta("model")`.
- The approach walk:
  - It releases only inside the stop while the target walks, or after a refusal. It then aims
    `MOVE_TARGET_STOP_DISTANCE` short of the stop, so an arrival is inside it.
  - `_release_pending_attack` keeps the attack in `_released_attack`, and anything the player does
    next clears it.
  - `_rewalk_after_refusal` re-arms a "too far away" refusal of a live, non-dying target, up to
    the cap.
- The QA hooks `SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_MOVE="dx,dz,speed,mode"` and `SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_LOG`, documented in
  World3D's QA header.
- The probe tool `client/tools/probe_monster_front.gd`, with a `client/tools/README.md` entry.

**Stand-ins, disclosed at their constants and in monster_ai.md:**

- the f32 speed field (retail `0x7021`/`0xB021` carry none);
- the mode -> clip inference;
- `RESYNC_DISTANCE`, `HEIGHT_RESOLVE_STEP`, `MAX_HEIGHT_RESOLVES_PER_FRAME`,

- the terrain-only height along a leg;
- the resync position, which is a lead (`FUN_008a5750`/`FUN_008a5640`), not a reading.

A model the probe did not settle would stay unturned and be logged "facing unmeasured"; all seven
roster models settled.

## Batch-13 review follow-ups (rounds 531-533): a refused skill is not re-cast, the approach-walk bookkeeping, the height budget, record wording (round 534)

The reviewers' notes on rounds 531-533. Each claim was re-checked before anything was written: the
server against `/var/tmp/srv.asm` and `/var/tmp/decomp_server` (read-only), the client against the
render box. One server fix a player can notice (a cast refused as too far away costs nothing), four
client fixes, one dev-tool fix, and wording.

**Round 533: the approach walk and skills.**

- **(a) A refused skill is not sent again.** `CombatNet.should_rewalk` takes the released attack's
  skill id and answers true only for a plain swing (skill 0); `World3D._rewalk_after_refusal`
  passes it and logs "not cast again" for a skill. The client plays a cast (its animation, the
  battle stance, the hit effect it arms) when the request goes out (`_send_attack`), so a second
  request after the walk played a second cast for one use. At round 533 the server had also already
  charged the refused cast (b), so the second request was refused on cooldown or spent the MP again.
- **(b) The server tests the reach before it spends (verified first, then changed).** The review
  asked whether the engine spends MP or arms the cooldown for a cast it cannot reach. It does not:
  - `CGCharAutoCommandActor::Tick_UseSkill` (`0x4ae590`) gates with mask `0x17` in phase 0 (`push
    0x17` at `0x4ae6af`) and `0x91` in phase 1 (`0x4aea11`, the call at `0x4aea18`), then tests
    `Action_IsTargetWithinReach` (`0x4aea39`). In reach it enters phase 2 (`0x4aea4b mov eax,2 ;
    call 0x4ac9e0`). Out of reach it walks (`MoveTowardObject`, `0x4aeaca`) and stays in phase 1.
    Phase 2 posts the 0x7070 command (`push 0x7070` at `0x4aebc6`).
  - Nothing is spent before that post. Neither the tick nor the 0x7074 handler (`0x4acc40`) calls
    `EngageSkill` (`0x593540`) or the reuse-timer arm `FUN_0064c700` (their direct calls, listed
    from `srv.asm`). The gate spends nothing: no instruction in `58d8f0`-`58e52f` references
    `+0x308`, the slot `EngageSkill`'s first step takes the costs through. The per-kind cast
    handlers call both; `Skill_BuildUseContext_B` (`0x586700`), for one, copies Consume_HP/MP
    (`+0xca`/`+0xcc`) into the context, arms the timer at `0x586c22` and calls `EngageSkill` at
    `0x586c44`. Which function consumes 0x7070 was not traced; the order does not depend on it.
  - The gate masks carry bit `0x1`, the cooldown row (`0x58e077 test al,0x1`, refusal at
    `0x58e095`), and bit `0x10`, the HP and MP rows (`0x58e1ac test byte [ebp+0x10],0x10`,
    refusals at `0x58e292`/`0x58e2b1`). So the engine refuses a cast on cooldown or short of
    HP/MP before it looks at the reach.
  - **Change.** `session/skill.go` now runs, in order: the cooldowns (unchanged); the new
    `skillCostRefusal`, the HP and MP comparisons without spending; `skillInReach`, still skipped
    for a `noCombat || zeroDmg` row; then the HP spend, the MP spend, `RecordUse`, the group arm.
    The too-far refusal still cancels a running keep-up, as it did when it came after
    `keepUp.Cancel`: the 0x7074 handler tests mask `0x37` but no reach before `Push`, so the engine
    queues such a cast and the keep-up ends at depth 2 (`auto_command.md`). A cast short of mana
    is refused for its mana wherever it stands, as before. Recorded in `skill_use_gate.md` ("The
    gate is a check, and the reach comes between it and the costs") and the SYSTEMS.md damage row.
  - The server change is live on deploy, not behind a flag: it changes no packet and needs no
    client. It only stops charging a cast the server refuses. A round-533 client that re-walks a
    refused skill now gets its cast on the retry instead of "skill on cooldown".
- **(c) The released attack could outlive its attack.** A swing the server drops inside its re-use
  delay gets no reply (`session/combat.go`, `swingReady`), and the debug panel's
  `_on_skill_use_pressed` sent `use_skill` itself. Either way `_released_attack` stayed set, and a
  later refusal could walk the old attack again. Now `_send_attack` clears it for every request
  (`_release_pending_attack` records its own attack after the send, as before), and
  `_on_skill_use_pressed` clears it before its send. There is no pure helper that decides
  staleness. The rule is "any newer request forgets it", tested on a bare World3D.
- **(d) The height budget takes turns.** `_step_monster_bodies` spent
  `MAX_HEIGHT_RESOLVES_PER_FRAME` (32, srrevamp's own) in `_monster_motion`'s insertion order every
  frame. Whenever more bodies wanted a ray than 32, the first ones took it every time and the later
  ones never got theirs. The loop now steps every body first and collects which want a ray. The new
  `MonsterMotion.height_turns(wants, cursor, budget)` then serves at most 32 of them, starting at
  `_mob_height_cursor` and wrapping, and the next frame starts just after the last one served.
- **(e) A death hold is marked, not inferred.** `MonsterMotion.swap_loop` treated any one-shot with
  no resume as a death. A body whose idle was never registered (a clip of one frame, or
  `SRREVAMP_NO_IDLE_ANIM`) has no resume after a HIT either, so it kept a non-looping entry and
  never got a walk clip. `World3D._play_once` now writes an eighth element, `hold`, and
  `swap_loop` leaves only that entry holding. A hit with nothing to resume is given the new clip
  as a loop to resume into, still one entry for the skeleton.

**Docs and tools.**

- **(f) `TODO.md`, the Earth Ghost example.** 9 of the 11 roster species run at 55 u/s or more
  (Earth Ghost 75); only Mangyang (22) and Yeoha (20) run slower (`monster_ai.md`, "The roster's
  real walk and run speeds"). So any running monster but those two outruns the 50 u/s player. The
  re-walk sentence now says it is for plain swings only, and why. The debug-panel bullet now says a
  refused cast costs nothing and that its reply no longer counts for a released attack.
- **(g) `probe_monster_front.gd` printed 25 `ERROR: Parameter "m" is null.` lines**, from the
  headless (dummy) renderer's `mesh_get_surface_count`, when it freed each skeleton. Measured on
  the render box: clearing each `MeshInstance3D`'s mesh before `skeleton.free()` leaves 0. Clearing
  the skin instead, or freeing the children before the skeleton, left all 25. The probe's printed
  readings are identical to the run before (diffed).
- **(h) Round 531's pointers and bindings.**
  - `place_minimap`'s doc sends the reader to `_toggle_ui_visibility` for the Hide UI button's

## Record correction: HOMING's destination offset is +R/3 .. +R/3+trunc(R/3) toward the monster (MoveHome 0x545c50), and a WANDER leg bisects the current direction and heading+t (PickWanderLeg 0x545860) (round 535)

**Why.** The round-534 attempt at the monster motion core aborted before any edit. Two pure rules it
was to build on did not match the binary. This round corrects both in the record and in
`server/internal/ai`, so the retry builds on what the engine runs. Behaviour is unchanged: the `ai`
package is still parked (`unwired_test.go`), and nothing outside its tests calls either rule. Every
step below was re-read on 2026-09-24 in `/var/tmp/srv.asm`, `/var/tmp/decomp_server` and the PE's
`.rdata` (read-only).

**HOMING (`CAIState_HOMING::MoveHome`, `0x545c50`).** Round 261 recorded the offset as
`rand % (1 + ftol(R/3)) - R/9`, so `-R/9 .. +2R/9`. That reading came from the decompiler's
`extraout_ST0 / 3.0`. It assumes `_ftol2_sse` (`0x9fbb40`) leaves its argument on the x87 stack.
It does not:

- its SSE2 path stores the argument with `fstp QWORD [esp]` (`0x9fbb52`) before `cvttsd2si`;
- its x87 path from `0x9fbb7f` (`fld st(0)`, `fistp`, `fild`, `fsubp`, `fstp`) also consumes
  `st0`.

With the pop, the stack at `0x545cff..0x545d70` runs as follows:

1. `fld R`, then `fld -3.0` (`0xb45e08`, read as a double).
2. `fdivr st,st(1)`: `st0 = R/-3`, `st1 = R`.
3. `_ftol2_sse` pops, and `ecx = 1 - trunc(-R/3)`.
4. `fild` the remainder, `fxch`, then `fdiv 3.0` (`0xb45ab8`): `R/3`.
5. `fstp`, then `fadd`: `rem + R/3`.
6. `fstp`.

Only this order leaves the stack empty. So the offset is
**`rand % (1 + trunc(R/3)) + R/3`**, which is `[R/3, R/3 + trunc(R/3)]`: 66.7 .. 132.7 units for
R = 200. It runs along `normalize(monster - home)`. `FUN_00430ad0` gets `esi` = the monster's
position (the owner's `+0x7c` record, passed by `HOMING::OnEnter` at `0x55a5fc`) and `edi` = home.
It returns `esi - edi` across regions, and `FUN_004328c0` normalizes the result. The destination is
exactly home when the owner's slot 243 (`+0x3cc`) answers non-zero.

**WANDER (`CAIState_WANDER::PickWanderLeg`, `0x545860`).** Round 251 recorded the leg as
`heading + t`, a full 45..135 degree turn. What the binary does:

- It computes `h = atan2(owner+0x2c, owner+0x24) + t`. `0x9fc1aa` is `_CIatan2`: its dispatch
  table at `0xc81760` spells `atan2`, and `+0x2c` is loaded first.
- The two helpers `0x489490` and `0x4894b0` reach `fcos` and `fsin`, giving `cos h` and `sin h`.
- It adds those to the owner's own direction: `0x5459b3` `fld [esi]` with `esi` = owner `+0x24`
  (set at `0x545989`), `fadd` the cosine; `+0x28` plus 0.0; `+0x2c` plus the sine.
- It normalizes the sum at `0x5459eb`.

So the leg is **`normalize(dir + (cos h, 0, sin h))`**. The draw `t = +-(45 + rand % 91)` degrees
and the 46..124 leg length are unchanged.

**What the owner's `+0x24` holds**, which decides the turn, was the open question round 534 left.
It is the **unit heading** `(cos a, 0, sin a)`, and these write it:

- **SetHeading, vtable slot 230** (`0x398`). `0x482440` is CGObj's version and `0x48ba10` is the
  `CGObjMobile` override that monsters inherit. Both write `cos a`, 0 and `sin a` to
  `+0x24/+0x28/+0x2c`.
- **`CGObj::EnterWorld`** calls it at `0x48541e` with the placement angle.
- **Every destination move's start** calls it: `CGObjMoverByDest::vslot_004` (`0x48c330`) calls its
  own slot 10 (`0x48c660`), which passes `FUN_00485c20`'s `atan2` toward the destination.
- **`CGObj::vslot_000`** (`0x4848e0`), the object's reset, zeroes it. Its callers were not traced.

The probes, and what they did not cover, are in `monster_ai.md`, "WANDER's leg". Unless the reset
runs after placement, a standing monster's leg bisects its heading and `heading + t`. That is a turn
of **t/2, 22.5..67.5 degrees** either side. A zeroed heading would give the absolute heading `t`
from `+x`. Two things stay unmodelled and unread:

- the `ctx+0x14c` term, which adds a unit vector toward that object;
- the 30-unit blocked-probe reversal.

**Changed.**

- **`ai.HomingScatterRange`** now returns `[R/3, R/3 + trunc(R/3)]`. Its doc comment carries the
  stack walk.
- **New `ai.WanderLegDirection(dirX, dirZ, turn)`** is the leg rule. The WANDER comment block is
  corrected, and `WanderTurnSpreadDeg`'s comment now says `t` is 45..135 and the leg turns `t/2`.
- **`monster_ai.md`**: "WANDER's leg and every state's dwell time (round 251)" and "HOMING: the way
  home (round 261)" each carry an inline "Corrected in round 535" note with the evidence. The
  original text is quoted, not silently rewritten.
- **`SYSTEMS.md`**: the Monster AI row is corrected.
- **`recovered_names.tsv`**:
  - the `0x545860` and `0x545c50` rows are corrected;
  - it gains `_ftol2_sse` (`0x9fbb40`: 612 direct call sites, and it pops its argument),
    `CGObj::SetHeading` (`0x482440`) and `CGObjMobile::SetHeading` (`0x48ba10`), all filed with
    origin `reading`.
- **`described_but_unnamed.tsv`** drops its `FUN_009fbb40` row, as `handler_names_test.go`
  requires once a name is filed.

`WORLD_ISSUES.md` rounds 251 and 261 are left as the log of what was believed then.

**Tests** (`server/internal/ai/state_test.go`).

- **`TestHomingRules`** now checks the band for R = 200, 100, 9, 2 and 0. The expected values are
  `R/3 .. R/3 + trunc(R/3)`, and it asserts the band never starts below `R/3`.
- **New `TestWanderLegBisectsHeadingAndTurn`** covers five unit headings and `t` in {45, 90, 135,
  -45, -135} degrees. It checks that:
  - the leg has unit length;
  - the leg sits at `heading + t/2`;
  - the leg is NOT at `heading + t` (round 251's rule);
  - the turn is within 22.5..67.5 degrees;
  - a zeroed heading gives the absolute heading `t`.
- **Negative cases.**
  - With `state.go` stashed, the package fails to build (`undefined: WanderLegDirection`).
  - For semantic negatives, the old `HomingScatterRange` body was restored alone in the working
    copy. `TestHomingRules` then FAILED: -22.2..43.8 for R = 200, "short of R/3".
  - Separately, `WanderLegDirection` was reduced to round 251's `(cos h, sin h)`.
    `TestWanderLegBisectsHeadingAndTurn` then FAILED: "turned the full t", 135 degrees.
  - With the file restored (byte-compared), both pass.
- `cd server && go build ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` is green, and was re-run after the
  doc edits. No client file changed.

## Server motion core (inert): grounded roster speeds, the engine mover with both clamps, a hub motion API, the corrected pure WANDER/HOMING rules, and the 0x007C/0x007F encoders (round 536)

**Why.** Round 533 built the client half of server-driven monster movement: it decodes and draws
`OpMonsterMoved 0x007c` and `OpMonsterMotionList 0x007f`, but no server sends either. This round
builds the server half's core without switching anything on. The roster carries its real speeds,
the hub can hold and advance a leg with the engine's own mover, the pure rules the AI tick will
run are in `server/internal/ai`, and the two messages have encoders. Nothing calls any of it yet:

- `OpMonsterListResult` and its handler are untouched (`TestMonsterListFlow` and
  `TestMonsterListResultRoundTrip` are the controls);
- the hub's motion methods have no caller outside tests (four `knownOrphans` lines, each "wired by
  mob-ai-tick");
- `ai` stays parked.

So the public server's behaviour is unchanged. Round 534's first attempt at this aborted on two
rules that did not match the binary; round 535 corrected them, and this round builds on the
corrected readings. Every citation below was re-read on the RE box on 2026-09-24, read-only, in
`/var/tmp/srv.asm`, `/var/tmp/decomp_server`, the PE's `.rdata` and `/var/tmp/tables`.

**The speeds.** `characterdata_5000.txt` cols 46 (walk) and 47 (run), selected by `RefObjID`, match
round 362's table for all 11 species. The same rows' Level (57), MaxHP (59) and BCRadius (50) match
the roster, which is the control. `monsterSpec` gains `WalkSpeed`/`RunSpeed`, and `combatSpeciesOf`
passes them to `combat.Species`, so the GM console's `/spawn` carries them too (round 488's drift
class). `SpawnSpecies` copies them onto `combat.Monster`. `client/tools/verify_monster_specs.py`
gains `"WalkSpeed": 46, "RunSpeed": 47` and was run on the box with the specs piped in, nothing
written there:

- specs without the speeds: 55 verified, 0 mismatched;
- specs with the speeds: **77 verified, 0 mismatched**, 22 more fields;
- control, Mangyang's walk set to 9: 76 verified, 1 mismatched (`WalkSpeed spec=9 table=8`).

The last line shows the new fields are compared, not skipped: the table's values are integers, and
`int()` parses them.

**The mover, and the new clamp finding.** `CGObjMoverByDest::FUN_0048bff0` builds a step: the
owner's unit heading (`+0x24`/`+0x2c`) times `min(|speed(+0x174) x dt|, 160.0f)`, where
`0xb45ea8` = `00 00 20 43`. It zeroes a component under 0.01f (`0xb45df8` = `0x3c23d70a`). Round 533
already cited the clamp in its caller for the client. This round reads it in full and files it:
**`CGObjMoverByDest::vslot_003` (`0x48c4e0`), now named `CGObjMoverByDest::ComputeClampedStep`.**

1. It calls slot 10 with `dt`.
2. It builds the step with `FUN_0048bff0` (`0x48c547`) into the out vector at `ebx`.
3. It takes dest - position with `FUN_00430ad0` (`0x48c5a9`): `(dest + region delta x 1920) - pos`,
   y = 0.
4. It takes both lengths through `0x405250`, a float square root (`0x9fc1c0`, `fsqrt` at
   `0x9fc1fc`).
5. At `0x48c622`, `fcompp` compares `st0` = |step| with `st1` = |remaining|.
6. `test ah,0x41; jne 0x48c63f` keeps the step when it is shorter or equal, and `0x48c62b..0x48c63c`
   copy dest - position over it when it is longer.

So the engine's mover never overshoots. `FUN_0048bff0` alone, the reading an earlier plan called
"the engine mover's rule", does overshoot. `combat.MoverStep` is the two together: a step that
reaches or passes the destination lands on it and reports arrival. The 0.01f zeroing is not
modelled. `MoverStep` takes the heading as the direction toward the destination, which is what the
move's start sets (`0x48c330` -> slot 10, `0x48c660`, `SetHeading` toward the destination, round
535).

**The hub's motion API** (`server/internal/combat/motion.go`). `combat.Monster` gains `WalkSpeed`,
`RunSpeed`, `HomeX`/`HomeZ` (the spawn point), `DestX`/`DestZ` (on the monster while it stands),
`MoveSpeed`, `MoveMode` and `Moving`.

- `SetMotion` returns the updated copy, whose position is the push's origin.
- `StopMotion` sets the destination to the position and clears `Moving`, keeping the speed and mode
  for the stop push.
- `StepAll(dt)` advances every moving monster under `h.mu`, the lock `ApplyDamage` deletes a killed
  monster under, and clears `Moving` on arrival.
- `All` returns copies.

**The IDLE roll, filed as `CAIState_IDLE::OnMsg_0x25` (`0x559cf0`).** This is IDLE's override of
slot 41, the message-`0x25` handler; the dump calls it `vslot_041`.

- `ebx = 0x19` at `0x559d01`.
- `r = |rand()| % 100 + 1` at `0x559da3..0x559dba`.
- `r < ebx` gives `ChangeState(1)` (IDLE); anything else gives `ChangeState(2)` (WANDER). That is
  WANDER for 76 of 100.

Four owner conditions raise the threshold to `0x65`, which means always IDLE: `IsMercenary` (slot
15); a TypeID word whose fields read 1, 2, 3, 8; `IsAttackableCOS` (slot 16) with the owner's
`+0x1cd8` -> `+0x1d18` set; and slot 243 (`+0x3cc`). None is modelled. Every roster species is
TypeID (1,2,1,1) (characterdata cols 9..12, read on the box), so its threshold is 25.

**The rest, re-read and encoded.**

- **`AITactics_Handler_110`** (`0x5489b0..0x548a20`) picks the clip byte:
  - run (`+0x170`) `<= 1e-6` (`0xb45c84`) gives 0;
  - else walk (`+0x16c`) `<= 1e-6` gives 1;
  - else WANDER gives 0, FLEE gives 0, and every other state gives 1.

  FLEE's bucket-below-3 branch writes nothing, but the one caller, `FUN_00541820`, zeroes the byte
  at `0x541833` (`mov byte [esp+0xa],0`) before the call.
- **`IsWithinRoamRadius`** (`0x545f70`): `fcomp` at `0x5460ae`, then `test ah,0x5; jnp`. Within
  only while dist < radius. Rule 1 multiplies the radius by 1.5 (`0xb45d78`), and any rule other
  than 0 or 1 is always within.
- **`HasArrived`** (`0x541f60`): `fcomp` against 5.0f (`0xb45b28`) at `0x541fb2`, then
  `test ah,0x5; jp`. Arrived only while dist < 5.0.
- **HasArrived keeps y; the roam test does not.** HasArrived's difference, `FUN_00430d40`, keeps y,
  where the roam test's `FUN_00430ad0` zeroes it. srrevamp compares on the ground plane, because its
  monsters carry no height of their own. This is a new detail, disclosed.
- **BATTLE draws no dwell.** `CAIState_BATTLE::OnEnter` (`0x559fb0`) calls only the base `OnEnter`
  (`0x558b70`: `+0x14 = 0`) and never `AIState_DwellMs`. The base `OnUpdate` (`0x558b90`) expires
  only a non-zero `+0x14`, strictly after it. Slot 17 (`0x559310`) and `ExtendDwell` (slot 18,
  `0x559450`) also write `+0x14`, and BATTLE inherits both; their callers were not traced.
- **`WANDER::OnEnter`** (`0x559df0`) refuses on the owner's `+0x170 <= 0.0` (`fldz; fcomp`), which
  is the **run speed**, not HP as round 251 had it. It also refuses a COS (slot 11) that is not a
  mercenary (slot 15). `monster_ai.md`, `recovered_names.tsv` and `ai.Enterer`'s comment are
  corrected.
- **`PickWanderLeg`** (`0x545860`) makes four `rand()` draws, in this order:
  - a sign (`0x5458cd`; odd -> +1);
  - `% 40` (`0x5458eb`), giving `dist = 85.0 + sign x rem` (`0xb46160`);
  - `|rand()| % 91 + 45` (`0x54591f`);
  - a sign (`0x545934`).

  Then `t = sign x m x pi/180`, and the leg is round 535's bisector.
- **`Nest_Hatch`** (`0x5607b0`) sets the heading to `rand() / 32767.0` (`0xb45af8`) times `2pi`
  (`0xb45c18`) for a species whose rarity is not 3.

**Changed.**

## Monster AI tick behind the -monster-ai kill switch (default OFF): SPAWN to IDLE to WANDER and back, HOMING inside a disclosed roam radius, a struck monster stops at the blow (round 537)

**Why.** Rounds 533 and 536 built both halves of server-driven monster movement and switched
neither on: the client draws `OpMonsterMoved 0x007c` and `OpMonsterMotionList 0x007f`, the server
can encode them and step a leg with the engine's mover, and `server/internal/ai` holds the pure
rules. This round is the runtime that drives them, behind a kill switch that is **off by default**.
The public server auto-deploys `dev`, so with the flag off it must be byte-identical on the wire,
and it is (control C1 below).

**Grounding, re-read read-only on the RE box on 2026-09-24** (`/var/tmp/srv.asm`,
`/var/tmp/decomp_server`, the PE):

- **`CAIState::OnAttacked`** (`0x558ea0`). It saves the record's `+8` (`0x558ea6`), calls behaviour
  `+0xf0` (the aggro link, `0x558ebb`), stores `ftol(saved x 1.15)` (`0xb46300`) back into `+8`
  (`0x558ebd..0x558ecc`), and calls behaviour `+0xec` (`0x558ed2`). A non-zero answer returns
  without a transition; otherwise it calls `SetTarget` with push 1 through `0x53ffe0` (`0x558eed`)
  and then `ChangeState` (`0x53ff30`) with `lea edi,[ebx+3]` (`0x558f01`). There is no aggression or
  range test.
- **`CAIState_IDLE::OnEnter`** (`0x559c80`). It calls the base `OnEnter` (`0x558b70`), stores the
  dwell from `AIState_DwellMs` (`0x559c9e` -> `+0x14`) and calls `SetTarget(0)` (`0x559cad`). Then,
  only when `0 < run` (`fldz; fcomp [owner+0x170]; test ah,0x5; jp`), it runs `IsWithinRoamRadius`
  (`0x559cca`) and dispatches `0x26` on false (`0x559cdf`). **No stop**: nothing in
  `0x559c80..0x559ce8` touches the mover.
- **`CAIState_BATTLE::OnEnter`** (`0x559fb0`). It calls the base `OnEnter`, arms timers 3 and 4
  (100) and 5 through `0x540d00`, calls `FUN_00541820` (`0x55a04a`), `0x485d90` on `ctx+0xbc`,
  `0x540580` and `0x541810` (slot 11), and sets `ctx+0xb8`. There is no `AIState_DwellMs` call and
  no stop. The base `OnUpdate` (`0x558b90`) expires only a non-zero `+0x14`, so a fight never times
  out.
- **`CAIState_WANDER::OnEnter`** (`0x559df0`). It refuses on `!(0 < run)` and on `IsCOS` (slot 11)
  without `IsMercenary` (slot 15). Then it calls the base `OnEnter`, `SetTarget(0)` (`0x559e4c`),
  `PickWanderLeg` (`0x559e63`), `AIState_DwellMs(2)` (`0x559e72`, or `ebp = 0x3e8` with no leg),
  `FUN_00541820` (`0x559e82`) and the move (`0x559e95`).
- **`CAIState_WANDER::OnUpdate`** (`0x559eb0`). On expiry it dispatches `0x25` (`0x559ec9`), whose
  default is IDLE. With a run speed, it runs the roam check and dispatches `0x26` (`0x559f38..0x559f65`).
- **`CAIState_HOMING::OnEnter`** (`0x55a540`). It stores the dwell (`0x55a5f1`, the default arm),
  calls `MoveHome` (`0x55a602`) and `FUN_00541820` (`0x55a64a`), and `SetTarget(0)` (`0x55a67a`).
- **`CAIState_HOMING::OnUpdate`** (`0x55a690`). On expiry it dispatches `0x25` (`0x55a6a8`).
- **`AIState_DwellMs`** (`0x545b70`). The jump table at `0x545c2c` was read from the PE:
  `0x545b84` (IDLE), `0x545bbb` (WANDER), `0x545c23` (BATTLE), `0x545c08` (FLEE), `0x545c23`
  (HOMING), `0x545c23` (MOVING), `0x545bd1` (EMOTION). IDLE draws its sign FIRST
  (`0x545b84..0x545b9f`) and then `rand % 2000` (`0x545ba2`).
- **`CAIState_BATTLE::OnUpdate`** (`0x55a090`). It dispatches `0x23` when `FUN_00540dc0` (which
  wraps `FUN_00540de0`: alive, slot 62 == 1) fails.
- **`FUN_00541820`** loads `[ctx+0x110]` at `0x541821` and calls it at `0x541838`. It is called
  from eight sites: the `OnEnter` of WANDER, BATTLE, FLEE, HOMING and PICKITEM, plus
  `AITactics_Handler_0fc`, `FUN_00549ac0` and `FUN_00549f80` (`monster_ai.md`'s behaviour-table
  row, corrected).
- **`AI::CTactics::Attach`** (`0x53f2a0`) stores 200.0 (`0xb45d68`, read from the PE) at `ctx+0x1cc`
  only when there is no nest, no positive caller radius and `row+0x84 <= 0`. That is exactly the
  case in which `IsWithinRoamRadius` (`0x545f70`) returns 1 without measuring
  (`cmp [row+0x84],0; jg` at `0x545fde`, unless slot 242 or 243 answers non-zero).
- **The aggro link** (`0x547570`) zeroes the record's `+4` (damage) at `0x547797` and scales `+8`
  (hate) by the ratio after each forward (`0x54780c..0x54781a`). `AITactics_CreditAttacker`
  (`0x5473c0`) reads the record as `{attacker, damage, hate, hatePercent}`.

**The review fixes applied.**

1. **Stop at the blow** (blocking). The tick steps the mover before it drains the blows, so a stop
   at the tick would come after up to 0.1 s x speed of walking. That carries a monster struck at
   `int(reach) + 2.9` out of reach and ends the keep-up. `noteStruck` now stops the monster at the
   blow under the runtime's lock, and the struck event records `wasMoving`, so the next tick still
   sends the one stop push. N1b is the test.

   out-of-reach line, the time dilation, GOTO from a fresh snapshot) are written into
   `monster_ai.md`.
6. **A stale motion list.** This round takes the first option, with the lock made per session
   rather than global. The client asks for the list on every attack result, so a global lock held
   across the tick's sends would let one stalled client freeze every fighting player's reader. The
   per-session lock stalls only that client's own replies and the tick, as regen already is. Two
   tests cover it.

**The hold's release (round 537's race notes), in `monsterai.go`. OWN DESIGN, disclosed in
`monster_ai.md`, "srrevamp's runtime".** A held monster now stays in BATTLE while any player in its
zone has a keep-up on it (`keptUpOn`: `keepUp.Target` for each player `world.Hub` puts in the
zone). It is released only once `MonsterHoldReleaseTicks` (2) ticks in a row have found none, and
every drained blow restarts that count (`brain.lastBlowTick` and `unheldTicks` replace
`heldSinceTick`). This closes three releases round 537 allowed:

- **The OpAttack gap.** `performAttack` notes the blow; the handler arms the keep-up only after
  `performAttack` returns. A release now needs that gap to outlast two tick periods from the blow.
- **The cast gap.** `useSkillHandler` runs `keepUp.Cancel`, then the blow, then the hand-off
  re-arm. A release now needs one period from the Cancel to the blow, or two from the blow to the
  re-arm.
- **The second player.** A second player's keep-up still holds the monster after the first
  player's ends.

Two effects are disclosed, not closed:

- The **target-gone exit** still follows only the first attacker, per the rule-0 stand-in. Closing
  it is mob-threat-retarget.
- The **drift window** between `firstSwingInReach` and `noteStruck`'s stop remains. Closing it
  would stop monsters for clicks that deal nothing.

With `-monster-ai` off none of this runs: the runtime is nil.

**The QA GOTO (client).** With a server, `SRREVAMP_QA_ATTACK_GOTO` now asks for the monster list
on every QA swing. `World3D._qa_goto_plan` picks the target from the list's own positions before
`_sync_monster_bodies` rewrites a walking monster's position into its drawn one. The choice is
`QaAttackGoto.pick`: the preferred id while listed alive, else the nearest by the list, never dead
or dying. `_qa_goto_from_list` then stands the player 8 units along +x from that position
(`QaAttackGoto.stand_spot`, the hook's own offset) and settles them onto the walkable graph at
once. Otherwise the next physics frame's height change would send an OpMove after the swing,
cancelling its keep-up. The swing goes out directly, because `_attack_monster` would measure the
reach to the stale drawn body. A player already on the spot is not moved again
(`QaAttackGoto.needs_teleport`): the OpMove would end the keep-up holding the monster. Without a
server the hook is unchanged.

the first physics frame, which comes while `_ready` still awaits the QA sign-in, so a run from the

and swings only once connected. The re-run's first `QA ATTACK` line (not the log's first line;
corrected in round 544), `QA ATTACK: armed at tick 0 (connected: false)`, confirms that ordering. Also fixed: World3D's comment beside the Ctrl+F3 binding now
reads "(Ctrl+F3 -> Copy)".

## Client: decode OpMonsterAttacked 0x007D and draw a monster's blow for everyone in the zone (round 540)

This round builds the client half of two new zone pushes. The client can now draw a monster's blow
for everyone in the zone, and a monster that has just appeared at the moment it appears. Nothing
changes in play until a server sends either push, and none does yet. The server half comes next,
each push behind its own default-off flag, and those flags are flipped only once this client has
been released. Client only: the server is unchanged, and no existing opcode or layout changed.

**Grounding, re-checked for this round.**

- **0x007D and 0x007E were free.** Before this round neither appeared in any non-test file under
  `server/` or `client/scripts/net` (grep, 2026-09-24), and `server/` still has neither.
  0x007A/0x007B are repair and 0x007C/0x007F are monster motion.
- **The counter pipeline** is `session/combat.go` `performAttack`, the branch after
  `combat.Hub.CounterattackReady` (rounds 254 and 505). The push repeats that branch's
  `PlayerDamageTaken`, `MonsterCritical`, `PlayerBlocked`, `PlayerDied`, `PlayerHP` and
  `DeathExpLost`, so it adds no new number.
- **A counter that lands deals at least 1.** `combat.ResolveBlow` floors the blow at 1 in
  `MitigateDamage` and again in `ApplyLevelAdvantage`, and `ApplyFloorBand` never takes it lower.
  So a result reports a counter exactly when its damage is above 0 or its block flag is set.
- **The hit timing** is the attack clip's first `EVENT_HIT` (`mangnyang_attack01` at 651). Its
  millisecond unit is inferred from the key times, not read (`docs/protocol/BSR_FORMAT.md`, "Events
  and walk points"). The code says so at `World3D._monster_strike_seconds`.
- **The spawn heading's frame** comes from `server/internal/ai/wander.go`: radians from +x toward
  +z. It was re-read on the RE box: SetHeading `GObjPC::FUN_00482440` (IGObj slot 230) writes
  +0x24 = `FUN_00489490` -> `0x009fc0b0`, +0x28 = 0, +0x2c = `FUN_004894b0` -> `0x009fbf80`.
  The two CRT functions' x87 paths run `fcos` at `0x9fc11d` and `fsin` at `0x9fbfed`, so the
  unit heading is (cos a, 0, sin a). The CGObjMobile override `0x0048ba10` writes the same three.
- **A finding the plan did not have: the client is not told its own character id when it enters
  the world.** `OpEnterWorldResult` (`session/world.go` `EnterWorldResult.Encode`) carries OK, the
  reason, the zone, the position, the gender, HP and MaxHP, and the others in the zone, but no id,
  and adding one would change a layout. (This entry first said "no other message tells the client
  its id"; corrected in round 544: a party reply carries one per member, `PartyResult` /
  `PartyMemberSnapshot.CharacterID`, which `party.gd` decodes -- but only once such a reply has
  arrived, and never outside a party.) The plan's "a 0x007D for (monster, self)" therefore cannot
  compare ids from the first swing. This round pairs a push with the attacker's own result instead
  (below), and files the id as a prerequisite of mob-battle-chase in `docs/TODO.md`.

**Wired.**

- **The protocol table** (`docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`, "srrevamp's own monster protocol
  (placeholders)") has two new rows and their fixtures:
  - `OpMonsterAttacked 0x007d`, sent to the zone with the attacker included, right after the
    attacker's `OpAttackResult`. 33 bytes: s64 monster, s64 target character, s32 damage, u8 flags
    (bit 0 critical, bit 1 blocked, bit 2 died), s32 target HP, s64 death exp lost.
  - `OpMonsterSpawned 0x007e`, sent to the zone: one `OpMonsterListResult` record, then an f32
    heading.
  - The new subsection "The strike and spawn pushes (round 540: the client half)".
- **`CombatNet`:** `OP_MONSTER_ATTACKED`, `OP_MONSTER_SPAWNED`, `MonsterAttacked`,
  `MonsterSpawned`, `MONSTER_ATTACKED_SIZE`, the three `STRIKE_*` flag bits,
  `decode_monster_attacked` (null under 33 bytes) and `decode_monster_spawned` (null when the
  record or the heading is cut short).
- **`NetClient`:** the signals `monster_attacked` and `monster_spawned`, and their `_dispatch`
  cases. A short payload is dropped, not emitted as null. The stale "no server sends either yet"
  note on the 0x007C/0x007F signals now says both are sent only with `-monster-ai` on.
- **New `client/scripts/world/monster_strikes.gd` (`MonsterStrikes`, pure).** It decides which of
  a counter's two reports the attacker's own client draws it from:
  - `result_countered` says whether a result reports a counter at all.
  - `expect` starts a wait for the counter a result reports.
  - `repeats` compares a push with a wait: damage, target HP, critical, block and death.
  - `claim` lets a push take the oldest unclaimed wait it repeats, and returns
    `CLAIM_NONE` / `CLAIM_HELD` / `CLAIM_DRAWN`.
  - `settle`, when the blow lands, returns the push that claimed the wait. With no push it marks
    the wait drawn, so a late push is swallowed instead of drawn a second time.
  - A new counter on the same monster drops waits already drawn.
- **`World3D`:**
  - `_on_attack_result` hands the counter to `_draw_counter_at_landing`, which draws at
    `lands_after` through `_settle_counter`: from the push when one claimed the wait, from the
    result otherwise. Drawing from the result is the pre-540 code, moved into
    `_draw_counter_from_result` and still printing its QA `counter-swing` line -- not unchanged,
    as this entry first said (corrected in round 544): the `_player_skeleton != null` test and the
    read of the attack clip's hit time (`strike_after`) moved from result time to landing time,
    since the function now runs when the blow lands. That path now also
    prints `World3D: monster %d counter from the result (no push)`.
  - `_on_monster_attacked` prints `World3D: monster %d strikes %d for %d (HP %d)` with the flags
    and how the push was taken. A push that claims nothing is drawn at once by
    `_draw_monster_strike`: the monster turns toward its target by its measured front and plays its
    attack clip, and at the clip's hit event the target plays its hit clip and a red number rises
    over it. The target is the player's own body or another player's body in `_other_bodies`. A
    blocked blow is the swing alone.
  - A claimed push sets the HUD's HP from its target HP and shows the death line (`_show_own_strike`).
    The result set both from the same numbers a moment earlier, so nothing visibly changes.
  - `_on_monster_spawned` makes the body through `_spawn_or_update_monster` and faces a standing
    body along the heading (`_face_monster_heading`, `MonsterMotion.heading_dir`). It prints
    `World3D: monster %d spawned (push)`.
  - The status label says "Took N" only when N > 0 (`_exchange_line`). A swing inside the
    ReuseDelay used to read "Took 0 damage".
  - `_set_other_gait` now goes through `MonsterMotion.swap_loop`, so another player's hit clip is
    not joined by a second loop entry on the same skeleton when that player's gait changes.
  - `_floating_damage` skips an anchor that is not in the tree.
  - A monster's waits are dropped at its death, at its removal from the list and on a zone change.
  - The QA hook `SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_STRIKE=1` stands in for a server with the push. It sends each
    counter result's push through `NetClient._dispatch`, deferred to the end of the frame. It is
    listed in World3D's QA header.
- **`MonsterMotion.heading_dir`**, and the `swap_loop` note about `_set_other_gait`.

**Plan items answered, and one changed.**

- **The send order** (result first, then the push) is relied on, not changed, and there is no
  layout change to `OpAttackResult`.
- The attacker's own swing plays at `lands_after`, not on receipt.
- Blows on other players are drawn on their `_other_bodies`.
- "Took N" appears only for N > 0.
- The live count takes blocked counters in: `result_countered` counts a blocked result, and a
  blocked push is claimed like any other. No blocked counter happened live, because the QA player

- The EVENT_HIT millisecond unit is disclosed as inferred.
- **Changed:** "a 0x007D for (monster, self)" is matched by pairing, because the client is not
  told its id when it enters the world (a party reply carries it, but only once one has arrived;
  corrected in round 544). A push is this player's only when it repeats a counter this client's result reported

**Tests.**
