## The monster's blow becomes a zone push, behind -monster-strike-push (default off) (round 541)

This round builds the server half of round 540's strike push. With the new flag on, a monster's
counterattack is sent to everyone in its zone as `OpMonsterAttacked 0x007D`, the attacker included,
after the attacker's `OpAttackResult`. The flag is **off by default**. Off, nothing is sent and the
wire is what it was, so the public server, which deploys `dev` automatically, sees no change. The
flag is to be flipped only once a client release that carries round 540 is out. No existing opcode
or layout changed.

**Grounding, re-checked for this round.**

- **The counter pipeline** is `session/combat.go` `performAttack`, the branch after
  `combat.Hub.CounterattackReady` (rounds 254 and 505). It was read in the current tree before the
  move: `defenderArmor`, `defenderParryRate` and `monsterBlow`, then `resolveBlow`, then
  `wearShield` / `wearArmour`, `chars.ApplyDamage`, `DeathPenaltyExp`, `RespawnHP`,
  `keepUp.Cancel` and the MP refill. The push adds no number: every field is one the attacker's
  result already carries.
- **The push pattern** is the ground-item zone push (`dropKillLoot`, `docs/protocol/ground_items.md`):
  one packet, sent to every session in `hub.EntitiesInZone`, with a failed write left to that
  session's own reader. `OpDuelOpponentDamaged` (`session/duel.go`) is the direct-push precedent.
  `gateway.Session.Send` takes the session's send mutex, so pushing from another session's
  goroutine is safe.
- **0x007D was free on the server.** Before this round it appeared in no non-test Go file under
  `server/` (grep, 2026-09-24). The client has decoded it since round 540, and the 33-byte layout
  and fixture are the ones in `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`'s table.
- **No new binary citation.** Every number is the existing counter's, and the layout is
  srrevamp's own.

**Wired.**

- **New `server/internal/session/monsterstrike.go`:**
  - `OpMonsterAttacked` (0x007d), `MonsterAttackedSize` (33), the flag bits `StrikeCritical` /
    `StrikeBlocked` / `StrikeTargetDied`, `MonsterAttacked` with `Encode`, and
    `DecodeMonsterAttacked`, which refuses a payload under 33 bytes and ignores bytes after the
    33rd, as the client does.
  - The flag: `monsterStrikePush` (an atomic) and `SetMonsterStrikePush`.
  - `monsterStrike(ctx, strikeDeps, monster, characterID, playerLevel)`: `performAttack`'s counter
    branch, moved **unchanged**. The only edits are that it writes to a `monsterStrikeOutcome`
    instead of the result, and returns a zero outcome with each error. A diff of the moved body
    against the old branch shows nothing else.
  - `pushMonsterStrike`: when the flag is on, it sends to every session in the zone; when it is
    off, it does nothing.
- **`performAttack`** calls `monsterStrike` in the counter branch and copies the outcome into
  `PlayerDamageTaken`, `MonsterCritical`, `PlayerBlocked`, `PlayerDied`, `PlayerHP` and
  `DeathExpLost`. It then sends the push **last**: after the attacker's result, and after the
  zone's `OpMonsterDamaged` for the same swing, which goes to everyone except the attacker. So the
  attacker gets the push right after its result, which is the order round 540's `MonsterStrikes`
  relies on. A kill has no counter and sends no push, and neither does a blow inside the ReuseDelay.
- **`cmd/server`**: `-monster-strike-push` (env `SRREVAMP_MONSTER_STRIKE_PUSH` via `envBool`; a
  value that does not parse leaves it off with a WARN). It is set before the gateway serves, and
  the boot log reports `monster strike push on: ...` or `... off (...)`.
- **Docs:**
  - `server/README.md`'s flag table.
  - `deploy/README.md`, the new section "Monster strike push (off by default)".
  - `monster_ai.md`: the table row (the order, and that the push needs the flag), "The strike and
    spawn pushes" (the server half now exists), and the new subsection "The strike push's server
    half (round 541)".
  - `SYSTEMS.md`'s Monster AI row (with the anchor `SetMonsterStrikePush`) and `TODO.md`.

**Plan items answered.**

- **Send order**: the result first, then the push, as the revision asked. This also answers the
  blocking review finding.
- **The `readReply` helper** is in `combat_test.go`. It skips 0x007C, 0x007D, 0x007E and 0x007F.
  The six counter-driven tests (`TestCombatFullFlow`, `TestCombatArmorMitigation`,
  `TestLevelAdvantageAppliedInCombat`, `TestDeathPenaltyAppliedInCombat`,
  `TestMonsterCriticalAppliedInCombat`, `TestShieldBlocksInCombat`) read through it. They now run

- **Relabelled**: the donwhang case and the inside-the-ReuseDelay case are controls. The red is

**Tests** (`server/internal/session/monsterstrike_test.go`):

## Respawns and GM spawns pushed to the zone (OpMonsterSpawned 0x007E) with the hatch heading (round 542)

This round builds the server half of round 540's spawn push. With the new flag on, a monster that
has just appeared is sent to everyone in its zone at once as `OpMonsterSpawned 0x007E`. That covers
the roster's first spawns and respawns and every monster a GM `/spawn` makes. The push carries the
list's own record and the heading the monster hatched facing. The flag, `-monster-spawn-push`, is
**off by default**. Off, nothing is sent and the wire is what it was, so the public server, which
deploys `dev` automatically, sees no change. No existing opcode or layout changed. The client
decode is round 540's, reused unchanged.

**Grounding, re-checked for this round.**

- **The spawn heading** is `Nest_Hatch`'s, re-read on the RE box (`/var/tmp/srv.asm`,
  `objdump -s` of `SR_GameServer.exe`):
  - The shape test runs `0x56098a..0x5609b4`, and the rarity test is `cmp BYTE PTR [edi+0x89],0x3`
    at `0x5609b6`. A rarity-3 species jumps to the nest row's `+0x1c` word (`0x5609bf`); every
    other species falls through to `0x5609ee`.
  - At `0x5609ee`: `call 0x9dd338` (`rand()`); `fdiv` by the double at `0xb45af8`,
    `0x40dfffc000000000` = 32767.0, rounded to a float (`0x560a01`); `fmul` by the double at
    `0xb45c18`, `0x401921fb60000000` = 6.2831854820251465 (2pi at float precision); `fadd` of the
    double at `0xb45ab0` (0.0); `fstp` to a float at `0x560a15`.
  - So the heading lies in [0, 2pi]. It is 2pi itself when `rand()` returns 32767. The plan's
    test said "[0, 2pi)", which is off by that endpoint; the tests check [0, 2pi].
  - `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`, "The `_RefNest` row", row 8, says the same. `ai.SpawnHeading`
    already implemented it (round 536).
- **The pattern** is the ground-item spawn push (`OpGroundItemSpawned 0x006c`, `dropKillLoot`,
  `docs/protocol/ground_items.md`): one packet to every session in `hub.EntitiesInZone`, with a
  failed write left to that session's own reader.
- **0x007E was free on the server.** At the base commit it appeared in no non-test Go file under
  `server/`. Two probes found only `combat_test.go`'s `readReply`: `git grep -i "0x007e\|OpMonsterSpawned"`
  and `git grep -iE "uint16 = 0x0*7e\b|= 126\b"`. The layout and the 55-byte fixture are the
  ones in `monster_ai.md`'s table, which the client has decoded since round 540.

**Wired.**

- **`internal/combat`**: `Monster.Heading`, and `Hub.SetSpawnHeadingRoll`. `SpawnSpecies` draws the

## Live check of the strike push: one push per counter, drawn once (round 543)

Round 541 built the monster's blow as a zone push behind `-monster-strike-push` and left its
render-box check unrun. It is now measured and passed; the numbers are in
`docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`, "The strike push's server half (round 541)", under "Measured (round
543)". In short: with the flag on, 45 of 138 attack results reported a counter and the client
logged exactly 45 strike lines from the push, in the same damage order, with no fallback draw
from the result and no script error. Not exercised: a blocked counter and an observer's screen.
This closes the live-check condition for FLIP 2 in the deploy sequence; the flag stays off on the
public server until the operator flips it after release B (v0.1.436).

## Pure BATTLE rules and the timer read (inert, S) (round 545)

The rule half of the BATTLE entry, built as pure functions with no runtime wiring: mob-battle-chase
runs them next. No opcode, layout or flag changed, and the public server's behaviour is the same
byte for byte -- nothing calls the new code. Every citation was re-read in `/var/tmp/srv.asm` and
`/var/tmp/decomp_server` before it was written; the reading is in `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`,
"The pure BATTLE rules and the timer read (round 545)".

**Grounding, re-checked for this round.**

- **The reach test is inclusive with a nest and strict without one** (`AITactics_IsTargetWithinChaseRange`
  `0x545e50`). Measured at the two `fcompp`s, not read off the decompile: no nest, `fcompp` at
  `0x545e97` then `test ah,0x5; jnp` -- only C0 (dist below `+0x7c`) jumps to `mov al,1`, an equal
  distance falls to `xor al,al`; a nest, `fcompp` at `0x545f38` with the reduced threshold in st(0)
  then `test ah,0x1; jne` -- only threshold < dist answers 0. The nest path's threshold is the raw
  `+0x7c` less the excess of the monster's distance from `ctx+0x1b4` over `ctx+0x1cc` x 1.5 (the
  double at `0xb45d78`, `fmul` at `0x545f02`), applied only when positive (`fcom` against 0.0 at
  `0x545f1a`). `+0x79` of 0 or 2 (`0x545e5c`, `0x545e6f`) and a zero `+0x7c` (`0x545e7f`) answer
  "within" before either path.
- **The give-up code compares the raw `+0x7c` with `>=`** (`AITactics_BattleGiveUpCheck` `0x5483c0`):
  `fild [eax+0x7c]` at `0x54842a`, `fcompp` at `0x54842d`, `test ah,0x41; jp` -- C0 or C3 alone falls
  to `mov byte [edi],1`. It runs only when tactics timer 6 is due (`mov ecx,6` `0x5483f0`, call
  `0x5483f5`), which `AI::CTactics::Init` arms once with base `0x5dc` (`0x53f6ec`, call `0x53f6f6`):
  1500 ms, due at once the first time. The plan's "unreachable under the stand-ins" is corrected to
  "all but": with no nest never; with a nest only at dist exactly `+0x7c` inside 1.5 x the radius,
  where both exits are IDLE. A test sweeps both paths and finds exactly that.
- **The order.** `CAIState_BATTLE::OnUpdate` (`0x55a090`): target validity (`0x55a0dc`, `0x23` at
  `0x55a116`), the reach test (`+0x100` at `0x55a175`, `0x27` at `0x55a187`), the give-up check
  (`+0x104` at `0x55a1a2`, `0x2a` at `0x55a1b9`), the swing (`+0xe8` at `0x55a1d0`). The vanished
  target's exit is `0x23`, grounded; round 537's stand-in "which branch fires is unread" is closed.
- **The slot-6 citation.** BATTLE's slot 6 is `CAIState_BATTLE::OnAttacked` (`0x55a2e0`), which calls
  behaviour `+0xfc` = `AITactics_Handler_0fc` (`0x548090`); the plan named the behaviour as the slot.
  `CAIState::OnAttacked` (`0x558ea0`) does `SetTarget(1)` (`push 1` at `0x558eed`, the call at
  `0x558eef`; round 547) and `ChangeState(3)` (`lea
  edi,[ebx+3]`), no aggression or range test; `CAIState_IDLE::OnEnter` (`0x559c80`) `SetTarget(0)`
  then the roam check.
- **The timer read** (`AITactics_TimerDue` `0x53d6e0`, `AITactics_ArmTimer` `0x53d600`, the table
  builder `0x53d4b0`). The first table has 9 entries (`mov dword [this+4],9` at `0x53d4bb`), so
  BATTLE's indices 3, 4, 5 and the give-up's 6 are first-table; the first-table arming path sets
  `last = 0` (`0x53d6c0`) and `fired = 1` (`0x53d6c7`) whatever the period, and `TimerDue` answers a
  fired entry at once (`0x53d751` -> `0x53d765`). Therefore: the first swing is immediate
  (`BATTLE::OnEnter` arms 5 with the selector's `+0x48`, `0x55a018`); `Handler_0e8`'s re-arm at
  `0x547342` also fires at once, so `ArmNextAttack`'s interval never delays a swing; the top-of-tick
  gate `0x542670` (waits on timer 5 only while the selector's `+0x4c` bit 0 is set, then re-arms with
  base 0 and clears it) never skips a tick after a swing; a refused Execute zeroes entry 5's `last`
  (`0x5455f0`, `0x545617`). The period applies only after a `PickSkill` that returns nothing, which
  no roster species has. The selector's initial `+0x48` is 0: `Init` -> `BindSkillsAndRanges`
  (`0x53f8d5` slot 1) -> `0x561400` (through the Basic vtables' slot-1 thunk `0x5619c0`, `jmp
  0x561400`; round 547) -> slot 2 -> `0x5619d0` -> `0x5614c0` (`mov [ecx+0x48],eax`,
  eax 0). Round 259's "a Mangyang swings every 3000..3600 ms" is corrected in place: the cadence is
  the action machine's `ReuseDelay` (round 254), 3000.
- **The floats**: `0xb45e10` = `00 00 c8 42` (100.0), `0xb45f04` = `00 00 16 43` (150.0), `0xb45d78`
  = 1.5 (double), read with `objdump -s`.
- **`BATTLE::OnEnter` issues no stop** (`0x559fb0..0x55a08b`): timers 3/4 (100) and 5, the `+0x164`
  sign, `FUN_00541820`, `CollectNearbyMonsters`, `+0xb8`, slot 11. The interim hold's stop at the
  blow stays own design until the chase replaces the leg (the review's blocking finding, recorded).

## Client: dead pose, input lock, Revive button, OpReviveResult (round 548)

The client half of the player's dead state (`mob-player-dead-state`, split by the batch-17 review so
this client is released before the server half's `-player-dead-state` flag is ever flipped). A
monster's killing blow that leaves the player at HP 0 -- the server's life state 2, which only that
server half will send -- now holds the die clip, locks movement and attack input, and offers a
Revive button that sends `OpRevive 0x0028`; `OpReviveResult 0x0029` is decoded and brings the player
back. **Inert against today's server**: every kill it reports carries the respawned HP
(`session/monsterstrike.go`'s `RespawnHP`, 40 % of the maximum, above 0) and it never sends the
result. Client only; no existing opcode or layout changed; the server tree is untouched.

**Grounding, re-read on the RE box for this round** (the full reading is in
`docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`, "The player's dead state: the client half (round 548)").

- **The retail resurrect handler was read first, as the plan asked.** `GObjPC_HandleResurrectMsg_053`
  (`0x50fee0`) reads ONE u8 option, acts only in life state 2 (`cmp al,0x2` at `0x510077`), turns
  away a siege countdown above `0xa5`, and then: death cause `[this+0x1cb4] == 2`
  (`leveldata.DeathCauseNoPenalty`) or option 2 with `IGObj::GetMaxLevel` at most 10 (`cmp al,0xa`
  at `0x51017f`) -> `GObjPC::Revive(1)` (`push 0x1; call 0x4df290` at `0x5100e3`) and
  `ApplyHPMPDelta(GetParam(3) x 0.4, GetParam(4) x 0.4, 8)`; option 1 -> `Revive(0)`, the
  return-point path, and `GameEventLog_Record(0x15, 2, 0)`. **The fraction is read off the binary:
  `fmul QWORD PTR ds:0xb460f0` at `0x5100fa`/`0x510130`, and `0xb460f0` = `00 00 00 a0 99 99 d9 3f`**
  -- the constant `character.RespawnFraction` already cites from the create/load path

## A player killed by a monster stays dead (life state 2), behind -player-dead-state (default off) (round 549)

The server half of `mob-player-dead-state` (the client half is round 548). Until this round a
monster's killing blow put the player back on its feet in the same call (`monsterStrike`'s
`RespawnHP`), so no player was ever dead on the wire. Behind `cmd/server`'s `-player-dead-state`
(env `SRREVAMP_PLAYER_DEAD_STATE`, **off by default**, named in `server/README.md` and
`deploy/README.md`), a monster's kill -- the synchronous counter and the AI's own swing alike --
now leaves the character in life state 2 at HP 0 with its potion queue emptied and its keep-up
cancelled; while dead its moves are neither stored nor relayed and its attacks, casts, items,
pick-ups, duel blows, trade requests, zone changes and GM teleports are refused; the monster AI
treats it as no target; it comes back through `OpRevive 0x0028` (in place, at
`character.RespawnFraction` of each maximum, answered by `OpReviveResult 0x0029` and a stats push)
or, for a session that never sends one, through a disclosed 30 s auto-revive. **Flag off: nothing
changes on a kill** -- it respawns at once and the kill's wire is what it was (the flag-off kill
tests of rounds 541/546 still pin the respawned HP); the entry revive of a stored HP 0 is
deliberately flag-independent (below; round 550 softened this sentence, which said "byte for
byte"). No opcode number or layout changed; the pair 0x0028/0x0029 is round 548's contract.

`docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`, "The player's dead state: the server half (round 549)").**

## Batch-17 review follow-ups (rounds 547-549): one death penalty per kill, the recover narrowed to the blow, the dead gates the client and docs missed, record wording (round 550)

The batch-17 review notes (rounds 547-549), each re-checked on the RE box (`/var/tmp/decomp_server`,
`/var/tmp/srv.asm`, `objdump -s` on `/var/tmp/SR_GameServer.exe`) before it was landed. Six code
changes -- four server, two client -- each with a test that fails without it; the rest are comments
and records. The batch-18 review of this round's first cut sent back two blocking follow-ups, folded
in before the commit: the CI failure below was unrecorded and its test slept, and the auto-revive
warning's entry outlived the revive by a pass (the `autoReviveTick` bullet). No opcode or layout
changed; every flag stays off by default. One review claim was
found WRONG on re-reading and is corrected rather than implemented: the retail resurrect handler
TRUNCATES its 0.4 products, it does not round.

**The CI failure on the base, closed.** Run `36061784919` on `7b321dc` (round 549; the
`kakariko-runner`, `go test ./... -v -p 1`; read with `gh run view --log-failed`) failed
`TestSwingOnAPlayerAlreadyDeadIsDropped` in 0.30 s: `monsterai_test.go:1767: 2 blows landed on one
player from two monsters' first swings, want exactly 1: the second found her dead` -- the double
kill of the first code note below (both workers past `runStrike`'s dead check, both `ApplyDamage`s
reporting `died=true`), surfacing on the slower runner where the dev box's 40 plain and 5 `-race`
runs had not shown it. The store's transition rule (the first server bullet) is its fix. The test's
only synchronisation with the two workers was a 300 ms `time.Sleep`; it now waits on both workers
through `monsterAI.strikeDone`, a per-swing completion hook the worker calls after each `runStrike`
(`observeStrikes` / `awaitStrikes`: a 5 s bound that fails loudly; nil in production), so a slow
runner can turn the test neither way. `go test -count=30 -p 1 -run
'TestSwingOnAPlayerAlreadyDeadIsDropped$' ./internal/session/` and `-count=10 -race` pass.

**Grounding, re-read for this round.**

- **`GObjPC::ApplyHPMPDelta` (`0x4a86a0`) is additive, through `GObjPC::FUN_004a87d0`
  (`0x4a87d0`).** The core reads the life state first (`call [vtable+0xf8]` at `0x4a87e6`, `cmp
  al,0x1; jne 0x4a88e0` at `0x4a87e8`: nothing lands off state 1), then for a non-zero HP delta
  (EAX): `GetHP` (`+0x108`, `0x4a8813`) into EDI, **`add edi,ebx` at `0x4a8821`**, `GetMaxHP`
  (`+0x110`), then `mov eax,edi; call 0x4a66f0` at `0x4a8849`/`0x4a884b` -- `GObjChar::FUN_004a66f0`,
  the setter, which clamps: at or above `GetMaxHP` it stores the maximum, below 0 it stores 0
  (its own "CLAMP() ==> min exceeded max" log when the maximum is negative). The MP half is the
  same through `+0x10c`/`+0x114`/`FUN_004a6790` (`0x4a8888` `add edi,[ebp+0x8]`). The `0x4a86a0`
  wrapper hands both deltas down -- BOTH floored at 0: `test esi,esi; jge 0x4a874d; xor esi,esi` at
  `0x4a8747..0x4a874b` for the HP delta, which `mov eax,esi` at `0x4a8759` hands to `FUN_004a87d0`
  in EAX, and `test ebx,ebx; jge 0x4a8753; xor ebx,ebx` at `0x4a874d..0x4a8751` for the MP delta
  (round 551 corrected this clause, which read "the MP delta floored at 0"; not load-bearing, a
  revive's deltas being positive) -- after scaling each non-zero one by
  `1 - param/100`: the HP delta by param 143 (`mov eax,0x8f` at `0x4a86bb` into `EvaluateParam`
  `0x4b3740`, `fdiv QWORD ds:0xb45af0` at `0x4a86c9`, `fld1; fsubrp; fimul` at `0x4a86cf..0x4a86d3`),
  the MP delta by 144 (`mov eax,0x90` at `0x4a8706`, `fdiv` at `0x4a8714`, `fimul` at `0x4a871e`);
  `0xb45af0` = `00000000 00005940` = 100.0 (`objdump -s`). Those are the panic and combustion
  percentages round 491 recorded (`AbnormalState_Panic_Apply21` writes 143,
  `AbnormalState_Combustion_Apply22` 144, each only while the state is on -- the 2026-09-15
  "structurally zero" was corrected there), so a revive's +1 and its trunc(0.4 x max) reach
  `FUN_004a87d0` unscaled unless one of the two is on (not modelled, as round 491 says), and
  `FUN_004a87d0` itself scales nothing.
- **The handler's products are TRUNCATED, not rounded.** `GObjPC_HandleResurrectMsg_053`
  (`0x50fee0`), the death-cause-2 / option-2 path: `push 0x1; call 0x4df290` (`0x5100e3`/`0x5100e7`,
  `Revive(1)`), `GetParam(3)` (`push 0x3; call [vtable+0x104]` at `0x5100f4`/`0x5100f8`), `fmul
  QWORD ds:0xb460f0` (`0x5100fa`), then **`fnstcw [esp+0x12]; movzx eax,...; or eax,0xc00; mov
  [esp+0x14],eax; fldcw [esp+0x14]; fistp QWORD [esp+0x18]; fldcw [esp+0x16]`** at
  `0x510102..0x51012a` -- rounding control bits 11, round toward zero, MSVC's inline `_ftol` -- the
  same for `GetParam(4)` at `0x510130..0x510159`, then `push 0x8; push eax; push edi; push esi;
  call 0x4a86a0` at `0x510148..0x51015d`. That is the death-cause-2 path (a); option 2's path (b)
  has its own identical pair after its `Revive(1)` at `0x51018b`: `fnstcw` at `0x5101a6`, `or
  eax,0xc00` at `0x5101af`, `fldcw` at `0x5101be`, `fistp` at `0x5101c6`, then the MP `fmul
  QWORD ds:0xb460f0` at `0x5101d4` and its `fnstcw` at `0x5101da` (round 551 named the paths;
  this entry first cited only (a)'s). The review note's "round(GetParam(3)*0.4)" was a misread
  of the `fistp`; `srrevamp`'s `int(float64(max) * 0.4)` is the same truncation.
- **So retail's option-2 HP is `min(MaxHP, 1 + trunc(0.4 x MaxHP))`**: `Revive(1)` (`0x4df290`,
  param-1 tail) does `SetLifeState(1)` (`+0x1f0`), `+0x55c`, `SetBodyMode` (`+0x318`) and
  `ApplyHPMPDelta(this, 1, 0, 8)` -- HP 0 + 1 -- and the handler then adds `trunc(0.4 x MaxHP)`.
  81 for a maximum of 200, where round 549 gave 80. MP: `min(MaxMP, MP at death + trunc(0.4 x
  MaxMP))`; no MP write was found in `GObjPC_OnDeath` (`0x4e6980`) or `FUN_004e67b0` (one probe over
  their decompiles for `+0x10c`/`+0x114`/`FUN_004a6790`/either `ApplyHPMPDelta`; not a proof).
- **`0xb460f0` = `00 00 00 a0 99 99 d9 3f` = `0x3FD99999A0000000` = 0.4000000059604645**, the FLOAT
  0.4 widened to a double (the exact double 0.4 is `0x3FD999999999999A`); **`0xb45e00` = `00 00 00
  a0 46 df 91 3f` = `0x3F91DF46A0000000` = 0.01745329238474369**, float32(pi/180) widened (the
  exact double pi/180 is `0x3F91DF46A2529D39`). Both re-read with `objdump -s`. For a pool the
  widened 0.4 changes no integer: every use truncates, and for an integer maximum m the fraction of
  0.4 x m is one of 0, .2, .4, .6, .8, so the extra 5.96e-9 x m cannot cross an integer below m =
  33 million (`character.RespawnFraction`'s comment).
- **The `0x4c07` `GUILDERR_IM_DEAD` returners** (`grep 0x4c07` over the decompile, then each read):
  `FUN_00514b20` (the founder's pre-check), `CGuildManager::RequestAddGuildPoints` (`0x5c62e0`),

## Round-550 follow-up: an alive character at 0 HP can be killed again (no immunity), and the revive prompt guards a freed panel (round 551)

Round 550's re-review found two BLOCKING defects in `118eaed`; this round fixes both as a new commit
on top of it. No opcode or layout changed; every flag stays off by default.

**Blocking 1, the exploit.** Round 550 made `character.Store.ApplyDamage`'s `died` -- the TRANSITION
from above 0 to 0 -- the kill arbiter, so that two racing kills charge one penalty. But a character
can be ALIVE at 0 outside any race: an HP-cost cast lands its caster at exactly 0 when the cost is
her whole pool, and `session/skill.go` pays through `ApplyDamage` without treating the transition
as a death (rightly: which death cause a self-emptied pool takes was never read). From then on
every monster blow -- the AI swing and the synchronous counter -- and every duel blow on her read
`(0, false)`, were dropped, and she fought on immune, her duel unable to end. Reachable by any
HP-skill user whose pool is a multiple of the cost. The round-550 record's "reachable only in the
window between the dead gate and the write" was false; corrected in place above.

**Blocking 2, the freed panel.** `HudPanels.show_revive_prompt` (round 550) replaced
`is_instance_valid(panel)` with `panel.is_inside_tree()` after its `await process_frame`. A
`hide_revive_prompt` in the same frame -- a kill result and a revive result in one `NetClient`
batch, or a second show, which hides first -- `queue_free`s the panel at the end of that frame, and
the coroutine resumes on the next, so `is_inside_tree` runs on a freed instance: a script error.

**Grounding, re-read on the RE box for this round (2026-09-24).**

- **The skill gate's HP row passes on EQUAL, and its addresses are the SERVER's.** In
  `/var/tmp/srv.asm` (`SR_GameServer.exe`): `58e279 cmp DWORD [esp+0x10],0x0`, `58e27e jle 58e29d`,
  `58e282 mov eax,[edx+0x108]` (slot 66, `GetCurHP`), `58e28a call eax`, **`58e28c cmp
  eax,[esp+0x10]`, `58e290 jge 58e29d`**, `58e292 mov ax,0x3013` -- every one an instruction start.
  The review's "0058e292 is not an instruction start in `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm`" looked the
  server's gate up in the client's image (`skill_use_gate.md`'s function is `SR_GameServer.exe`'s
  `FUN_0058d8f0`), where the same offsets fall mid-instruction; the citation stood. So the retail
  rule is `CurHP >= hpCost` -- `combat.CanPaySkillHealth` is unchanged and its comment now names the
  binary and the file -- and a cast at exactly the cost is retail's own behaviour. What retail does
  with the emptied pool afterwards is still not recovered (the cost is spent later, by
  `EngageSkill`'s slot `0x308`; no `OnDeath` call was traced from there): srrevamp leaves her ALIVE
  at 0, disclosed at the payment and in `skill_use_gate.md`, and guarantees she stays killable.
- **`GObjPC::FUN_004a87d0` lands nothing off life state 1** (`cmp al,0x1` at `0x4a87e8` after the
  `+0xf8` call at `0x4a87e6`; re-read) -- the reason a blow that finds the dead state is dropped.
- **The review's nits, each verified in `srv.asm` before it was landed**: the `0x4a86a0` wrapper
  floors BOTH deltas (`test esi,esi; jge 0x4a874d; xor esi,esi` at `0x4a8747..0x4a874b`, the HP
  delta that `mov eax,esi` at `0x4a8759` hands to `FUN_004a87d0`; `test ebx,ebx; jge 0x4a8753; xor
  ebx,ebx` at `0x4a874d..0x4a8751`, the MP delta); the truncation pair round 550 cited
  (`0x510102..0x510122`, `0x510136..0x51014e`) is the death-cause-2 path's, and option 2's own is at
  `0x5101a6` (`fnstcw`) / `0x5101af` (`or eax,0xc00`) / `0x5101be` (`fldcw`) / `0x5101c6` (`fistp`),
  with the MP `fmul QWORD ds:0xb460f0` at `0x5101d4` and its `fnstcw` at `0x5101da`.

**Wired, server.** The kill arbiter moves from the store's write to a per-character KILL LOCK in
`session` (`monsterstrike.go`: `killLocks`, `killLock`, `fallen`). The rule, stated for each path:

- `monsterStrike` (the AI swing and the synchronous counter alike): a blow whose damage leaves the
  pool at 0 (`hp == 0 && incoming > 0`) takes the character's lock and reads her back under it. Not
  in the dead state and still at 0: it is THE kill, and completes the death under the lock -- the
  penalty from that same read (one `GetByID` fewer than an arbiter-plus-penalty design would make:
  the penalty's read is the arbiter's; against round 550 the kill path still makes two, the
  arbiter's and the reborn re-read -- round 555 corrected "fewer than before"), then `markDead`
  (flag on) or `RespawnHP` + `keepUp.Cancel` + the MP refill (flag off).
  In life state 2, or above 0 again: another kill got there first, `dropped` (nothing reported;
  the roll and the armour wear before the write stand, as round 550 disclosed). A blow that lands
  nothing -- blocked, or a zero roll -- kills nobody at any pool and is reported as it is, at the
  HP it found. The store's `died` is no longer read. GUARANTEES: flag on, the second of two racing
  kills reads the first's life state 2 (the swap is under the lock); flag off, it reads the first's
  `RespawnHP` (written under the lock) -- so ONE penalty either way; and a character alive at 0
  reads back alive at 0, so she dies to the next blow.
- `revivePlayer`: the compare-and-swap 2 -> 1 AND the pools under the same lock. Round 550's
  state-first order closed the "alive at 0" window only under the transition rule; under the
  round-551 rule a blow between the state and the pools would read "alive at 0" and kill her, and
  the revive's `Heal` would then land on a dead character. Under the lock it reads life state 2
  (dropped) or the revived pool (lands as usual).
- `handleDuelAttack`: the same arbiter. A blow whose damage leaves the opponent at 0 takes her lock:
  alive and still at 0, it is the duel's kill and `ResetHP` happens there (a monster's blow racing
  it then finds her above 0); in the dead state, the blow is answered with the dead gate's own
  refusal ("your opponent is dead"); above 0 again (a monster's kill and respawn got there first),
  it is reported at the HP she has. `OpponentDied` no longer comes from the store.
- `performAttack`: a dropped counter re-reads `PlayerHP` for the attacker's `OpAttackResult` (the
  review's cosmetic note: the value seeded at the top was read before the racing kill).
- `character.Store.ApplyDamage`'s contract, rewritten: `died` is a fact about the write -- whether
  THIS call emptied the pool -- and not the verdict on a death; nothing in `session` reads it now,
  and the store tests pin the arithmetic. `MemStore` and `SQLStore` are unchanged.
- `runStrike`'s dropped trace says why ("another blow's kill got there first"); `markDead`'s
  comment names the lock (`handStrike`'s did not until round 555, which this line claimed; it does
  now).

OWN DESIGN, disclosed at `killLocks`: the engine has no such lock -- its blows and revives run on
one game-object queue. One mutex per character ever taken to 0, never removed. Lock order: the kill
lock is taken with no other lock held (a strike worker's, a handler's, the auto-revive pass's
goroutine), and under it only `world.Hub.mu`, the potion queue's and `keepUp`'s are taken, none of
which ever takes it back.

is_instance_valid(panel) or not panel.is_inside_tree(): return` -- the validity test round 550

Restored after each (`git stash pop`), all green again, the client shipped again. **The client
negative is behavioural, not a harness FAIL, and that is a gap worth knowing**: `remote_godot.sh
tests` marks a suite failed on `FAIL|FAILURES|Parse Error` in its output, and a GDScript runtime
error prints `SCRIPT ERROR:` and lets the run go on to `ALL PASS`. No script can observe its own
coroutine's abort (an errored coroutine still emits `completed`), so the new case asserts what a
script can see and the error line is the evidence. Widening the harness's grep to `SCRIPT ERROR`
would make this class fail loudly; it is outside this item's files and would need a pass over all
85 suites for existing error lines first -- filed here, not done.

caster reaches it) is killable again -- the pre-round-550 behaviour restored, without round 550's
double penalty. Two simultaneous kills still charge one penalty under either flag. Nothing else on
the wire moves; every flag stays off. Round 549's order stands: tag and confirm the round-548
client before `-player-dead-state` is ever flipped.

## Four species draw their second attack skill (round 554)

`mob-second-skill`. Until this round every roster species swung its col-83 attack skill alone, and
round 260's `ai.SkillWeight` sat uncalled in `orphans_test.go`. Now, **with `-monster-battle` on**
(no flag of its own: the swing is that flag's, and an older client draws the legs and blows as the
same `OpMonsterMoved 0x007C` / `OpMonsterAttacked 0x007D`), a monster in BATTLE draws each swing
among its attack skills by AI_AttackChance and reach margin, walks to the drawn skill's band, fires
it and cools down for its ReuseDelay: Mangyang (160/161), Water Ghost slave (166/167), Water Ghost
(168/169) and Yeoha (176/177) carry two; a Yeoha that draws its 100-unit ATTACK03 swings from where
it stands, and a Water Ghost's ATTACK02 -- a zero-damage `att` block beside a `ps` status param --
lands an explicit 0 rather than the flat disclosed Attack it would have fallen through to. Single-
skill species are unchanged. **Flag off: nothing changes** (the counter rolls the primary range). No
opcode or layout changed; `-monster-battle` is off by default, so pushing to `dev` deploys nothing
new to a player.

**Grounding, re-read on the RE box for this round (2026-09-25; the reading is in
`docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`, "The second attack skill: the runtime (round 554)", and "The skill
choice" was corrected in place).**

- `AI::CTactics::BindSkillsAndRanges` `0x53f780`: the ten dwords at `RefObjChar+0x260`
  (`add eax,0x260` `0x53f95b`, `mov dword [esp+0x14],0xa` `0x53f941`, the loop `0x53f964..0x53f98a`
  through `ResolveUsableSkillRef` `0x59d600` and `RegisterAISkill` `0x53fa70`) -- characterdata cols
  83..92 by the `+0x230` = col 71 anchor. The plan's citation holds.
- `/var/tmp/tables`: col 84 = 161 / 167 / 169 / 177 for exactly the four species, 0 for the other
  seven, cols 85..92 all 0; the eight rows' cols 14 / 21 / 66 and `att` blocks (the tables in the
  section). 169: `att` 9,0,0,0,100, chance 10, ReuseDelay 4000, plus `ps` 28787 (34,100,16). The
  plan's data holds; its "169 has no att" was already corrected by the review's CHANGES.
- `AI::CAISkill_Basic::PickSkill` `0x561b00`, re-read in `srv.asm` and `.rdata`: **the plan's
  formula was incomplete.** Between the margin compare and the `ftol` sit `fmul QWORD [0xb45b00];
  fdiv QWORD [0xb45c60]` (`0x561c93..0x561c9f`), and `objdump -s` reads `0xb45b00` =
  `0x4014000000000000` = 5.0, `0xb45c60` = `0x4024000000000000` = 10.0: a skill gains HALF its reach
  margin in whole units, not the whole margin round 260 recorded (the decompile drops both
  FPU-stack operations, the trap of round 535's `ftol2` pop). The margin is float arithmetic (`fstp
  DWORD` `0x561c72`, `0x561c7e`; the float `GObj_DistanceBetween` stored at `0x561bae`), added only
  above 0 (`test ah,0x41; jne` `0x561c91`). The draw: `r = |rand()| % (total + 1)`
  (`0x561cee..0x561cfc`), the first cumulative weight `>= r` (`cmp [esi],eax; jae` `0x561d2e`), so the
  first entry takes one outcome more than its weight. And **`0x5632d0`, which the plan and round 260
  called "the cumulative draw", is the `invalid vector<T> subscript` throw** the bounds checks jump
  to; the draw is inline in `PickSkill`. Carried as a grounded correction, not an abort: the
  function is the one cited and the corrected rule is read off it and the binary's own constants.

## Batch-18 review follow-ups (rounds 551-554): the level cache off the AI tick, the stale armed pick, the untested link branches, the names-file rows, record wording (round 555)

The review notes on rounds 551-554, each re-checked on the RE box before it was landed
(`/var/tmp/srv.asm`, the decomp dump, `.rdata`; 2026-09-25). Two behaviour changes, both inside
flags that are OFF by default (`-monster-battle`; the level cache is read only by it), no opcode or
layout changed, no new flag, client untouched.

**1. No character-store read on the AI tick or the strike worker.** Round 553's `linkAggro` read the
attacker's level with one `chars.GetByID` per link event UNDER `a.mu`, so one slow store read
stalled every monster's tick, and round 546's `runStrike` read the target's level with one per
swing. Now `world.Entity` carries `Level`: the row's at `Hub.Enter` (a parameter, so no entity ever
exists without one -- `handleEnterWorld` passes `owned.Level`), carried by `ChangeZone`, and moved
by `Hub.SetLevel` at the two places a level changes -- `performAttack`'s level-up next to its
`SetLeveling`, and gm's `/level` (`gm.Deps.World`, the hub `cmd/server` passes). Nothing else moves a
level: a death penalty takes experience only (`GObjPC_OnDeath` touches no `CurLevel`, round 550's
reading in `monsterstrike.go`) and a stat-point spend keeps it (`stats.go`). `linkAggro` reads
`self.Level` off the entity it already resolves (the character-store gate is gone: the link needs
the party hub and the world hub only); `runStrike` makes one hub read for the dead check and the
level, and falls back to the row only for a target no longer in the world (the hand-off window of
round 547 -- the swing still resolves, and its level is then the row's, the one store read left
before the blow). `world.Hub.Enter`'s signature changed (level after name); 30 test call sites updated.

**2. The armed pick is cleared with BATTLE.** The review's question was what the engine does with
the selector's `+0x44` across `ChangeState`. Answered: `CAIState_BATTLE::OnLeave` (`0x55a240`) calls
only `AI::CTactics::ResetThreat` (`0x53fb20`, `call 0x53fb20` at `0x55a243`), and `ResetThreat` zeroes
the selector's armed pick inline -- `xor eax,eax` `0x53fb28`, `mov ecx,[edi+0x9c]; mov [ecx+0x44],eax`
`0x53fb78..0x53fb7e` -- with the two threat seats `+0xbc..+0xe0`, the `+0xac` byte and `+0xa4`/`+0xa8`
-- after its first instruction past the prologue, `call 0x540cb0` at `0x53fb23`: `FUN_00540cb0`
(`0x540cb0..0x540ce3`) loads `+0xa4` and, when it is non-zero, hands it and the object to
`FUN_0055de60` (`push edi; lea eax,[esp+0x8]; push eax; call 0x55de60`), then zeroes `+0xa4`/`+0xa8`
itself; this entry's first form omitted the call (added in round 564; the `+0x44` clear at
`0x53fb7e` is unaffected) -- (its other callers: `Init` at `0x53f4e7`, and the unnamed
`FUN_00559140` at `0x55915a`). The
vtable-slot-6 clear `0x561a40` (`mov [ecx+0x44],0`; slot 6 of `0xaf9d24`/`0xaf9dcc` -- `401a5600` at
each vtable's `+0x18` in `.rdata`) that round 554 could not cheaply trace is reached through the
slot-6 thunk `FUN_00540cf0` (`mov ecx,[eax+0x9c]; mov edx,[ecx]; push eax; mov eax,[edx+0x18]; call
eax`, `0x540cf0..0x540cfc` -- the `push eax` at `0x540cf8` was missing from this quote until round 564),
whose only callers are `0x558fb3` and `0x558fe5` inside the unnamed `FUN_00558f70` (itself
vtable-reached: no direct `call 0x558f70` in `srv.asm`, and `708f5500` sits in the state vtables in
`.rdata`, 18 entries) -- not the BATTLE exit's path. This entry's first draft also named
`CSockDatagram::vslot_004` as a caller of the clear; neither `srv.asm` nor the decomp dump supports
it (`0x561a40` is referenced nowhere outside its own body, and `FUN_00540cf0`'s two callers are both
in `FUN_00558f70`), so that attribution is withdrawn. `BATTLE::OnEnter` (`0x559fb0`) READS the
selector and is not seen to clear it -- the first draft's "touches the selector not at all" was wrong,
and contradicted the ArmContextTimer row already in `monster_ai.md`: `FUN_00540d80` at `0x55a001`
loads the selector's `+0x48` and `+0x44` (`mov eax,[eax+0x9c]; mov ecx,[eax+0x48]; mov
eax,[eax+0x44]` `0x540d80..0x540d89`) and hands them out through two out-params (`mov [esi],ecx; mov
[edx],ecx`, the second replaced by the armed pick's `+0x78` when `+0x44` is non-null,
`0x540d92..0x540d97`), timer 5's base among them (that row), writing nothing of the selector's; and
`0x541810` at `0x55a081` is a thunk into the selector's vtable slot 11 (`+0x2c`: `mov ecx,[eax+0x9c];
mov edx,[ecx]; mov eax,[edx+0x2c]; jmp eax`), whose target is unread. So the clear that IS read is
`OnLeave`'s, the engine draws afresh on every BATTLE entry, and the runtime now does too:
`brainState.leave`, BATTLE's
`leaveBattle`, run by `ai.Machine` on every exit -- the `0x23`/`0x27`/`0x2a` releases among them --
clears `armed`/`hasArmed`. Until this round a pick armed but not fired (seed 1's Yeoha drawing its
range-7 176 at 60 units and losing its target on the way in) survived the exit and was swung in the
next fight with no draw, so round 554's "the draw's moment: the entry tick" was true only of a
monster that had never armed one. The rest of `ResetThreat` has no counterpart in a brain (the
threat table is mob-threat-retarget's; the target, one of the seats, is zeroed by IDLE's `OnEnter`
through `SetTarget(0)`); the cooldown (`lastSwing`) is the action machine's and persists.

**3. The two untested link branches, pinned.** A gathered neighbour already in BATTLE keeps its own
target under rule 0 and still uses up one of the n places; a DEAD neighbour is passed over -- brain
untouched, no target set, no transition attempted -- and uses up its place too (the engine forwards
command `0xe` to the first n gathered whatever each one's state). Tests below; a mutation of each
branch fails its test.

**4. The names file and the `fallen` wording.** `recovered_names.tsv`'s `00561b00`
`AI::CAISkill_Basic::PickSkill` row still carried round 260's reading -- the whole margin, and "rand()
draw (0x5632d0)" -- which round 554 corrected everywhere else: it now reads half the margin
(`fmul QWORD [0xb45b00]; fdiv QWORD [0xb45c60]` `0x561c93..0x561c9f`, 5.0 and 10.0 in `.rdata`), the
inline draw (`0x561ce9..0x561d2e`) and `0x5632d0` as the `invalid vector<T> subscript` throw. The
`fallen` comment and `monsterStrikeOutcome.dropped`'s: a blow a heal covered between its write and
the lock did land (the pool went to 0) -- the blow is UNREPORTED (no push, no counter, no penalty),
and with `-player-dead-state` on a potion step in that microsecond window keeps her alive at the
healed HP with no death; not an exploit (she stays killable), and now worded so. `runStrike`'s dropped
comment likewise.

**5. Record wording, each re-verified.** (a) BATTLE's slot 6 is `CAIState_BATTLE::OnAttacked`
`0x55a2e0`, which calls behaviour `+0xfc` (`AITactics_Handler_0fc` `0x548090`: `mov edx,[ecx+0xfc];
call edx` `0x55a2ea..0x55a2f3`), then `test eax,eax; je 0x55a30c` and, on a non-zero answer -- the 1
`Handler_0fc` returns only when the `+0xec` accounting refuses, the round-546 section's "a refusal
returns 1 (-> IDLE)" -- `ChangeState(1)`s to IDLE (`xor ebx,ebx; push 0; lea edi,[ebx+1]; call
0x53ff30` `0x55a2fe..0x55a305`), and has no `+0xf0` call -- `linkAggro`'s comment and the round-553
section had "slot 6 is `Handler_0fc`", one step short; the round-546 section already had it right.
(This round's first draft of that comment and section wrote "`Handler_0fc` and nothing else", which
the IDLE branch refutes; the load-bearing fact, no `+0xf0` call, stands.)
(b) `CAIState_BATTLE::OnAggroLinked` `0x55a320` credits through `+0xec` and, on the accounting's
refusal, `ChangeState(1)`s to IDLE (`lea edi,[ebx+1]; call 0x53ff30` `0x55a342..0x55a345`; the
round-258 paragraph had it) -- "only credits"/"credit only" corrected in the comment, the section
and the round-553 entry; the refusal stays unmodelled. (c) The every-blow-carries-hate stand-in now
cites the stronger ground: `AITactics_CreditAttacker` `0x5473c0` returns 1 (drop) for a code-0
record whose hate lands below 1 (`if ((iVar4 == 0) && (iVar3 < 1)) return 1`), and
`CAIState::OnAttacked` only `SetTarget`s and `ChangeState(3)`s when `+0xec` returns 0, so a zero-hate
first blow would not even engage its victim, which round 546's BATTLE entry on every blow already
assumes -- consistent with the existing model, not a fresh inference. (d) The round-552 selector
nits: `mov eax,[edx]; cmp eax,ebx` at `0x546719..0x54671b` (the comment's `cmp [edx],ebx` was the
wrong mnemonic); and the fidelity overstatement, read to the end this round -- the PC branch
(`0x546563..0x546675`) stores `ValidTargetOrNull`'s result back over the candidate (`0x546590`; 0 at
`0x5465a9` on the owner's slot-355 refusal), lets a nearer valid summoned object replace the
candidate and its distance (`0x546646`, `0x546642`), reloads the result at `0x546675` and runs the
radius and best-so-far compares on it with NO null test before `mov [eax],esi` `0x546702`
(`ScanForTargets` `0x5405b0` hands every player of the regions but the owner to the selector and
goes on to the next) -- so a rejected, dead player leaves a NULL pick at its own distance that a
later candidate must be strictly nearer than; `acquire` drops dead players before the scan and so
does not model a dead body shadowing a living player. Disclosed in `ai.Nearest`'s comment,
`acquire`'s and the section; not modelled (the flag's operator would want the living player
noticed). (e) The engine consumes tactics timer 1 (`TimerDue` at `0x54793f`) BEFORE the aggression
byte gate (`0x547958`); `acquire` tested `b.aggressive` first, so a non-aggressive monster never
consumed its timer -- now in the engine's order (unobservable under the mode-0 stand-in; a
per-species mode would see it). (f) `ArmTimer`'s first-table path draws `rand()` twice, the second
(`call 0x9dd338` at `0x53d6bb`) to no effect -- the second-table twin at `0x53d65e` seeds that entry's
last (`0x53d663..0x53d66b`), the first-table path zeroes it -- noted in `acquire.go`'s cadence
comment; srrevamp's rng is its own. (g) `handStrike`'s comment names the kill lock, as the round-551
entry claimed. (h) `battleTick`'s note: a monster with no skill carrying an `AI_AttackChance` stands
in BATTLE, neither chasing nor swinging, until the give-up check or the target's exit releases it;
no roster species reaches it. (i) Round 551's "one `GetByID` fewer than before" is one fewer than an
arbiter-plus-penalty design, not than round 550 (the kill path still makes two); corrected in place.

**Tests** (`cd server && go build ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` green; re-run after the doc

## A GDScript runtime error fails a client suite: remote_godot.sh tests counts SCRIPT ERROR lines (round 556)

Developer tooling and one test suite; nothing on the wire, no flag, no server change. Round 551's
review note filed it; round 522 had observed it. Everything below was measured on the render box
(2026-09-25, each Godot under the box lock as ghidra) or in this checkout.

**The gap.** `client/tools/remote_godot.sh tests` marked a suite failed on `FAIL|FAILURES|Parse
Error` in its output. Godot prints a GDScript runtime error as `SCRIPT ERROR: <message>` with an
`at:` line under it, aborts only the function it happened in, and lets the run go on -- so a suite
reached `ALL PASS` and exited 0 with the error on its output, and the harness counted it green.
Round 522 watched `hud_window_test.gd` do it on every run; round 551's negative (a freed panel in
`show_revive_prompt`) printed the error and `ALL PASS` in one output.

**The audit first: all 85 suites, each run once with its full output kept** (the harness discards
a passing suite's), then grepped.
- `SCRIPT ERROR`: one suite, `hud_window_test.gd`, two lines -- `Compile Error: Identifier not
  found: NetClient` at `GDScript::reload (res://scripts/ui/hud/hud_panels.gd:685)` and a follow-on
  empty `Compile Error:` at `hud_window_test.gd:-1`, with the engine's `ERROR: Failed to load
  script "res://scripts/ui/hud/hud_window_test.gd" with error "Compilation failed"` under them --
  and then all eleven checks `ok` and `ALL PASS`. The cause is round 514's measurement: `hud_panels.gd`
  names the `NetClient` autoload, which a `--script` suite registers only after `_init`, and the
  suite read `HudPanels.PANELS` and `HudPanels.MENU_ITEMS` by class_name from `_init`, so the
  script was compiled before the autoload existed. A defect in the suite, not in `HudPanels`;
  fixed below, no allow-list entry.
- `ERROR:`: 23 suites, none a defect, so it does not join the failure pattern. 20 are a reader's
  `push_error` on the bad input a negative case feeds it (`at: push_error` under each: `ban: bad
  magic`, `bsk: 1 bone name(s) announced but never resolved`, `environment: file too small to
  contain a header`, `mapm`, `mapo`, `mapo2`, `mapt`, `nvm`, `tile2d`, `ObjectLoader: ... not found
  in archive`, and the bmt/bsr/cpd/ddj/efp/objidx/regioninfo/terrain-builder readers' own), each
  printed beside the `ok` line of the negative case that fed it. 3 are the dummy renderer's housekeeping at exit
  (`Pages in use exist at exit in PagedAllocator`, `RID allocations ... were leaked at exit`, in
  `character_assembler_test`, `monster_assembler_test` and `hud_window_test` -- the last three lines
  of `DummyTexture`, `ShapedTextDataAdvanced` and `FontAdvanced` RIDs from the Label, gauge and
  lattice the suite builds in `_init`, which the fix below does not touch; `object_loader_test`,
  one of the 20, also gets its `Parameter "m" is null` from `mesh_get_surface_count` in the dummy
  mesh storage). Before the fix `hud_window_test` printed the engine's `Failed to load script ...
  "Compilation failed"` echo of its SCRIPT ERROR as well; the fix removes that line and leaves the
  RID lines, so the count is 23 suites before and after -- measured both ways, the BASE suite run
  once more on the box under a probe name (deleted after) printing the two SCRIPT ERRORs, the echo
  and the same three RID lines. (The first draft of this entry counted 2 renderer suites and
  called the 23rd the compile echo, "gone with the fix"; the review's own full-output run of the
  committed tree, then a second full-output run of all 85 suites on the final tree -- 23 `ERROR:`
  suites, 20 with `at: push_error`, 3 with `RID allocations`, no overlap -- corrected it.) No suite
  prints `USER ERROR`.
- No passing suite prints `FAIL` (`error_text_test.gd`'s echo-the-key-only-on-a-miss precaution
  holds). Three suites end with their own pass line rather than `ALL PASS` (`level_up_effect_test`,
  `npc_facing_test`, `qa_attack_goto_test`); left as they are, they print no FAIL and exit 0.

**Change.**
- `client/tools/remote_godot.sh` `tests`: the failure pattern is now `FAIL|FAILURES|Parse
  Error|SCRIPT ERROR`, and a failed suite's `SCRIPT ERROR` lines are printed with the `at:` line
  under each (`grep -A1`). Found by the first proof run and fixed in the same edit: the two print
  lines end in `|| true`, because a `grep` with no match exits 1 and under the script's `set -euo
  pipefail` that ended the whole run at the first suite whose only failure was a SCRIPT ERROR --
  `FAILED: res://scripts/qa/script_error_probe_test.gd`, no offending line, no summary, exit 1,
  and the 21 suites after it (it was suite 65 of 86) never ran. The BASE script carried the same
  latent trap for a suite exiting non-zero without a FAIL line.
- `client/scripts/ui/hud/hud_window_test.gd`: the two `HudPanels` constant checks moved from `_init`
  to a new `_initialize`, which loads `hud_panels.gd` by path (`load(...) as GDScript`,
  `can_instantiate()`, `get_script_constant_map()` -- the idiom of `npc_service_reader_test.gd`'s
  check (j) and `monster_motion_test.gd`) and reports. A new check requires `PANELS` and
  `MENU_ITEMS` to be non-empty, so a renamed constant fails instead of letting the two loops pass

## Moving monsters take their height from the navmesh, not the terrain-only ray (round 557)

Client only; nothing on the wire, no flag, no server change (the server binary built for the live
checks is this tree's, used for its monster list alone). Inert in normal play until the monster AI
is switched on: nothing moves a monster on the public server today. Everything below was measured
on the render box (2026-09-25, each Godot under the box lock as ghidra) or read in this checkout.

**Grounding, re-read for this round.**

- The NPC height path, `World3D._try_spawn_region_npcs`: the region's own graph (matched by its
  group on `_region_nav_graphs`) -> `NavGraph.landing_height_at` on the authored region-local
  position; the new helper reaches the same function through `_nav_graph_for` -> `group.to_local`
  -> `to_global`, the click-target / zone-entry placement pattern (a review correction: the first
  record named that chain as the NPC path). `landing_height_at`'s own doc comment carries the measurement -- Jangan's octagonal
  plaza deck 13.8 units above the terrain at local (985, 1000), against `SURFACE_REACH_UP` 12.0
  (`WORLD_ISSUES.md`'s record of that round: terrain -46.4, the deck `cj_jang_gate` at -32.6).
- `server/internal/worldmap`'s `ToWorld` comment: a real placement row's authored y is not used --
  the client resolves the standing height from the region's walkable graph because the authored y
  and the navmesh disagree by 10-40 units on real rows (the four Mangyang columns in
  `cmd/server/main.go`: authored -29.4, 0.03, -28.4, -30.5 against measured -45.0, -41.4, -39.6,
  -51.9).
- Round 533/534's height path: `_step_monster_bodies` resolved a walking body's height with
  `_terrain_height_at` alone, every `HEIGHT_RESOLVE_STEP` (2) units and for at most
  `MAX_HEIGHT_RESOLVES_PER_FRAME` (32) bodies a frame, round-robin (`MonsterMotion.height_turns`).
  That ray is cast on the terrain layer only (`TERRAIN_ONLY_COLLISION_MASK`, layer 4), so a body
  walking onto a placed structure -- the plaza deck, a bridge, a floor -- was drawn on the ground
  under it.

**Change.**

- `World3D._navmesh_height_at(pos)`: the landing height of the loaded region under a world position,
  through the NPC path, brought back to world space with the group's `to_global`; NAN when no loaded
  region covers the point. `_moving_monster_height_at(pos)`: that, else `_terrain_height_at`.
  `landing_height_at` is the HIGHEST walkable surface, so a body under an overpass is drawn on top of
  it -- the limit the NPC path already has; disclosed at the helper.
- `_step_monster_bodies` resolves with it on the same throttle and budget (nothing in the throttle
  changed); the resolve loop is timed, and the 10-second `monster height resolves` line now carries
  the milliseconds spent and the most in one frame. Under `SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_LOG` -- the env var, not
  the `/wire` switch, because it fires a second ray -- each resolve prints the navmesh and the
  terrain-ray answers side by side.
- `_spawn_or_update_monster`: a list refresh of a WALKING body resolves the same way (the refresh
  books `h_xz`, so the ray's answer would otherwise have stood for the next two units of walking). A
  standing body's placement, live on the public server today, still takes the ray: out of this
  item's scope and disclosed at the helper.
- `MonsterMotion.HEIGHT_RESOLVE_STEP`'s comment and the QA header line for `SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_LOG`.

**Tests (render box).**

- `monster_motion_test.gd`, new `_test_world_height`: a bare World3D (the suite's idiom) given a
  synthetic flat region and a placed 40-unit deck `SURFACE_REACH_UP + 1.8` up (the plaza case,
  `nav_graph_test.gd`'s fixture), a body over it walking a leg, `_step_monster_bodies` once: drawn
  at 13.80, the resolve booked at the body's position, and `_navmesh_height_at` 0 off the deck and
  NAN outside every loaded region. The region's group node must be in the tree for `to_local`, and
  a `--script` suite's root enters the tree only after `_initialize` returns
  (`hud_click_routing_test`'s measurement; this suite's first run printed `!is_inside_tree()` seven
  times), so the check waits one frame behind a 60 s watchdog. The terrain-ray fallback is not
  exercised headless (no physics world on a bare World3D); the live runs below cover it.
- NEGATIVE, proved with only the two production files stashed to BASE (`git stash push --
  client/scripts/World3D.gd client/scripts/world/monster_motion.gd`, shipped with `sync`): `FAIL a
  walking body over a placed deck 13.8 up is drawn on it ... (got y 0.00)`, `1 FAILURES`, exit 1 --
  with `SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid get index 'direct_space_state' (on base: 'null instance'). at:
  _terrain_height_at (World3D.gd:8974)`, the ray with no physics world, and the nonexistent
  `_navmesh_height_at`. Restored (`git stash pop`): `ALL PASS`, no `ERROR:` line.
- `remote_godot.sh tests`: `ran 85 suite(s), 0 failing`; `check`: `checked 256 scripts and 5
  scenes`, `ALL LOAD` (256 is the box's working copy: the repo's 255 plus the stray
  `tools/dump_item.gd`, round 556).
- `cd server && go build ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` green (58 packages `ok`), re-run
  after the doc edits.

**Live (render box, hardware GL): the leg, and the probe that was wrong first.**
`SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_MOVE=-45,180,20,1 SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_LOG=1 qa_shot.sh --server --frames 1300`: the
nearest monster, Yeoha 19 at world (70, -220), sent on a run to (25, -40) -- Jangan local (985,
1000), the plaza deck's measured column. Both runs: 119 resolves, arrival at (25.0, -40.0), no
`SCRIPT ERROR`, 1302 frames, none empty; the frames were deleted.

- **Run 1, the default `--region`, was in the wrong frame.** Every resolve read `navmesh 41.04,
  terrain ray 41.44` from start to arrival, the 0.40 being the ray's own lift (`0.05 x
  PLAYER_SCALE_RATIO`, 0.05 x 14.34 / 1.8). No deck anywhere, including at the column where one is
  recorded 13.8 up. The probe, not the code: `qa_shot.sh` always exports `SRREVAMP_MAPM_PATH` from
  `--region`, whose default is `98\168.m` (the palace, one region north), and
  `_load_initial_region_neighborhood` centres the world on it before it looks at the server session

  `_qa_columns_report` comment already warns of this frame split; round 533's live leg ran in the
  same frame (its numbers were about the walk, not the ground, and stand). Now in `qa_shot.sh`'s
  `--server` note.
- **Run 2, `--region '97\168.m'`, is the measurement.** The navmesh answer is `-30.12` on every
  one of the 119 resolves, from (69.4, -217.7) to (25.0, -40.0); the terrain ray reads `-30.27`
  for the first 92 (0.55 under the surface with its lift removed), then falls from (39.4, -97.8) on
  -- `-31.32, -32.37, ... -43.22` -- to `-43.52` for the last 10, arrival included. With the lift
  removed the terrain at (25, -40) is -43.92, so the deck stands **13.80** above it: the figure
  `landing_height_at`'s comment recorded, reproduced by a different probe (the walking body's own
  resolves against the physics ray; both numbers sit 2.48 above that round's -32.6/-46.4, so the
  region's vertical anchor differs between the two measurements and the difference is what
  matters). Before this round the body would have been drawn 13.8 units down, inside the plaza, for
  the leg's last 40 units.
- **The mid-leg refresh.** The hook asks for the list at half the leg; the list put the monster at
  the server's (70, -220), 93 units from the drawn body -- past `RESYNC_DISTANCE` 32 -- so
  `reconcile` set the body back there and the leg re-walked from the start (`178.5 to go` after
  `95.5 to go`): round 533's rule, on a QA-only move the server never made (round 533's 40-unit leg
  kept the refresh under the 32). The refresh's height came through `_moving_monster_height_at`'s
  walking branch.
- **Cost, from the timed loop.** Run 1's two 10-second windows: `8/s, max 1 in a frame; 3.00 ms in
  them over 10.0 s, max 0.071 ms in a frame` and `3/s ...; 1.31 ms over 10.0 s, max 0.060 ms` --

  `7.75 ms over 10.0 s, max 0.257 ms` -- about 0.23-0.26 ms a resolve in the town, where the
  column's cell lists many placed objects and every triangle of each is tested. Not measured: a
  crowd. At the 32-a-frame budget the town's per-resolve cost extrapolates to about 8 ms in a
  frame -- an extrapolation, not a reading, and the budget bounds it; the constant is not changed
  here on one body's numbers.
- **The `--columns` cross-check, a probe with a different failure mode.** In the server runs the
  columns report printed `region 97/168 is not loaded` (run 1, the named form) and `not standing
  in any loaded region` (run 2, the bare form) six times each: it runs on `_qa_step`'s first tick,

  '97\168.m' --at 1002,1020 --radius 0 --frames 10 --columns '1030,1180;1010,1100;990,1020;985,1000'`,
  the graph's own report, region-local, no physics ray -- read `(1030, 1180): terrain -33.2,

  -32.61], landing -32.6`. One placed surface at -32.61 spans the whole leg, 0.55 over the terrain
  at its start and 13.8 over it at the plaza column -- what the walking body's resolves read, and
  the -32.6 / -46.4 of the round that wrote `landing_height_at`'s comment, to the decimal. Run 2's
  world-frame numbers sit 2.49 above these region-local ones, uniformly, deck and terrain alike;
  the offset between that run's frame (radius 2, a server) and this one's (radius 0, none) was not

## Scripted one-process reconnect: QA hook, texel probe and frame-colour measurement for the white ground (round 558)

Client only, QA tooling: nothing on the wire, no flag, no server change, nothing a player sees.
This round MEASURES the tester's "disconnect and reconnect without closing the client, and the
ground is white" (2026-09-25) in a scripted run, so that the next two items
(`map-object-template-cache`, `map-reconnect-fix`) claim only what a log line supports. Every
number below is from the render box (2026-09-25, hardware GL through VirtualGL, each run under the
box lock as ghidra, this tree's server binary in memory) or from this checkout.

**Grounding, re-read for this round.**

- The disconnect path: `NetClient._process` sees the peer leave `STATUS_CONNECTED` ->
  `disconnect_from_server()` -> `disconnected` -> `World3D._on_disconnected` ->
  `change_scene_to_file(Login)`; `CharacterSelect._on_enter_world_result` ->
  `change_scene_to_file(World3D)` builds a brand-new instance. The System menu's Restart lambda in
  `_try_initialize_pk2_ui` (which `_ready` calls; "`_ready`" until round 564) calls
  `disconnect_from_server()` (whose emit already queues Login) and then queues Login
  itself -- twice, as the plan's citation says; left alone here.
- What outlives a World3D instance, in this checkout: `World3D.gd`'s `static var`s
  (`_ground_texture_cache`, `_water_frames_cache` + `_water_frames_load_attempted`,
  `_environment_table` + `_environment_load_attempted`), the `NetClient` autoload, the root
  viewport's `debug_draw` (`debug_panel._on_draw_mode_selected` sets it; nothing resets it), the
  `Environment_world3d` sub-resource the scene shares and mutates in place, and the function-local
  `templates` dict of `_try_load_real_map_objects` plus `_npc_model_cache` -- template Nodes never
  freed or parented. `/var/tmp/yawshot.log` (a radius-1, 9-region run: nine `ground textures for`
  lines) reports at exit `1234 RID allocations of type 'N5GLES34MeshE'`, `1234 ... 'N5GLES38MaterialE'`,
  `1235 ... 'N5GLES37TextureE'`, `1057 ... 'P11GodotBody3D'` and `1057 ... 'P12GodotShape3D'`.
- Why a live texture cannot draw white by itself (the verifiers' correction, confirmed in code): a
  static Dictionary keeps its `Ref<ImageTexture>`, and every terrain surface's `StandardMaterial3D`
  holds its own Ref (`MapmTerrainBuilder._build_textured_mesh_from_cells`: `albedo_texture` per
  texture pass, `vertex_color_use_as_albedo`, `SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED` when the light is baked,
  albedo `(1, 1, 1, 1)`); the flat fallback is `UNKNOWN_TILE_COLOR` 0.5 grey and prints
  `NOTHING resolved`. The plan's step-7 rule ("white + rid_valid=true => the cached-texture path")
  was therefore inverted and is NOT used; the rule written below is the orchestrator's.
- The marble reference: `docs/WORLD_ISSUES.md`'s two-hundred-and-fifty-second round measured
  `c_marble_jang_02`'s decoded DXT1 top mip at (0.40, 0.38, 0.31) -- a texel mean of one tile
  texture, not a frame mean. It is used here only against the TEXPROBE texel means.
- Server side, reworded from the plan: `Hub.Enter` removes the SAME session id; the first socket's
  entity leaves through `WorldDisconnectHandler -> hub.Leave` when the gateway sees the close, and
  `handleEnterWorld` has no per-character dedupe, so two `QaTester` entities can coexist briefly.

**Change.**

- `World3D._qa_step`: `SRREVAMP_QA_RECONNECT=<tick|drain>`. At that QA tick, or -- `drain` -- on
  the first tick that finds the entry's loading screen up, the env var is cleared and
  `_qa_reconnect` is `call_deferred`: direct route (default) disconnects `_on_disconnected`, drops
  the socket and changes scene straight back to `World3D.tscn`; with
  `SRREVAMP_QA_RECONNECT_VIA_LOGIN=1` it only calls `NetClient.disconnect_from_server()`, the same
  call `NetClient._process` makes when the peer drops, and the tester's path runs from there.
  Deferred because the first run fired it from inside `_physics_process` and the remainder of that
  call ran on the detached node (ten `!is_inside_tree()` errors and a `direct_space_state` on a
  null world at `_physics_process`) -- the hook's own artefact, gone in every later run.
- `World3D._ready`: the entry count lives in `SRREVAMP_QA_ENTRY` (bumped per instance, never a
  static -- statics are what is measured), `QA ENTRY <n>: world instance ...` beside the tables
  line; `QaSignIn.run` now runs only when `NetClient` is not already connected, because a reconnect
  through Login and CharacterSelect arrives signed in as a player does. `_drain_initial_load` prints
  `QA ENTRY <n> loaded: ...` (`RenderingServer.get_rendering_info` texture/buffer/video memory,
  `Performance` object/node/orphan/resource counts and static memory, the viewport's `debug_draw`,
  the static caches with their cached-null count, the baked-light and fog inputs) and one
  `QA TEXPROBE <n> surface <i>: ...` line per surface material of `RealTerrain_<x>_<y>/SubPatch`
  (texture set, RID valid, size, mean of 64 texels read back through `Texture2D.get_image`,
  shading mode, albedo, `vertex_color_use_as_albedo`, transparency, min/mean of the baked vertex
  colours) -- `_qa_print_entry_probe`, `_qa_texel_mean`.
- `World3D._initial_load_done`: the QA shots wait for the entry drain. The negative run showed
  `QA SHOT square frame 13` printed during the sign-in, 160 log lines before `region grid loaded`:
  under the loading-screen drain a shot armed at tick 0 named a frame of no world.
- `Login._qa_sign_in` / `CharacterSelect._qa_start` (both under `SRREVAMP_QA_RECONNECT_VIA_LOGIN`):
  fill the fields from `SRREVAMP_QA_SERVER` and the QA account and press Connect; select the QA
  character in the real list and press Start; the status texts go to the log as
  `QA RECONNECT: Login: ...` / `QA RECONNECT: CharacterSelect: ...`.
- `QaSignIn.account_credentials()` / `character_name()` (shared with the two screens), and a bug
  the first direct run exposed: `who in listed[1]` compared a String against
  `CharacterNet.Summary` objects, so every sign-in after a server's first tried to create the
  character again and stopped at `could not create QaTester (name already taken) -- rendering
  offline`. Unseen while every in-memory QA server was fresh; the reconnect's second sign-in
  reached the same server. Fixed by comparing `char_name`; the second entry then re-enters for
  real (`QaTester is in the world at jangan` twice).
- `qa_shot.sh --reconnect <when>` (exports `SRREVAMP_QA_RECONNECT`, `SRREVAMP_QA_FORCE_LOADING=1`
  so both entries take the real drain -- `drain` cannot fire otherwise -- and `SRREVAMP_QA_NOUI=1`,
  the HUD sits in the measured band) and `--reconnect-via-login`; documented in the header, in
  `client/tools/README.md` and in `World3D.gd`'s QA header.
