| D | direct | `drain`: tick 15, frame 14, 7 cells queued | 197.76 / 52.68 / 250.45 | 5,947 / 14,102 / 470,910 / 110 | 1037.0 | (0.271502, 0.260978, 0.249705) | 0 / 1 (the same line) |

- **The ground is textured on pass 2, on every route.** Pass 2's lower-40% mean is 1e-6 from
  pass 1's at the printed precision (a difference of 0.000001 in red and blue, none in green, in
  `measure.sh`'s six-significant-digit `%[fx:mean]`; round 564 aligned this wording with round
  560's), far from the 0.9 "white" bound.
  Every `QA TEXPROBE 2` line equals its `QA TEXPROBE 1` line: 48 of 48 texture passes
  `rid_valid=true size=512x512`, texel means intact (26 distinct, from (0.16, 0.23, 0.06) to
  (0.54, 0.42, 0.23); one pass reads exactly **(0.40, 0.38, 0.31)**, round 252's offline decode of
  `c_marble_jang_02`, reproduced here by the renderer's own read-back), `shading=0` (unshaded, the
  light is baked), albedo `(1, 1, 1, 1)`, `debug_draw=0`; the `ground textures for 97\168.m -- 26
  ids, 26 resolved` line prints on both passes (it prints on cache hits too). Pass 2's
  `cache_ground=43` with 0 nulls, `cache_water_frames=30`, `env_table=loaded`: the statics are
  simply reused. So, by the orchestrator's rule, case (ii): **not reproduced under Mesa/VirtualGL**
  (radeonsi on the RX 5700 XT through VirtualGL); recorded plainly, not as "does not reproduce"
  -- the tester's machine is Windows, a different driver and a different GL texture path.
- **What a reconnect does cost, measured.** Orphan nodes exactly double, 3,770 -> 7,540 (x2.000)
  on both routes; texture memory 139.96 -> 236.84 MB (x1.69); video memory 186.41 -> 293.45 MB
  (x1.57); buffer memory +10.2 MB; static memory +119.6 MB; the node count returns to 14,102 (the
  tree is rebuilt at the same size) while `objects` grows by ~9,000. The mid-load drop's pass 2
  sits between: 5,947 orphans, 198 MB of textures -- the first instance had built its centre cell,
  one queued cell (7 of the 8 neighbours were still queued when the hook fired: the in-play stream,
  `_process_stream_queue` at one cell a frame, drains the same queue beside the loading screen) and,
  as the next bullet shows, one more batch. The orphans are the never-freed
  per-region `templates` (and `_npc_model_cache`) Nodes; this is the before figure for
  `map-object-template-cache`'s before/after on the SAME `--reconnect` run.
- **The mid-load drop (runs C and D, both routes): what `map-reconnect-fix` guards.**
  `change_scene_to_file` detaches the old instance at once; what the logs show is that it was
  detached and not yet freed when the next `process_frame` reached it (two `!is_inside_tree()`
  errors, then `data.tree` null, and no `previously freed`) -- the order of the engine's own
  free is not read here -- so `_drain_initial_load`, suspended on the loop's `await
  get_tree().process_frame` with 7 cells queued, RESUMES on the detached instance: by the loop's
  own order it builds one more batch
  (`LOADING_CELLS_PER_FRAME` = 2 cells -- the two `!is_inside_tree()` / `get_global_transform`
  errors are that build), updates the screen, and dies at the next await -- the second `await
  get_tree().process_frame` in `_drain_initial_load`, the one at the bottom of the loop -- with
  `SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid get index 'process_frame' (on base: 'null instance'). at:
  _drain_initial_load` plus `ERROR: Parameter "data.tree" is
  null. at: get_tree (scene/main/node.h:413)`. Exactly one SCRIPT ERROR per drop, the same line on
  both routes; `previously freed` / `instance is gone` never appear (the node is detached, not yet
  freed, when it resumes). A tester whose server redeploys mid-load therefore pays one more batch
  of region building into a dead world before the login screen is usable. The guard is an
  `is_inside_tree()` check after each await in the drain (or cancelling it from `_exit_tree`); not
  done here, this round only measures (round 560 guards it; re-anchored there from a code line
  number to the await itself).
- **The Login route works unattended.** Run B: `QA RECONNECT: leaving ... route login` at frame
  200, `Login signing in to 127.0.0.1:15899 as qa at frame 200`, `Login: Login OK.`,
  `CharacterSelect starting QaTester at frame 203`, `entering the world at frame 204`,
  `QA ENTRY 2` at frame 204 with `connected: true` and no second `QA sign-in` (World3D skipped it).
  The only difference from the direct route in the numbers: `resources` 110 -> 112 (two Resource
  objects the two front-end screens leave behind; not chased).
- **Server log.** Each run's `server.log` has two `session disconnected` lines -- the first at the
  reconnect (e.g. run A2 `04:43:11.951Z` against the hook's fire) and the second at exit -- and
  logs no entry, so the window in which two `QaTester` entities coexist is not readable from it;
  the transient duplicate is accepted and recorded, not measured.
- The frame files and the `f.wav`s (3.0 GB) were deleted after measuring; the logs stay under
  `/var/tmp/r558/` with `run.sh` and `measure.sh`, the exact commands.

**Decision rule for the next two items (the orchestrator's, not the plan's).** (i) pass-2 frame
>= 0.9 with `rid_valid=true`, sizes intact, texture/video memory roughly doubled -> resource
growth is the live hypothesis, tested by `map-object-template-cache`'s before/after on the same
run; (ii) pass 2 textured within a few % of pass 1's own mean -> not reproduced on the box, ship the
hygiene items, the tester's log decides; (iii) `debug_draw=<n>` with n != 0 -> the persisted
viewport state (only if a tester touched Ctrl+F3 Draw). **This round lands in (ii)** on both
routes and both timings, with the growth of (i) measured regardless (x2.00 orphans, x1.69 texture
memory per reconnect). One more measured fact narrows the tester's picture: on 42 of the 48
texture passes the baked vertex colour is `vcol_min=1.000 vcol_mean=1.000` (diffuse 0.7255 plus
terrain ambient 0.9985 clamps to 1), so the texture is the ground's only colour source there, and
a sampler that resolves to GLES3's default white texture draws exactly white -- the tester's
symptom -- while a missing texture draws the 0.5-grey flat fallback. Which of the two it was is in
the tester's log.

**The tester's log decides, in minutes** (`user://logs/srrevamp.log` from a reconnect, the SECOND
`character/item/NPC tables loaded` block): its `ground textures for 97\168.m -- N ids, N
resolved` line (or `NOTHING resolved, the region draws the flat fallback`), any `pk2: could not
open`, any `SCRIPT ERROR` / `previously freed` between the two blocks, and whether the buildings
and water were white too (a static cache explains neither). The orchestrator is asking for that log
in parallel.

**Records.** This entry; `docs/WORLD_ISSUES.md`'s five-hundred-and-fifty-eighth round (the table);
`client/tools/README.md` and `qa_shot.sh`'s header (`--reconnect`, `--reconnect-via-login`, the
measurement); `World3D.gd`'s QA header. `docs/SYSTEMS.md` has no row for world loading or the
client's reconnect, so nothing there to change.

**Deploy note.** Nothing to deploy: QA hooks, prints and two QA-only fixes (the sign-in's name
check, the shots' wait for the drain). Not tag-worthy on its own.

## One object template per .bsr per world, freed with the world: no re-parse per region and no leaked scenery templates (round 559)

Client only, tag-worthy: faster region loads where models repeat (towns especially) and no GPU/RAM
growth per region load, zone change or reconnect. Nothing on the wire, no flag, no server change.
Visuals unchanged by construction -- a placement is still a `duplicate()` of the same built
template -- and measured below against the before run's own frame. Every number is from the
render box (2026-09-25, hardware GL through VirtualGL) or from this checkout.

**Grounding, re-read for this round.**

- `World3D._try_load_real_map_objects` at BASE (`6787d63`): `var templates := {} # resolved .bsr
  path -> loaded template Node3D`, `node = templates[entry.path].duplicate()`, the template never
  parented and never freed -- one dictionary per CALL, i.e. per region. Contrast `_npc_model_cache`,
  instance-level and cross-region (and also never freed; not this round's). `ObjectLoader.load_object`
  builds a `MeshInstance3D` plus a `StaticBody3D`/trimesh per piece with geometry, and
  `build_godot_material` decoded and uploaded a fresh `ImageTexture` per material. `World3D.gd` had
  no `_exit_tree`.
- The leak, measured before this change on the identical command (run `before`, below): at exit
  `2468 RID allocations of type 'N5GLES34MeshE' were leaked at exit`, 2468 Material, 2469 Texture,
  2468 `RendererSceneCull::Instance`, 2114 `GodotBody3D`, 2114 `GodotShape3D`, 10,447 `leaked`
  lines -- twice `/var/tmp/yawshot.log`'s single-entry 1234 / 1234 / 1235 / 1057 / 1057, which is
  a radius-1, 9-cell run (the verifiers' correction, not radius 2). Orphan nodes 3,770 -> 7,540
  across the reconnect, x2.000 (round 558's figure, reproduced).
- Why freeing a template is safe for placed copies: `Node.duplicate()` copies the node tree and
  shares its Resources (Mesh, Material, Texture) by reference, so a template's own cost is its
  Nodes and their instance/body/shape RIDs. The census agrees: every leaked Body/Shape (2114) was
  a template piece, and the meshes and textures still reported after this change, 354 and 355,
  are exactly 2468 - 2114 and 2469 - 2114 -- the leaked pieces that had no `StaticBody3D`
  (scenery pieces with geometry always get one, skinned NPC pieces never do), consistent with
  `_npc_model_cache`'s templates, which `map-reconnect-fix` frees. Consistent with, not proven
  from the census alone.
- `ObjectLoader.find_file` compares names lower-cased, so the cache keys (model path, texture
  path) are lower-cased too.
- The 600-template cap is an own safety limit, disclosed in the code comment, not a game value: a
  radius-1 Jangan grid holds 226 (below).

**Change.**

- `client/scripts/world/object_template_cache.gd` (new, `ObjectTemplateCache`, RefCounted):
  `instance(path, region_key)` builds a template once per lower-cased path through a loader
  Callable and returns a `duplicate()` per placement, recording the region as a user;
  `release_region(key)` frees the templates whose last using region left; `forget_regions()` (a
  zone change) withdraws every use but keeps the templates; `free_all()`; `NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE`
  frees whatever is still held; a cap (`DEFAULT_MAX_TEMPLATES` 600) evicts the oldest, unused
  first, and prints each eviction pass. A failed load is not cached, as before. Counters `loads`,
  `reuses`, `evictions`.
- `World3D`: `_object_templates` (built on first use with `_load_object_template`, the
  ObjectLoader call against this world's Data.pk2) and `_object_textures` replace the per-call
  dictionary; `_try_load_real_map_objects` keys placements by the region's own `.o` path;
  `_maybe_stream_regions`' unload releases that key (`region x/y unloaded -- N scenery templates
  only it placed freed, M held`); `_clear_region_grid` calls `forget_regions()`; the new
  `_exit_tree` frees them all (`left the tree -- N scenery templates freed`) and clears the
  texture cache. The load print gains `%d templates reused, %d held for the world`; its `distinct
  real models` now counts every distinct model path the table resolved for the region, loaded or
  not (BASE counted loaded templates only: 97\169 reads 63 here against 61 before, two of its
  models fail to load). `QA ENTRY` gains `object_templates=%d object_textures=%d`; the
  loading-screen drain's `region grid loaded` line gains the same `(terrain, objects, npcs)` split
  the synchronous QA path already printed.
- `ObjectLoader.load_object` / `_load_compound_object` / `build_godot_material` take an optional
  `texture_cache: Dictionary` (`.ddj` path, lower-cased -> `{texture, four_cc}`), passed down the
  compound recursion; only a decoded texture is remembered, a miss reports and retries as before. A
  call without one gets a fresh dictionary per call (checked: two plain loads do not share), so the
  pieces of one object share their textures and nothing outlives the call. `SkinnedBsrAssembler`,
  `GroundItems` and `check_npc_models` call it as before.

**Tests.**

- NEGATIVE, proven with only the production files at BASE (`git stash push -u --
  client/scripts/World3D.gd client/scripts/assets/object_loader.gd
  client/scripts/world/object_template_cache.gd`; the new and changed tests shipped with
  `remote_godot.sh sync`): `object_template_cache_test.gd` fails to parse (`Identifier
  "ObjectTemplateCache" not declared in the current scope`), `object_loader_test.gd` fails to parse
  (`Too many arguments for "load_object()" call. Expected at most 2 but received 3`); and the
  `before` reconnect run below is the same command on that tree -- orphans x2.000, the 2468 / 2469 /
  2114 census. Restored with `git stash pop`.
- POSITIVE: `object_template_cache_test.gd` (new, 31 checks): one build for three placements over
  two regions and three spellings; each placement its own copy, per-placement state never on the
  template; a failed load asked again and not held; `release_region` frees only the template whose
  last user left while placed copies survive; `forget_regions` keeps a template, the next zone
  reuses it, its new last user frees it; `free_all`, and deleting the cache frees what it still
  held; a cap of 2 evicts the unused before the older in-use, then the oldest, and a placed copy
  survives its template's eviction. `object_loader_test.gd` gains the texture-cache case (four
  pieces over two loads through one cache share one texture, held under `prim/mtrl/walltex.ddj`;
  two plain loads give two). Both `ALL PASS` on the box; `remote_godot.sh check`: `checked 258
  scripts and 5 scenes`, `ALL LOAD`; `remote_godot.sh tests`: `ran 86 suite(s), 0 failing` (85 before plus the new one).
- Two defects the first positive run caught, both fixed before the final live run: (1)
  `free_all()` from `_notification(NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE)` on a RefCounted is `Attempt to call
  function 'free_all' in base 'null instance'` -- at its predelete the object has no reference
  left, so `self` as a call base is null; the freeing is inlined there (members and the
  templates' own methods are reachable), and the run `after` shows the error twice where `after2`
  shows none. (2) A `replace_all` of `parsed_tex.four_cc` -> `four_cc` also rewrote the new
  assignment into `four_cc = four_cc`, so the flag-less fallback treated every texture as
  uncompressed; `object_loader_test.gd`'s existing DXT3 case (`real DXT3 alpha yields the real
  cutout foliage material`) failed and named it.
- `cd server && go build ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` green before and after the doc
  edits.

**Live (render box).** Round 558's command (`qa_shot.sh --server --region '97\168.m' --radius 1
--frames 400 --reconnect 200 --shots 'square@1002,1020:0,-25,700'`, round 558's server binary --
`server/` is unchanged since `504b68f`), `before` with production at BASE, `after2` with the code

## No state crosses World3D instances: per-instance asset caches, an _exit_tree that frees the templates and resets the viewport, one change_scene on Restart (round 560)

Client only, hygiene, tag-worthy together with round 559 (one client release after both): a second
login in one client process starts from nothing the first one built. Nothing on the wire, no flag,
no server change. **What this round does not claim**: that it cures the tester's white ground after
a reconnect. Round 558 did not reproduce that on the render box (pass 2's lower-40% frame mean
1e-6 from pass 1's at the printed precision, on both routes and both timings, Mesa/VirtualGL), and
this round's runs say the same after the change; the tester's `user://logs/srrevamp.log` from a reconnect
decides it (below, "Deploy note"). What this round removes is every piece of World3D state that
outlived the instance, each measured or read in rounds 558/559, with the before/after on round
558's own command. Every number is from the render box (2026-09-25, hardware GL through VirtualGL,
lane-local lock `/var/tmp/r560/lock`, round 558's server binary -- `server/` is unchanged since
`504b68f`) or from this checkout.

**Grounding, re-read for this round.**

- The five `static var`s in `World3D.gd` at BASE (`e9c203b`): `_ground_texture_cache`,
  `_water_frames_cache`, `_water_frames_load_attempted`, `_environment_table`,
  `_environment_load_attempted` (`grep -n 'static var' client/scripts`: five in `World3D.gd`; the
  other four statics in `client/scripts` (three files; "three" until round 564) -- `ui_builder.gd`'s `_flat_texture`, a 1x1 white UI
  texture, `regioninfo_names.gd`'s `_overrides`, `object_loader.gd`'s `missing_count` /
  `missing_recent` -- are not world state and are left alone). A GDScript static is one value per
  loaded script, not per instance (the GDScript reference, "Static variables"); round 558 measured
  it: entry 2 printed `cache_ground=43 (0 nulls) cache_water_frames=30 env_table=loaded` before it
  had loaded a region, and this round's BASE run below decodes 0 ground textures on entry 2.
- `_npc_model_cache`'s doc comment: "The template is never parented, so unloading a region frees
  the duplicates, not it" -- never freed anywhere at BASE. Round 559's exit census after freeing the
  scenery templates still reported 354 meshes / 354 materials / 355 textures / 354 scene-cull
  instances, consistent with these (not proven from the census).
- `debug_panel._on_draw_mode_selected` sets `get_viewport().debug_draw = mode`; nothing in
  `client/scripts` resets it; the viewport is the root Window, which outlives every scene.
- The Restart lambda (`World3D._try_initialize_pk2_ui`, which `_ready` calls -- "`World3D._ready`"
  until round 564; `system_restart_requested`) called
  `NetClient.disconnect_from_server()` and then `change_scene_to_file(Login)`;
  `NetClient.disconnect_from_server` emits `disconnected` unconditionally, and `_on_disconnected`
  (connected in `_ready`) already changes scene to Login -- the Log Out button relies on exactly
  that (`_on_disconnect_pressed` only disconnects).
- `World3D.tscn`'s `Environment_world3d` sub-resource had no `resource_local_to_scene`, so every
  instance of the scene shared one `Environment`. Its writes in `World3D.gd` are all absolute
  (`sky`, `background_mode` in `_try_add_real_sky`; `ambient_light_color` in
  `_apply_real_environment_lighting`; the fog block's `fog_enabled` / `fog_light_color` /
  `fog_density` / `fog_sun_scatter` / `fog_aerial_perspective`; `SRREVAMP_QA_NOFOG`'s fog-off
  writes), so it was benign by reading -- mutated idempotently, as the grounding verifier said.
- The mid-load drop: round 558's runs C and D, re-anchored this round from a code line number to
  the await itself -- the second `await get_tree().process_frame` in `_drain_initial_load`, the
  one at the bottom of its loop -- and its wording softened to what the logs show (detached and not
  yet freed when the next `process_frame` reached it: two `!is_inside_tree()` errors, then
  `data.tree` null, no `previously freed`). Reproduced at BASE on this tree before the change
  (below).
- `hud_window_test.gd`'s `_initialize()` pattern: a script that needs the `NetClient` autoload
  compiles there and not in `_init`. `World3D.gd`'s instance initialisers are constants, env reads
  and one `preload`, so `S.new()` headless is feasible (the grounding verifier's check, confirmed by
  the suite running).

**Change.**

- `World3D.gd`: the five statics are instance vars, doc comments updated; `_load_real_ground_textures`'
  per-region line gains `, D decoded now in M ms` (after `N ids, N resolved`, which round 558's
  tester instructions and measure scripts grep), and `_load_real_water_animation` prints `water
  animation -- N of 30 frames decoded in M ms` once per world -- the price of the change, on the
  tester's own log.
- `World3D._exit_tree` (round 559's, extended): frees the scenery templates and clears the texture
  cache as before; frees every `_npc_model_cache` template (`character.skeleton.free()`, the
  never-parented root) and clears the dictionary; clears the five caches; frees a loading screen
  still up; resets the root viewport's `debug_draw` to `DEBUG_DRAW_DISABLED` (null-guarded for a
  detached call); prints `left the tree -- N scenery templates and M NPC templates freed`. The
  reset lives here and not in the debug panel's Close button because a draw mode is chosen to look
  at the world with the panel out of the way; the panel now reads the viewport's mode when it is
  built (`debug_panel._build_tools_row`), so its dropdown says what is drawn.
- `_drain_initial_load`: `if not is_inside_tree(): return` after each of its three awaits (the
  first frame, the loop's, the closing one) -- a socket drop while it is suspended has
  `_on_disconnected` change scene, which removes this instance at once, and out of the tree there
  is nothing to load for. The same one-line guard after `_on_change_zone_result`'s `await

  always passes `--write-movie`; Godot 4.2's command line reference says of `--write-movie`
  "`--fixed-fps` is forced when enabled" and of `--fixed-fps <fps>` "Force a fixed number of
  frames per second. This setting disables real-time synchronization"; the ProjectSettings
  reference: `editor/movie_writer/fps = 60`, "Simulation speed will adjust to always match the
  specified framerate" (`client/project.godot` sets no `movie_writer` key). The project had met it
  already: `World3D.gd`'s worldmap hook comment ("movie-writing mode advances scene time by a
  fixed 1/60 a frame regardless of how long the frame really took") and `docs/TODO.md`'s
  tester-tools item (5), the `SceneTreeTimer` that did not fire under the writer.
- `World3D` has no `_process`; its per-frame work is `_physics_process` (no `await` in it,
  checked, so a timing wrapper is safe) plus what the drain's `process_frame` coroutine builds
  outside any callback of this scene. `_load_tile_index` and `_load_npc_tables` are cached after
  the first call (their own guards), which is why the centre cell's laps below carry them whole.
- The crossing start: `walk_probe.gd --region=97/168 --from=120,1020 --heading=270 --steps=400`
  walks terrain at y 0.0 to local -280 with 0 wall contacts; from (150, 1020) the probe starts on
  `cj_armo[19]` and meets a wall at x 138. The probe's heading is region-local (motion (sin h, cos
  h)), so 270 is -x, the direction the live client's world heading 270 walks (memory
  `reference_qa_walk_gotchas`). The run speed is the character table's 50 units a second

## The loading screen is up before the first cell builds, and it reuses the held Media.pk2 handle (round 562)

Client only, tag-worthy: the first visible fix of the map/loading epic (2026-09-25), to ship in the
next tag. Nothing on the wire, no flag, no server change. Every number below is from the render box
(2026-09-25, hardware GL through VirtualGL, lane lock `/var/tmp/r562/lock`, round 558's server
binary -- `server/` is unchanged since `504b68f`, `git diff --stat` between it and BASE empty) or
from this checkout.

**Grounding, re-read for this round.**

- The order at BASE (`e2a65df`): `World3D._ready` ran `_load_initial_region_neighborhood()` (the
  synchronous centre cell), `_try_initialize_pk2_ui()`, `_try_load_cursors()` and only then
  `await _drain_initial_load(_t_region)`, whose screen branch did `_loading_screen =
  LoadingScreen.new()` and awaited one frame before its first batch. `_show_loading_screen()`
  served the teleport path alone (`_on_change_zone_result` awaits it before `_reload_zone_assets`),
  and the drain reused a screen a caller had put up. So the entry's centre cell was built with no
  screen in existence: round 561's baseline log (`/var/tmp/r561/entry.log`) has no `LoadingScreen`
  line at all, and `cell 97/168 built in 5373 ms at frame 13`.
- `LoadingScreen._init(backdrop_ddj)` took no archive; its `_ready` called `FrontEndUi.open_media()`,
  which is `Pk2Reader.open(Pk2Config.media_path())` -- a reader of its own on every login and every
  teleport, while `World3D._media_pk2` was already open (`_load_character_assets` at the top of
  `_ready`; `_open_media_pk2_if_set` returns it, or opens it for a world without character tables).
  Media.pk2 is 1,547,583,488 bytes on the box (`ls -l /opt/sro-files/client/Media.pk2`). The
  feasibility verifier's correction stands: `Pk2Reader.open` reads the 256-byte header and walks
  directories lazily (`_read_block_chain`, cached per reader), so the saving was to be measured by
  the new print, never taken from round 160's ~1 s, and the NEGATIVE is "no `media` line / a second
  reader", not a non-zero time.
- CanvasItem draw order is child order, and `ui_control.add_child` for the minimap, world map,
  underbar, player info, panels and chat all run inside `_try_initialize_pk2_ui`, after the point
  where the screen now goes up (the grounding verifier's finding, answered with
  `cover_siblings()` after the HUD is built).
- `SRREVAMP_QA_NOUI=1` hides `$UI/Control` on the first physics tick (`_qa_step`), and the screen
  is that Control's child, so the benchmark's own frames can never show it: the benchmark proves
  the order by its log, and a run without `NOUI` proves it on the frames.
- The plan's "black window" is not what a QA run's frames show (below: the placeholder scene). A
  real player's window before this round kept whatever it had drawn last while the main thread
  built the centre cell; nothing here calls it black.
- The plan's "frame 0" was a guess too: the QA sign-in awaits ahead of the world, so the screen's
  frame is 13 in every run here, one before the centre cell's 14 -- the order is the measurement,
  not the absolute frame.

**Change** (client only: `World3D.gd`, `ui/loading_screen.gd`, `tools/README.md`, and the new
`ui/loading_screen_test.gd`).

- `World3D._ready`: `var screen_frames: int = await _show_loading_screen()` before
  `_load_initial_region_neighborhood()`, with round 560's `is_inside_tree()` guard after the await;
  after `_try_initialize_pk2_ui()` and `_try_load_cursors()`, `_loading_screen.cover_siblings()`
  puts the screen back over the HUD; `_drain_initial_load(_t_region, screen_frames)` so the
  `region grid loaded` line's awaited-frame count covers the span its total covers (the clock
  `_t_region` stays ahead of the screen, so the total compares with round 561's).
- `_show_loading_screen() -> int` builds `LoadingScreen.new(LoadingScreen.DEFAULT_BACKDROP,
  _open_media_pk2_if_set())` and returns the frames it awaited (1, or 0 under QA / with a screen
  already up). The drain's own fallback creation passes the same handle.
- `_drain_initial_load` draws one frame before its first batch whether or not it made the screen,
  and the gauge counts the centre cell (`total = queue + 1`, the first tick `1 / total`). This is
  the round's own finding, not the plan's: the first AFTER run (`/var/tmp/r562/entry1.log`) had the
  drain's first batch join the centre cell's frame -- the await that used to separate them was the
  screen's creation, which moved -- and the benchmark's longest work frame read `7506 ms at frame
  14 (cell 97/167)` for a 5,234 ms centre cell. The player sees the same frozen art either way;
  the metric the later items are measured on has to read the centre cell alone.
- `_qa_step`'s `--reconnect drain` hook gains `and not _load_queue.is_empty()`: with the screen up
  from before the centre cell, "the first tick that finds the screen up" is `_ready`'s own await
  with nothing queued; the hook keeps round 558's meaning (mid-drain, cells queued). QA header
  updated.
- `LoadingScreen._init(backdrop_ddj := DEFAULT_BACKDROP, media: Pk2Reader = null)`; `_ready` uses
  the handle when given (`media_source = "reused"`), else the old `open_media()` path (`"opened"`,
  timed in `media_open_ms`, or `"none"`); prints `LoadingScreen: up at frame %d (media %s, %d ms;
  backdrop %s, %d ms; built in %d ms)`; `cover_siblings()` is `move_child` to the last index, a
  no-op without a parent.

## Streaming unload forgets the region: NPCs respawn on return and per-region caches stop growing (round 563)

Client only, tag-worthy: the third item of the map/loading epic (2026-09-25), required for the
whole-map walk. Nothing on the wire, no flag, no server change (`server/` untouched; `go build`
and `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` green before and after the doc edits). Every number below is a
log line from the render box (2026-09-25, hardware GL through VirtualGL, lane lock
`/var/tmp/r563/lock` -- the box lock is still held by round 558's orphaned re-run -- no server,
the QA path's synchronous grid at `--radius 1`) or from this checkout; the runs and how to read
them are in `client/tools/README.md` (the `--shots` paragraph).

**Grounding, re-read at BASE (`b402675`).**

- `World3D._maybe_stream_regions`' unload loop, for every loaded cell outside
  `_region_load_radius() + 1`: `queue_free()` of `RealTerrain_<x>_<y>` and `RealMapObjects_<x>_<y>`,
  `_object_templates.release_region()` (round 559) and `_loaded_cells.erase(key)`. Nothing else.
- `_try_spawn_region_npcs` returned at its first line on `_npc_regions_done.has("x_y")`, set the
  mark after finding the region's terrain group, and parented every `Npc_<id>_<n>` holder to that
  group -- so the unload freed the NPCs with the terrain and left the mark. `grep` at BASE: the mark
  was cleared in `_clear_region_grid` (a zone change) and nowhere else.
- `_region_nav_graphs` (an Array of `[NavGraph, Node3D]`) was appended in `_build_region_nav_graph`
  and cleared in `_clear_region_grid` only; `_nav_graph_for` did `var group: Node3D = pair[1]`
  BEFORE its `is_instance_valid` check.
- `_navmesh_cache` (key `(x << 8) | y`, `_load_region_navmesh`), `_parsed_region_heightmaps`
  (`"x_y"`, `_parsed_region_heightmap`, filled for a region's eight neighbours by
  `_placements_belonging_here` whether or not they are cells) and `_object_collision_cache`
  (resource id, `_load_object_collision`): no `erase` or `clear` anywhere in the client.
- One reader outside `World3D.gd`: `monster_motion_test.gd` appended a pair to
  `world.get("_region_nav_graphs")`.
- `docs/SYSTEMS.md` has no row for world loading, streaming or the client's NPC placement
  (re-checked: `stream|unload|respawn|prune|region grid` hit only the item, packet and monster rows),
  so nothing there to change; `docs/TODO.md` has no map/loading section.

**The baseline, measured before any edit** (`/var/tmp/r563/before.log`; the box's client copy
byte-identical to BASE, `World3D.gd` md5 `4bf3246d…`). The tour: `--region '97\168.m' --radius 1
--at 1002,1020 --frames 270 --shots "w1@-30,1020;w2@-30,1020;w3@-30,1020;e1@1950,1020;

rows match exactly, `AGENTS.md`), 28 ticks a hop. What BASE did with it:

- The grid: `region grid loaded in 11497 ms … 9 cells` at frame 0, then the /166 row; `18/19 NPC(s)
  placed in 97/168`, `7/7 … in 97/169`, `2/2 … in 98/169`, `8/8 … in 97/167`.

**Change** (client only: `World3D.gd`, the new `world/region_grid_state.gd` and its suite,
`world/monster_motion_test.gd`, `tools/README.md`).

- `RegionGridState` (RefCounted, per World3D instance as `_grid`): `loaded_cells` ("dx_dy" ->
  `Vector2i(region_x, region_y)`, so an unload by region finds its cell), `queued_cells`,
  `npc_regions_done`, `nav_graphs` ("x_y" -> `[NavGraph, Node3D]`), `navmesh_cache`,
  `parsed_heightmaps`, `object_collision_cache`; `mark_loaded`, `mark_npcs_done` / `npcs_done`,
  `add_nav_graph`, `nav_graph_for_region` and `nav_graph_pairs()` (both test `is_instance_valid`
  before anything is assigned typed); **`unload(x, y)`** drops the region's cell, NPC mark, nav
  graph, navmesh and heightmap, then `prune_heightmaps()` (heightmaps of regions neither loaded
  nor next to a loaded one) and `prune_object_collisions()` (ids no cached navmesh lists), and
  returns the names of what it dropped; `clear_all()`; `counts_line()`.
- `World3D`: every site of the seven members reads the state; `_maybe_stream_regions`' unload loop
  counts the terrain node's `Npc_` children, keeps round 559's release and line, then calls
  `_grid.unload()` and prints `World3D: region x/y forgotten -- <what>; N NPC holder(s) freed with
  its terrain`; `_clear_region_grid` calls `clear_all()`; `_nav_graph_for` iterates
  `nav_graph_pairs()`; `_nav_graph_for_region` and `_place_at_region_local` read the dictionary;
  `_try_spawn_region_npcs` documents why its guard now clears on unload; `_qa_advance_shots`
  prints a `QA GRID <name> frame <n> at <x/y> local <lx>,<lz>: <counts> object_templates=…
  objects=… orphans=… static_mem=…` line beside each `QA SHOT` line (a line of its own, so the
  `QA SHOT … frame n` contract is untouched).
- `monster_motion_test.gd` injects its pair through `_grid.add_nav_graph`.

## Terrain cells prepared on a worker thread (read, parse, images, mesh arrays) and committed on the main thread (round 565)

Client only, tag-worthy: the loading-freeze item of the map/loading epic (2026-09-25). Nothing on
the wire, no flag, no server change (`server/` untouched; `go build ./...` and `go test -count=1
-p 1 ./...` green before and after the doc edits). A streamed region cell's terrain -- the `.m`
read and parse, the `.t` lightmap and the ground tiles decoded to Images, the mesh surfaces and
the collision faces as arrays, the navmesh, the wall triangles and the walkable graph -- now
prepares on a `WorkerThreadPool` task, and only its commit (the uploads, the nodes, the shapes,
the water, the graph's registration) runs on the main thread; the objects and NPC phases stay
synchronous in the commit's frame. `SRREVAMP_SYNC_LOAD=1` restores the synchronous schedule for
one release (the schedule, not the pre-change code: "Also measured" below; worded "path" until
round 568). Every number below is a log line from the render box (2026-09-25, hardware GL through
VirtualGL, lane lock `/var/tmp/r565/lock`, round 558's server binary) or from this checkout; the
logs are `/var/tmp/r565/{base_entry,base_cross,after_entry,after_cross,sync_cross,drain,qa}.log`
with `run.sh` and `after.sh`, the exact commands (frames deleted).

**Grounding, re-read at BASE (`d255c92`).**

- `World3D._load_region_cell` called `_try_load_real_terrain`, `_try_load_real_map_objects` and
  `_try_spawn_region_npcs` back to back on the main thread, and `_try_load_real_terrain` built
  everything from the file read to the nav graph inside one call; `grep -rn
  "Thread\|WorkerThreadPool\|Mutex" client/scripts` was empty. `docs/WORLD_ISSUES.md`, round 154:
  "it does not thread the build, so a very heavy cell can still hitch -- threading the region
  build off the main thread is the next step if it is still felt" (the quote's last four words
  restored in round 568).
- `Pk2Reader`: one `_file: FileAccess` per handle, `read_file` = `seek` + `get_buffer`,
  `_read_block_chain` a seek and a get_buffer per block, `_dir_cache` per handle -- not
  thread-safe, and every World3D reader shares the world's three handles.
- Godot 4.2's "Thread-safe APIs" page (fetched 2026-09-25): "Interacting with the active scene
  tree is **NOT** thread-safe"; "creating scene chunks (nodes in tree arrangement) outside the
  active tree is fine"; resources "can be loaded and manipulated on a thread"; "Accessing servers
  from threads is supported (for RenderingServer and Physics servers, ensure threaded or
  thread-safe operation is enabled in the project settings!)". `client/project.godot` sets
  neither; read on the box's 4.2.2 (a throwaway `--script`, deleted):
  `rendering/driver/threads/thread_model` 1 (Single-Safe), `physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread`
  false, `threading/worker_pool/low_priority_thread_ratio` 0.3, 10 cores. The WorkerThreadPool
  4.2 reference: `add_task(action, high_priority = false, description = "")`, and
  `wait_for_task_completion` returns `ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER` for a task that was "already awaited
  and disposed of" -- waiting is what disposes of a task.
- The BEFORE, re-measured today on BASE with the README's two commands (the box's client copy
  md5-identical to BASE): see the tables below. Round 561's figures (centre 5,373, crossing 328)
  were from before rounds 562-563; today's BASE is what this round is measured against.

**The findings and the orchestrator's notes, answered.**

- *The QA path* (verifier (a)): `_drain_initial_load`'s no-screen branch dispatches, waits for
  each task (`_pump_cell_jobs(TERRAIN_JOBS_IN_FLIGHT, wait = true)`) and commits every cell before
  it returns. Measured (`qa.log`, `--radius 2`, no server, no `FORCE_LOADING`): all 25 `built in`
  lines `at frame 0`, `region grid loaded in 12465 ms ... at frame 0`, then `QA SHOT square frame
  13` -- the contract holds.
- *The bound* (verifier (b), the orchestrator's acceptance): measured, below -- the crossing's
  longest work frame 334 -> 144 ms. The verifier was right that `create_trimesh_shape()` would stay
  in the commit; this round does not keep it: the prepare builds the face list the trimesh would
  have read back out of the mesh (`MapmTerrainBuilder.surface_faces`, held equal to
  `create_trimesh_shape().get_faces()` element for element by the builder's suite), and the commit
  calls `ConcavePolygonShape3D.set_faces` alone -- the `collision` lap fell from 52-61 ms a cell to
  25-33 with the shape unchanged. `NavGraph.build` moved into the prepare as suggested (its inputs
  -- the navmesh, Data.pk2 behind the new lock, the object index and a copy of the object
  navigation meshes -- are all in the job).
- *The prepare-thread rule* (verifier (c), orchestrator): written at `World3D._terrain_prepare`
  and in `client/tools/README.md`, "Load benchmark" (rules 1-4). `_terrain_prepare` and its
  helpers are `static`, so they cannot reach the node's state; they print none of their own lines
  (those go in the job, printed in order by the commit) -- a reader they call may still
  `push_error` from the task on a malformed file (`DdjReader.to_image`, `MapmTerrainBuilder`,
  `MapmReader`, `NvmReader`; "print nothing" until round 568) -- and record their laps in the job (LoadTimings is the
  main thread's).
- *The cache race* (verifier (d)): `_terrain_job` snapshots, on the main thread before dispatch,
  the ground-tile cache as filename -> decoded flag (never the texture), the region's cached
  navmesh and a copy of the object-collision cache; the commit merges back what the prepare read
  (a tile another job's commit uploaded first is kept). `_last_terrain_shadow_map`, a member the
  lightmap loader stashed for the mesh builder, is gone -- the map travels in the job (at BASE a
  region without a `.t` handed the builder the previous region's, harmless only because the
  builder does not apply it, `MapmTerrainBuilder._shadow_at`).
- *Three sittings* (verifier (e)): one round, as the item was issued, in three parts each with its
  own test and negative -- the Pk2Reader lock, the builder's surfaces split, the job pipeline.
- *The co-pumped queue* (round 561's correction): `_pump_cell_jobs` is the one place that
  dispatches and commits; while `_drain_initial_load` runs it is the only caller
  (`_drain_pumping` makes `_process_stream_queue` step aside). Per frame under the screen: at most
  `LOADING_CELLS_PER_FRAME` = 2 commits, as many as have finished -- the logs show two `built in`
  lines at each of frames 15-26 (entry) and 17-28 (crossing), against three at 14-21 at BASE. The
  gauge is `1 - (queued + preparing) / total`.
- *Headless negatives*: (a) the concurrent reads fail without the lock -- 11, 10 and 13 of 800
  wrong in three runs, so it did not happen to pass; (b) the surfaces path fails to parse against
  the pre-split builder; (c) the forbidden-object walk, with a positive control of its own (it
  finds a mesh in an Array, a Node in a Dictionary, a shape, and an ImageTexture inside a reader
  struct's variable).
- *The stale-cell guard and the exit*: a prepared cell is committed only if it is still wanted
  (`cell x/y prepared but not committed -- already loaded | the player left its window while it
  prepared`); `_clear_region_grid`, `_load_region_neighborhood` and `_exit_tree` wait for every
  task still running and drop it (`N cell(s) still preparing dropped (<why>) -- waited M ms`).
  Round 558's `--reconnect drain` variant (`drain.log`): `QA RECONNECT: leaving the world at frame
  15, tick 15 (drain, route direct, entry 1, 6 cells still queued, 2 preparing)`, then `World3D: 2
  cell(s) still preparing dropped (the world left the tree) -- waited 18.8 ms for their tasks`,
  entry 2 loaded and shot; **0 `SCRIPT ERROR`**, and the `ERROR:` set identical to round 560's
  drain run (two missing `.bsr`s, the gacha machine, the exit-time texture leak). The hook fires on
  queued OR preparing cells now.

**What changed.**

- `pk2/pk2_reader.gd`: `_lock` (a `Mutex` per handle) around `read_file`, `_read_block_chain`
  (its body is `_read_block_chain_locked`) and `close`.
- `assets/mapm_terrain_builder.gd`: `build_full_region_surfaces_textured` (the surfaces as data:
  arrays, texture key, blend, unshaded; `texture_lookup` read for its keys only),
  `surfaces_to_mesh` + `_surface_material` (the ArrayMesh and the materials the builder always
  made), `surface_faces` (the trimesh's faces, each corner snapped to 0.0001 -- the snap is what the
  suite measured, on off-grid heights), `build_full_region_arrays` / `arrays_to_mesh` (the
  untextured surface). `_build_textured_mesh_from_cells` became `_textured_surfaces_from_cells`,
  returning data; `build_full_region_mesh(_textured)` are built on top, unchanged for callers.
- `ddj/ddj_reader.gd`: `to_image` (everything `to_texture` did before its `ImageTexture`);
  `mapt/mapt_reader.gd`: `parse(data, with_texture = true)` with an `image` field for
  `with_texture` false.
- `world/load_timings.gd`: `offthread(group, name, usec)` -- on the cell line after the groups
  (`; off the main thread: terrain P [...]`), in the drain's `offthread_ms` and the summary (`+
  terrain X ms off the main thread`), never in `built in`, a group total or a frame's work.
- `World3D.gd`: `_terrain_job` (main thread: the one-time tables, the snapshot, the light terms),
  `_terrain_prepare` = `_terrain_prepare_read` + `_terrain_prepare_build` (static), with
  `_prepare_ground_textures`, `_decode_ground_image`, `_read_terrain_lightmap`,
  `_read_region_navmesh`, `_prepare_navmesh_walls`, `_prepare_nav_graph` and a static
  `_load_object_collision(cache, ...)`; `_terrain_commit`; `_try_load_real_terrain` runs both
  halves inline (the grid's centre, always, and every cell under `SRREVAMP_SYNC_LOAD=1`), applying
  the centre's environment between them since the mesh bakes its light;
  `_load_region_cell(..., prepared)`; `_pump_cell_jobs`, `_dispatch_cell_jobs`, `_dispatch_cell`
  (a high-priority task: at the 0.3 ratio a low-priority pair could share one thread on a small
  machine), `_finish_cell_job`, `_drop_cell_jobs`, `_outside_stream_window`, `_threaded_load`;
  `TERRAIN_JOBS_IN_FLIGHT` = 2, an own tuning choice disclosed at the constant; the drain's two
  branches; `_grid_loaded_line`'s off-thread total; the QA reconnect hook and its line; the
  header's `SRREVAMP_SYNC_LOAD`. The centre cell stays synchronous: its height anchors every
  neighbour, its environment lights them, and the caller places the player on it next.
- Comments naming the removed `_load_real_ground_textures` updated in `tile2d/tile_index_reader.gd`
  and `docs/protocol/TILE2D_FORMAT.md`.

## Object placements prepared off the main thread, with the alpha probes reading the decoded Image instead of a GPU readback (round 566)

Client only, tag-worthy: the second loading-freeze item of the map/loading epic (2026-09-25), on
top of round 565's terrain pipeline. Nothing on the wire, no flag, no server change (`server/`
untouched; `go build ./...` and `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` green before and after the doc
edits). A streamed region cell's objects -- the `.o`/`.o2` read, merged and de-duplicated, the
placement-ownership test with its neighbour heightmaps, and every model the world holds no
template for parsed down to mesh arrays, trimesh faces, decoded Images and an alpha
classification -- now prepare on the cell's WorkerThreadPool task after its terrain, and only the
commit (the texture uploads, the ArrayMeshes, materials and shapes of new templates, and each
placement's duplicate) runs on the main thread. Both halves of the item landed in this round --
the ObjectLoader split and the World3D job fold -- each with its own tests and negative. Every
number below is a log line from the render box (2026-09-25, hardware GL through VirtualGL, lane
lock `/var/tmp/r566/lock`, round 558's server binary) or from this checkout; the logs are
`/var/tmp/r566/{base_entry,base_cross,after_entry,after_cross,alpha_before,alpha_after,mats_before,mats_after,sync_cross,drain,qa}.log`
with `run.sh`, `base.sh`, `after.sh` and `mats.sh`, the exact commands (frames deleted); the review
fix's runs (below) are `/var/tmp/r566/{fixA_entry,fixA_cross,fixB_entry,fixB_cross,fixB_qa}.log`
with `fixrun.sh`, and the second review fix's `/var/tmp/r566/{fix2A,fix2B}_{entry,cross,qa}.log`
(the same `fixrun.sh`), summed by `fixsum.py`, `nbsum.py` and `overlap.py` beside them.

**Grounding, re-read at BASE (`f8704c4`, round 565).**

- `ObjectLoader.load_object` did, per model, on the caller's thread: `find_file` + `BsrReader.parse`,
  `load_material` (`BmtReader.parse`, whose zlib path is GDScript `Inflate`), per piece
  `BmsReader.parse` + `to_array_mesh` + `array_mesh.create_trimesh_shape()`, and per layer
  `build_godot_material` (`DdjReader.parse` + `to_texture` = `ImageTexture.create_from_image`).
  Its three alpha probes, `_alpha_is_binary_cutout`, `_has_real_alpha_variance` and
  `_real_alpha_fraction`, each began `texture.get_image()` -- `RenderingServer.texture_2d_get`, a
  readback of the uploaded texture on the GL renderer (World3D's own `_qa_texel_mean` comment says
  so) -- which a task preparing a model before its texture exists cannot do.
- `World3D._try_load_real_map_objects` ran the whole region on the main thread inside
  `_load_region_cell`, in the frame the cell's terrain was committed in; `_placements_belonging_here`
  read its own and its eight neighbours' heightmaps through `_parsed_region_heightmap`, which
  read and parsed any the grid did not hold (on the main thread); templates came from round
  559's `ObjectTemplateCache` through `_load_object_template` -> `load_object`.
- BASE re-measured today with the README's two commands (the box's client copy md5-identical to
  BASE): objects **5,346 ms** of the entry's 25 cells (`templates` 3,526 = centre 1,573 + 1,953
  over the 24 neighbours; `own` 1,202 = 308 + 894), and 26-83 ms a cell of the crossing's column
  (65, 83, 42, 30, 26, in commit order: 97, 96, 98, 95, 99/165). The item's figures (templates 3,356, own 1,069) are round 561's, before
  rounds 562-565.
- Godot 4.2's trimesh, read from the 4.2-stable sources (raw GitHub, 2026-09-25):
  `Mesh::generate_triangle_mesh` copies `vr[index]` for every index of an indexed triangle surface
  (a non-indexed one uses the vertices as the list); `TriangleMesh::create` snaps each corner to
  0.0001 and skips no triangle; `TriangleMesh::get_faces` rebuilds the faces from the snapped
  corners; `Mesh::create_trimesh_shape` returns null for no faces, else `set_faces` on a new
  ConcavePolygonShape3D. `MapmTerrainBuilder.surface_faces` (round 565) builds exactly that list.

**The findings and the orchestrator's notes, answered.**

- *The prepare-thread rule* (grounding verifier, orchestrator): written at
  `ObjectLoader.prepare_object` and `World3D._objects_prepare`, and in the README's rule 1.
  `_objects_prepare`, `_cell_prepare`, `_placements_belonging_here` and `_job_heightmap` are
  static; `prepare_object` constructs no Node and no RID-owning Resource and writes no static
  state -- what `_missing` would report and the QA lines go in its result for `commit_object` to
  report, in order (a reader's own `push_error` on a malformed file still prints from the task, as
  the terrain readers' do). Both new walks (`object_loader_test`, `objects_prepare_test`) fail on
  any Node or non-Image Resource in a prepared result, each with a positive control -- as first
  written only `objects_prepare_test`'s had one (the second review: `object_loader_test` only ever
  asked its walk to find nothing); the second review fix adds `object_loader_test`'s (below).
- *The heightmaps* (orchestrator: say which and why): **read under the Pk2Reader mutex inside
  the prepare**, not pre-parsed on the main thread. The job snapshots the heightmaps the grid
  already holds (references to parsed, read-only structs); one it lacks is read (every
  `read_file` takes the handle's lock, round 565) and parsed on the task into
  `job["new_heightmaps"]`, which the commit merges (a heightmap another commit cached first is
  kept). The region's own heightmap is the terrain prepare's parse, handed over by `_cell_prepare`
  (`objects_prepare_test` checks it is the same object). Why: the parse is what the `own` lap
  costs -- at BASE four cells with `.o2` placements to test and every heightmap they sample
  already cached (97/170, 98/169, 96/169, 95/170: 23, 95, 229 and 38 `.o2` entries) show `own 0`,
  while the rest run 14-154 ms and the centre, which parses its whole ring, 308 -- so pre-parsing
  would put the lap back in the frame. Measured: `own` over the 24 neighbours 894 ms on the main thread at
  BASE, 1,172 ms on the tasks as first written; none of it in a frame. The first write put the
  difference down to two in-flight tasks each parsing the same neighbour; the review fix then
  counted it (`prepared again`, below), and the second review fix re-counted it without the
  region's own heightmap, which the objects take over from the terrain's parse: **2** heightmaps
  the objects read twice over the entry's 24 cells with the pump dispatching first, **1** once it
  commits first, while `own` read 1,221 and 1,068 ms in those two runs (1,202 and 1,152 in the
  first pair). So duplicate parses are not what the ~170-330 ms over BASE is; the tasks share the
  CPU and Pk2Reader's lock with the other task in flight, which is not separated out here --
  unattributed.
- *The commit-side owner* (orchestrator): `ObjectTemplateCache` stays the owner. `prepare_object`
  returns plain data; `_objects_commit` exposes the job's prepared models to the cache's loader
  (`_prepared_models`), `_load_object_template` commits the prepared model into the cache
  (`commit_object`) the first time the world places it, and every placement is still a
  `duplicate()` of that one template. A model whose template the grid released or evicted between
  the dispatch and the commit is built whole on the main thread by the same loader, and the
  objects line counts it (`K template(s) built unprepared`): 0 in every streamed cell of every
  run below (21 entry cells, 26 crossing, 21 QA, 8 reconnect).
- *The alpha probes* (orchestrator): the readbacks are gone. The probes take the Image
  (`_alpha_is_binary_cutout(Image)`, `_has_real_alpha_variance(Image)`, `_real_alpha_fraction(Image)`,
  same rules, same thresholds, a copy decompressed so the uploaded Image is untouched), called
  through `_alpha_stat`, which measures once per texture and keeps the statistic in the texture
  cache entry (`"alpha"`), so a texture the world holds is neither decoded nor measured again; one
  whose statistic is missing is decoded from the archive for it, never read back.
  `build_godot_material` (SkinnedBsrAssembler's NPC and item path) is the same two halves back to
  back. The count, with a print behind `SRREVAMP_QA_ALPHA_LOG` as asked: see "Measured".
- *Size* (verifier, orchestrator): both parts fit the sitting and landed together, each tested
  and each with a negative; nothing deferred from the item's steps.
- *Finish before dispatch* (orchestrator, added after round 565's review): **missed by the first
  write of this round and answered in the review fix** (the round's review found it neither done
  nor answered, while this list said every note was). `_pump_cell_jobs` now calls
  `_finish_cell_job(flight)` BEFORE `_dispatch_cell_jobs()` -- until then it dispatched the next
  cell first, so that job's snapshot (`_terrain_job`: the ground tiles, the navmesh, the object
  navigation meshes; `_objects_job`: the heightmaps, the templates held, the textures held)
  missed everything the finishing cell was about to commit, and its task prepared that again.
  Measured with a count, not inferred: `_prepared_again` runs in `_finish_cell_job` before the
  commit merges anything and counts what the job read or built that the world had cached since
  its snapshot -- one `World3D: cell x/y prepared again what an earlier commit had cached -- N
  ground tile(s), N navmesh(es), N object navigation mesh(es), N heightmap(s) the objects read, N
  model(s), N object texture(s) decoded` line per committed streamed cell.

  **The count as first committed was wrong, and so was every number built on it** (the second
  review of this round). It counted every texture KEY a job's prepare filed, but a texture the
  job's snapshot already held is only named there, not decoded (`ObjectLoader._prepare_material`'s
  `known` branch files it with a null image), so every held texture a newly prepared model used
  counted as "decoded twice". The review showed it on the render box's own log: in `fixB_entry.log`
  (finish-first) `cell 97/169 prepared again ... 0 model(s), 2 object texture(s)` -- 97/169 is the
  first streamed commit after the centre, nothing committed between its snapshot and its commit
  (0 models again, 20 templates reused), so both textures were false. It also counted the region's
  own heightmap, which the objects take over from the terrain prepare's parse (`job["here"]`,
  `_cell_prepare`) and did not read. Fixed: a texture counts only if its entry carries an Image
  AND its key is not in the job's `known_textures` snapshot (the prepare decoded it from the
  archive), and a heightmap only if it is not the `here` parse; the line's fields now say so
  (`heightmap(s) the objects read`, `object texture(s) decoded`). `objects_prepare_test` holds both
  with a negative that fails on the first counter (below). The first pair's textures row (64 / 51
  / 90 / 65), its totals (103 -> 66, 145 -> 84) and the claims drawn from them are withdrawn; the
  pair was re-run with the corrected counter, and the table is that run's.

  The README's two commands plus the QA drain, the same instrumented code with only the two
  calls' order changed (A: dispatch first, as first written, restored temporarily in the copy
  shipped to the box for that run and reverted after, `grep -c MUTATION` 0; B: finish first, the
  shipped code), one run each, same box, same day
  (`fix2A_*.log`, `fix2B_*.log`, summed by `fixsum.py` / `nbsum.py`, which reproduce the first
  pair's and the first write's figures from their logs):

  | | (a) entry, 24 streamed cells: A | B | (b) crossing, 29: A | B |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | ground tiles decoded twice | 10 | 3 | 14 | 5 |
  | the `decoded now` sum over the run's `ground textures for` lines | 58 | 51 | 68 | 59 |
  | object navigation meshes read twice | 8 | 4 | 16 | 6 |
  | heightmaps the objects read twice (the terrain's parse of the region not counted) | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 |
  | models prepared twice (the copy thrown away) | 16 | 7 | 23 | 7 |
  | object textures decoded twice (decoded by the prepare, not named from its snapshot) | 31 | 13 | 47 | 13 |
  | region navmeshes read twice | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
  | all of it | 67 | 28 | 102 | 32 |

  The `decoded now` sums fall by exactly the tiles no longer decoded twice (58 - 51 = 10 - 3; 68 -
  59 = 14 - 5), a cross-check between two probes with different failure modes. The rows the review
  confirmed the first counter had right came back close (A: tiles 10, object navmeshes 9 -> 8,

  dispatch). The pump's order cannot hand a job what a job preparing at the same time has not yet

  Timing, A against B: entry `region grid loaded in 17858 ms ... at frame 29 -- 25 cells 7659 ms,
  10199 ms outside the cells over 16 awaited frames` against `18078 ms ... at frame 29 -- 25

- *The QA-drain contract*: `fix2B_qa.log`, the shipped order (`--radius 2`, no server, no
  `FORCE_LOADING`): all 25 `built in` lines `at frame 0`, `region grid loaded in 12268 ms ... at

- *Stale jobs and the exit*: unchanged rules; the objects ride in the cell's job, so a dropped

  their tasks` (this run, 15:48 on the box, is the first write's: the pump still dispatched before

  wait was not re-measured -- round 568), entry 2 loaded and shot; **0 `SCRIPT ERROR`**, and the `ERROR:` lines identical to round 565's same run
  (`/var/tmp/r565/drain.log`: two missing `.bsr`s, the gacha machine once per entry, the
  exit-time texture leak). The wait
  was 18.8 ms in round 565's run: a task now prepares the objects too, so a drop waits for more of
  it -- bounded by the longest cell's prepare (97/169: 408 ms terrain + 541 ms objects in the

**What changed.**

- `assets/object_loader.gd`: `prepare_object(archive, path, known_textures, textures)` (data:
  `{"path", "root", "textures", "missing", "log"}`, `root` a node description --
  `{"kind": "bsr", "name", "pieces": [{"name", "arrays", "faces", "material"}]}` or
  `{"kind": "cpd", "name", "children"}`), `commit_object(prepared, texture_cache)`,
  `snapshot_textures`, `commit_textures`; `load_object` = `commit_object(prepare_object(...))`;
  `_prepare_node` / `_prepare_compound` (was `_load_compound_object`) / `_commit_node`;

## Terrain collision from the height grid (HeightMapShape3D) instead of a per-region trimesh BVH (round 567)

Client only, tag-worthy: the third loading-freeze item of the map/loading epic (2026-09-25), on
top of rounds 565-566's off-thread prepare. Nothing on the wire, no server change (`server/`
untouched; `go build ./...` and `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` green before and after the doc
edits). A region's terrain collision is now one `HeightMapShape3D` over its 97x97 height grid, cut
into the drawn mesh's own triangles (`TerrainCollision`), in place of a `ConcavePolygonShape3D` of
every triangle of every surface of the mesh, whose BVH the commit built on the main thread;
`SRREVAMP_TERRAIN_TRIMESH=1` builds the old trimesh for A/B. The item was gated on a measured
share, and the gate said yes. Every number below is a log line from the render box (2026-09-25,
hardware GL through VirtualGL, lane lock `/var/tmp/r567/lock`, round 558's server binary) or from
this checkout. The logs are `/var/tmp/r567/{base,after,tri}_{entry,cross}.log` (the README's two
commands on BASE, on this round, and on this round with `SRREVAMP_TERRAIN_TRIMESH=1`) and
`rays3_{entry,cross}_{hf,tri}.log` (the ground probes, below), with `run.sh`, `base.sh`,
`after.sh`, `rays.sh` and `rays3.sh`, the exact commands (frames deleted), and `gate.py`,
`nbsum2.py` and `raysab.py` beside them, which sum the cell lines and diff the ray runs.
BASE ran from `git archive f25ab65` in `/var/tmp/r567/base_client`. The benchmark runs ran this
round's code before `SRREVAMP_QA_GROUND_RAYS` was changed to wait for the grid (a QA-only hook they
do not enable); the `rays3_*` runs ran the committed code. An earlier ray pair (`rays_*`) fired its
probe on a fixed timer, which in a run signed in to the server lands before the grid is built --
its entry pair probed an empty world -- and is superseded; `rays2_*`, on the fixed hook but before
the non-planarity count was added to its line, read the same numbers as `rays3_*` below.

**The gate, measured.** The item's own gate (`collision` >= 25 % of the terrain phase) was
answered NO by round 561's BEFORE (~57 of ~267 ms a neighbour cell, ~21 %); the orchestrator
re-gated it on collision's share of what still runs on the main thread per streamed cell after
rounds 565-566 -- the commit. Round 565 recorded, for this gate, `collision` 25-33 ms of a 39-51 ms
terrain commit (14 % of the cells' main-thread time then, with the objects still on the main
thread). Round 566 took the objects off it, so the share was re-read from round 566's own
shipped-code logs (`/var/tmp/r566/fix2B_entry.log`, `fix2B_cross.log`) and re-measured today on
BASE with the README's two commands, summing each streamed cell's own line:

| | streamed cells | `built in` sum | terrain commit | `collision` | its share of the cells | per-cell median |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) entry, round 566's `fix2B` | 24 | 2,372 ms | 1,154 | 643 | 27.1 % | 52 % |
| (b) crossing, round 566's `fix2B` | 29 | 2,665 | 1,353 | 783 | 29.4 % | 53 % |
| (a) entry, BASE today | 24 | 2,399 | 1,177 | 657 | 27.4 % | 52 % |
| (b) crossing, BASE today | 29 | 2,617 | 1,367 | 791 | 30.2 % | 53 % |

`collision` is over 25 % of the streamed cells' main-thread commit in all four (22-39 ms a cell,
55-58 % of each cell's terrain commit), so the item was done. Round 156's "the real bottleneck is
terrain, and within it `terrain_mesh.create_trimesh_shape()`" is a pre-round-160 reading: round
160's archive fix took the grid's terrain phase from 37.4 s to 6.4 s, and round 561 re-measured the
trimesh as the terrain's second-largest lap, not its largest. This round's gate is the re-measure.

**Grounding, re-read at BASE (`f25ab65`).**

- `World3D._terrain_commit`: `ConcavePolygonShape3D.set_faces(job["faces"])` alone in the
  `collision` lap, the faces `MapmTerrainBuilder.surface_faces` built in the prepare (its `faces`
  lap) -- every index of every surface, so each ground triangle about 2.5 times over (round 565:
  45,768 faces for 97/168 against the base surface's 18,432). The terrain group:
  `position = (placement.x, placement.y, -placement.z)`, `scale.z = -1`, no rotation; the
  StaticBody3D (`TERRAIN_COLLISION_LAYER`) under the `SubPatch` MeshInstance3D, at identity.
- `MapmTerrainBuilder._textured_surfaces_from_cells` and `_mesh_arrays_from_cells`: vertex
  (r, c) at local `(c * TILE_SIZE, h, r * TILE_SIZE)`, TILE_SIZE 20, 97 a side (the builder's doc
  comment; `docs/protocol/MAPM_FORMAT.md`); quad (r, c) drawn as `[i00, i10, i11, i00, i11, i01]`,
  so its diagonal joins (r, c) to (r + 1, c + 1). `_full_region_cells` stitches the blocks in
  nested file order, a later block winning a shared edge.
- Godot 4.2.2's heightmap, read from the 4.2.2-stable sources (raw GitHub, 2026-09-25;
  `servers/physics_3d/godot_shape_3d.{h,cpp}`, `scene/resources/height_map_shape_3d.cpp`):
  `GodotHeightMapShape3D::_get_point` places `heights[z * width + x]` at `(x - (width - 1) / 2, h,
  z - (depth - 1) / 2)`; `cull` (every shape query) and `_heightmap_cell_cull_segment` (rays) cut
  cell (x, z) into `(x, z), (x + 1, z), (x, z + 1)` and `(x + 1, z), (x + 1, z + 1), (x, z + 1)`,
  whose diagonal is (x + 1, z)-(x, z + 1). `HeightMapShape3D::set_map_data` copies the array and
  the server's `_setup` builds a 16-cell min/max grid -- no BVH. **The item's plan was wrong here**:
  `map_data[r * 97 + c] = height(r, c)` under a (TILE_SIZE, 1, TILE_SIZE) scale puts every vertex
  in place but cuts every quad along the OTHER diagonal, so inside any quad whose corners are not
  coplanar the collision is not the drawn ground. Measured, not argued: built that way in
  GodotPhysics, its vertical rays miss the drawn triangles by up to 17.4 units on the suite's
  synthetic hills, and on the real grid 252 of the 1,600 probed quads are non-planar enough that it
  would be off the drawn ground by over 0.5 at the probe point (below). So the rows are stored
  reversed (`z = 96 - r`) and the shape's z axis flipped back (`TerrainCollision.shape_transform`:
  basis diag(20, 1, -20), origin (960, 0, 960)); shape cell (x, z) is then mesh quad (95 - z, x)
  and its diagonal the mesh's own. The plan's NEGATIVE ("map_data[1 * 97 + 2] must be 12, not 21")
  holds in the flipped layout's own terms: the sample the shape reads for mesh (1, 2) is 12.
- `CollisionShape3D::get_configuration_warnings` (4.2.2) warns on any non-uniform scale ("A
  non-uniformly scaled CollisionShape3D node will probably not function as expected"); it is an
  editor configuration warning and is not printed at run time -- 0 lines matching
  `uniform|scaled` in this round's six benchmark logs.
- Face sidedness, read from the same sources: a ConcavePolygonShape3D's triangles are one-sided
  (`backface_collision` false by default) to rays and shape queries alike; a heightmap cell's are
  two-sided to a ray that stays in one cell when the query hits back faces (the default), one-sided
  to a ray crossing cells, and two-sided to every shape query (`cull` sets `backface_collision =
  !p_invert_backface_collision`). So the two may differ where a probe meets the ground from below.

**The findings and the orchestrator's notes, answered.**

- *The re-gate* (orchestrator): the table above -- 27-30 % of the streamed cells' main-thread
  commit, over 25 % in both runs of both commands.
- *The non-uniform, negative scale* (both verifiers, orchestrator): the shape's own transform is
  diag(20, 1, -20), non-uniform and a reflection, but composed with the group's `scale.z = -1` its
  GLOBAL basis is diag(20, 1, 20) -- no reflection left (measured in the suite). The configuration
  warning applies and does not appear in a run's log (above). GodotPhysics honours the scale:
  measured three ways -- the suite's rays, sweeps, body motions and walk against the trimesh under
  the same group transform; the real 25-region grid (below); and the crossing walk.
- *Rays on sloped columns and a `--walk` crossing as the acceptance* (orchestrator): below -- every

## Every town's centre is the same on the server and the client: Donwhang, Constantinople and Hotan from the game's own tables, Samarkand disclosed as unresolved, and the client resolves the server's "donwhang" label (round 569)

Server and client, tag-worthy: the first item of batch 22 of the map/travel epic (2026-09-25, "I
want this whole map loaded and explorable"). A first attempt at the batch's frame-on-the-wire item
aborted before any edit, because the server's `worldmap.ZoneCentre` and the client's
`World3D.gd` `*_ZONE_REGION` constants disagreed for three of the six zone labels -- the frame
could not be named on the wire while the two sides meant different regions by it. This round makes
them agree for every label, from the game's own tables where the tables agree. No opcode, no
packet layout and no flag changes.

**What was wired.**

- `worldmap.ZoneCentre` (server): `dunhuang`/`donwhang` 98/157 -> **102/153**, `constantinople`
  100/98 -> **105/79**, `hotan` 87/118 -> **92/135**, `samarkand` 88/130 -> **106/107**; `jangan`
  97/168 unchanged. Its comment claimed the entries mirrored the client's constants, which was
  false for three of them; it now states the rule, the table below and the Samarkand disclosure.
- `World3D.gd` (client): `DUNHUANG_ZONE_REGION` "98/157" -> **"102/153"**,
  `CONSTANTINOPLE_ZONE_REGION` "104/80" -> **"105/79"**; `HOTAN_ZONE_REGION` "92/135" and
  `SAMARKAND_ZONE_REGION` "106/107" unchanged, now documented as confirmed and as unresolved
  respectively. `_resolve_zone_region` resolves **"donwhang"** (the server's spelling) to the same
  region as "dunhuang".
- `cmd/server`: `realSpawnWorld(zone, row)`, the one conversion both the roster spawn loop in `main`
  and `gmSpecies` (/goto) now place a real npcpos row through; the Earth Ghost's roster comment
  records what its own-design anchor means under the new centre (below).

**1. The measurement** (render box, 2026-09-25, read-only, `/var/tmp/tables`; each table's UTF-16
BOM stripped before the join). `npcpos.txt`'s first column (12,367 rows; the NPC's id) was joined
to `characterdata_*.txt`'s SECOND (its ID -- characterdata's first column is the Service flag;
"on the FIRST column (id)" until round 574, which re-read both tables' rows: npcpos `2023` is
characterdata `1, 2023, NPC_CH_PRIEST`), never by grepping an id; 1,710 rows did not join (ids
38148-38257, beyond the six characterdata parts on the box; none of them sits in any region of the
table below). The
town codes are the game's own: `teleportdata.txt`'s five `GATE_<code>` rows name
`SN_ZONE_22001..22005`, which
`textdata_object.txt` resolves to Jangan (CH), Donwhang (WC), Hotan (KT), Constantinople (EU) and
Samarkand (CA). `teleportbuilding.txt`'s `STORE_<code>_GATE` row is the gate's building (region id
column 42), and `textzonename.txt` names each region by id:

| town | NPC_<code>_ rows, by region | GATE_<code> (teleportdata) | STORE_<code>_GATE (teleportbuilding) | client before | server before (textzonename) | centre now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jangan (CH) | 97/168 18, 97/167 8, 97/169 7, 98/167 5, ... of 67 | 97/168 (969, 1369) | 97/168 | 97/168 | 97/168 | 97/168 |
| Donwhang (WC) | 102/153 15, 103/153 6, 5 elsewhere, of 26 | 102/153 (957, 1508) | 103/153 at local (962, 8) | 98/157 | 98/157 "Donwhang Ferry" | **102/153** "Donwhang" |
| Constantinople (EU) | 105/79 10, 107/79 3, 105/78 3, 105/77 3, 104/80 3, 104/78 3, ... of 33 | 105/79 (950, 1070) | 105/79 | 104/80 | 100/98 "Cleopatra's Gate" | **105/79** "Constantinople" |
| Hotan (KT) | 92/135 6, 91/135 4, 92/136 3, ... of 29 | 92/135 (1138, 153) | 92/135 | 92/135 | 87/118 "Aircraft dock" | **92/135** "Hotan Kingdom" |
| Samarkand (CA) | 107/108 5, 106/108 4, 107/107 4, 106/107 3, 3 elsewhere, of 19 | 106/108 (270, 1421) | 107/107 at local (1917, 108) | 106/107 | 88/130 "East-Karakoram" | **106/107**, unresolved |

The server's three disagreeing values arrived in `edc6fea` (the Mangyang transform round) with no
recorded source (`git log -S` on `worldmap.go` finds that commit only, and neither its message nor
any doc names them); by the game's own region names none of them is its town. The client's picks
were densest-architecture scans (Dunhuang's by `cmd/scanlandmarks`, 2026-08-26; the other three by
`cmd/findregionassets`, `docs/PROGRESS.md` 2026-08-24), which missed the town twice:
Constantinople's 104/80 is its diagonal neighbour, and Dunhuang's 98/157 lies 4 regions off on
both axes. (Until round 574 this said they "chose a neighbour of the town twice" and cited only
the 2026-08-24 entry.)

**A correction to the plan's measurement.** The plan (from its verifier) read Samarkand's NPCs as
`NPC_SD_*` in 91/48-94/48 and its gate as "GATE_SD 106/108". `SD` is Alexandria:
`textdata_object.txt` names the `SN_NPC_SD_*` rows "Alexandria Trade center", "Weapon Trader
Hemaka" and so on, `GATE_SD1`/`GATE_SD2` are `SN_ZONE_21836_15`/`_16`, "Alexandria (South)" and
"(North)", in 90/48 and 92/51, and `textzonename.txt` names 90/48-94/48 "Alexandria". Samarkand's
code is `CA` (`GATE_CA` = `SN_ZONE_22005` "Samarkand", `SN_NPC_CA_GATE`). The rule's outcome for
Samarkand is the same either way -- its rows and its gate do not agree on one region -- so the
item was implemented as planned; the evidence is corrected here.

**2. The rule, one for every town.** Where a town's NPC rows (the region holding the most of them)
AND its `GATE_<code>` row agree on a region, that region is the centre on both sides. Where they
disagree, the server takes the client's current constant, so both sides agree, and the
disagreement is recorded as an open question; no choice is made between conflicting rows.

- Jangan, Constantinople, Hotan: rows and gate agree (97/168, 105/79, 92/135), and the gate
  building is in the same region.
- Donwhang: the most rows and `GATE_WC` agree on 102/153. The gate's building row puts its origin
  in 103/153 at local z 8 -- ToWorld in the 102/153 frame gives (2, -968), 8 units past the
  region's edge at z -960 -- so the building straddles the line while its landing point is well
  inside 102/153; both regions are named "Donwhang". Recorded, not a disagreement about the town.
- **Samarkand: unresolved, disclosed.** Its 16 in-town `NPC_CA_*` rows split 5/4/4/3 over 107/108,
  106/108, 107/107 and 106/107, the four regions that meet at one corner; its gate soldiers stand
  on the walls on both sides of those lines (`SOLDIER_SO1`/`SO2` 133 units apart across the 107/108
  line in region x 106, `WE1`/`WE2` at 107/107's low-X edge, `EA1`/`EA2` at 107/108's high-X edge);
  `GATE_CA` lands in 106/108; and the gate building stands in 107/107 at local (1917, 108), about
  108 units from the corner. Both sides take the client's 106/107, one of the four (textzonename:
  "Samarkand"). Open question: which region, if any, the real client treats as the town's.

**3. Records corrected.** `worldmap.ZoneCentre`'s comment; `docs/PROGRESS.md`'s 2026-08-24 entries
("cont'd 80": 102/153 is Donwhang itself, not "a river/ferry crossing near Dunhuang"; "cont'd 79":
Constantinople's 104/80), each with a dated note in place; `docs/GROUNDING_AUDIT.md`'s named-zone
row (the new evidence) and a new row for Samarkand as UNRESOLVED.

**4. "donwhang" on a tagged client, read from the code before the change.** The server's roster zone
