## The server names the coordinate frame on the wire (trailing FrameRegion) and the client builds its grid inside that frame (round 570)

Server and client, tag-worthy: the second item of batch 22 of the map/travel epic (2026-09-25, "I
want this whole map loaded and explorable"). A world coordinate only means something once you say
which region the frame is centred on (`worldmap.go`'s header). Until this round that was implicit:
the server converted into `worldmap.ZoneCentre`, and the client built its grid around
`World3D._resolve_zone_region`. Now the server names the frame in both world results, and the
client builds the zone's grid inside the frame it is told. Round 569 made the two sides agree on
every town's centre, and the frame named here is that centre for every zone. So nothing changes in
what the coordinates mean, and no grid a client builds changes. This is the groundwork the
single-frame item needs. No opcode changes and no flag. The one packet change is a field appended
after the entity list, where a tagged client stops reading.

**First, the check the re-spec required: the frame is the centre for all six labels.** I read the
current tree before any edit:

| label | `worldmap.ZoneCentre` (server) | `_resolve_zone_region` (client) |
|---|---|---|
| jangan | 97/168 | `JANGAN_ZONE_REGION` "97/168" |
| dunhuang, donwhang | 102/153 | `DUNHUANG_ZONE_REGION` "102/153" (both labels) |
| constantinople | 105/79 | `CONSTANTINOPLE_ZONE_REGION` "105/79" |
| hotan | 92/135 | `HOTAN_ZONE_REGION` "92/135" |
| samarkand | 106/107 (unresolved, disclosed in round 569) | `SAMARKAND_ZONE_REGION` "106/107" |

All six agree. An "x/y" label is its own frame on both sides: the server parses it, and the client
passes it through. So the first attempt's abort case (a frame that is not the centre) cannot arise
from any label.

**What was wired.**

- `worldmap.ParseRegionLabel("x/y")` parses a label into a region. Each part must be 0..255,
  because a real region id carries each coordinate in one byte (`RegionXY`).
  `worldmap.FrameFor(zone)` returns the zone's `ZoneCentre`, else the region an "x/y" label names,
  else no frame. `ToWorld` is unchanged.
- `session.EnterWorldResult.FrameRegion` and `session.ChangeZoneResult.FrameRegion` are a
  u16-prefixed "x/y" string (`encodeStrings`), appended after `Others`. `handleEnterWorld` sends
  `frameFor(spawnZone)` and `handleChangeZone` sends `frameFor(req.Zone)`. `frameFor` returns
  `FrameFor`'s region as "x/y", or "" for a label with no frame, such as "Jangan" or a typo; the
  client then keeps its own case-insensitive reading of the label, which lands on the same centre.
  `decodeFrameRegion` reads "" when nothing follows the list and returns an error when the field is
  cut short.
- `WorldNet` (client): `EnterWorldResult.frame` and `ChangeZoneResult.frame`, read by
  `_decode_frame` after the list with the same rule as the Go side. `NetClient` passes the decoded
  objects through unchanged, so it needed no edit.
- `RegionGridState` holds the frame helpers:
  - `frame_world(rx, ry, lx, lz, fx, fy)` is a term-for-term port of `ToWorld`, in world space
    after the mirror.
  - `cell_world_offset(dx, dy)` is `(dy*1920, 0, -dx*1920)`, also after the mirror.
  - `cell_at(rel)` is `_maybe_stream_regions`' floor test, moved here unchanged and now called
    from there.

  These live in the existing RegionGridState rather than a new file, as the re-spec allowed:
  `region_grid.gd` does not exist. The pre-mirror offset stays `World3D._cell_offset`, which is
  reused, as the re-spec asked. The terrain group's placement moved out of `_terrain_commit` into
  `World3D._group_position(world_offset, anchor)` with the same arithmetic, so the test holds the
  real placement to `ToWorld`, not a copy of it.
- `World3D` changes:
  - `_reload_zone_assets(zone, frame)` takes the server's frame. The first entry
    (`_load_initial_region_neighborhood`, `result.frame`) and a zone change
    (`_on_change_zone_result`) pass it. `SRREVAMP_QA_ZONE` and `SRREVAMP_MAPM_PATH` pass none.
  - `_frame_coords(centre, frame)` returns the named frame if it parses, else the centre.
  - `_load_region_neighborhood(..., frame)` builds the centre at `_cell_offset(centre - frame)`. It
    sets `_grid_origin_region` to the frame and a new `_grid_centre_region` to the centre. It keys
    the centre's cell, `_last_stream_cell` and every neighbour relative to the frame. It sets
    `_grid_origin_world` to the centre group's position minus `cell_world_offset(centre - frame)`.
  - With frame == centre, every one of those values equals what it was before this round.
  - `_reload_zone_assets` prints one line whenever the server named a frame (`is built in its own
    frame -- the server's FrameRegion x/y`), so a later run can measure the frame rather than infer
    it from a missing line.

**2. Server first is safe: I read the decoders before the change.** Go's `DecodeEnterWorldResult`
and `DecodeChangeZoneResult` returned straight after the `Others` loop and never looked at the
leftover bytes. GDScript's `WorldNet.decode_enter_world_result` and `decode_change_zone_result` did
the same. So a tagged client reads every byte it read before and ignores the new tail.
`TestWorldResultsCarryTheFrameAfterTheList` checks this: it builds the pre-570 payload by hand and
confirms the new one is that payload, byte for byte, plus the frame. The precedent is
`StorageListResult`'s trailing capacity ("where an older client stops reading, so the list still
decodes there").

**3. The transform and the sign rule**, with the axes checked: region y drives world X, region x
drives world Z, and Z is mirrored (AGENTS.md; the terrain group has `scale.z = -1` and its
position's z negated).

- `ToWorld` gives `x = (ry-fy)*1920 + lx-960` and `z = (fx-rx)*1920 + 960-lz`.
- `World3D._cell_offset(dx, dy) = (dy*1920, 0, dx*1920)` is the offset BEFORE the mirror.
  `_group_position` negates its z, so a group stands at `(-960 + dy*1920, -anchor, 960 - dx*1920)`,
  and a local point lands at that position plus `(lx, y, -lz)`. That is `ToWorld`.
- `_maybe_stream_regions`' `floor(-rel.z/1920), floor(rel.x/1920)` against the frame region's
  corner gives `(rx-fx, ry-fy)`.

The rows the client test reproduces were generated by `ToWorld` itself, using a throwaway test file
that was deleted afterwards. `worldmap_test.go`'s `TestFrameTableTheClientReproduces` holds the Go
side to the same rows, so the client's literals are `ToWorld`'s, not typed from prose:

- In the frame of 97/168, the rows are the measured table from `worldmap.go`'s header: 97/168
  (1002, 1020) is (42, -60); the middles of 97/169, 97/167, 98/168 and 96/168 are (1920, 0),
  (-1920, 0), (0, -1920) and (0, 1920). Also 98/157's middle is (-21120, -1920) and 102/153's is
  (-28800, -9600).
- In the frame of 98/157, the same points are (21162, 1860), (23040, 1920), (19200, 1920),
  (21120, 0), (21120, 3840), (0, 0) and (-7680, -7680).
- Moving a point from the 97/168 frame into 98/157's shifts it by minus 98/157's middle in the
  97/168 frame, which is **(+21120, +1920)**. Both tests derive this. The batch plan's
  "(21120, -1920)" had the sign of z wrong, and a test written to it would fail a correct
  implementation.

**4. Where World3D could assume centre == frame, and what I checked.**

- `_grid_origin_region`, now the frame:
  - `_maybe_stream_regions` uses it for the zone label (frame + cell), for the new cells' regions
    (frame + dx) and for the unloaded region (frame + key). All three are correct for any frame.
  - `_qa_columns_report` prints it as "the frame centred on". That is correct, and its comment now
    says so.
  - The `SRREVAMP_QA_GROUND_RAYS` wait and `QA TEXPROBE` used it to mean "the centre's terrain
    node". Both now read `_grid_centre_region`.
- `_grid.loaded_cells` keys and `_grid.mark_loaded`: relative to the frame everywhere.
  `_load_region_cell`, `_load_region_neighborhood`'s neighbours (now `cdx + dx`), `_dispatch_cell`,
  `_finish_cell_job`, `_build_one_queued_cell` and `_process_stream_queue` all take dx/dy from the
  queued cell. `RegionGridState.unload` finds a cell by its region, not its key.
- `_last_stream_cell` is set to the centre's cell. `_outside_stream_window` compares
  frame-relative dx/dy.
- `_grid_origin_world` is read only as `rel.x` and `rel.z` in `_maybe_stream_regions`.
- These are frame-agnostic, because each goes through a nav graph's group transform:
  - the minimap and world map (`_refresh_zone_label_position` reads the region and the local
    position from the group);
  - `_place_at_zone_spawn` and `_place_at_region_local`;
  - `_teleport_local` (`SRREVAMP_QA_AT`);
  - `_where_report` (the console's /where lines);
  - NPCs, which are parented to their region's group.
- `_place_player_at_world` (a GM /goto position) is in the server's frame, which is the grid's
  frame by construction.
- The stream tests: `objects_prepare_test.gd` sets `_last_stream_cell` to (0, 0) with frame ==
  centre, which is unchanged.

**5. What happens when the frame is not the centre.** Nothing reaches this today; the later
single-frame item must satisfy two constraints, and both are also written into the code:

- **The landing.** The server's position is in the FRAME. `spawnPos` (0, 0, 0) is the frame
  region's middle, which is off the grid the client builds around the centre. A server naming
  another frame must send a position inside the centre region. This is recorded at
  `ChangeZoneResult`'s doc, at `_on_change_zone_result` and at `worldmap.FrameFor`. Nothing was
  built for it here.
- **The height anchor.** With frame == centre, the centre calibrates itself on its own near-row
  vertex (`anchor` NAN), as before. With any other frame, `_frame_anchor_height` reads the frame's
  own `.m` on the main thread and returns its `near_row_middle_height`, so every grid built in one
  frame shares one height origin. It returns NAN, and the centre calibrates itself, when that
  `.m` cannot be read. Whoever names another frame must first check each zone's drawn heights
  under that frame's anchor.

For the frame the single-frame item is expected to name, 97/168, round 569's recorded raw ranges
minus 97/168's anchor (-2.49, measured with `heightat` in the aborted attempt and in round 569)
give these town centres:

| centre | raw (round 569) | drawn under 97/168's anchor |
|---|---|---|
| 97/168 | -60.86 .. 3.91 | -58.37 .. 6.40 |
| 102/153 | -154.15 .. -86.70 | -151.66 .. -84.21 |
| 105/79 | -141.16 .. 112.38 | -138.67 .. 114.87 |
| 92/135 | 0.00 .. 251.70 | 2.49 .. 254.19 |
| 106/107 | 180.00 .. 186.36 | 182.49 .. 188.85 |

Every one lies inside `_snap_player_onto_terrain`'s +-1000 ray and above `WORLD_FLOOR_Y` (-500).
That is the reason one Jangan-anchored frame is acceptable for the centres. The radius-2
neighbours were NOT measured and are that item's to check. The aborted attempt's 87/118 (2497.52)
is why the check matters: it is no longer any zone's centre or frame. (That value came from the
aborted attempt's own report, which is not committed, and round 569's list of its readings left
87/118 out; round 574 re-read it with the same read-only `heightat -region 87/118 -at 160,0` on
the render box: `raw heightmap at local (160, 0) = 2497.52`. The table's 97/168 minimum, -58.37,
subtracts the rounded -60.86 and -2.49; round 569's -58.36 subtracted before rounding.)

**Tests.**

  - `TestWorldResultsCarryTheFrameAfterTheList` (new) checks four things. Each new payload is the

## One world frame behind -single-frame (default OFF): every monster and player in the Jangan-centred frame and one bucket, so a walk from Jangan reaches Donwhang's monsters (round 571)

Server, plus one client fix the review asked for (the grid's corner, below); not tag-worthy: the
third item of batch 22 of the map/travel epic (2026-09-25, "I want this whole map loaded and
explorable"). Rounds 569 and 570 made the server and the client
agree on every town's centre and put the frame on the wire, each zone still in its own frame and its
own broadcast bucket. So a player who walked out of Jangan toward Donwhang stayed in Jangan's bucket
and never met Donwhang's monsters, which were converted into Donwhang's frame. This round adds ONE
frame and ONE bucket behind a new flag, `-single-frame` (env `SRREVAMP_SINGLE_FRAME`), **default
off**. Off, every byte on the wire is what it was. No opcode and no packet layout changes.

**What was wired.**

- `worldmap`:
  - `WorldOrigin` = {97, 168}, Jangan's centre.
  - `WorldBucket` = "world", the hub zone every framed label shares.
  - `Landing(zone, frame)`: the middle (960, 960) of the zone's centre region (`FrameFor`), named
    in the given frame.
  - `Rebase(x, z, from, to)`: the same place named in another frame.
  - The header and `FrameFor`'s comment now say what the flag changes.
- `session`:
  - `SetSingleFrame` / `SingleFrame`, an atomic like the monster flags.
  - `ZoneBucket(label)`: the label, or `WorldBucket` for every label `FrameFor` knows while the flag
    is on.
  - `arrival(zone)`: the bucket, position and `FrameRegion` for an entry or a zone change.
    - Flag off, or a label with no frame: the label's own bucket, `spawnPos`, `frameFor(zone)`.
    - Flag on and a framed label: `WorldBucket`, `Landing(zone, 97/168)`, "97/168".
  - `handleEnterWorld` and `handleChangeZone` enter the hub, answer and broadcast through it.
  - `handleChangeZone` skips "already in that zone" for a one-world arrival (below).
- `cmd/server`:
  - The flag, with the env WARN pattern and the boot lines `single frame off (-single-frame /
    SRREVAMP_SINGLE_FRAME)` / `single frame on: origin 97/168 ...`.
  - `session.SetSingleFrame` is called before the roster spawns.
  - `realSpawnWorld` converts every npcpos row against 97/168 under the flag, whatever its zone.
  - `anchorWorld` moves an own-design anchor, which is relative to its zone's centre, into 97/168's
    frame with `Rebase`.
  - `rosterInstances` is the spawn loop's body, factored out unchanged so a test can hold it. It
    gives every instance the bucket `session.ZoneBucket(spec.Zone)`.
  - `gmSpecies` places through the same two conversions and keeps the zone LABEL.
  - The review's consistency fix: `realSpawnWorld` converts under the flag only for a zone
    `worldmap.FrameFor` knows, and `anchorWorld` rebases from `FrameFor` rather than `ZoneCentre`,
    so both key on what `session.ZoneBucket` keys on. A zone with no frame then gets no instance at
    all under the flag: before, its rows converted into world-frame coordinates in a bucket of its
    own. `gmSpecies` leaves out a species with no place, rather than offering an anchor-only one at
    (0, 0). Latent: the roster's zones are jangan and donwhang, both framed.
- client, `World3D.gd` (the orchestrator's note from round 570's review, below):
  `_frame_corner`, and `_load_region_neighborhood` takes `_grid_origin_world` from it.
- Comments only: `world.Entity.Zone` (it is the bucket), `Hub.ChangeZone` (a same-bucket change),
  `gm.Actor.Zone`, `gm.Species.Zone`, the label mapping in `session/gm.go`, `tradeInRange`'s
  (its "handleChangeZone puts everyone at the one spawnPos" is untrue under the flag), and three
  in `World3D.gd` that called this "the later single-frame item" (`_frame_coords`,
  `_frame_anchor_height`, `_on_change_zone_result`). `ChangeZoneResult`'s
  stale "Position is always spawnPos: this project has no confirmed real transform" is corrected;
  the transform is `worldmap.ToWorld`, measured (round 569's record has the table).

**The grounding.** The frame and the bucket are OWN DESIGN, disclosed: the retail client addresses a
position by region id plus region-local offset, and srrevamp's placeholder protocol has no world
frame to copy. Jangan is the origin because every character enters there (`spawnZone`), because
`ToWorld` was measured in its frame, and because Jangan's coordinates are then identical with the
flag on or off. Everything else is earlier rounds' measurements, re-read against the current tree:
`ToWorld` (the measured table in `worldmap.go`'s header), `ZoneCentre` (round 569's NPC rows and
gates), `FrameRegion` and the client's grid built inside it (round 570). The axes, checked for every
expected value: region y drives world X, region x drives world Z, and Z is mirrored (AGENTS.md; the
client's terrain group has `scale.z = -1`). No dump address is involved.

**The landing (the orchestrator's note).** Under the flag a zone change lands at the town's landing
named in the one frame, not at `spawnPos`. Round 569's step 6 measured each corrected centre's middle
as open, walkable terrain, and the client moves a Jangan arrival on to `ZONE_SPAWN_LOCAL` itself.
`Landing` is that middle: (0, 0) in the zone's own frame, which is `spawnPos`, where every zone
change has always landed. Under the flag it is the same place, named in 97/168's frame. Every value
below is `ToWorld(centre, 960, 960, 97, 168)`, derived in the tests:

| town | centre | landing in the one frame | float32 step at the landing, X / Z |
|---|---|---|---|
| jangan | 97/168 | (0, 0) | -- |
| donwhang, dunhuang | 102/153 | (-28800, -9600) | 1/512 / 1/1024 |
| constantinople | 105/79 | (-170880, -15360) | 1/64 / 1/1024 |
| hotan | 92/135 | (-63360, 9600) | 1/256 / 1/1024 |
| samarkand | 106/107 | (-117120, -17280) | 1/128 / 1/512 |

The y stays `spawnPos`'s 0, and the client snaps it (below). The client builds the zone's grid
around its centre, in the frame the server names (round 570's `_load_region_neighborhood`), so the
landing is inside that grid. (0, 0, 0) would be 97/168's middle, which is off the grid.

**Float precision (recorded, not fixed).** The last column is `math.Nextafter32`'s step at each
coordinate. A float32 is the wire's position type, and Godot's too. Constantinople's grid reaches
X -175,680, still 1/64 of a unit. Re-basing the origin is the deferred map-origin-rebasing item.

**Heights under ONE frame (the orchestrator's note).** Under the flag, every grid the client builds
takes 97/168's near-row vertex as its anchor, -2.49 (round 570's `_frame_anchor_height`). With the
flag off, a town's grid takes its own centre's vertex. I measured every town centre and its radius-2
neighbours: 125 regions, every vertex of every `.m`. The measurement was read-only against the render
box's Map.pk2. A scratch copy of `internal/pk2` and `internal/mapm` read the archive through a
Python process on the box that only `seek`s and `read`s; nothing was written there, and none of it
is committed. It reproduces round 569's numbers exactly: 97/168 anchor -2.49, raw -60.86 .. 3.91,
middle -54.39; 102/153 -99.12, -154.15 .. -86.70, -106.56. "Drawn" is raw minus the anchor:

| town | own anchor | radius-2 raw min .. max | drawn, own anchor (flag off) | drawn, -2.49 (flag on) | landing (middle) drawn off / on |

The note asks for whole-region ranges inside the +-1000 snap ray and above `WORLD_FLOOR_Y` (-500).
Taken literally, that envelope is broken today, with the flag off, by 1 of Jangan's 25 regions
(99/170 peaks at 1075.41), 15 of Donwhang's, 23 of Hotan's (a floor at about raw -600 across 90-93/134-137,
and 92/136 at -820.49) and none of Constantinople's or Samarkand's. With the flag on it is broken by 1,
14, 19, 0 and 2. The one frame takes no region out of the envelope for Jangan, Donwhang, Hotan or
Constantinople; Donwhang's 100/153 and four of Hotan's come back into it. It takes two out for
Samarkand: the peaks of 108/105 and 108/106 draw at 1052.1 and 1108.7, against 869.6 and 926.2 under
Samarkand's own anchor.

A whole-region envelope that the default Jangan grid already fails cannot be the gate. So I checked
the places where the client actually puts something at a height the server chose:

- **The landing.** A zone change places the player at the server's y 0. `_snap_player_onto_terrain`
  casts from y +1000 down to -1000 and only lifts. Every landing draws at -104.07 .. 246.32 under
  the flag: inside the ray, and above -500.
- **Monsters -- NOT covered on a first placement.** A monster also arrives at y 0. The first draft
  of this entry said the client places it on its region's walkable graph first and falls back to
  the +-1000 ray; the review read the code and that is wrong for a NEW body.
  - `_spawn_or_update_monster` places a new body at `_terrain_height_at(pos)` alone. That ray
    returns `pos.y`, the server's 0, when no terrain is loaded under the point. The navmesh-first
    height (`_moving_monster_height_at`) is for walking bodies: the existing-body branch while one
    moves, and `_step_monster_bodies`, which steps only bodies with a motion state.
  - Nothing re-grounds a standing body when its region loads: no loop over `_monster_bodies` does.
    The next monster list re-places it (the existing-body branch's `_terrain_height_at`, at the
    list's y 0 again). The client asks for a list on world entry and a zone change, after an attack
    result, a damage or monster-died push, a kill's death hold, a GM reply that asks for it, the
    Refresh button, and (with the monster AI on) a move for a body it does not know.
  - Under the flag a player who enters Jangan is sent every monster in the one bucket, the Earth
    Ghost's 65 rows among them, while Donwhang's regions are unloaded. Each ghost is drawn at y 0
    and stays there after a walk to Donwhang until one of those lists. The rows
    (`/var/tmp/tables/npcpos.txt` joined on the first column, id 1963) sample at raw -119.27 ..
    121.95, which is -116.78 .. 124.44 under the flag (-20.15 .. 221.07 with it off): a ghost can
    stand up to 116.78 above its ground or 124.44 below it.
  - With the flag off the same limit holds for any listed monster outside the regions a player has
    loaded; the flag is what puts the Earth Ghost's rows in a Jangan player's list.
  - Not fixed here (a client change to re-ground standing bodies as cells load is the next client
    round's); written into `deploy/README.md`'s flip conditions.
  - Jangan's rows keep Jangan's anchor with the flag on or off. Nothing is placed near Samarkand's
    two peaks.
- **The floor.** `WORLD_FLOOR_Y` returns the player to their last grounded spot only when they are
  below -500 AND the ground ray finds no terrain within 20 units under them. Standing on Hotan's floor
  near raw -600 is grounded. Under the flag that floor draws 246.30 HIGHER than with the flag off, so it
  moves away from -500.
- **A GM `/tp` onto a peak.** The ray starts at the GM's own height. If it misses, the buried-player
  probe (`_recover_if_below_terrain`, a 1920-unit reach) lifts them, flag or no flag.

So no town needed gating for the player, and none is gated; the monsters' first placement is the
recorded client limit above. Samarkand's two newly-high peaks are recorded here. They matter only
if something is ever placed on them at y 0. The review re-read the heights independently and
reports that they match; the probe that measured them is not committed (above), so they are not
reproducible from the repo alone.

**Walking out of Jangan is the same with the flag on or off.** A grid streams every neighbour under
its centre's anchor, so a player who walks from Jangan draws every region under -2.49 either way.
Over the walking box between the two towns (x 95-104, y 151-170, 200 regions, 15 of them missing
from the archive, all at x 103-104), 4 regions dip below -500: 97/151 -700.90, 97/159 -538.32,
98/159 -514.99, and one vertex of 104/162 at -21586.9, a spike in the data. 73 regions peak above
+1000. All of this is the same with the flag off; the flag changes only the grids centred on the
other towns.

**Label -> bucket, every comparison mapped (the orchestrator's note).** `world.Entity.Zone` is the
BUCKET. Under the flag the label is never stored; it lives only in the results and on the client.

- The bucket-to-bucket comparisons are unchanged and correct: every player and roster monster of a
  framed zone is in `WorldBucket`. These are `handleMonsterList`'s `monsters.InZone(entity.Zone)`,
  the AI paths (`monsterai.go`'s `InZone(b.m.Zone)`, `e.Zone != b.m.Zone`, the held keys, the
  pushes), `combat.go` and `keepup.go`'s `attacker.Zone != m.Zone`, the ground-item drops and lists,
  `chat.go`'s zone broadcast, and `tradeInRange`, whose 320-unit test now compares positions in one
  frame.
- `handleChangeZone`'s `req.Zone == current.Zone` compared a LABEL with the bucket. Under the flag
  it is skipped for a one-world arrival: a label names no place the character is "already in", since
  it can have walked from Jangan to Donwhang with its label unchanged. A change to a town is always
  a warp to its landing. `hub.ChangeZone` re-enters the same bucket, so everyone else gets the
  mover's `OpEntityLeft` and then its `OpEntityEntered` at the landing. That is a flicker, not a
  bug, and the test holds it.
- `session/gm.go` hands the GM console the bucket as `gm.Actor.Zone`:
  - `/spawn` spawns into it and `/kill`'s broadcast goes to it; both want the bucket.
  - `/tp` is in its frame.
  - `gm.gotoSpot` compares it with LABELS. No label equals `WorldBucket`, so `/goto <zone>` always
    travels, and `/goto <monster>` always carries the species' label (`gm.Species.Zone`, kept by
    `gmSpecies`), so the client re-centres on that town before it moves the GM.
  - The reply's `Zone` is therefore always a label; `/kill`'s bucket is cleared from it, as before.
- A label with no frame (a typo, "Jangan" with a capital) keeps its own bucket, `spawnPos` and
  `FrameRegion` "" with the flag on too. The client builds it in its own frame, so its coordinates
  cannot join the world's. A label spelled like the bucket, "world", lands in the world's bucket at
  (0, 0), Jangan's middle in the one frame: a real place in it, and harmless.

**Also disclosed.** One bucket has no spatial filter: moves, local chat and the monster and
ground-item lists (the round's verifier counted 413 roster monsters with `-npcpos-csv`: Jangan's
348 and the Earth Ghost's 65) reach every player. Four limits of the client, which this round does
not change, and one of the list are written into the deploy section as flip conditions:

- `/unstuck` returns to the ENTRY position, Jangan's middle in the one frame.
- `_apply_gm_move` compares a `/goto` reply's zone with the label the player ENTERED with, so a GM
  who walked to Donwhang and types `/goto jangan` stays put. The zone box has no such check.
- A monster's first placement at y 0 over unloaded terrain (above).
- The float steps above.
- The monster list's headroom (the review's count, re-derived here). The list is one packet,
  capped at 32,767 payload bytes (`sizeMask`, `internal/proto/packet.go`); each monster is 40 bytes
  plus its name and code name (`MonsterSnapshot.Encode`), and the list adds 4. Counting the real
  npcpos rows per roster id on the box (read-only: 1933 55, 1934 37, 1935 37, 1936 41, 1937 30,
  1938 20, 1939 31, 1950 35, 1941 36, 1943 26, 1963 65) against the roster's names gives 23,769
  bytes for Jangan's 348 with the flag off and 28,189 for the one bucket's 413. A Mangyang is 64
  bytes, so 72 more overflow the one bucket (141 overflow Jangan's with the flag off). A GM
  `/spawn` is at most 20 (`gm.MaxSpawn`) and never respawns; `combat.Hub` drops a monster only when
  it dies. Past the cap every list fails in `proto.Write` and the gateway closes the session, for
  every player with the flag on.

`handleChangeZone`'s `!oneWorld &&` guard cannot change an outcome under the flag (the review's
note): a framed label never equals the bucket "world", which `FrameFor` does not know, and with the
flag on no one sits in a framed label's bucket. It stays as the statement that a one-world arrival
is always a warp.

Persisting a position with its frame is the next item's.

**The grid's corner (the orchestrator's note from round 570's review).**
`World3D._load_region_neighborhood` took `_grid_origin_world`, the corner `_maybe_stream_regions`
measures the player from (`RegionGridState.cell_at`), as the centre group's position less the
centre's `cell_world_offset`, and used `Vector3.ZERO` as the group's position when the centre's
terrain had failed to load. The review estimated the error at half a region; that is the frame == centre case.
With the frame not the centre -- every town but Jangan under the flag -- `grid_origin_test.gd`
derives it from the code: Donwhang's corner in 97/168's frame came out (28800, 0, 9600) against
(-960, -anchor, 960), and its landing streamed as cell (10, -30), region 107/138, not 102/153. The
stream window would have been built and pruned around the wrong region.

- `_frame_corner(anchor)` is `_group_position(Vector3.ZERO, anchor)`: where the frame region's own
  group stands, or would stand, on the grid's anchor (`_grid_shared_anchor_height`). Every cell's
  group stands at that corner plus its `cell_world_offset` (region_grid_state_test.gd holds it for
  every FRAME_ROWS region). So the corner needs no centre.
- `_load_region_neighborhood` now takes the corner from it, whether or not the centre loaded. With
  the centre loaded it is the value read off the group before: `_grid_shared_anchor_height` is the
  height the centre was placed on (its own near height, or the frame's anchor).
- With no height known (neither the frame's nor the centre's `.m` read), y is 0, as the old
  fallback's was. Only x and z are read.
- This also changes one flag-off path, the only one: a zone in its own frame whose centre fails to
  load. Its corner was (0, 0, 0), half a region off, and is now the region's corner.

## A monster whose height ray found no ground at spawn keeps retrying until the ground commits (round 572)

Client only, tag-worthy: the user's "Mangyangs are now floating" (2026-09-25, a tagged client --
most likely v0.1.446 or v0.1.447 -- against the public test server). No opcode, packet or server
change.

**1. What the logs showed, re-measured -- and the condition that decides it: the loading-screen
drain.** `World3D._spawn_or_update_monster` prints a body's position after its height ray, so its
`-> model ... at x,y,z` line is the height it is drawn at; a miss hands back the server's y, which is
0 for every Jangan monster. The render box holds 63 first entries with monsters from rounds 558-569
(this round's four aside), and they split on one condition, whether the entry took the
loading-screen drain:

| first entries (render box) | loading screen | code | the list is applied | bodies at the server's y 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14: `/var/tmp/r558` (6), `r559` (3), `r560` (3), `r561` (2) | yes: `--reconnect`, which exports `SRREVAMP_QA_FORCE_LOADING=1` (round 558's `neg` run exported it by hand, per its record), or the variable itself (round 561's runner); round 561's grid line says `over 9 awaited frames` | rounds 558-561: the screen goes up after the centre cell | after the centre's commit, before any neighbour's (96/168 among them) | 4 of 23 in every one: the Mangyangs, `at 130,0,2280`, `882,0,2279`, `301,0,2857`, `-406,0,2409` |
| 33: `/var/tmp/r562` (3), `r565` (6), `r566` (18), `r567` (the 6 `SRREVAMP_QA_FORCE_LOADING` runs) | yes: `LoadingScreen: up at frame <n>`, the list's line right after it | round 562 on: the screen's frame comes before the centre cell | before any terrain | 23 of 23 in every one |
| 16: `/var/tmp/r567/rays{,2,3}_{entry,cross}_{hf,tri}.log` (12), `/var/tmp/r569/{constantinople,donwhang,hotan,samarkand}.log` (4) | no: the QA path, `over 0 awaited frames` | round 565 on | after the whole grid: its 25 cells (radius 2) or 9 (radius 1) all commit in one frame (12, 13 or 14) before `server reports 23 monster(s)` | the Mangyangs on the ground in every one (e.g. `rays_entry_hf.log`: `130,-37,2280`); 7 of 23 in the 10 heightfield runs -- the 7 vertex bodies where the plain ray misses (step 5) -- and 0 of 23 in the 6 `SRREVAMP_TERRAIN_TRIMESH=1` runs |

This round's runs (`/var/tmp/rfloat`, step 8) are loading-screen entries and read like the second
row at spawn: 23 of 23 listed before any terrain, at y 0.

The loading-screen drain is the real player's path: `_should_show_loading_screen` is true whenever
`SRREVAMP_MAPM_PATH` is unset, and a player's client never sets it. A QA render sets it (`qa_shot.sh
--region`) and builds the grid in one frame unless `SRREVAMP_QA_FORCE_LOADING` asks for the screen --
World3D's own `QA RECONNECT` refusal says the same ("the QA path builds the grid in one frame"). So a
default QA render, `--server` included, applies the list to a finished grid and draws every monster
whose ray finds the ground where it belongs: the 16 runs of the third row are the counter-case, and
why a default QA render does not show the float. Only the loading-screen runs measure what a player
sees.

The two second entries of round 558 (`runB`, `runC`, a reconnect whose terrain was already built)
print the same four Mangyangs at -38, -49, -37 and -42: the ground there, not 0. Nothing re-rays a
standing body afterwards: the callers of `NetClient.list_monsters()` are `_ready`'s guarded block,
the zone change, the Monsters tab's refresh button, an attack result, a damage or death push, the
death path (its hold's timer, or at once when no die clip played), a move for an unknown monster, a
GM command's refresh and two QA hooks; `_step_monster_bodies` returned at once when no body had a
leg; and nothing in a region's commit looks at the monsters.

**2. Why the ray missed, measured.** The list is asked for in `_ready`'s guarded block and applied
whenever the reply arrives. In every in-memory log above, the reply is applied on the first frame
the entry awaits, so what decides the float is where that frame falls:

- **Loading screen, before round 562.** In rounds 558 to 561's code (each read, round 560's as
  tagged v0.1.442), `_ready` calls `NetClient.list_monsters()` and then
  `_load_initial_region_neighborhood()` -- the centre's synchronous build -- with no await between
  them; the first awaited frame is the drain's, after the centre and before its neighbours. So the
  list lands between 97/168 and 96/168 (round 561's `entry.log`: the centre at frame 13, 96/168 at
  frame 14) and only the Mangyangs, in the neighbour 96/168, miss.
- **Loading screen, round 562 on.** Round 562 (first tagged in v0.1.443) put `await
  _show_loading_screen()` between those two calls, and the list lands in the screen's frame, before
  any terrain. `/var/tmp/r562/entry.log`, round 562's own code, is the first log with 23 of 23 at y
  0 (the list at its log line 24, 97/168's commit at line 85, frame 14). In this round's runs,
  likewise, `server reports 23 monster(s)` comes before `loaded real terrain from 97\168.m ... at
  frame 13` (or 14), and the Mangyangs' 96/168 commits at frame 17, 18 or 19.
- **No screen (the QA path).** No frame is awaited between `_ready`'s request and the end of the
  grid build (`over 0 awaited frames`; every cell's commit names the same frame), so the list is
  applied to every cell's terrain (the third row).

**The "why now" hypothesis is not confirmed.** The plan's reading -- that the public server's
latency used to let 96/168 commit first, and rounds 565-567 (neighbours prepared on a worker and
committed one a frame, v0.1.444+) took that away -- would need a public-server log or a delayed-list
knob run against a pre-565 build, and neither was done. What the logs do establish: on the
loading-screen path the float is not specific to the public server -- the in-memory server floated
at least the Mangyangs in every such entry since round 558 -- and from round 562's code on it is not
specific to Mangyangs.

**3. The change** (`client/scripts/World3D.gd`, `client/scripts/world/ground_items.gd`,
`client/scripts/world/monster_motion.gd`, `client/scripts/assets/terrain_collision.gd`).

- `_terrain_hit_height(pos)`: the terrain-layer ray, returning NAN on a miss; `_terrain_height_at`
  calls it and keeps its contract (pos.y on a miss) for its other callers. `_moving_monster_hit_height`
  is the same for a walking body's rule (navmesh first, then the ray). The ray itself is
  `TerrainCollision.vertical_ray` (step 5), and it passes through the scene's two stand-in floors
  (step 6).
- `_monster_heights_pending` (monster id -> the physics frame its ray first missed) and
  `_book_monster_height`: a new body, or a list refresh of an existing one, whose ray misses is
  drawn at the server's y as before and goes on the list; a hit takes it off. The spawn line says
  so -- `... (height pending: no ground under it yet)` -- and the resolve prints once:
  `World3D: monster <id> <name> height resolved after <n> frame(s): <y> at frame <drawn frame>`.
- `_step_monster_bodies` serves the waiting bodies inside the existing budget
  (`MonsterMotion.height_turns`, `MAX_HEIGHT_RESOLVES_PER_FRAME`, 32): a body with a leg entry
  wants a resolve every frame while it waits and is resolved by the step's own rule; a standing one
  is added after the walking ones and resolved by the terrain ray its placement took. A miss leaves
  the height as it is (what the walking resolve already did). The step runs when either set is
  non-empty. The rule follows the leg entry, not the gait: a body that has stopped at the end of a
  leg keeps its entry, so its retry is navmesh first, while a list refresh of the same standing body
  fires the terrain ray -- the split its arrival resolve and its refresh already had before this
  round.
- **The ground items' fair share.** `World3D._step_heights` runs the frame's height work: the
  monsters may take `MonsterMotion.monster_height_share(32, items waiting)` -- the budget less the
  items' want, up to half of it -- and `GroundItems.resolve_pending` takes whatever the monsters
  left. So two queues that both want more than half split it 16/16, and either takes what the other
  does not want. The even split is srrevamp's own design, not a tuned number. The first pass gave
  the items only what the monsters left, which from 32 monster bodies that never resolve (listed
  outside every loaded region) is nothing.
- **The retries' own counter.** `SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_LOG`'s 10-second line counts a resolve for a body
  still on the wait list as a retry, apart from the walking legs' resolves: `monster height
  resolves N/s, max M in a frame; T ms in them over 10.0 s, max U ms in a frame; waiting-for-ground
  retries R/s, max S in a frame, V ms in them`. The first pass counted both as resolves.
- The wait list is emptied wherever a body leaves `_monster_bodies`: `_sync_monster_bodies` (the
  only place one body is erased), `_on_change_zone_result` (all bodies cleared), and the step itself
  (an id whose body is gone). The death path keeps its body drawn until the list drops it, so a
  dying body may still resolve. `_exit_tree` needs nothing: the dictionary is instance state (round
  560) and goes with the instance.
- `TerrainCollision.place_group`: `_terrain_commit`'s terrain-group placement, moved unchanged
  (position (offset.x - 960, -anchor, 960 - offset.z), `scale.z = -1`; the long comment on why stays
  in `_terrain_commit`), because the heightfield's grid lines follow from it (step 5) and the grid
  probe should run the game's own placement, not a copy. On dev, round 570 had put the same
  arithmetic in `World3D._group_position`, which round 571's `_frame_corner` reads for the grid's
  corner: `_terrain_commit` places through `place_group`, `_group_position` stays for the corner,
  and a test holds the two equal (step 9).
- Physics timing, measured rather than assumed: in the suite, a terrain-layer ray fired right after
  a StaticBody3D is added to the tree, with no physics step in between, already hits it (`info: ...
  hits at y -50.00`). The retry does not depend on it either way -- it runs every physics frame
  and never from inside a commit; in the live run the bodies resolve on the frame after their
  region's commit.

**4. The same pattern elsewhere** (a height ray fired once when something is placed):

- **Ground items -- identical, fixed.** Listed in `_ready` beside the monsters, placed by one ray in
  `GroundItems.spawn`, and a kill's drop carries the monster's listed y (`session/grounditem.go`
  `dropKillLoot`) -- 0 for a Mangyang. `setup` took `_terrain_height_at`, so a miss fell back to the
  server's y exactly as a monster's did; with `_terrain_hit_height` passed instead, a miss is
  kept on `GroundItems._pending` and `resolve_pending(budget)` retries it with the items' share of
  the frame's 32 (a missed item goes to the back of the queue). The list line says how many wait:
  `N item(s) on the ground in this zone (M with no ground under them yet)`. Held by the suite only:
  the live runs had no items on the ground.
- **Other players' bodies**: no ray -- drawn at the y their own client sent. Not the pattern.
- **NPCs**: placed when their own region commits, from that region's walkable graph
  (`landing_height_at`). No ray, no race.
- **The player** (`_qa_goto_from_list`, `_qa_attack_nearest`'s goto, `_qa_retreat`,
  `_place_player_at_world` for a GM move): one ray each (`_terrain_height_at`), but the player is
  grounded again every physics frame (the walkable graph, or gravity and
  `_recover_if_below_terrain`). No retry added; the ray now steps off the grid lines and passes
  through the stand-in floors like every other placement's.
- **A walking body's own resolve that misses** keeps its height and is tried again two units later;
  one that misses on its arrival keeps it. Not put on the wait list (not a placement at spawn);
  disclosed.

**5. Round 567's heightfield has no answer on its own grid lines -- fixed with one ray helper.**
The first pass of this round left 7 of the 23 Jangan bodies waiting to the end of its run, all in
97/168 and all on grid vertices of it (world x and z multiples of 20); `SRREVAMP_TERRAIN_TRIMESH=1`
placed all 23. Nine of the 23 stand on 97/168's vertices: the first pass's ray (a plain one)
answered at the other two, (-300, -880) and (-300, -760), and at all 10 bodies that lie on exactly
one grid line.

- *Why, read from Godot 4.2.2's source* (`servers/physics_3d/godot_shape_3d.cpp`,
  `GodotHeightMapShape3D::intersect_segment`, and `core/math/geometry_3d.h`,
  `segment_intersects_triangle`, at the 4.2.2-stable tag): a ray whose begin and end fall in the
  same cell tests only the cell `floor()` of its shape-local x and z picks, and each of its two
  triangles with Moller-Trumbore's closed bounds (`u < 0` or `v < 0` rejects). A point on the
  cell's edge has a barycentric of zero; the neighbouring cell, which it lies on too, is never
  tried. Which rounding makes the zero negative was not traced; the counts below fit a coin flip
  per coordinate (4,512 of 9,312 points on one line miss, 6,909 of 9,409 on two).
- *Measured, the grid probe* (`terrain_collision_test.gd`, committed; synthetic heights, no game
  data): 25 regions of a radius-2 grid placed by `TerrainCollision.place_group` -- the placement
  `_terrain_commit` calls (step 3: the arithmetic moved, not changed) -- at the frame
  origin, over one world-continuous non-planar field, plain vertical rays from +1000 to -1000 at
  every vertex: **6,909 of the centre region's 9,409 miss, and 50,391 of the 25 regions' 235,225**,
  in 13 regions (as (dx, dz) from the origin: (0, 0) 6,909; (0, 1) 5,358; the other seven of the
  dx = 0 column and the dz = 0 row 4,558-4,564 each; the other four of the dz = 1 row 1,552 each;
  the other 12 none). A region 60
  spans out misses at none: there the shape-local coordinates are not exact, and rounding puts the
  point inside the cell `floor()` picks. The centre's cell-edge midpoints: 4,512 of 9,312 on lines
  of constant z and 4,512 of 9,312 on lines of constant x.
- *The fix*: `TerrainCollision.vertical_ray(space, x, z, top, bottom, mask, exclude)`. It fires at
  the column itself when it lies `RAY_GRID_EPSILON` or more off every grid line, and otherwise at
  `RAY_GRID_EPSILON` off the nearest line, on the side the column is on first and the other side
  if that misses (`ray_columns`): a line that is a region's edge has ground on only one side while
  the neighbour is not loaded. Grid lines are world multiples of `TILE_SIZE` (20) on x and z,
  because of the placement (half-span 960 = 48 x 20, offsets of whole 1920 = 96 x 20 spans); the
  probe checks every vertex of the 25 regions against that (0 off). The shape is not changed.
  With the helper: **0 misses** at the 235,225 vertices, 0 at the centre's 18,624 midpoints, 0 at
  a lone region's 9,409 (its outer edges answer from the second side; plain rays miss 6,909), 0 at
  the far region's.
- *`RAY_GRID_EPSILON` = 0.01 world units, srrevamp's own engineering choice, disclosed at the
  constant.* The probe's band: every vertex moved (d, d) into its cell, plain rays miss at 50,391
  of 235,225 for d = 0.00001 (as many as on the vertices: below float32's spacing at most of these
  coordinates), 3,416 for d = 0.0001, **0 for d = 0.001 and 0 for d = 0.01**. 0.01 is ten times the
  smallest distance with no miss, and above float32's spacing (the physics server's precision for a
  ray's coordinates) everywhere below 131,072 world units (0.0078 there). Its cost: a height read up
  to 0.01 off on each axis, only for a column within 0.01 of a line, can differ by at most 0.01
  times the triangle's |dh/dx| + |dh/dz|. Measured on Jangan's 25 regions from their parsed
  heightmaps (`QA TERRAIN SLOPE`, step 8's run): the steepest triangle is **19.165** (99/170, quad
  row 67, column 89), so at most **0.19**; in 97/168, where 19 of the 23 monsters stand, 3.314, at
  most 0.033; the others 1.650-11.120. In the suite the hits land within 0.0298 of the drawn vertex
  height against a bound of 0.0293 for its field's steepest 2.933 (float32's spacing at those
  coordinates, 0.00049, makes up the difference; the check allows 0.001).
- *Every vertical ray onto the terrain now goes through it* (`grep` of `PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create`
  and `intersect_ray` in `client/scripts`, all in `World3D.gd`): `_terrain_hit_height` (and so
  `_terrain_height_at`, the walking fallback, the ground items, `_place_player_at_world`, the QA
  goto and retreat placements, `_where_report`'s terrain line and the `SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_LOG` compare
  line); `_snap_player_onto_terrain` (the server's spawn (0, 0, 0) is itself a vertex of the entry
  region; round 567's snap there hit -- one of the vertices that answer); `_recover_if_below_terrain`;
  `_avoid_spawning_under_roof`'s ring (from a vertex, its 0/90/180/270-degree points lie on lines);
  `_physics_step`'s ground check; `_drawn_surface_height`; and the QA reports -- `_qa_step`'s `QA
  <tick> local` drawn-surface ray, `SRREVAMP_QA_RIG`'s column ray (all layers, as before),
  `SRREVAMP_QA_FLOAT`, `SRREVAMP_QA_SCAN` (at 48 samples its lattice is on the vertices), `QA GROUND
  SNAP` (the snap's own ray) and `SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_HEIGHTS`. Left as they are: `QA GROUND`'s lattice
  of vertical rays (a probe of the shape itself, at 0.45 and 0.55 of a tile -- 9 and 11 units off
  the lines, where the helper fires the same single ray); `_has_roof_overhead` (upward, every
  layer, from half a character height above the feet: its question is a roof, not the ground);
  `SRREVAMP_QA_MOB_HEIGHTS`' plain ray (kept on purpose, the negative inside the report); and the
  rays that are not vertical -- the six camera picks, `QA THROUGH`'s and `QA NPCBODY`'s horizontal
  rays, `QA GROUND`'s slanted rays and sweeps: a ray that crosses cells walks the grid
  (`_intersect_grid_segment`), not the one-cell test.
- *Round 567's record corrected in place* (this file and `docs/WORLD_ISSUES.md`): its "1,600 of
  1,600 hit on both" / "every vertical ray hits both" held only off the lines -- verified from its
  code: `_qa_ground_rays_report` fires at `(floor(...) + QA_GROUND_IN_QUAD) * tile`, 0.45 and 0.55
  of a tile, and `terrain_collision_test.gd`'s rays at (0.45, 0.55), (0.3, 0.2) and (0.7, 0.9) of a
  cell; none on a line.

**6. The scene's placeholder ground no longer answers the height ray -- fixed.** `World3D.tscn`'s
`Ground` is a StaticBody3D at the origin with `collision_layer = 9` -- the terrain-only bit
included -- and a 200 x 1 x 200 `BoxShape3D`, top at y 0.5; it is switched off
(`ground_collision.disabled`) when the first terrain group commits and on again by
`_reload_zone_assets`. On the loading-screen path the list is applied before the centre commits
(step 2), so the first pass's `_terrain_hit_height` placed a body listed within 100 of the origin on
it, at 0.898, for good (the review's probe; no Jangan monster is inside it -- the nearest, Yeoha at
(70, -220), is 220 out on z). The same class, found here: `VoidCatchFloor` (layer 9, 200,000 wide,
top at y -1995) answers the ray of a body listed at y -995 or lower -- the suite's body listed at
-1500 was placed on it at -1994.60.

- *Chosen: the placement ray passes through both* (`_stand_in_floor_rids`, the ray's `exclude`),
  rather than taking the placeholder off the terrain-only layer. Read first what else relies on
  them being there: the player's body stands on the placeholder until the terrain commits
  (`move_and_slide`, layer 1 of its mask 17 -- unaffected either way); `_physics_step`'s ground
  check keeps `_last_grounded_position` on it in that window (the void-fall return needs it --
  taking it off the layer would stop that); the snap runs deferred after the centre's commit, which
  has switched it off; `VoidCatchFloor` is the void catch itself. So only the placement ray --
  `_terrain_hit_height`, and so every monster, ground item and player placement through
  `_terrain_height_at` -- ignores them; everything else is as it was.

**9. Landed on round 571's code (the combined-code measurements).** The branch was cut from round
569; rounds 570 and 571 landed on dev first. The cherry-pick conflicted only in `_terrain_commit`,
where round 570 had placed the group with `terrain_group.position = _group_position(world_offset,
anchor_height)` and `scale.z = -1`, and in the two records' append points.

- *One placement.* The same arithmetic both ways: `place_group`'s half is (SIDE - 1) x TILE_SIZE /
  2 = 96 x 20 / 2 = 960 = `REGION_SPAN` / 2, the same z negation, the same `scale.z = -1`.
  `_terrain_commit` now calls `place_group` alone. `_group_position` stays, because `_frame_corner`
  and round 570's frame test read it without a node. `region_grid_state_test.gd` holds the node
  that `place_group` positions to `Transform3D(Basis(1, 1, -1), _group_position(...))`. It checks
  every `FRAME_ROWS` cell (14 of them, in the frames of 97/168 and of 98/157), Constantinople's
  105/79 in 97/168's frame, and the far corner cell of its radius-2 grid (107/77, group at world x
  -175,680). Each cell is checked at four arbitrary anchors: 0, 12.5, -37.25 and 1234.5. Result:
  16 of 16 equal. NEGATIVE: with `place_group`'s half set to SIDE x TILE_SIZE / 2 (970), all 16
  FAIL (`16 FAILURES`), and every other frame check in the suite still passes. So without this
  test, the grid corner and the heightfield's grid lines could drift apart unnoticed.
- *Checked against rounds 570-571, hunk by hunk. Nothing else interacts.*
  - The frame wire (`result.frame` into `_reload_zone_assets`): no hunk of this round touches it.
    The wait list is still cleared in `_on_change_zone_result`, beside `_monster_bodies.clear()`,
    which round 570 left where it was.
  - The frame anchor (`_frame_anchor_height`): it moves y only. Grid lines are x and z.
  - `_load_region_neighborhood`'s centre offset: `_cell_offset(cdx, cdy)` is whole region spans in
    any frame, so every region's grid lines stay on world multiples of 20. `place_group`'s doc
    comment relies on exactly that, and the grid probe checks it.
  - `_grid_origin_world = _frame_corner(...)`: that is `_group_position`, held equal above.
  - `region_grid_state`: `_qa_drawn_mesh_height` and `_qa_terrain_slope_report` read
    `_grid.parsed_heightmaps` through `RegionGridState.region_key`, which round 570 left as it was.
    They find groups by their `RealTerrain_<x>_<y>` names, which are frame-independent.
  - The QA hooks round 570 moved to `_grid_centre_region`: `SRREVAMP_QA_GROUND_RAYS`' gate is one
    of them. This round changed only the snap ray inside that report.
  - The placeholder `Ground`, which `_reload_zone_assets` re-enables: it stays at the world origin,
    which under `-single-frame` is 97/168's middle, not the town's. `_terrain_hit_height` passes
    through it either way.
  - The rays: no hunk of rounds 570-571 adds one. A grep of `PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create`
    in the combined `World3D.gd` finds exactly the rays step 5 lists as left off the helper: the
    NPC-body, `QA THROUGH`, `QA GROUND` lattice and six camera-pick rays, `_has_roof_overhead` and
    the report's plain ray. Every other vertical ray goes through `TerrainCollision.vertical_ray`.
  - `_step_monster_bodies`' only caller is `_step_heights`.
- *Float32 under `-single-frame`* (disclosed at `RAY_GRID_EPSILON`; the arithmetic was checked with
  numpy's float32). Under round 571's flag, world x reaches -175,680 at the edge of
  Constantinople's radius-2 grid. From 131,072 to 262,144 float32's spacing is 1/64, so a column
  0.01 off a line is stored 0.015625 off it: further off the line, still clear of it, and the
  height bound grows by the same factor. From 65,536 to 131,072 the offset is stored as 0.0078125.

## A character logs back in where it left off, behind -persist-position (default OFF), and the client honours a restored position (round 573)

Server behind a new default-OFF flag, `-persist-position` (env `SRREVAMP_PERSIST_POSITION`), plus a
client change; tag-worthy. With the flag on and round 573's client, a disconnect, a logout or a
server restart no longer sends the player back to Jangan's square: the next entry answers where
the character stood. With the flag off nothing is saved or read and the wire is byte for byte what
it was. Tagged clients ignore a restored position in Jangan (measured, step 7), so the flag's flip
waits for the client tag that carries this round. No opcode changes; `OpEnterWorldResult` gains
one trailing byte, sent only when a position was restored.

**1. Grounding, re-checked on the tree at bbafa37.**

- The engine keeps the position on the character row. `_CHAR` declares `LatestRegion`, `PosX`,
  `PosY`, `PosZ` (`persistence.TableColumns["_CHAR"]`, held equal to
  `character.EngineCharColumns`), and `CharData_BindDBColumns` binds them to charData `+0x94`,
  `+0x98`, `+0x9c`, `+0xa0` (`docs/protocol/db_bind_offsets.tsv`; `persistence.ColumnOffsets`,
  whose controls include exactly these three Pos offsets). Until this round
  `character.EngineOnlyColumns` listed all four as "position, which srrevamp keeps in the live
  world rather than on the row".
- `session.handleEnterWorld` always entered `arrival(spawnZone)`: "jangan", `spawnPos`, and the
  zone's frame (or the one frame under `-single-frame`).
- The character store's migration pattern is `ALTER TABLE characters ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ...`
  inside `character/sqlstore.go`'s `schema`, run by `OpenSQLStore`.
- The client threw a Jangan position away on every entry, tagged or not:
  `World3D._load_initial_region_neighborhood` -> `_place_at_zone_spawn(zone)` ->
  `ZONE_SPAWN_LOCAL["97/168"]` = local (1002, 1020) for any label that resolves to 97/168 (the
  grounding verifier's finding; read, and measured in step 7). So a server-only change would have
  passed its Go test and done nothing where testers log out.
- A trailing byte after `FrameRegion` reaches every tagged client unread. Go
  `DecodeEnterWorldResult` / `decodeFrameRegion` and GDScript `decode_enter_world_result` /
  `_decode_frame` all return after the frame without looking at what is left (read), and the
  round-570 decoder decodes a payload with a trailing 0x01 with error `''` (step 6's negative run
  of `world_test.gd` on the pre-573 `world.gd`). Clients before round 570 stop after the entity
  list.

**2. Own design, disclosed at each constant (`session/position.go`'s header).**

- The SHAPE: a zone label, the frame region the coordinates are relative to ("x/y", the
  `FrameRegion` the session named) and a world point in that frame -- not the engine's region id
  and region-local point. `character.Mapping` records it: `Frame` -> `LatestRegion`, `PosX/Y/Z` ->
  `PosX/Y/Z` with that divergence noted, `Zone` -> no column (a divergence: the engine has no
  label).
- WHEN it is saved: on a disconnect (`WorldDisconnectHandler`, from the entity `hub.Leave`
  returns), on each successful zone change (the arrival), at most once every
  `positionSaveInterval` = 30 s from the move handler, and for every character still in the world
  when the server stops (`SaveAllPositions`, called after the listener stops, because the gateway
  runs no `OnDisconnect` for sessions open at a stop -- so a deploy keeps them). Each write is
  bounded by `positionSaveTimeout` = 5 s and a failure is logged, never returned. The retail save
  cadence was not read.
- The FRAME RULE (`inFrame`): the same frame keeps the point exactly; two different regions move
  x and z by `worldmap.Rebase` -- the region-delta form of `worldmap.ToWorld` -- and set the
  height to `spawnPos.Y` (0), because the client anchors each frame's heights on that frame's own
  region (round 570's `_frame_anchor_height`) and the server knows no ground; the client lifts the
  player as it does every arrival. A frame that cannot be converted ("" or not a region, and not
  equal to today's) enters at the spawn.
- The label is remembered on the session (`placeKey`): the hub keeps only the bucket, which under
  `-single-frame` is `world` for every framed label.

**3. The sign rule, as checked.** Region y drives world X, region x drives world Z, Z mirrored
(AGENTS.md; `worldmap.go`'s measured columns). A point saved under 98/157 and read under 97/168
moves by `ToWorld(98, 157, 960, 960, 97, 168)` = (-21120, -1920): 157 < 168 puts it at negative X
and 98 > 97 at negative Z. The plan's test said (21120, -1920); the feasibility verifier caught it,
and the test derives the shift from `ToWorld` and asserts its signs from the convention instead.
A mutation that swaps `Rebase`'s frames gives (21220, 1720) for the saved (100, -200) and fails it.

**4. The change.**

- `character`: `Character.Zone`, `Frame`, `PosX/PosY/PosZ`; `Store.SavePosition`; `SQLStore` adds
  `latest_zone`, `latest_frame` (TEXT, default '') and `pos_x/pos_y/pos_z` (DOUBLE PRECISION,
  default 0) with the usual `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` and selects them in `ListByAccount` and
  `GetByID`; `MemStore` the same. An existing row reads `latest_zone` '' -- nothing saved.
- `session`: `position.go` (`SetPersistPosition`, `rememberPlace`, `savePosition`,
  `savePositionEvery`, `SaveAllPositions`, `restoredArrival`, `inFrame`); `handleEnterWorld`
  enters `restoredArrival` when it answers -- the saved label, that label's bucket and frame as
  `arrival` gives them that day, the saved point named in that frame -- and sets
  `EnterWorldResult.Restored`; `handleChangeZone` remembers the new label and frame and saves the
  arrival; `handleMove` saves every 30 s; `WorldDisconnectHandler(hub, chars)` saves on leave
  (its callers in tests pass nil). `EnterWorldResult.Restored` is ONE byte, 0x01, after
  `FrameRegion`, sent only when true; `decodeFrameRegion` now returns what follows it.
- `cmd/server`: the flag (the `envBool` pattern, a WARN on an unparsable value), its boot line,
  `SetPersistPosition` before the gateway serves, and `SaveAllPositions` after the listener stops.
- Client: `WorldNet.EnterWorldResult.restored` from the byte after the frame (`_decode_frame`
  returns the offset past the field); `World3D._load_initial_region_neighborhood` skips
  `_place_at_zone_spawn` for a restored entry and prints `World3D: the server restored <zone> at
  (x, y, z) in frame <f> -- kept, not moved to the zone's landing spot`; `_unstuck_player` takes a
  restored entry to the current zone's landing (`_place_at_zone_landing`: `ZONE_SPAWN_LOCAL`, else
  the centre region's local (960, 960), `worldmap.Landing`'s point) and leaves the move sync to
  report it. No placement ray was added or changed.

**5. A restored position inside geometry (the orchestrator's question), read from the code.** What
runs on a restored entry: the centre region's deferred `_snap_player_onto_terrain` (its terrain
build's `snap_player` job), which only LIFTS -- it returns when the terrain under the point is not
above the player's feet -- and `_avoid_spawning_under_roof` only after such a lift; and
`_recover_if_below_terrain` every physics frame, which lifts a player with terrain overhead. So a
character saved standing under a roof, on a deck or in a building is left where it stood; only a
saved height below the drawn ground is lifted. `/unstuck` returned to the ENTRY point, which for a
restored entry is the saved spot itself -- so the plan's "`/unstuck` handles it" was false until
`_unstuck_player` above; it now lands at the zone's landing.

**6. Tests.**

- Client: `net/world_test.gd`'s `_test_decode_restored` (0x01 after the frame is restored, 0x00 and

- NEGATIVE, proved. With the production files stashed (`character.go`, `sqlstore.go`,

## Batch-22 review follow-ups (rounds 568-573): record wording, run counts, doc consistency -- no behaviour change (round 574)

The nonblocking review notes on rounds 568-573 and the orchestrator's settled facts, each re-checked
before it was landed -- against this checkout, the logs under `/var/tmp/r567`, `/var/tmp/r572` and
`/var/tmp/r573` on the render box, the box's `/var/tmp/tables`, its read-only
`/opt/srrevamp-server/heightat`, and (read-only) srrevamp-01. Nothing a player sees changes:
comments, records, a usage string and three test changes. Nothing on the wire, no flag, no server or
client behaviour. No Godot benchmark was re-run for a wording fix; the client suites and `check` ran
on the final tree, plus the negatives below. Lane lock `/var/tmp/r574/lock`; no render, no frames.

**1. Round 568's notes.** (a) `World3D._prepared_again`'s doc comment justified the held-texture
rule ("counts if a statistic it measured ... is in the world's entry now") with "a snapshot taken
after that commit would have spared the decode", which holds only if EVERY re-measured statistic was
carried in. Read in `ObjectLoader._prepare_material`: without `SRREVAMP_QA_MATS` each fourCC needs
exactly one statistic (DXT1 `fraction`, DXT3/DXT5 `variance`, uncompressed `binary_cutout`, none for
a flagged layer); `SRREVAMP_QA_MATS` adds `fraction` beside the other two, so only there can one job
measure two on one held texture. **Reworded, not re-coded** (this item changes no behaviour): the
comment now says ANY, says when ANY and EVERY differ, and that the count can run over by such a
texture in QA runs only. (b) Round 568's log-counter change under a "no behaviour change" title:
disclosed there already; recorded. (c) `_test_stale_cells_are_not_committed` fed the guard a cell
out of the window along dx only: closed by a test (below). (d) `docs/TODO.md`'s "Two entry drains at
once": re-read in `_drain_initial_load` and `_show_loading_screen` -- the second drain reuses the
first's screen; both test the one queue as they resume, so they usually leave the pump loop in the
same frame, and whichever resumes second after their last awaited frame then calls `queue_free()` on
the `_loading_screen` the other has nulled; the `_drain_pumping` gap needs them to leave it in
different frames. The item says both, by reading. (e) The 8 `ERROR: Parameter "m" is null.` lines in
`objects_prepare_test` (`mesh_get_surface_count`, the dummy renderer): **they predate round 568**.

## Server-side teleport tables (teleportdata/teleportlink/teleportbuilding as CSVs like npcpos) and the grounded fee, waiver and restriction rules (round 575)

The first round of the town-teleporter batch (the user, 2026-09-25: "there's crystals in each town
... that teleport you between towns for gold (it should be free for gms or while testing)"). No
behaviour change: a package, an exporter mode and a flag that loads the tables at boot. The
handler that charges and moves is the next item (map-teleport-protocol).

**What was wired.**

- `cmd/export-refdata -mode teleport -out <dir> teleportdata.txt teleportlink.txt
  teleportbuilding.txt` (`exportTeleport`): the three Media.pk2 tables (UTF-16LE, BOM on row 1, read
  with the existing `readTable`) -> `teleportdata.csv`, `teleportlink.csv`, `teleportbuilding.csv`,
  each with a header; the output is loaded back through `teleport.Load` before the tool returns,
  so an export the server cannot load fails at export time. teleportdata and teleportlink rows
  whose service column is 0 are skipped, as the client's loader skips them (`FUN_00b9cc80` returns
  the column's integer; the loader parses the row only when it is non-zero, `0x954b1a` /
  `0x954b9d`); every retail row has service 1, so nothing is skipped today. teleportbuilding's
  loader is elsewhere (`Client_LoadAllRefData`, `0x844cd0`) and its service handling is not read,
  so its column 0 is not filtered. A row with fewer fields than the columns read (14 / 23 / 59 in
  every retail row) is an error, not a skip: every table's widths are checked before anything is
  written, and the tool exits 1 naming the file and the row (`export-refdata: ...teleportlink.txt:
  row 4 (not counting blank and // lines) has 4 fields, fewer than the 22 the export reads`), with
  no output directory created.
- `internal/teleport` (new): `Load(dir)` / `Read` -> `Table{Points, Links, Buildings}` in file
  order; `PointByID`, `PointByBuildingCode` (STORE_CH_GATE -> GATE_CH through the building's id),
  `LinksFrom` (file order), `LinkBetween`. `Read` refuses a missing or foreign header (checked
  name by name -- the npcpos loader's rule, tightened), a short row, a non-numeric field, a fee
  that is not a 32-bit unsigned word, duplicate ids, codes or links, and a link whose end is not a
  point. `rules.go`: `QuoteFee(link, level, isGM, freeFlag) (fee, Waiver)` and
  `CheckRestrictions(link, level, pvp) uint16`, with the refusal codes as constants carrying their UIIT
  tokens.
- `cmd/server -teleport-dir` (env `SRREVAMP_TELEPORT_DIR`): loads the directory after the npcpos
  block and logs `level=INFO msg="teleport network loaded" dir=<dir> points=222 links=292
  buildings=77` on a retail export (slog's text handler; `server/README.md` quotes it so); a configured directory that does not load is fatal (`os.Exit(1)`, as `-npcpos-csv`).
- `client/tools/qa_shot.sh`: `-teleport-dir $PK2_DIR/teleport` (or `SRREVAMP_TELEPORT_DIR`) when
  `teleportdata.csv` is there. `deploy/README.md`: the extract/export lines and the compose mount.

**Grounding, re-verified this round** (dump `/var/tmp/decomp_server`, `srv.asm`, the client dump,
the tables under `/var/tmp/tables`, all read-only):

- The fee: `GObjPC::HandleTeleportUse` (`getfn.sh 00513590`): `uVar7 = piVar5[1]` (`mov
  esi,[edi+0x4]` at `0x5136d7`), zeroed when `GetMaxLevel` (vslot 74, `+0x128`) is not above 20
  (`cmp al,0x14; ja; xor esi,esi` at `0x5136de`; the second `cmp al,0xa` is redundant), the
  fortress tax when the gate's vslot 276 says so, then the 64-bit gold compare -> `0x1c07` at
  `0x513749`. `CMainProcess::FUN_004f2b50` has the same fee block after the evaluator.
- The restrictions: `FUN_00513a70` (`getfn.sh 00513a70`, 1,058 bytes) walks the 12-byte triples
  at `link+0x10..+0x14`; the arms (1 level via vslot 73 unsigned -> `0x1c15`; 2 and 7 `IHaveCart`
  -> `0x1c10`; 3 the character's PvP state against a mask -> `0x1c19`; 4/5 a held item -> `0x1c23`; 6 `GetJobState`
  != 4 -> `0x1c24`; anything else passes) and their instruction addresses are in
  `docs/protocol/teleport_network.md`, "The restriction triples are enforced". Call sites in
  `srv.asm`: `0x4ef7b9` (`CGObjPC::vslot_309`), `0x4f2e24` and `0x4f34a0`
  (`CMainProcess::FUN_004f2b50`, the first before the fee). `error_emitters.tsv` lists it as the
  only emitter of `0x1c15`.
- The columns: the client's `RefParse_teleportdata` (`0x976840`) and `RefParse_teleportlink`
  (`0x976c80`) after the loader's service-column reads (`0x954b1a`, `0x954b9d`); the server's
  `RefTeleport_ExtractData` layout (`refdata_tables.md`); the `_RefObjCommon` prefix for the
  building (`refobj_binary_format.md`). **One disagreement, recorded rather than resolved:** the
  client's link parser reads five direct tokens before the triples, the file has six (columns
  1-6), so by the parser alone the triples would start at column 6. The data puts them at 7: all
  1,125 type-0 slots have blank or zero data words there (3 blank, all on link 1 -> 5, and 1,122
  zero; read from column 6 the types would include 999 x69, 110 x14, 102 and two blanks, and every

  the type-4 arm looks up before refusing with the Roc-entrance code.
- Retail measurements (the three tables copied to the scratchpad, exported, loaded; never
  committed): 222 / 292 / 77 rows, 0 skipped; every link joins; no duplicate ids, codes or
  point-per-object; the five town gates resolve by building code (STORE_CH/WC/KT/EU/CA_GATE ->
  points 1/2/5/20/25); Jangan's links in file order 2, 175, 176, 5, 20, 25; at level 50, 245 links
  pass, 46 refuse `0x1c15`, the Roc link refuses `0x1c23`; 188 links are free.

**Stand-ins, disclosed** (in `rules.go` and the teleport page): Level stands in for MaxLevel
(equal unless a character lost levels, which srrevamp cannot do); no fortress tax (no fortresses);
types 2 and 7 pass (no trade carts); type 3 tests the PvP state the caller passes, and the caller
passes `PvPNeutral` because srrevamp models no PvP state (no PK system; `internal/duel`'s
own-design duel sets none); types 4 and 5 refuse when their data 1 is non-zero and type 6 refuses
on (0, 0) -- the inventory and the job state are not consulted, so the rule fails closed with the
engine's code; the GM waiver and the testing-flag waiver are own design (the user's ask), reported
after the engine's level waiver; `CheckRestrictions` returns 0 for a pass where the binary returns
1. **Enforcing the rules at all is a stand-in**: the evaluator enforces them only when the mode
byte at `link+8` is 0 -- after each rule (`0x513ccf`) and after the last (`0x513d35`), any non-zero
mode other than 1 drops every rule failure and ends like a clean walk, and 1 asserts and returns 2
-- and which value fills `+8` was not read: the `_REFTELELINK` table loads through a reflective
descriptor (`FUN_0082d770` registers `"_REFTELELINK"` as `CRefTeleLink`, `0x30` bytes), and the
three columns between the fee and the first triple are 0 in every retail row. srrevamp enforces
them, as mode 0 does. `0x1c19` has no text (`error_codes.md` has no row). Teleportdata's columns
10/11 are named by the interaction ids they register (7, 9), not by a service: which services
those are is still open (round 454), so the plan's "recall designate / return" names were not
used. The point's associated object is `ObjectID`, not "BuildingID": of the 222 retail points 71
name a teleportbuilding, 32 a characterdata `NPC_*` row (GATE_NPC_CH_FERRY -> 2011 NPC_CH_FERRY),
118 none (0), and one -- point 228 `GATE_JOBTEMPLE`, object 49143 -- names an object in no table
under `/var/tmp/tables` (every table's id column searched, and a second probe grepping every
decoded table for the number as a field finds it only in teleportdata). The first draft said "33
retail points name an NPC", counting that one as an NPC.

**Review follow-ups, folded into this round's commit.** The first draft's code comments
(`tables.go`'s `Link.Rules`, the exporter's `tlRules`) said every type-0 slot carries BLANK data
words; recounted read-only over `/var/tmp/tables/teleportlink.txt`: 1,125 type-0 slots of 1,460,

rule, then assert and return 2"; per `0x513a70` and `srv.asm` that is mode 1 only -- any other
non-zero mode walks every rule, drops their failures and ends like a clean walk (the post-pass,
`1` or `0x1c23`); `teleport_network.md` and `rules.go` now say so. Round 454's "the server's copy
has no zone-name column" is softened: `RefTeleport_ExtractData` calls the column-skip helper
`FUN_006b1a80` right after the associated-object dword, so whether the server's copy lacks the
column or skips it is open; the Interaction7/9 columns are 10/11 either way. And the exporter now
skips service-0 rows (above), which also gives the round-trip test a row that proves the BOM is
stripped.

**Re-review fix, folded in: rule type 3 is the character's PvP state.** The first draft read the
type-3 arm as "a bit of a ref-object byte, not identified" and refused whenever D1 was non-zero.
Re-read in `srv.asm`: `0x513b46 mov eax,[ebx+0x30]; 0x513b49 mov cl,[eax+0xc]; 0x513b4c mov
edx,1; 0x513b51 shl edx,cl; 0x513b53 test [esi+0x4],edx; 0x513b56 je 0x513ccc` (pass), else
`0x1c19` at `0x513b5c`. EBX is the PC -- all three callers do `mov ebx,ebp` right before the call
(`0x4ef7b7`, `0x4f2e22`, `0x4f349e`), and in `CGObjPC::vslot_309` EBP is `this` (`mov ebp,ecx` at
`0x4ef4cb`); every other arm reads the character through EBX too (its vtable for level, cart and
job; its inventory at `+0x1c10`). `+0x30` is the chardata
pointer and chardata `+0xc` is `PvPSTATE` -- 0 `NEUTRAL`, 1 `ASSAULTER`, 2 `MURDERER` -- which the
state dump `FUN_00567190` indexes its `PTR_s_PvPSTATE_NEUTRAL_00c6404c` table by
(`character_state.md`, "The chardata offsets, from the index expressions"; re-read with `getfn.sh
00567190`). So **the engine refuses iff `D1 & (1 << pvpState)` is non-zero**: D1 is a mask of
barred states, and `(3,2,0)` bars assaulters and lets a neutral character through, where the draft
refused it. `CheckRestrictions` now takes the state (`PvPState`, `PvPNeutral` / `PvPAssaulter` /
`PvPMurderer`) and the constant is `ErrPvPState`. srrevamp models no PvP state (a grep of
`server/` for PvP / PK / assault / murder finds only the own-design duel, the PK columns
`character/schema.go` lists as unmodelled, and the death-penalty branches that say there is no PK
system), so the teleport handler will pass `PvPNeutral` -- a disclosed stand-in, recorded in
`rules.go` and in `orphans_test.go`'s `CheckRestrictions` line until that call site exists. **No
retail link uses type 3**: 0 of the 1,460 triple slots in `/var/tmp/tables/teleportlink.txt` (BOM
stripped), counted twice with different decoders (`iconv` + `awk`, and Python over the raw
UTF-16; the type tallies sum to 1,460: 1,125 type 0, 84 type 1, 245 type 2, 3 type 7, one each
of 4, 5, 6), and no cell of columns 7-21 is `3` at all -- so there are no D1 values to report and
the fix changes no retail link's outcome. The label is corrected in `rules.go`,
`teleport_network.md` (the type-3 row and "The columns srrevamp reads"), `SYSTEMS.md`'s Teleport
network row, this entry and the commit message.
