## OpTeleportUse 0x00F3 / OpTeleportResult 0x00F4: the gate link is charged and the arrival reuses the zone-change warp and loading screen (round 576)

The second round of the town-teleporter batch (the user, 2026-09-25: "there's crystals in each town
... that teleport you between towns for gold (it should be free for gms or while testing)"). The
server now answers a gate's MOVE: it checks the link, charges the table's fee (free below level 21
as the engine does, always for GM accounts, and for everyone under a new default-OFF
`-teleport-free`), and moves the player to the destination gate's point through the zone change's
own arrival, so the client reloads behind its loading screen. The client half decodes the reply,
prints the receipt or the refusal in the archive's words, and keeps the arrival point instead of
moving a Jangan arrival on to the square. Nothing sends the request yet: the clickable gate and
its board are the next items (map-teleport-gate-talk, map-teleport-board).

**What was wired.**

- `server/internal/session/teleport.go` (new): `OpTeleportUse 0x00F3` {u16 gate, u16 destination
  -- teleportdata ids} and `OpTeleportResult 0x00F4` {u8 ok, u16 code, u8 waiver, u64 gold charged,
  string destination `SN_ZONE_*` token, string reason}, srrevamp's own placeholders (free: the
  highest op in `server/internal/session` and `client/scripts/net` was `0x00F2`, and no file under
  `server/`, `client/scripts` or `docs/` named `0x00F3`/`0x00F4`, re-grepped this round).
  `TeleportHandler(chars, eq, hub, network, gate, free, logger)`; `teleporter.use` runs, in order:
  in the world, alive (handleChangeZone's own-design dead refusal), the gate point, which must
  belong to a teleportbuilding row (`gateBuilding`, through `PointByBuildingCode`; a ferry point's
  object is an NPC), the link (`LinkBetween`), a destination srrevamp can place (a dungeon point, a
  negative region, is refused), `CheckRestrictions(link, level, teleport.PvPNeutral)` with the
  stand-in disclosed at the call site, `QuoteFee(link, level, gate.Allows(username), free)`, the
  charge (`DeductGold`; `ErrInsufficientGold` -> `0x1c07`, nothing moved), a log line, the receipt,
  then `warpTo`. Refusals carry the engine's code (2, 0x1c07, 0x1c15, ...) or 0 for srrevamp's
  own, and the server's wording as `Reason`, the client's fallback. A move that fails after the
  charge (the session left the world in between) refunds it.
- `session/world.go`: `warpTo(ctx, sess, eq, chars, hub, zone, bucket, pos, frame)` -- the tail of
  `handleChangeZone` (hub move, keep-up cancel, `rememberPlace`, `savePosition`, the mover's
  `OpChangeZoneResult`, `OpEntityLeft` to the old bucket, `OpEntityEntered` to the new), factored
  out unchanged; `handleChangeZone` calls it. `0x0026`/`0x0027`'s layouts are untouched.
- `cmd/server`: `-teleport-free` (env `SRREVAMP_TELEPORT_FREE`, `envBool`, a WARN on a bad value,
  a boot line either way), the loaded network handed to `session.TeleportHandler` with the
  `-gm-accounts` gate, registered after the GM console; `-teleport-dir`'s help says what uses it.
- `internal/systems/orphans_test.go`: `PointByID`, `PointByBuildingCode`, `LinkBetween`, `QuoteFee`
  and `CheckRestrictions` leave `knownOrphans`; `LinksFrom` stays, reworded -- the destination list
  is the client's own (the retail dialog builds it from the client's link records,
  `UI_TELEPORT::FUN_006fd3e0`), so no server message carries it.
- Client: `client/scripts/net/teleport.gd` (`TeleportNet`: the opcodes, `encode_use`,
  `decode_result` -- null on any truncation -- the waiver constants and `receipt_line`);
  `NetClient.teleport_use` and `teleport_result`; `ErrorText` gains `0x1c10` and `0x1c15` and
  `teleport_line`; `World3D._on_teleport_result` prints the receipt (`TeleportNet.receipt_line`,
  the place through textdata_object, `_teleport_place_name`) or the refusal, and marks the next
  `OpChangeZoneResult` as the teleport's arrival (`_teleport_arrival_pending`);
  `_on_change_zone_result` then keeps the server's position -- not `_place_at_zone_spawn` -- and
  stands it on the walkable graph (`_land_teleport_arrival`), holding the player at the point, no
  walk, no fall, while its region is still queued (`_step_teleport_landing`, stepped from
  `_physics_step`), released to the ordinary ground snap if the drain ends with no graph there.

**Grounding, re-verified this round** (read-only: `getfn.sh` on `/var/tmp/decomp_server` and
`/var/tmp/decomp_client` with zero-padded addresses, `srv.asm`, `sro_client.asm`, `objdump -s` on
the box's `sro_client.exe`, the tables under `/var/tmp/tables`):

- `GObjPC::HandleTeleportUse` (`getfn.sh 00513590`): `0x1c14` first (`GetTeleportState`), the range
  test, then kind 2: `call 0x485d60` (the link); `test edi,edi; je 0x513910` and `cmp [edi],0; je
  0x513910` -> `mov [esp+0x14],0x2` at `0x513910` -- **code 2 is the engine's "no such link"**; the
  fee `mov esi,[edi+0x4]` (`0x5136d7`), `cmp al,0x14` (`0x5136de`), the gold compare refusing
  `mov [esp+0x14],0x1c07` at `0x513749`, and only after it `CGObjPC::FUN_004e0a40` (the teleport
  state). The gate lookup's miss (`FUN_00485d90` returning 0) is a bare `return`: no reply.
- `FUN_00513a70` (`getfn.sh 00513a70`): the refusal codes `0x1c15`, `0x1c10`, `0x1c19`, `0x1c23`,
  `0x1c24` (round 575's reading; its callers run it before the fee on `CMainProcess::FUN_004f2b50`'s
  path).
- The retail pair, for the record: `CIF_NPCTalk::FUN_0081ddf0` builds `0x705a` -- `"TELEPORTGATE ->
  Type(%d), Target(%d)"`, then a u32 (the gate), the u8 kind and, for kind 2, a u32 target. The
  reply `0xb05a`: **`FUN_008809d0` does not contain the constant** (the verifier was right; it is
  76 bytes) -- `FUN_0086fbb0` registers it for `0xb05a` (`local_1c = 0xb05a; local_18 =
  FUN_008809d0`), and it reads a u8 result and, on 2, a u16 code passed to `FUN_00778190(0xd, code,
  0xffdbc99b, 0, 1)`. So the teleport reply's message category is READ: `0xd`, the interaction
  table.
- The category-`0xd` jump table (`objdump -s --start-address=0x7bbaac`, `code - 0x1c07`): entry 9
  (`0x1c10`) `0x7ba0a7` pushes `0xdc2458` `UIIT_MSG_INTERACTION_FAIL_CANT_USE_TELEPORT_WITH_TRADECART`;
  entry 14 (`0x1c15`) `0x7ba111` pushes `0xdc4e88`
  `UIIT_MSG_INTERACTION_FAIL_OUT_OF_REQUIRED_LEVEL_FOR_TELEPORT` (the names read as UTF-16 out of the
  exe); entry 0 is `0x1c07`'s `0x7ba085` as recorded. Code 2 has no message there: the chain below

  (`0x7b8b7b`), with no other write to it in the function -- and 4, and sends the rest to the
  default `0x7b913a`. Code 0 would be `UIIT_STT_ERR_COMMON_INVALID_TARGET` (`0x7ba04e`); srrevamp's
  client does not route code 0 through the table.
- textuisystem.txt (`/var/tmp/tables`): two rows each of `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_RESULT` ('Teleport to
  [%s] for [%d] Gold.' and 'Teleport to [%s]area. [%d]gold') and `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_FREE_RESULT`;

- teleportdata / teleportlink / teleportbuilding rows used by the fixture, read this round: GATE_CH

  5000 `(2,0,0)`; buildings 2094 (25000, 1254/-6/1374), 2095 (26521 = 103/153, 962/-35/8), 19555

**The orchestrator's notes, answered.**

- *The destination label.* `teleportZoneFor`: the town whose `worldmap.ZoneCentre` IS the point's
  region, else the town whose centre is one region away, else the region's "x/y". Jangan, Donwhang,
  Hotan and Constantinople arrive under their own labels in their own frames; Samarkand's GATE_CA
  (106/108) arrives under "samarkand" in 106/107's frame at `ToWorld(106, 108, 270, 1421, 106,
  107)` -- one region over in world X (region y drives world X, region x drives world Z, Z
  mirrored: AGENTS.md; every expected value in the tests is derived from `worldmap.ToWorld`, none
  written from prose). `ZoneNames` is sorted, so Donwhang's 102/153 is "donwhang" (the roster's and
  /goto's), not "dunhuang". Under `-single-frame` the label's frame is `WorldOrigin`'s and the bucket
  the world's (`arrival`). The plan's '"102/153"' label is superseded as the note said.
- *The arrival spot.* The server sends the destination's teleportdata point; the client keeps it.
  Choice: the client remembers the receipt (the server sends `OpTeleportResult` first on the same
  ordered stream, then the `OpChangeZoneResult`), rather than a trailing byte on `0x0027` -- the
  item's step 1 forbids touching `0x0027`'s layout, and no older client ever sends the request, so
  nothing older needs a flag. The Jangan override (`ZONE_SPAWN_LOCAL`, local 1002, 1020) no longer
  applies to a teleport arrival: GATE_CH's point (969, 1369) is kept. The landing height is the
  walkable graph's (`landing_height_at`), as a typed `@x,z` lands; no new straight-down ray was
  added (the existing snap and the hold's release use `TerrainCollision.vertical_ray` already).
- *Citations.* `FUN_008809d0` is the handler and `FUN_0086fbb0` the registrar (above); the
  opcode census re-run.
- *Free rules.* GM accounts always (`gm.Gate`, the console's gate, passed into the handler), everyone
  under `-teleport-free` (default OFF), the engine's own waiver below 21 -- in `QuoteFee`'s order, so
  a level-1 GM reports the engine's waiver (1), a level-30 GM the GM waiver (2). `server/README.md`
  names the flag; `deploy/README.md`, "Town teleporters", says the public server's flip is the
  user's call.
- *The PvPNeutral call site.* `teleporter.use` passes `teleport.PvPNeutral` with the disclosure at
  the call.
- *The QA teleport CSVs.* Not placed on the box. The box was running another lane's renders
  (`/opt/srrevamp-client-white`, `/var/tmp/rwhite`) throughout, and `qa_shot.sh` kills every Godot
  on the box before it starts, so no live client run was made this round (the end-to-end run with
  the gate click is map-teleport-board's acceptance). Instead the retail tables were copied into
  this session's scratch (never committed), exported with `export-refdata -mode teleport` (222
  points, 292 links, 77 buildings) and measured two ways, below.

## The Dimensional Gate is clickable: the placed portal object is bound as the gate NPC and its talk menu offers 'Select a teleport area:' (round 577)

This is the third round of the town-teleporter batch. The user asked on 2026-09-25 for the town
"crystals" that teleport you between towns for gold. Clicking a town's Dimensional Gate now opens
the talk window. The window is titled with the gate's own name, "Dimensional Gate". It lists the
client's own lines for a gate: the return-point designation, the teleport-area line and the end
line. Choosing a line does nothing new yet. "teleport" and the recall lines answer "... is not
available yet" until the board (map-teleport-board) and a return-point model exist.

**Answer to the title.** The title's quote, 'Select a teleport area:', is the text of the EARLIER
16-column row. The player's textuisystem.txt holds `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_TARGET` twice, and
`UiTextTable` keeps the later 19-column row. So the line reads **"Select teleport area"**, and the
designate line reads "Designate as return/recall point". The job-guild lines of round 526 work
the same way.

**What was wired.**

- `client/scripts/npc/teleport_reader.gd` (new, `TeleportReader`). It parses the three Media.pk2
  tables: `server_dep\silkroad\textdata\teleportdata.txt`, `teleportlink.txt` and
  `teleportbuilding.txt`.
  - It reads the 0-based columns that `server/cmd/export-refdata` reads (round 575). teleportdata:
    id 1, code 2, object 3, zone 4, region 5, x/y/z 6-8, radius 9, interaction flags 10/11.
    teleportlink: from 1, to 2, fee 3. teleportbuilding: id 1, code 2, name 5, region 41,
    x/y/z 43-45.
  - teleportdata and teleportlink rows are kept only when their service column is a non-zero
    integer. The client's loader parses a row only when that column is non-zero (`0x954b1a`,
    `0x954b9d`). teleportbuilding's column 0 is not filtered. A row whose id is not an integer is
    skipped.
  - The API: `buildings_in_region(rx, ry)`, `point_for_building(code)`, `links_from(point_id)`
    (file order), `place_token(point_id)` and `summary()`. `point_for_building` joins teleportdata's
    object column to the building's id. Region ids unpack as `(x << 8) | y`, as npcpos does. A
    negative region (a dungeon) or region 0 belongs to no region.
- `NpcServiceReader.gate_services(has_links, designate, recall)` returns the gate's lines in the
  real client's order. `FUN_00700440` asks for id 7 at `0x700c57` (item 9), id 9 at `0x700ca7` (item
  0x10) and id 8 at `0x700cfb` (item 0xa, after the desert-gate company lines).
  - Each item's token was re-read this round in `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm` and in the exe's
    `.rdata`, decoded as UTF-16. `FUN_006fcd60`'s index bytes are at `0x6fd394` and its jump table
    at `0x6fd2d8`.
  - Item 9 takes index 8 -> `0x6fcf10` `push 0xdadc38` = `UIIT_CTL_RECALL_POSITION`.
  - Item 0x10 takes index 0xd -> `0x6fcf1a` `push 0xdadbf0` = `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_TO_RESURRECT_POS`.
  - Item 0xa takes index 9 -> `0x6fcf24` `push 0xdadbb8` = `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_TARGET`.
- `World3D`:
  - `_load_npc_tables` loads the reader and keeps its textdata_object parse as
    `_object_name_table`, so the table is not parsed twice. Its load line adds `222 teleport
    point(s), 292 link(s), 77 gate building(s)`.
  - `_try_spawn_region_npcs` calls `_bind_region_gates` right after the region's NPC mark. Both
    callers, the grid centre and `_load_region_cell`, commit the region's objects just before, so
    the portal is in the tree. The mark goes when a streamed-out region is unloaded (round 563), so
    the fresh copies are bound again when the region comes back.
  - `_bind_region_gates` handles each teleportbuilding row in the region whose point registers
    interaction id 7 (teleportdata column 10 = 1) -- the town gates; see "Review fix" below. It
    takes the nearest child of `RealMapObjects_<rx>_<ry>` (positions region-local) within
    `GATE_BIND_RADIUS` (10) of the row's x/z. It tags that node `npc_name` (the name string through
    textdata_object), `npc_code` and `gate_point_id`. It ORs `NPC_COLLISION_LAYER` into every
    StaticBody3D under the node (`_tag_gate`).
  - When no object is that near, the gate is left unbound (not clickable) and the log says so.
    The first cut put a stand-in cylinder there; the review fix removed it (below).
  - `_npc_services` appends `gate_services` when the code is a gate: the point's two flags, plus
    whether `links_from` is empty.
  - `_qa_click_target_for` has a new `"gate"` kind (`SRREVAMP_QA_CLICK=gate`). It picks the
    nearest node under the terrain groups' `RealMapObjects_*` containers whose `npc_code` is
    `STORE_*_GATE`. `_qa_gate_target` aims at the middle of its drawn world box, and the QA click
    line marks a point outside the viewport `OFF-SCREEN`.

**Grounding, checked this round.**

## The authored teleport board (ifteleportboard + ifteleportareaslot): destinations with fees, five a page, MOVE sends the request, the receipt and the loading-screen arrival (round 578)

The fourth round of the town-teleporter batch, and the one that makes a gate usable. Talk to a
town's Dimensional Gate, choose 'Select teleport area', and the authored Dimensional Teleporter
opens with the gate's destinations and their fees. Move asks the server (round 576's
`OpTeleportUse`), which charges or waives the fee and moves the player to the destination gate's
point behind the zone change's loading screen.

**Grounding, re-read this round** (read-only on the render box):

- **The layouts**, `/var/tmp/resinfo` (extracted from the player's Media.pk2, never committed).
  `ifteleportboard.txt` (section Create): `GDR_TB_STATIC_TITLE` CIFStatic 13,17,393,21 with
  `UIIT_PAG_TELEPORT`; `GDR_TB_BTN_CLOSE` CIFCloseButton 406,15,16,16; `GDR_TB_STATIC_NAME`
  CIFStatic 8,65,432,21 with `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_TARGET`; `GDR_TB_SPIN_PAGE` CIFSpinButtonCtrl
  181,520,80,24; `GDR_TB_TASLOT1..5` CIFTeleportAreaSlot 47,{105,185,265,345,425},357,76.
  `ifteleportareaslot.txt`: `GDR_TAS_BTN_MOVE` CIFButton 252,20,92,36 with `UIIT_CTL_MOVE` and
  DDJ ""; `GDR_TAS_STATIC_PRICE` 70,44,182,21; `GDR_TAS_STATIC_PLACE` 70,14,182,21;
  `GDR_TAS_STATIC_ICON` 6,6,64,64. No control sits at the origin: the board has no frame.
- **The texts**, `/var/tmp/tables/textuisystem.txt`. The 16-column rows: `UIIT_PAG_TELEPORT`
  "Dimensional Teleporter", `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_TARGET` "Select a teleport area:",
  `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_RESULT` "Teleport to [%s] for [%d] Gold.", `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_FREE_RESULT`
  "Teleport to [%s] (no cost).", `UIIT_CTL_MOVE` "Move". The later 19-column rows, which
  `UiTextTable` keeps: "Dimensional door", "Select teleport area", "Teleport to [%s]area. [%d]gold",
  "Teleport to [%s]area.", "Move".
- **The list** (docs/protocol/teleport_network.md, "The client's list, read"):
  `UI_TELEPORT::FUN_006fd3e0` builds the destinations from the client's own link records in
  order, and formats each with `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_FREE_RESULT` when the link's fee word is 0,
  `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_RESULT` with the fee otherwise. Neither `tpt_window` nor
  `ifteleportboard`/`CIFTeleportAreaSlot` appears in the client decompile
  (`grep` over `/var/tmp/decomp_client/funcs_*.c`); `UIIT_CTL_TELEPORT_TARGET` does (funcs_007.c),
  so the window art's use stays unread.
- **The feasibility finding answered.** `HudWindow.build`'s empty title does NOT fall back to
  `GDR_TB_STATIC_TITLE`: `_authored_title` reads only a frame at the origin, and this layout has
  none, so the window's own title bar is left empty. The authored static is built by UiBuilder and
  resolves `UIIT_PAG_TELEPORT` itself, so `PANELS["teleport"]` passes "" -- a title there would
  draw a second caption over the authored one.

**What was wired.**

- `client/scripts/ui/hud/teleport_board.gd` (new, `TeleportBoard`). The pure helpers:
  `page_count(n)` (ceil(n / 5), 0 for none), `page_rows(entries, page)` (at most five, empty past
  the end or for a negative page) and `price_text(place, fee, waived, result_fmt, free_fmt)` (the
  free format for a 0 fee or the waiver, the fee format otherwise, srrevamp's own "No cost" /
  "<n> gold" when a format is not exactly those placeholders -- `TeleportNet._fits`). The node
  work: `build_rows` builds ifteleportareaslot's section inside each CIFTeleportAreaSlot once and
  connects its Move; `fill_rows` writes PLACE and PRICE (with the whole sentence as a tooltip)
  and the row's destination onto Move, hiding slots past the page; `move_button_for`.
- `HudPanels`: `PANELS["teleport"] = ["resinfo\\ifteleportboard.txt", "", 0]`, signal
  `teleport_requested(dest_id)`, `open_teleport_board(gate_name, entries)` (rows built once, the
  spinner's range set to the page count and reset to page 1, a line with the counts) and
  `qa_press_teleport_move(dest_id)` (turns to the page, prints the page as drawn, emits that
  row's own Move).
- `World3D`: "teleport" in `_on_npc_service_selected` opens `_open_teleport_board` -- one entry
  per `TeleportReader.links_from(point)` in file order: the destination id, the place
  (`_teleport_place_name` of the point's zone token, else its teleportdata codename -- never the
  SN_ token), the link's fee, and `waived` for a character of level 20 or below. Move ->
  `_on_teleport_requested` -> `NetClient.teleport_use(gate point, dest)` ("Teleporting needs the
  server." offline). `_on_teleport_result` closes the board on the server's yes and prints the
  receipt it logs; `_on_change_zone_result` closes it and the gate's talk box on any successful
  zone change (`_close_gate_ui`, the review fix below). `_player_level` comes
  from `_on_world_stats`. `SRREVAMP_QA_TELEPORT=<id>` (`_qa_advance_teleport`): once a gate's
  talk box is up, choose the line through the talk box's handler, then press Move.
- `TeleportReader.point_by_id` (the codename fallback). `qa_shot.sh --teleport <id>`;
  `client/tools/README.md` "A town teleport is a run too".

**Disclosed stand-ins.** The slot icon stays empty (nothing attributes per-destination art). The
board's window art (`interface\teleport\tpt_window_zangan.ddj`, 420,372 B; a

## A player-runnable /groundprobe for the white ground after reconnect (round 579)

Client only, tag-worthy: the tester needs a release that carries it. A chat command and an F3
button any player can use, one renderer line per world entry, and metadata on the terrain; nothing
on the wire, no flag, no server change. Nothing a player sees changes unless they run `/groundprobe`,
whose checks flash the ground until its chat line says it is done and put everything back (a few
seconds is a guess, not a measurement on a player's machine: every step reads the frame back and
walks it in GDScript, about 88k samples a step at 720p and 9x that at 4K). **Building it turned
up two measured findings that change what the tester's file will be read against** (below: the
project's renderer setting never takes effect, so a plain launch runs Forward+ on Vulkan; and the
box DOES draw flat, untextured terrain after a reconnect -- the base surface drawn over the
textured passes when recycled material RIDs invert their draw order). No fix is in this round.

**Why.** The tester reported the white ground after a disconnect + reconnect in one process again
on 2026-09-26, with a screenshot: buildings, walls, trees, bushes, sky and HUD textured; the terrain
near-white with soft green/brown gradients that follow the mesh's quads. Rounds 558-560 never
reproduced it on the render box, and a Windows release cannot set `SRREVAMP_QA_*`.

**Change.**

- `client/scripts/world/ground_probe.gd` (new, `GroundProbe`): the probe. `start` runs the read-only
  half at once and, in full mode inside the tree, arms the A/B steps it walks in `_process` (a
  frame-counted state machine, no `await`, so a world that leaves the tree just frees it). No
  static state: the entry count, the previous entry's exit record and GL names, and the run count
  live in the process environment (`SRREVAMP_WORLD_ENTRY`, `SRREVAMP_WORLD_LAST_EXIT`,
  `SRREVAMP_GROUNDPROBE_PREV_GL`, `SRREVAMP_GROUNDPROBE_RUNS`), as round 558's `SRREVAMP_QA_ENTRY`
  does.
- `World3D._ready` prints, for every player at every entry, `World3D: entry <n> (instance <id>,
  <first entry | re-entered after: ...>) -- running=... adapter=... api=...` plus the renderer
  settings (`GroundProbe.entry_line`), so any log carries the GPU without the command. It does NOT
  ask for the driver version (`driver_info=(not queried at entry ...)`; the probe's `gpu` line
  does): on Windows, Godot 4.2.2 answers `OS.get_video_adapter_driver_info` with a synchronous WMI
  query, `SELECT * FROM Win32_PnPSignedDriver WHERE DeviceName = ...`, waiting up to 5 s in
  `IEnumWbemClassObject::Next`, on the main thread, cached only once it returns
  (platform/windows/os_windows.cpp, `OS_Windows::get_video_adapter_driver_info`, 4.2.2-stable) --
  read from source, not measured on Windows, and not a cost a world entry should carry while the
  loading freezes are open.
- `World3D._run_ground_probe` (console host `ground_probe`), `_world_entry`, `_grid_builds`
  (`_load_region_neighborhood`), `_terrain_commits`; `_terrain_commit` leaves a `ground_probe` meta
  on each terrain group (the prepare's ground counts -- `_prepare_ground_textures` now also puts them
  in the job --, tiles uploaded, lightmap, the baked light, the commit's number for that `.m`);
  `_exit_tree` calls `GroundProbe.record_exit` before it clears the caches.
- `MapmTerrainBuilder._surface_material` tags each terrain material with its tile ID (meta
  `terrain_texture_key`), so a pass whose ID missed the lookup is told from one drawn with none.
- `Console`: `/groundprobe [quick]` (client-side, any player; "quick" skips the A/B steps), in the
  help line. `DebugPanel`: a **Ground probe** button; the panel closes first and the probe runs a
  quarter second later, because the panel covers the left of the picture the probe measures.
- `docs/DEBUG_TOOLS.md` (and its bundled copy): the command, and step 4 of "Sending a report".
- The chat line and the docs ask the player to hold still until the probe's "done" line, not for
  a time; `fresh_textures` skips a pass whose texture something else cleared after the probe
  listed it (it would otherwise raise a SCRIPT ERROR on `get_rid` of null).

**What `/groundprobe` records** (`GROUNDPROBE <entry>.<run> <section>: key=value ...`, to the log,
to `user://logs/groundprobe-e<entry>-r<run>-<time>.txt`, and a two-line summary in chat):

- `frame baseline` FIRST, before anything binds a texture: over a box of the picture (35-80% of the
  width, 62-92% of the height -- our choice, printed) and over the whole frame, the mean, the
  neutral-pixel fraction (max-min <= 6) with its p5/p50/p95, the bright-neutral fraction (>= 180, a
  cut between the tester's flats as the investigators measured them, 205-227, and the base grey
  the box draws under GL Compatibility, 161 -- a GL-only cut: under Forward+ the base computes to
  ~217, finding 2's last bullet, above it), red/magenta/blue fractions (a
  channel 60 over the others), and for every later step the fraction `changed` against this
  baseline (|dr|+|dg|+|db| > 24). All cuts are ours and printed with the numbers.
- `build`, `gpu` (`running=RenderingDevice(Forward+/Mobile)|GL-Compatibility` from
  `RenderingServer.get_rendering_device()`, adapter, vendor, API string, driver info, the project's
  rendering method, GL driver, ANGLE fallback, depth prepass and its vendor list, shader cache,
  thread model, `--verbose`), `entry` (entry number, how it was reached, grid builds, zone,
  connected, cells queued), `viewport` (debug_draw, MSAA, scaling, mipmap bias), `render`
  (`RenderingServer.get_rendering_info` texture/buffer/video memory and the frame's draw calls,
  objects, primitives; Performance object/node/orphan/resource counts, static memory), `env` (the
  baked-light terms, the sun, tonemap, ambient, fog, glow), `caches`.
- `region` (the region UNDER THE PLAYER, not the grid centre, and how many terrain groups cover
  the spot), `commit` (its meta), one `surface <i>` line per terrain material -- kind
  (base / opaque / opaque_flat / overlay), tile ID, class, **the material's RID index**, shading,
  transparency, depth draw, cull, priority, vertex colour as albedo, albedo, filter, repeat, UV1
  scale, AO; for a textured pass the file, the texture's RID index and validity, its GL name
  (`RenderingServer.texture_get_native_handle`), the RenderingServer format, **whether the
  RenderingServer material's own `texture_albedo` is that texture's RID** (`material_get_param`),
  size, and a read-back's format, mip count and 64-texel mean (labelled: `texture_2d_get` binds the
  GL name and reads the object's content, drivers/gles3/storage/texture_storage.cpp,
  TextureStorage::texture_2d_get, 4.2.2-stable -- it says nothing of what a draw binds); the vertex
  colours' min/mean luma and alpha.
- `order`: the base's RID index against the opaque and overlay passes', and how many opaque passes
  sit below the base. `regions`: the same counts, param matches and zero GL names for every loaded
  region. `object 0..2`: the three nearest scenery materials, for contrast. `water`: the region's
  AnimatedTexture. `glnames`: every ground, lightmap and water GL name, any shared by two live RIDs,
  any 0, and how many the previous entry held, with `handle_kind` -- under Forward+ / Mobile
  `texture_get_native_handle` returns the texture's VkImage handle, not a GL name
  (drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_vulkan.cpp, `RenderingDeviceVulkan::texture_get_native_handle`,
  4.2.2-stable), and the same holds for every `gl=` field. `shadercache`: files under
  `user://shader_cache`, how many this process wrote, and how many it wrote before the first probe
  A/B steps of the process (`written_before_probe_checks`, `probe_checks_from_unix`): the steps can
  compile shaders of their own -- `opaque_as_alpha` gives the passes a different
  StandardMaterial3D shader -- and GLES3 saves a version it did not find in that cache
  (drivers/gles3/shader_gles3.cpp, `ShaderGLES3::_initialize_version`, 4.2.2-stable), so a second
  `/groundprobe` in one process would otherwise count the first one's writes as H5's signal (on the
  box the cache was already warm: r6's entry-2 line reads `written_by_this_process=0` after entry
  1's steps). `logscan`: counts, in this entry and the whole log, of the lines the hypotheses
  predict (not in the lookup, Invalid image, Expected Image data size, NOTHING resolved,
  `Parameter "shader" is null`, Failed to load cached shader, shader failed to compile, SHADER ERROR,
  compilation failed, unable to bind shader, uninitialized RID, previously freed,
  texture_allocs_cache, GL ERROR, SCRIPT ERROR, pk2: could not open, terrain loads, world exits),
  up to four examples, and the region's own `ground textures for` line.
- The A/B steps, on EVERY loaded region's terrain, each held 4 frames, measured and put back:
  `after_readback`, `sun_off`, `tint` (opaque passes red, bases magenta, overlays blue),
  `base_first` (bases at `render_priority` -1), `opaque_as_alpha`, `fresh_materials` (duplicate
  StandardMaterial3Ds as surface overrides: new RenderingServer materials; the note says how many
  opaque passes got an RID index below their region's new base), `duplicates_hidden` (only if two
  groups cover the spot), `fresh_textures` (tiles decoded again from the `.ddj`), `retex`
  (albedo_texture null, then back), `remesh` (mesh null, then back), `final`; then a `summary` of
  changed/neutral/neutral-p50 per step.

**Finding 1, measured: the project's renderer setting never takes effect; a plain launch runs
Forward+ on Vulkan.**

- `client/project.godot` puts `#` comment lines before `renderer/rendering_method="gl_compatibility"`
  (and before `file_logging/enable_file_logging` and `fonts/dynamic_fonts/use_oversampling`), since
  the commit that added the setting (8fb499c, 2026-08-25): every revision of the file since
  (8fb499c, 977f89f, 97e44fe; `git show <rev>:client/project.godot`) has the same ten `#` lines
  above that key.
  Godot 4.2.2 reads project settings with `VariantParser::parse_tag_assign_eof`
  (core/variant/variant_parser.cpp, 4.2.2-stable): only `;` starts a comment; every other printable
  character before `=` is appended to the key, and a `"` reads a quoted string that replaces the
  key so far.
- On the render box, with this project's own `project.godot` (`ProjectSettings.get_property_list`,
  a headless script): `rendering/renderer/rendering_method = forward_plus` (the engine default);
  the `gl_compatibility` value sits under a 400-character key that begins
  `rendering/not rightvisuals--#allatonce,whichisconsistentwithaVulkandriver/GPUincompatibility`;
  `debug/file_logging/enable_file_logging = false` with its `.pc` default `true` (so desktop logging
  is on) and the project's `true` under a 180-character key; the `use_oversampling=false` under a
  296-character `gui/#Offsothewindow...` key, so the engine default applies.
- A plain launch of this project on the box (no `--rendering-driver`) printed `Vulkan API
  1.4.305 - Forward+ - Using Vulkan Device #1: Unknown - llvmpipe`. `qa_shot.sh` passes
  `--rendering-driver opengl3`, which picks gl_compatibility (main/main.cpp, `Main::setup`: a driver
  with no method named takes the method matching the driver), so every box render has been GL
  Compatibility while a release launched normally is Forward+ on Vulkan. The release workflow
  exports with no override (`export_presets.cfg`, `release.yml`); that an export carries the same
  parse is read, not measured on an exported build. It matches the tester's own banner, `Vulkan API
  1.4.349 - Forward+`, which `docs/WORLD_ISSUES.md`'s 2026-08-26 second round read as a stale build:
  that banner is what every build since 8fb499c prints on a plain launch, so it is no evidence of a
  stale build. Whether the exe tested that day was stale is still not known (the same round also
  found it loading a Data.pk2 from another folder).
- What it means here: the investigators' GLES3 code paths may not be the tester's; `gpu:
  running=` in their file settles it. The mechanism of finding 2 exists in Forward+ as well by
  source reading -- RenderForwardClustered sorts its opaque list with `sort_by_key`, whose key
  holds the material's RID local index (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_clustered/
  render_forward_clustered.h, the `sort` union; render_forward_clustered.cpp,
  `_geometry_instance_add_surface`, `p_mat_src.get_local_index()`, 4.2.2-stable) -- not run under
  Forward+ here.
- Not changed: fixing the comments switches every player's renderer, a decision for the project
  (docs/TODO.md).

**Finding 2, measured on the box: after a reconnect the base surface is drawn over textured
passes.** Viewpoint: 97/168 local (80, 1020), yaw 270, pitch -20, distance 45 -- open grass inside
Jangan's west wall (a first run at round 558's square viewpoint showed `tint` turning none of the
box red: it framed the square's paving objects, not terrain). Route Login -> CharacterSelect ->
World3D (`qa_shot.sh --reconnect 200 --reconnect-via-login`, `--server`, radius 1), runs r1 and r3:

- **RID order.** Entry 1: every region's base has a lower material RID index than all its opaque
  passes (97/168: base 148, opaque 149..170, `opaque_below_base=0 of 22`). Entry 2: 97/168 base 79,
  opaque 14..147, **4 of 22 below the base** (7 in r1, 6 in r4); 97/167 25/25, 98/168 22/22, 97/169
  22/22, 96/167 18/18, 98/167 25/25, 96/169 16/16, 98/169 26/26, 96/168 0/21. The world's
  materials were freed and the new ones took the freed slots: RID_Alloc keeps its free slots as a
  stack -- `free` writes the freed index at the top, `_allocate_rid` takes the top one
  (core/templates/rid_owner.h, 4.2.2-stable, read for this round) -- so a world allocating after a
  mass free gets indices in the reverse of the order they were freed in.
- **The picture.** Entry 2's baseline has a flat neutral area entry 1 does not: whole-frame
  neutral fraction 0.078 with p50/p95 161/161 (entry 1: 0.032, 36/89); the movie frame's crop at
  (1050, 280, 200x100) is (157.2, 157.4, 156.2) with pixels at exactly (161, 161, 162), where entry 1
  drew sand at (128.6, 123.8, 100.1). r1's frames differ in 46,953 pixels (5.1%, ImageMagick
  `compare -fuzz 2%`), that area.
- **The A/B steps say which surface it is.** `tint`: 4.9% of entry 2's frame turns magenta -- the
  bases' tint -- and 0.0% of entry 1's (the box, on textured grass, turns red, 0.802, in both).
  `base_first`: changes 5.2% of the frame and puts it back to entry 1's figures (neutral 0.032,
  p50 36; the crop reads (128.6, 123.8, 100.1) again). `opaque_as_alpha` does the same.
  `fresh_materials`: entry 1, "0 of 197 opaque passes got an RID index below their region's new
  base", changed 0.2%; entry 2, **"184 of 197"**, and the whole box goes flat base grey (neutral
  0.949, p50 161, bright_neutral 0.000 -- below the probe's own 180 cut for "white"; 44.6% of the
  frame changed) with the overlays' soft green gradients over it: the tester's pattern, not their
  brightness (205-227, the last bullet); their `/groundprobe` decides whether it is their white.
  What RID order alone does here is measured; that it is what the tester sees is not.
  `fresh_textures`, `retex`, `remesh`:
  <= 0.3% changed in both entries; `after_readback` 0.0%; `sun_off` 0.1% of the box (the terrain is
  baked and unshaded), 2.2% of the frame (shaded objects). Every surface `rid_valid=true`,
  `param_match=true` (48/48 in 97/168), texel means equal to entry 1's, `glnames` 82 audited, 0
  zero, 0 shared; `logscan` 0 of every error pattern.
- Direct route (r2, World3D -> World3D): the same inversion in five regions (97/167 25/25, 96/168
  15/21, 98/168 22/22, 96/167 18/18, 96/169 16/16) but not in 97/168 (0 of 22), 97/169, 98/167 or
  98/169, and this viewpoint's frame equals entry 1's; `fresh_materials` turns the box the same flat
  base grey in entry 2 (neutral 0.949, p50 161, bright_neutral 0.000). Which regions invert
  depends on the order the previous world freed and this one allocates.
- Brightness, not settled: the box draws the base at 161 (GL Compatibility, Mesa); the
  investigators measured the tester's flats at 205-227 on their JPEG. A calculation, not a
  measurement: Godot 4.2's Forward+ Filmic curve (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/effects/
  tonemap.glsl, `tonemap_filmic`, 4.2.2-stable; the environment's tonemap 2, exposure 1, white 1
  from the probe's `env` line) takes the base's linear 0.498 to 0.692, sRGB 0.850, **217** -- inside
  the tester's range, if they run Forward+ (finding 1) and glow and fog add nothing there.

**The hypotheses (the investigators', as hypotheses) and what each shows in the probe.**

| Hypothesis | Mechanism (short) | What the tester's file would show |
|---|---|---|
| H-base (CODE H3) | coplanar opaque passes drawn in material-RID order; after the free, the base gets a higher index than passes and covers them | `order`/`regions` `opaque_below_base` > 0 on entry 2 only; `tint` magenta where white was; `base_first` and `opaque_as_alpha` restore it (`changed` ~ the white area, neutral back to entry 1's); `fresh_materials` turns more of the ground flat (neutral up, at the base's grey) when its note says the new bases landed above. **The mechanism is measured on the box (finding 2), as flat grey at 161 under GL Compatibility; whether it is the tester's white is what their file decides.** |
| H-white-sampler (WEB H1 / CODE H2) | opaque passes sample GLES3's default white texture (stale texture cache or skipped bind) | surfaces `tex=true rid_valid=true param_match=true`, texel means intact; `tint` turns the white RED; `retex` (or `fresh_textures`) restores it; `sun_off` changes nothing |
| H-default-material (CODE H1 / WEB H3) | opaque passes fall back to the renderer's default material (no valid shader data) | `tint` leaves the white white while overlays turn blue; `sun_off` darkens it (the default material is shaded); `fresh_materials` may restore it; `logscan shader_param_null` > 0 |
| H-GL-name (WEB H2) | a deleted or aliased GL texture name; binds fail and units keep stale textures | GL Compatibility only (`glnames handle_kind=GL-name`; under Forward+ the handles are VkImages and this row's "recycled/shared GL name" reading means nothing): `glnames shared_by_two_rids` > 0 or `gl_zero` > 0; read-backs wrong or `no-image`; `fresh_textures` restores, `retex` does not; `GL ERROR` lines under `--verbose` |
| H-per-texture / duplicate (CODE H4 / WEB H4) | a tile resolved but not uploaded, or a second terrain for the region | `commit` `uploaded` < `resolved`; an `opaque_flat` pass with a key != -1; `logscan not_in_lookup` / `invalid_image` > 0; `groups_covering_here` > 1 or a commit number > 1; `duplicates_hidden` restores |
| H-shader-cache (WEB H5 / CODE H5) | program binaries re-exported in-process and misread by the driver | `shadercache written_before_probe_checks` > 0 on entry 2 (not `written_by_this_process`, which also counts an earlier probe's own steps); `logscan cached_shader_failed`; the tester's override.cfg with the cache off stops it |
| H-water (WEB H6, Godot #79070) | AnimatedTexture frames white after a scene change | `water` line; cannot whiten land |
| H-trigger (WEB H7) | region/environment, not the reconnect | `region`, `commit` (baked, light), `env` differ from Jangan's; the same after a zone change |
| Excluded (CODE H6) | viewport debug_draw, RenderingServer globals, NetClient, Pk2 handles | `viewport debug_draw=0`, `env light_ready=true` as entry 1 |

Reading notes, by renderer (the file's `gpu running=` says which):

- **`bright_neutral` separates H-base from H-white-sampler under GL Compatibility only.** Its 180
  cut sits between the box's GL base (161) and the tester's flats (205-227); under Forward+ the base
  computes to ~217 (finding 2), above the cut, so there a base drawn over the passes and a pass
  sampling white both read bright. `tint` separates them on either renderer (magenta where the
  flat area was = a base; red = an opaque pass), and `neutral_p50` does when read against that
  renderer's own base value.
- **`gl=`, `ao_gl=`, `glnames` and the H-GL-name row mean GL names under GL Compatibility only**;
  under Forward+ they are VkImage handles (`handle_kind`).
- **H5 reads `written_before_probe_checks`**, not the total, on any run after the first probe's
  A/B steps.

**Tests.**

- `client/scripts/world/ground_probe_test.gd` (new, headless): the console routes `/groundprobe`
  and `/groundprobe quick` to the host and refuses other modes, the non-GM help lists it; the frame
  statistics on synthetic pictures (a grey box under a blue sky: box bright-neutral 1.0, median 219,
  sky outside the box; `changed` against a reference: none of the box, about half the frame);

  `ground_probe`; the probe on a bare World3D holding a synthetic RealTerrain_97_168 (base, one
  opaque pass, one overlay, built by `MapmTerrainBuilder._textured_surfaces_from_cells` from 3x3

- `client/scripts/world/terrain_prepare_test.gd`: the commit leaves the `ground_probe` meta (ids 2,

- `client/scripts/world/ground_probe_ab_test.gd` (new, headless): the A/B state machine, with the

- NEGATIVE: the two suites against BASE (98c52ff's `client/` from `git archive`, with only the two

- `client/tools/remote_godot.sh check`: `checked 274 scripts and 5 scenes`, `ALL LOAD`; `tests`:
  `ran 99 suite(s), 0 failing` (both on the committed tree; the lane's own `RENDER_DIR`,

## The terrain's flat base is always drawn before its textured passes, so a reconnect no longer turns the ground flat (round 580)

Client only, tag-worthy (the user asked for one release carrying the probe, this fix, the renderer
switch and the teleports). Nothing on the wire, no flag, no server change. What a player sees
changes only where a re-entered world had drawn a region's flat base over its textured passes:
that ground is textured again. Round 579's (/groundprobe) finding 2 (above) is the grounding; this
round re-verified it and fixed it.

**Why the order depended on RID indices, and why priority fixes it (read, Godot 4.2.2-stable
source).**

- GL Compatibility: `RasterizerSceneGLES3::render_scene` fills the opaque list, sorts it with
  `sort_by_key`, and draws it with `glDepthFunc(GL_LEQUAL)` (also in the depth prepass), so of two
  coplanar opaque surfaces the one drawn LAST shows (drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp).
  The key is `GeometryInstanceSurface::sort` (drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.h): two 64-bit
  words, `sort_key1` = lod_index 8, surface_index 8, geometry_id 32, material_id_low 16 and
  `sort_key2` = material_id_hi 16, shader_id 32, four flag bits, depth_layer 4, **priority 8**,
  from the low bit up; `SortByKey` compares `sort_key2` first. So **priority is the most
  significant field of the whole key**, above the shader id and every part of the material id.
  `_geometry_instance_add_surface_with_material_chain` passes `p_mat_src.get_local_index()` as the
  material id and `material_get_shader_id` as the shader id; `SceneMaterialData::set_render_priority`
  stores `p_priority - RS::MATERIAL_RENDER_PRIORITY_MIN` (MIN = -128, servers/rendering_server.h),
  so -1 is 127 and 0 is 128 in those 8 bits (drivers/gles3/storage/material_storage.cpp).
- The base and the textured passes share one shader: BaseMaterial3D's `MaterialKey` (the key its
  generated shaders are cached by, scene/resources/material.h) has no bit for whether a texture is
  set, and the base and the passes differed only in the albedo texture. Their order was therefore
  decided by the material RID's local index -- which RID_Alloc hands out last-freed-first after a
  world is freed (core/templates/rid_owner.h; finding 2).
- Forward+ (read, not run): the same union with the same field order and widths
  (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_clustered/render_forward_clustered.h, `sort`), the same
  `SortByKey` on `sort_key2` first, `sort_by_key` on the opaque list
  (render_forward_clustered.cpp), the same `p_mat_src.get_local_index()` and
  `sdcache->sort.priority = p_material->priority` (`_geometry_instance_add_surface_with_material`),
  and the same `- RS::MATERIAL_RENDER_PRIORITY_MIN` offset
  (scene_shader_forward_clustered.cpp, `MaterialData::set_render_priority`). The colour pass there
  compares depth `LESS_OR_EQUAL`, or `EQUAL` after the depth prepass (scene_shader_forward_clustered.cpp),
  so coplanar surfaces again resolve by draw order. **The fix holds under Forward+ by reading**;
  nothing here ran Forward+.
- The alpha overlays are transparent: they go to the alpha list, sorted by
  `sort_by_reverse_depth_and_priority`, apart from the opaque list. They are untouched.

**Change.**

- `MapmTerrainBuilder`: `BASE_RENDER_PRIORITY` (-1) and `PASS_RENDER_PRIORITY` (0) with the
  reading above. The base surface's data carries `"base": true` (surface 0 only);
  `_surface_material` gives that material `render_priority` -1 and every other surface 0 (the
  default), so every region's base sorts before every one of its opaque passes -- textured and the
  flat `-1` fallback pass alike -- whatever the RID indices. The untextured fallback
  (`arrays_to_mesh`, one surface) has no passes to order and is unchanged.
- `GroundProbe` (the fix is reported and can be undone on demand):
  - `unfix_inverted` (new A/B step): per loaded region, one blank material per base and opaque
    pass is created FIRST, the blanks are sorted by RID index (`sorted_by_rid`), the passes take
    the lowest and the base the highest, each blank becomes a copy of its surface's material
    (`copy_material`) set as the surface override, and the base's copy is put back at the pre-fix
    priority 0 (`PRE_FIX_BASE_PRIORITY`). Deterministic, unlike `fresh_materials`, whose
    duplicates get whatever order the allocator's free list gives (0 of 197 passes below the base
    in a first entry). Held 4 frames, measured, overrides put back; the originals are never touched.
  - `unfix_inverted_tint`: the same, with the copies tinted as `tint` does (passes red, bases
    magenta) and the overlays blue, so the file carries the magenta fraction with the fix undone.
  - `fresh_materials`' description and note say whether the build runs with the fix (the
    duplicates keep the bases' priority), `base_first` notes how many bases were at -1 already,
    `order` and `regions` print the priorities and `base_first_by_priority`, and `summary` ends
    with the tinted steps' whole-frame magenta and `with the fix: <n> of <m> regions draw their
    base first by render priority`.
  - `copy_material` copies every property, not only the `PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE` ones:
    measured headless on the box, `duplicate()` of an unshaded StandardMaterial3D with
    `ao_enabled` and an `ao_texture` returns one with neither (their usage is 0 on an unshaded
    material). So `fresh_materials`' duplicates (unchanged, `duplicate()`) drop the terrain's
    lightmap AO, which the unshaded terrain does not draw anyway; `unfix_inverted`'s copies keep
    it, so they match the originals.
  - The chat line and `docs/DEBUG_TOOLS.md` (both copies) now say the ground may flash "red,
    magenta, blue or flat grey": `unfix_inverted` shows the flat grey on purpose.

**Tests.**

- `mapm_terrain_builder_test.gd` `_test_base_drawn_first` (headless): on both fixture cases, through
  `build_full_region_mesh_textured` and `surfaces_to_mesh`, the base's priority is below every
  opaque pass's and the overlays keep 0; only surface 0 is marked as the base. A sort-order check
  through the engine is not possible headless: the headless renderer is the dummy one, whose
  material storage allocates no RIDs (`material_allocate` returns `RID()`,
  servers/rendering/dummy/storage/material_storage.h) and keeps no render list -- the order is
  measured live (below).
- `ground_probe_ab_test.gd`: the two new steps are armed in order; while `unfix_inverted` is held
  every base and opaque pass in both regions draws a copy (base at priority 0, pass at 0, the
  pass's texture, the base's shading, AO texture and tile-ID metadata copied), the overlay has no
  override, the original base stays at -1 and the note says `with the fix: 2 of 2`; while
  `unfix_inverted_tint` is held the copies are magenta/red and the overlays blue, the originals
  not; `fresh_materials`' note begins `with the fix` and its base copy keeps -1; the full run and
  the stop path (the terrain leaving the tree at each of the two new steps, as at the others) put
  every material, override, colour and priority back; `sorted_by_rid` orders synthetic indices
  (79, 14, 147, 15) lowest first. The `base_first` stop case now starts from bases at 0 (a
  pre-fix mesh), since on the fixed builder the step changes nothing.
- NEGATIVES (box, lane directories): the two suites against the pre-fix tree (2a3662e's `client/`
  from `git archive`, only the two test files copied in): `mapm_terrain_builder_test` 5 FAILURES

## The client runs the Compatibility renderer it was meant to: project.godot's comments no longer swallow three settings (round 581)

Client only, tag-worthy: it switches every player's renderer. The user decided on 2026-09-26 that
players run GL Compatibility. `client/project.godot` has asked for that since 2026-08-26, and its
own comment gives the reason: a playtest showed "missing HUD, flat/textureless ground, generally
"not right" visuals", read as a Vulkan driver problem. The choice never took effect, and the
quoted "not right" in that comment is what broke it. This round rewrites the comments so Godot
reads the settings, and makes `ClientSettings` work with the oversampling setting that now
applies too.

**Grounding** (round 579's Finding 1 -- the `/groundprobe` round -- re-measured here on
this branch's tree). Godot 4.2.2 reads `project.godot` with `VariantParser::parse_tag_assign_eof`
(core/variant/variant_parser.cpp, 4.2.2-stable, re-read this round). Only `;` starts a comment.
Every other printable character before `=` is appended to the key, and a `"` replaces the key read
so far with the quoted string. So each of the file's three `#` blocks became part of the key
after it. `ConfigFile` uses the same parser, and on the box it read the pre-change file as 18 keys,
three of them `[debug] no logging to check(2026-08-26,seedocs/WORLD_ISSUES.md)#hadnothingtoattach
...file_logging/enable_file_logging` (180 characters with its section), `[rendering] not
rightvisuals--#allatonce,...renderer/rendering_method` (400) and `[gui] #Offsothewindow...fonts/
dynamic_fonts/use_oversampling` (296). `ProjectSettings.get_property_list` listed the same three.
The engine's own longest setting name is 81 characters
(`rendering/lights_and_shadows/directional_shadow/soft_shadow_filter_quality.mobile`).

**Change.**

- `client/project.godot`: the three comment blocks now start with `;` instead of `#`. There is
  also a header note that `#` is not a comment in this file, and a line in the rendering block
  saying when the setting took effect. No key or value changed. What the engine read, before and
  after (the box, headless; `ConfigFile` found 18 keys both times, and the other 15 are identical):

| key | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `rendering/renderer/rendering_method` | `forward_plus`, the engine default (the file's `gl_compatibility` sat under the 400-character key) | `gl_compatibility` |
| `debug/file_logging/enable_file_logging` | `false`, the engine default (the file's `true` under the 180-character key); `.pc` override `true` | `true`; `.pc` `true` |
| `gui/fonts/dynamic_fonts/use_oversampling` | `true`, the engine default (the file's `false` under the 296-character key) | `false` |
| `rendering/renderer/rendering_method.mobile` | `gl_compatibility` (the line after the block parsed) | the same |
| `debug/file_logging/log_path`, `max_log_files` | `user://logs/srrevamp.log`, `10` (they follow the swallowed key) | the same |

- `client/scripts/client_settings.gd`: `apply_ui_scale` now sets the root window's
  font-oversampling FLAG: on at a whole-number scale, off otherwise. It also sets the content
  scale. The `size_changed` hook and `_apply_oversampling` are gone (why: below).

**What applies now, setting by setting.**

- **Renderer.** When no command-line flag names a renderer, `Main::setup` takes `rendering_method
  = GLOBAL_GET("rendering/renderer/rendering_method")`, then the driver from
  `rendering/gl_compatibility/driver` (main/main.cpp, 4.2.2). A plain launch of `Boot.tscn` on the
  box, as ghidra under the lane lock, through `xvfb-run` and `vglrun -d egl0` with no
  `--rendering-driver`:
  - The pre-change tree printed `Vulkan API 1.4.305 - Forward+ - Using Vulkan Device #1: Unknown -
    llvmpipe`.
  - This tree printed `OpenGL API 4.6 (Core Profile) Mesa 25.0.7-2+deb13u1 - Compatibility - Using
    Device: AMD - AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT`.

  `GroundProbe` is not on this branch, so a script used the probe's own `running=` rule
  (`RenderingServer.get_rendering_device()` present means Forward+/Mobile, none means
  GL-Compatibility). The pre-change tree gave `running=RenderingDevice(Forward+/Mobile)` and this
  tree `running=GL-Compatibility`. `remote_godot.sh check` on this tree also prints the engine's
  own "Screen-space ambient occlusion (SSAO) can only be enabled when using the Forward+ rendering
  backend" and "Glow is not supported when using the GL Compatibility backend yet" when it loads
  `World3D.tscn`.
- **File logging: on before, on after.** `GLOBAL_GET` is `get_setting_with_override`
  (core/config/project_settings.h). `main.cpp` defines `debug/file_logging/enable_file_logging.pc
  = true`, so on Windows and Linux the `.pc` value decides. Measured headless: before, the base key
  was `false` and the override `true`; after, both are `true`. The path and the count applied both
  times. A player on a desktop platform sees no change. Only a platform without the `pc` feature
  would, and none is exported.
- **Font oversampling: engine default `true` before, `false` now.** `Main::start` hands the value
  to the root window (`set_use_font_oversampling`). On every viewport update (a resize, a
  content-scale change), `Window::_update_viewport_size` then sets the text server's global
  oversampling: to the content scale factor when the flag is on, to 1.0 when it is off
  (scene/main/window.cpp, 4.2.2; the project's stretch mode is disabled). `size_changed` is
  emitted INSIDE that update, from `Viewport::_set_size` (scene/main/viewport.cpp), before the
  oversampling block. So the old `ClientSettings` hook on `size_changed` always lost to the
  window's own value, although its comment said it re-applied the value "after every resize". The
  text server's value after `apply_ui_scale` and after a resize was measured headless, and in an
  Xvfb window on the box:
  - **Before (as shipped):** at 2.35 the value was 1.000 after `apply_ui_scale` and 2.350 after a
    resize. At 2.5 a resize left 2.500. The whole scales 2 and 3 held.
  - **The fixed `project.godot` with the old `ClientSettings`:** fractional scales stayed at 1.000
    after a resize. But whole scales 2.0 and 3.0 fell to 1.000 at the first resize, which would
    have lost the crisp text that README promises at whole scales.
  - **This tree:** 2.0 gave 2.000, 2.35 gave 1.000, 3.0 gave 3.000, 2.5 gave 1.000 and 1.0 gave
    1.000, and each value was the same after a resize. The window now holds the value itself,
    because the flag is what `ClientSettings` sets.

    viewport; the default theme font, Open Sans). Two texts were drawn:
    - A Label "Register" at 16. Its ink reached 62.80-63.20 units, against 57.00 for the advance

      flat, size 13, outline 3), but in the default font. Its ink spanned 142.98-144.00 units,
      against 141.00 for "...accoun" and 146.00 for "...account".

    Each was drawn at UI scales 2.0, 2.35, 2.5 and 3.0, with and without a resize, in three runs:
    the pre-change tree under Forward+, the same tree with `--rendering-driver opengl3`, and this
    tree. All 36 cases drew the last glyph, including those at oversampling 2.35 and 2.5. So the
    2026-09-11 loss did not reproduce in this probe. The limits: `Login.gd` applies the client's

    nothing.

The packs were deleted.

**What players will see change** (read in 4.2.2-stable; nothing was rendered under Forward+ here).
`World3D.tscn`'s Environment, plus what `World3D.gd` turns on:

- The procedural sky and the ambient colour: kept (`sky.glsl`).
- The `DirectionalLight3D`'s shadows: kept (`RasterizerSceneGLES3::_render_shadow_pass`, with a
  directional shadow atlas).

Every box render so far was already Compatibility (`qa_shot.sh --rendering-driver opengl3`), so
the look this project has verified is the one players now get. Every tester report to date,
including the white ground after a reconnect, came from a Forward+ build. Round 579's

## A second Move before the teleport's reply can no longer charge twice (round 582)

Client only, a fix to round 578. Nothing on the wire changes, there is no flag, and the server is
unchanged. It ships in the release with rounds 579-581.

**Why.** Round 578's review found that `World3D._open_teleport_board` cleared
`_teleport_request_pending` on every open. The talk box stays up behind the board
(`HudPanels._on_npc_talk_choice`). So a player could press Move, reopen the board from the talk
box's "Select teleport area" line, and press Move again before the reply. That sent two
`OpTeleportUse`. The server has no range test (`session/teleport.go`'s header), so it served the
second request from the first one's arrival point and charged the fee again.

**Change.** `_open_teleport_board` no longer touches the flag. It is cleared only by the reply
(`_on_teleport_result`) and by a zone change (`_close_gate_ui`, from `_on_change_zone_result`).
Leaving the world takes the flag with it. The flag is instance state, and a dropped connection
sends the instance to Login (`_on_disconnected`), so a reply lost that way still cannot wedge
Move. A reply the server never sends on a live connection would wedge Move until the next zone
change. The server answers every `OpTeleportUse` (round 576), so this is not guarded further.

**Tests.** `teleport_board_test.gd`, in `_world_checks`: with a request pending, the talk box's
teleport line reopens the board. The flag stays set, and a second Move is ignored (offline it
does not reach the "needs the server" line). In `_zone_change_checks`: a request pending at an
accepted zone change is cleared. NEGATIVE, run on the box with this test against round 578's
`World3D.gd`: `FAIL reopening the board keeps the pending request` and `FAIL a Move after
reopening the board, before the reply, is still ignored (chat: * Teleporting needs the server.)`,
2 FAILURES. With the fix it gives ALL PASS.

**Record correction.** `docs/WORLD_ISSUES.md`'s round 576 bullet said "all 34 links of the five
town gates resolve to their towns' labels". The RE_COMPLETION round 576 entry above says the four
beyond the towns and Alexandria's two go to their own "x/y" labels. It was re-counted for this
round with a throwaway test (not committed) running `teleportArrival` over the round-576 retail
export (`/var/tmp/r579/teleport` on the render box, never committed). Jangan, Hotan,
Constantinople and Samarkand each have 6 links: 4 to town labels, plus `90/48` and `92/51`.
Donwhang has 10: 4 to town labels and 6 to "x/y" (the Alexandria two, `80/95`, `81/79`, `88/90`
and `126/228`). That makes 34 links: 20 to town labels and 14 to their own "x/y" labels. The
bullet now says so. Round 578's review bullet above (a reopened board clears the flag) now notes
this round.

**Verified on the combined tree (rounds 579-582 on round 578; render box lane
`/opt/srrevamp-client-r579`, `GODOT_LOCK=/var/tmp/r579/lock`, this tree's server built for
linux).**

## Seasonal event decorations are hidden by default (round 583)

Client only. Nothing on the wire changes, and the server is unchanged.

**Why.** The user decided on 2026-09-26 that early testing gets no seasonal event decorations. The
user chose four sets: Christmas, Halloween, the China open-beta (OBT) event set and the summer
festival set. All four are hidden by default, and each can be shown again on its own. **The choice
is ours, not the retail client's.** No switch for them was found in the client's `.o2` loader
(`FUN_00a361b0`, `MapCallBack.cpp`). The loader builds every record in its second and third lists
unless byte 27 bit 0 is set, and no seasonal record has that bit. A Go scan (`mapo.Parse2`) over
the 4,559 region `.o2` files covered the files under Map.pk2's numbered folders; it did not cover
the 15 root files, `50.o2` to `64.o2`. It finds 878 seasonal entries: 686 in `lists[1]` and 192
in `lists[2]`; christmas 262, halloween 156, obt 439, summer 21. Bytes 26-27 are zero in all of
them. The list totals match the skip-bit census below (202,672 and 31,930).

What `sro_client.exe` holds (`strings -a`, ASCII and UTF-16LE, this round): no `x_mas`,
`halloween`, `obt_event`, `summer_event` or `layerobj` string. It does hold five UTF-16 UI
message ids, `UIIT_MSG_XMAS_EVENT_CHANGE`, `_COMPENSATION`, `_ERROR_INVENTORY`, `_ERROR_SOCKS`
and `_SO-OK`. Those are messages for a Christmas event exchange, not a map switch as far as
anything read shows. The decompilation (`/var/tmp/decomp_client`) names neither layer file.
**Correction:** as first committed, this record said the investigation "found no seasonal
string", and `seasonal_objects.gd` said the binary "carries no seasonal string". Both were
wrong, and round 583's review found the five message ids.

**What is seasonal.** A seasonal piece is identified by the folder in its model path, read from
Map.pk2's own `object.ifo` (the table placements resolve against), lowercased. It is never
identified by an id range: id 3297, between two Halloween ids, is `res\npc\npc\arabia_fouad.bsr`.

| Set | Path rule | Map.pk2 `object.ifo` ids |
|---|---|---|
| christmas | `\etc\x_mas\` (covers `res\etc\x_mas\` and `compound\struct\etc\x_mas\`) | 3254-3266 (13) |
| halloween | `res\etc\halloween\` | 3287-3296, 3298 (11) |
| obt | `res\etc\obt\obt_event` | 3268-3283, 3285, 3286 (18) |
| summer | `res\etc\summer_event\` | 2095-2109 (15) |

The folder-to-event mapping comes from Map.pk2's `layerobjdef.txt`, read this round from the box's
archive and decoded as cp949. Its layers are 1 `축제(DECO)` (festival), 4-5 `할로윈` (Halloween),
6-7 `크리스마스` (Christmas), 8-9 `중국OBT` (China OBT), 10 `바그다드 남문 닫기` (Baghdad south gate
closed) and 11 `구정(DECO)` (Lunar New Year).

How `layerobjectlist.ifo`'s 3,334 rows were joined to placements: by position, to the `.o`
records and every `.o2` list of the row's own region file (row columns 4 and 3 give the region),
with every axis within 0.05. Each distinct row is counted once, so a record repeated across
sectors does not add rows. A row matching records of two different type ids is counted as
ambiguous. 929 rows match, 6 of them ambiguous. The unambiguous ones are all of their layer's
own folder:

| Layer | Pieces matched |
|---|---|
| 1 | 91 `summer_event` |
| 4-5 | 12 + 202 `\halloween\` |
| 7 | 233 `\x_mas\` |
| 8-9 | 15 + 304 `obt_event` |
| 2 | 65 guard-post and `bagh_mong_fort_bari` pieces |
| 10 | 1 `bagh_city_gate_door_01` |

The review's own join (tolerance 0.05, `.o` and all `.o2` lists) got the same 929 rows and 6
ambiguous. Its layer 1 and layer 9 counts were 94 and 307, 3 more each than this join's. That difference
was not traced.

`alex_burner` (`res\bldg\north africa\alexandria\`) matches no row by position. A key-only
join does pair it with rows on layers 1, 5, 7, 9 and 11, but every such pair is 0.40 to 1,889
units apart. That is a key collision, not a listing, so the first commit's "layers 1 and 9 list
alex_burner" is withdrawn. So is its 938 / 476 / 349 / 727 / 114 set of counts: that
investigation join counted `.o` and `.o2` records per placement, sector repeats included, and
could not be reproduced as stated. alex_burner is in none of the four folders and stays either
way.

The first column of `layerobjdef.txt` is 1 for BASIC and both guard-post layers and 0 for every
event layer. What that column means is not established.

**A lead, not followed:** every layer row that matched an `.o2` record by position (561 rows)
carries, as its id, exactly the loader's object key `CONCAT22(bytes 28-29, bytes 22-23)` of
every record it matched (561 of 561). The review measured 674 of 674 by its own method. So the
map's layer list and the loader name objects the same way. Whether anything in the client or
the server turns layers on and off by that key has not been searched beyond the string and
decompilation checks above.

**Change.**
- `client/scripts/world/seasonal_objects.gd` (`SeasonalObjects`) holds the classifier, the id
  -> set map over an object index, the enabled-list parser, the placement filter and the log line.
- `World3D._objects_job`, on the main thread, builds the hidden id set once per object index
  (`_seasonal_hidden_for`). It uses the four folder rules, minus the sets shown again.
- `_objects_prepare` drops those placements after the `.o` + `.o2` list 2 de-duplication and
  before `_placements_belonging_here` and the model loop, so their models and textures are never
  read. It logs `World3D: <r>.o -- hid N seasonal placement(s) (christmas a, halloween b, obt c,
  summer d)` when N > 0.
- Each placed piece carries its own `StaticBody3D`, so leaving it out removes its collision too.
- Navigation is unchanged. No `.nvm` object record uses a seasonal id: the investigation's census
  of 6,279 `.nvm` files found 0 of 48,044 records, all four sets included. This round's probe
  re-checked the nine Jangan regions through the client's own `NvmReader`: 0 of 600 records.
- **Showing a set again:** set `SRREVAMP_SEASONAL` to a comma list, `christmas,halloween,obt,summer`
  or any subset (case and spaces ignored, unknown names ignored). The same list can go in
  `user://settings.cfg` under `[world]` as `seasonal="christmas,halloween"`
  (`ClientSettings.seasonal_shown`). **The value must be quoted.** Measured on the box, an
  unquoted `seasonal=christmas,halloween` makes `ConfigFile.load` fail with ERR_PARSE_ERROR
  (43). `ClientSettings` then returns every setting's default, and the next setting it saves
  rewrites the file from only the keys above the bad line plus its own. The two sources are
  added together. Both are read once per world scene, when it builds its first objects job, so a
  change shows after the next login or restart. **No window writes the setting.** A live toggle
  would also have to rebuild the hidden set and reload the loaded regions' objects, and the debug
  panel belongs to the UI lane. So the environment variable and the settings key are the whole
  interface for now (`docs/TODO.md`).

**Measured on the box's archive** (`client/tools/probe_seasonal.gd`, run headless with
`remote_godot.sh script` in lane `/opt/srrevamp-client-r583`, `GODOT_LOCK=/var/tmp/rseason/lock`).
The probe runs World3D's own `_objects_job` and `_objects_prepare` over the nine Jangan regions.
It loaded `object.ifo` with 3,307 entries. The default hides 57 type ids (christmas 13, halloween
11, obt 18, summer 15). Hidden per region, counted before the ownership step:

| Region | christmas | halloween | obt | summer | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 96/167 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 96/168 | 1 | 9 | 0 | 0 | 10 |
| 96/169 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 97/167 | 5 | 12 | 5 | 5 | 27 |
| 97/168 | 26 | 34 | 25 | 30 | 115 |
| 97/169 | 6 | 15 | 5 | 5 | 31 |
| 98/167 | 4 | 5 | 3 | 3 | 15 |
| 98/168 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 98/169 | 3 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 9 |

- **This matches the investigation's per-region table**, which it computed from its own scan of
  `.o` + `.o2` list 2 after de-duplication. There is one difference. 98/169's sixth Halloween
  record is a list-2 `halloween_pu03` whose bytes 28-29 name 97/169 (0x61a9), not 98/169. The
  investigation's table left that record out, and this filter counts it because the filter runs
  before the ownership step.
- **With the prepare run to the end (`--full=1`)**, the default leaves 0 seasonal placements in
  what any of the nine regions hands the commit. With `SRREVAMP_SEASONAL=christmas`, only
  Christmas pieces come back: 97/168 places 307 (281 + 26), with 26 Christmas and nothing else
  seasonal; 96/168 places 1, 97/167 5, 97/169 6, 98/167 4 and 98/169 3.
- With all four shown, the hidden set is empty and the filter passes everything through, as
  before this round. 97/168 places 396, and 98/169 places 5 Halloween pieces, because the
  ownership step drops the 97/169-owned one.

**Recorded in passing** (`docs/protocol/MAPO2_FORMAT.md`, "Corrected (round 583)"; read in
`/var/tmp/decomp_client` via `getfn.sh 00a361b0`):
- Record bytes 22-23 are the object's uid and bytes 28-29 its owner region, `(Y<<8)|X`. Together
  they are the key the loader files the object under. This settles the doc's "`0x6464` suffix,
  genuinely unresolved".
- Byte 27 bit 0 is the loader's skip bit. In the 4,559 region `.o2` files, 240 of the 31,930
  `lists[2]` records set it, and `World3D` draws them. They span 19 model paths:
  `bagh_masin_lightwall` (120), guild barricades (48), Baghdad's event barricades (46), Petra's
  fires (24) and `res\dun\jupiter\piety\piety_golddoor.bsr` (2). None of them is seasonal or in
  Jangan. The item is open in `docs/TODO.md`.
- The field read before the first list is a bare `uint16`, and no entries follow it.

**Tests.**
- `client/scripts/world/seasonal_objects_test.gd` checks the classifier over the real path shapes.
  Each of the four rules matches its own paths, in either case. `arabia_fouad`, `alex_burner`,
  `alex_burner02`, the Jangan gate and `cj_s` wall, the new-year piece, the season door and the
  `event_area_rockevent` do not match. The test checks the id map by path and the enabled-list

- The same test runs World3D's prepare over a synthetic `97\168.o` holding a wall, a Christmas

  the line. `SRREVAMP_SEASONAL=christmas` brings back only the tree, and all four shown places all
  four with no line.
- **NEGATIVE**, run on the box against round 582's tree (a detached worktree at `f2b00fa` with
  only this test added): `FAILURES: 7`. The classifier is absent, the prepare places `[1, 2, 3,
  4]`, the hidden models are read, and there is no count and no line.

## Window frames are sliced from each piece's own texture, and windows are sized from what they actually draw (round 584)

Client only. Nothing on the wire changes and the server is unchanged. Three defects from the
read-only GUI audit (its v0.1.450 baseline), each re-measured before it was fixed.

**1. Every frame piece at its own size -- read from CNIFFrame, not assumed.** `UiBuilder._build_frame`
sized all eight pieces from `left_up`. Most eight-piece sets are not uniform: `sframe_wnd_` has
a 36-tall top and a 16-tall bottom, `msgbox2_window_` 40/16, `mframe_wnd_` 68/48, `game_window_`
42x42 corners around 8-thick edges, `opt_inner_box_` 20x24 corners with a 28-tall top edge and a
12-tall bottom one. So the bottom corners were stretched, the bottom edge was drawn at the top's
thickness (the doubled line under the Quest list), and the side rails stopped 20 pixels short.
The geometry now follows the client's own code (decompile on the render box,
`/var/tmp/decomp_client/funcs_001.c`):

- the frame's loader `FUN_004745a0` (just before `CNIFFrame::vslot_000`, same object offsets)
  passes the four corners to `FUN_004750a0` and the four edges to `FUN_00475400`, which keeps
  each texture's own width and height beside it (edges at `+0x76c..+0x788`, in the order
  left_side, mid_up, right_side, mid_down -- the order the draw then places them in);
- `FUN_00474d00` lays each corner quad at that corner's own width and height, anchored at its
  corner of the window rect;
- the draw, `FUN_004736a0` (slot 13 of 41 window classes' vtables; the one hierarchy the dump
  prints, CNIFGPHistoryWnd's, runs through CNIFMainFrame to CNIFFrame), tiles each
  edge at its **own** thickness across the gap between the corners it meets, and crops the last
  tile through its UV: the top edge at y = top, x from left + left_up.w to right - right_up.w; the
  bottom at y = bottom - own.h, x from left + left_down.w to right - right_down.w; the left at
  x = left, y from top + left_up.h to bottom - left_down.h; the right at x = right - own.w, from
  top + **left_up**.h for height - right_up.h - right_down.h. The last detail is copied as read.
  All 18 eight-piece bases named by the archive's 229 layouts have left_up and right_up the same
  size, so it changes nothing today.
- the layouts' own control types (`CIFFrame`, `CIFSubFrame`, `CIFMainFrame`) are a separate CIF
  family with its own copy of this code, and the review read that one too: loader
  `FUN_00815300` (corners through `FUN_0081ae80`, edges through `FUN_0081b1b0`), corner layout
  `FUN_0081a740`, draw `FUN_00815490` (slot 13 across 93 classes). The geometry is identical,
  the object offsets are shifted by +0x24, and the right edge starts at left_up's height there
  too. The CNIF functions above were read first; the link from the layouts to them was assumed
  until the CIF copy was read.

Godot's `STRETCH_TILE` tiles from the rect's origin and crops the last tile, which is the same
thing. Six-piece sets (no `mid_up`/`mid_down`) are a different class, laid out by
`FUN_00499e10` around an inner rect. How that maps onto a control's rect is not read, so their
geometry is left as it was. It is unchanged for `com_lattice_outline_` and `com_blacksquare_`,
which are 4x4 in every piece. It is open for `com_square_` (4x64 sides, one control in the
archive). The clamp fix in point 2 does change `com_square_`'s drawing: its top and bottom,
which reuse the 4x64 side piece, are no longer forced to 64 tall. Its only control is in
ifskillpracticebox, which no panel builds, so nothing on screen changes today.

**2. A piece shorter than its texture is no longer clamped up to it.** `_add_slice` set `size`
before `expand_mode = EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE`. With the default expand mode a TextureRect's minimum
size is its texture, so the size was clamped to it, and switching the mode afterwards never gave
it back. The Action window's 117-tall subframes grew 128-tall side rails that ran into the next
subframe. The same happened to the Party Match search frame's 52-tall rails (for a 29 gap) and
to the Exchange subframes. The modes are now set first. The other caller, `_add_row_bar_from`,
is affected once: of the 134 row-bar controls in the layouts, only ifjobcontributionrank's
150x22 bar is shorter than the 24-tall art, and it now draws 22 tall instead of 24.

**3. `UiBuilder.section_size` counts what is drawn.** It ignored art with a zero-size rect, which
`build_control` draws at the art's natural size (UI_TODO rule 4). It also counted ifexchange's
controls parked at `x = 9999`. It now takes the builder (`section_size(sec, builder)`, passed by
both `HudWindow` callers) and counts a zero-size control at its natural size. It skips any
control with `x >= 9999` (`UiBuilder.PARKED_X`, `is_parked`). That convention is the data's.
ifexchange has 13 such controls: the message box and its two backings under
`UI_UPDATE_2009_FIRST`, the six avatar-view controls under `APPLY_EXCHANGE_UPDATE_1TH`, and the
two `ch_line.ddj` dividers. No other control in the 229 layouts reaches past x = 864 (ifunderbar's
`800,0,64,52`) or y = 652. Whether the client later moves them into view is not read. They are
still built where the layout puts them, and only the size ignores them.

## Windows show one control of each authored alternate, the HUD's text sits on its authored rows, and the underbar and minimap are built once (round 585)

Client only. Nothing on the wire changes and the server is unchanged. Three more defects from the
read-only GUI audit of v0.1.450 (its causes 4, 6 and 7), fixed on top of the previous round.
Every decision below was read from `sro_client.exe` (the decompile in `/var/tmp/decomp_client`
and the linear `sro_client.asm` on the RE box) or measured in the node dump of every panel. None
was chosen by how a picture looked.

Two conventions are used throughout. They were checked in the asm, and the equipment window's
click table independently confirms them. `FUN_008b51f0(id, 1)` fetches a child control by its
layout `ID`, and returns 0 for an ID the layout lacks, without asserting. Virtual `+0x5c` (slot
23) is ShowWindow(bool): `CIFEquipment::vslot_023` (`0x6ac010`) is that slot.

### A. Same-rect alternates: every group, its decision and its evidence

The audit found 47 `SAMERECT` lines, which are named, visible controls drawn at one rect. This
section covers each of them.

**The #ifdef define set cannot be read from the binary.** The layout parser's `#ifdef` handling
is `IFTVariable` `0xb37a30`. It asks `0x5004a0` whether a symbol is defined, and `0x5004a0` looks
the symbol up in a hash_map at `0xeed4e0`. A raw byte search of the whole file for the addresses
`0xeed4d0`..`0xeed50c` finds only that lookup (`0x500503`, `0x50053f`, `0x50054b`). Nothing
visible constructs or fills the map, so the defined set is not readable. **Evidence for a branch
therefore comes from the class code.** If a class fetches a control that exists only in one
branch and uses it with no null check, a build reading the other branch would crash there. That
is inferred from the code, not read from a define.

| Window | Group (authored rect) | Decision | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| inventory (docked ifequipment) | `GDR_EQ_BTN_CHANGE_AVATAR_SLOT` (ID 13) / `_CHANGE_EQUIP_SLOT` (14), 1,305,40,40 | **13 shown, 14 hidden; either one toggles** | `CIFEquipment::Create` `0x6ac1c0` loads `resinfo\ifequipment.txt` (`push 0xda7410`). It fetches 13 (`0x6ac29d`, into `+0x26b0`), 14 (`0x6ac2ee`, `+0x26b4`), 100..112 (loop `0x6ac930`, array `+0x26a0`), 113..117 (`+0x5e4`..`+0x5f4`) and 500 (`0x6aca00`, `+0xf0c`, hidden at once). The refresh is `0x6abde0`. With the flag `+0xf08` clear it shows 100..112 and 13, and hides 113..117, 14 and 500. With the flag set it hides 100..112 except array index 8 (ID 108), shows 113..117 and 14, and hides 13. It shows 500 only for an avatar item of one type with a value above 0. Buttons 13 and 14 both run `0x6abf60` (`cmp [ecx+0xf08],0 / sete / jmp 0x6abde0`). Their click-table entries are `0xeb8378` and `0xeb83a0`; the same table maps 10/11/12 to the rotate handlers, which confirms the reading. The constructor clears the flag (`0x6ab569`), and so does ShowWindow(false). |
| inventory | `GDR_EQUIPMENT_SLOT_100..104` / `GDR_AVATAR_SLOT_01..05` (5 pairs) | **worn slots shown, avatar slots hidden; the toggle swaps them** | Same refresh. |
| inventory | (no pair) `GDR_AVATAR_SKILL_WND` (ID 500), 0,240,177,50 | **hidden** | Hidden at create (`0x6aca12`). The condition that shows it needs avatar items, which this client does not have. |
| academy | `GDR_APPRENTICESHIP_PICTURE` (41) / `_LEADER_STATUS` (46), 9,33,28,28 | **PICTURE hidden, LEADER_STATUS kept** | `CIFApprenticeShip::vslot_010` `0x6e9770` fetches 0x29 (`0x6e9833`, into `+0x370`) and calls ShowWindow with `ebx` (`0x6e9848`). `ebx` is zeroed at `0x6e97b5`. `HudPanels.HIDDEN_AT_CREATE` carries the academy and alchemy entries. `HudPanels._wire_equipment_modes`
