unaffected, because `_equipment_slot_at` already skips slots that are not visible. `HudChat` reads
its layout with `UI_UPDATE_2009_FIRST` (`LAYOUT_DEFINES`) and hides `HIDDEN_LISTS`.

### B. The HUD's labels settle

`UiBuilder.apply_authored_rects` ran only from `HudWindow._process`. A Label built before it is in
the tree is clamped to the height of Godot's default 16px face, 23 pixels, so every authored
label in the five HUD widgets that are not HudWindows stayed 23 tall. The settling pass is now
one shared function, `UiBuilder.settle_authored_rects(root)`. It applies the authored rects over
`root` on each of the next `SETTLE_FRAMES` (3) frames, starting when `root` enters the tree.
`HudWindow` uses it (`_settle`: the built layout and the title bar, which now carries its rect in
the same meta), and so do `HudWorldmap` (it called `set_process(true)` for the old pass), the
underbar, minimap, player info, chat and both target pieces. HudWindow's pass is deliberately
scoped to `panel_root` and the title bar, as the old `_process` was. Settling the whole window
first moved HudWorldmap's registry frame to its screen position (100,100), which is what the tree
diff below caught.

A Label still cannot be shorter than its font's line height. That is Godot's minimum-size rule
(`Label::get_minimum_size`), not a size this pass chooses, so a 12-pixel row settles at 14 in the
client's font, as it already did in every window.

Measured in the audit's node dump, label heights before -> after:

| Widget | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| underbar | 6 labels, all 23 (3 of them the second copy) | 3 labels, all 14 |
| minimap | 6, all 23 | 3, all 14 |
| chat | `GDR_CHAT_STA_PENALTY` 23 | 20 (authored 20) |
| player info | 31: 25 at 23, 5 at 28, 1 at 24 | 20 at 14, 2 at 13, 2 at 15, 1 at 20, 5 at 28, 1 at 24 |
| target | 6, all 23 | 3 at 14, 2 at 20, 1 at 16 |

The 28 and 24 are labels authored that tall. The gem art `GDR_TWCE_GEM_art` / `GDR_TWSM_GEM_art`
went from 20x23 to 20x20.

### C. The underbar and minimap are built once

`World3D._try_initialize_pk2_ui` called `ui_control.add_child(widget)`, which runs `_ready` ->
`setup()`, and then called `setup()` again. The only guard was `_ready`'s own
`if get_child_count() == 0`, so the second call built a second copy stacked exactly on the first.
It also connected a second set of quickslot handlers to the second copy's slots. `HudUnderbar`
and `HudMinimap` now keep a `_built` flag: `setup()` builds once and a later call returns.
World3D's two explicit calls are removed, because nothing between `add_child` and them depended
on a second build: the anchors and offsets set in between do not feed `setup()`. Every other
caller was checked. `hud_click_routing_test`, `npc_service_reader_test`,
`hud_underbar_test` and `hud_minimap_test` all call `setup()` before `add_child`, which leaves
`_ready` a no-op, and the audit tool calls it after, as World3D did. Measured: the underbar goes
from 279 nodes to 140 (the second copy's background, root and 137 controls are gone), and the
minimap from 29 to 15.

The audit tool (`zz_gui_audit.gd`, the previous round's scratch tool, not committed) was run in
the gui2 lane on the RX 5700 XT (GL Compatibility), `--norender`. BEFORE is d640880's scripts,
and its 47 SAMERECT lines are identical to that round's own post-fix dump. AFTER is this tree.
0 `SCRIPT ERROR` in either run.

- **SAMERECT: 47 -> 7.** By window, before -> after: inventory 6 -> 0, academy 1 -> 0, alchemy
  1 -> 0, chat 1 -> 0, underbar 24 -> 0, minimap 7 -> 0. Unchanged: community 1 and guild 1
  (open), exchange 3 (parked, never moved), storage 1 (layered, not alternates), target 1 (ours,

- **Tree diff, every widget.** No window changed size, and no node was added or removed except

    their children;
  - academy: PICTURE hidden;

  - chat: 4 lists hidden, and the input line at 38,378,360;
  - the HUD label heights above.

  and `FAIL target: the gem art is at the authored 8,5,20,20 (got [P: (8, 5), S: (20, 23)])`.
  With no archive loaded, the font minimum here is Godot's default face at 12px, 17 tall.
- `hud_build_once_test.gd` sets up each widget, adds it to the tree, sets it up again, and
  counts copies. It also reads World3D's init for the removed calls. Against d640880:
  **8 FAIL lines**, for example `FAIL underbar: one GDR_BTN_MENU after a second setup() (got 2)` and
  `FAIL minimap: a second setup() adds no children (3 -> 6)`.

All three print ALL PASS on this tree.

**Verified.** `remote_godot.sh check`: 285 scripts and 5 scenes, ALL LOAD. `remote_godot.sh
tests`: ran 107 suite(s), 0 failing, 0 SCRIPT ERROR. `cd server && go build ./... && go test
-count=1 -p 1 ./...`: 59 packages ok.

**Found, not fixed here (for later rounds):**
- `HudPanels._update_storage_gold_labels` writes the stored amount into
  `GDR_STORAGE_STA_GOLD`, and the carried amount into `GDR_INVENTORY_STA_GOLD`. Those are the
  "Gold" unit labels; the client writes amounts into `STA_MONEY` (ID 10, `FUN_006cc470`).
- `UiBuilder` ignores `ClientRect`, the text insets that separate the storage strip's three texts.
- ifexchange's `APPLY_EXCHANGE_UPDATE_1TH` and `UI_UPDATE_2009_FIRST` controls (153, 156 and
  304) are used with no null check, which is evidence that both branches are in this build.
  Selecting them would change several exchange rects, which was not measured here.
- `LayoutDef.get_section` falls back to the first section when a name is missing, so a missing
  extra section silently builds "Create" a second time.
- CIFMainFrame's own title, drag and close geometry (`0x816f80`: title `{10, 12, width-0x15,
  12}`, close `{width-0x1a, 10, 16, 16}`) is a lead for the non-registry outer-frame item. The
  drag strip's width was not read directly.

## Storage, exchange, system, party match, auto potion and help open inside their registry frame, with the caption, drag strip and close button where the client puts them (round 586)

Client only. Nothing on the wire changes and the server is unchanged. This is cause 2 of the
v0.1.450 GUI audit: `HudWindow.build` ignored `resinfo\ginterface.txt`, so the windows the client
frames from that registry were sized to their layout alone, drew no outer frame, and carried
ifalchemybox's caption row and a 42-pixel drag strip over empty space. Every value below was read
from `sro_client.exe` (`/opt/sro-files/client/sro_client.exe`, the decompile in
`/var/tmp/decomp_client`, and `objdump` of the PE where the decompile lost arguments) or measured
in the audit's node dump. Nothing was decided from a picture.

### Premise: the client reads ginterface.txt, and how it places a registry window

**ginterface.txt is read.** Three probes with different failure modes:

- ASCII: `resinfo\ginterface.txt` is at file offset 0x9b97c4 (VA 0xdb97c4). UTF-16: no copy
  (`strings -el` finds nothing). The control probe answers as expected: `ifcommunity.txt` is in
  neither encoding (round 585, the alternates round), and neither is `ifalchemybox.txt`.
- Code: `CGInterface::Create` (0x78c910) pushes 0xdb97c4 at 0x78c9ce, loads it (0x8b50a0), and
  builds its "Create" section (the string at 0xd82368) with the interface as parent (`push edi`
  0x78c9da, builder call 0x78c9ff).
- The other sections are built by name when a window is first wanted, on the same layout object:
  "PartyMatch" (0xdb9ea8) at 0x79c1e5 on `esi+0x36c`, then a fetch of ID 0x82; "AutoPotion"
  (0xdb9ef4) at 0x79c7a4, then ID 0x87; "GameGuide" (0xdb9d50) at 0x79b191, then ID 0x20. Those
  IDs are GDR_PARTY_MATCH's 130, GDR_AUTO_POTION's 135 and GDR_GAMEGUIDE's 32. The review traced
  the layout register for all three to the same `+0x36c` object: PartyMatch `lea edi,[esi+0x36c]`
  at 0x79c1dd; AutoPotion `lea ebp,[esi+0x36c]` at 0x79c75b, then `mov ecx,ebp` at 0x79c7a2;
  GameGuide `lea edi,[ebp+0x36c]` at 0x79b14b, then `mov ecx,edi` at 0x79b18f. Right after its
  section is built, GameGuide is moved by slot 0x98 to (0xe6, 0x50) = (230, 80) (0x79b1a5..
  0x79b1b4), a lead for the registry screen positions below.
  `UiBuilder.window_def` looked only in "Create" and found none of the three. It now searches
  "Create" first and then every section.

**Every registry window framed here is a CIFMainFrame, and its Create builds CIFMainFrame's
chrome before its layout.** The RTTI chains of CIFStorageRoom, CIFSystemWnd, CIFExchange,
CIFStore, CIFStoreForPackage, CIFPartyMatch, CIFAutoPotion, CIFGameGuide, CIFWorldMap, CIFCommunity
and CIFMainPopup all run through `CIFMainFrame : CIFFrame`. Each Create calls
`CIFMainFrame::vslot_010` (0x816f80) first, then pushes its layout path and builds it:

| Class | Create | calls 0x816f80 | layout pushed |
|---|---|---|---|
| CIFStorageRoom | 0x6cc780 | 0x6cc78b | `resinfo\ifstorageroom.txt` at 0x6cc796 |
| CIFSystemWnd | 0x6f6610 | 0x6f661e | `resinfo\ifsystemwnd.txt` at 0x6f6629 |
| CIFExchange | 0x7b27d0 | 0x7b27db | `resinfo\ifexchange.txt` at 0x7b27e6 |
| CIFPartyMatch | 0x73ae90 | 0x73ae9e | `resinfo\ifpartymatch.txt` at 0x73aea9 |
| CIFAutoPotion | 0x741980 | 0x74198a | `resinfo\ifautopotion.txt` at 0x741995 |
| CIFGameGuide | 0x765920 | 0x76594e | `resinfo\ifgameguide.txt` at 0x765959 |
| CIFWorldMap | 0x6964e0 | 0x6964e9 | `resinfo\ifworldmap.txt` at 0x6964f4 |

**The chrome** (`CIFMainFrame::vslot_010`, 0x816f80, read in objdump). It reads the window's own
rect with 0xb8f420, which returns {x, y, width, height}. The third field is the width: the
relayout below adds it to x. It then creates three children with the window factory 0xba20b0, at
rects relative to the window. The class of each child is what its `vslot_000` returns:

- `CIFStatic` (0xee9720), rect (10, 12, width − 0x15, 12), ID 0. This is the caption.
- `CIFDragableArea` (0xeea6bc), rect (10, 0, width − 0x15, 0x22), ID 1.
- `CIFCloseButton` (0xee9868), rect (width − 0x1a, 10, 16, 16), ID 2.

Each child gets a zero ClientRect (0x6527d0), font index 0 (`0xba5460(0)`), text-board slot 0x14
set to 1 and slot 0x18 set to 0. The layout parser stores HAlign at +0x88 (0x82c785) and VAlign
at +0x8a (0x82c7a3), and the layout builder passes those two fields to those two slots
(0x8b56a6 / 0x8b56b8). So the caption is centred horizontally and top-aligned. The resize slot 21
(0x817210) calls the base resize and then 0x817170, which re-lays the same three children: moves
to (x + 10, y + 12), (x + 10, y) and (x + width − 26, y + 10), with the same sizes. Ghidra's C
rendered the drag strip at x + 20 and the close button 12 lower and a pixel left; the asm
does not. The caption
text: the builder calls every control's slot 45 with its `Text` (0x8b5706). On a CIFMainFrame,
slot 45 is 0x817230, which jumps to the caption static's slot 45. On CIFStatic that is 0x64d810,
which stores the string (0x653ac0) and re-lays the text. **The caption's colour was not read.**
Nothing in OnCreate sets it, and the entry's `FontColor` (+0x90, 0x82c7c1) goes to the frame's
own text board (0x8b56d4), not to the caption. The caption keeps the colour it had.

This also settles the lead round 2 left: the drag strip is width − 21 wide and 34 tall.

**The layout's origin is the window's origin. This is read, not fitted.** Each Create passes the
window itself as the parent to the builder 0x8b5580 (`push esi`, or `push ebp` in CIFPartyMatch;
CIFPartyMatch's four builder calls, for Create and its three extra sections, at
0x73aedd/0x73af03/0x73af29/0x73af4f, and CIFAutoPotion's three at 0x7419c8/0x7419f2/0x741a1c all
pass the same parent). The builder hands the
control's Rect (`[esi+0x48]`) to 0xba20b0 unchanged (0x8b5639..0x8b564b). The factory stores it
at the new window's +0x40..+0x4c (0xba21f6..0xba2214) and then, when there is a parent, adds the
parent's position: `add [new+0x40], [parent+0x40]` and the same for y (0xba223e..0xba2247). A
layout rect is therefore relative to the registry window's top-left. The 9-17 pixel margins the
table in the audit showed are the layouts' own coordinates. ifstorageroom's frame starts at 9,38
in a 254x317 window, and ifsystemwnd's at 17,45 in a 214-wide one.

### Per window: decision and evidence

| Window | Entry | Decision | Size before -> after | Caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| storage | GDR_STORAGEROOM, Create section, `0,0,254,317` | **framed** | 245x307 -> **254x317** | UIIT_STT_STORAGEROOM = "Storage" |
| exchange | GDR_EXCHANGE, `200,200,254,361` | **framed**, defines `APPLY_EXCHANGE_UPDATE_1TH` + `UI_UPDATE_2009_FIRST` | 245x352 -> **254x361** | UIIT_STT_EXCHANGE = "Exchange" |
| system | GDR_SYSTEM, `300,200,214,245` | **framed, then sized in code** (below) | 197x230 -> **214x212** | UIIT_PAG_SYSTEM = "System" |
| partymatch | GDR_PARTY_MATCH, "PartyMatch" section, `0,0,785,480` | **framed** | 774x470 -> **785x480** | UIIT_PAG_PARTYMATCH_PSEARCH = "Party Matching" |
| autopotion | GDR_AUTO_POTION, "AutoPotion" section, `0,0,394,520` | **framed** | 381x507 -> **394x520** | UIIT_PAG_MACROPOTION_TITLE = "Auto potion" |
| help | GDR_GAMEGUIDE, "GameGuide" section, `100,100,420,452` | **framed**, caption not used | 408x441 -> **420x452** | ours, "Help" (below) |
| worldmap | GDR_WORLDMAP, `100,100,652,424` | already framed; now through the shared path, with CIFMainFrame's chrome | 652x424, unchanged | unchanged |
| community | GDR_COMMUNITY | **open, not framed** | 464x381, unchanged | |
| store | GDR_STORE | **open, not framed** | 245x356, unchanged | |
| alchemy | GDR_ALCHEMYBOX | **open, not framed** | 357x207, unchanged | |

Every caption shown is the archive's own text, resolved through `textuisystem.txt`. They matched
the titles this client already hard-coded, except that auto potion's is "Auto potion".

- **Exchange's defines.** The entry's Rect sits in three `#ifdef` branches: 254x361 with both
  defines, 363x363 with `APPLY_EXCHANGE_UPDATE_1TH` alone, and 254x361 without it. Both defines
  are selected. The evidence is round 2's: `CIFExchange::Create` uses controls declared only in
  those branches (153, 156, 304) with no null check. Two of the three branches give 254x361
  anyway.
- **System is sized in code.** `CIFSystemWnd::Create` does not keep the layout's or the entry's
  geometry. After the layout it:
  - hides IDs 10, 11, 13 and 14 (0x6f66b6..0x6f66e3);
  - maps rows to buttons: 0 -> 10, 1 -> 11, 3 -> 13 and 4 -> 14 (0x6f66f7..0x6f673e);
  - hands ID 12 (`GDR_SYSTEM_BTN_CAS_HELP`) to 0xba0e40. That function clears the window's +0x38
    and queues it on the factory's deferred list at 0x110f96c. The review traced the list: its
    consumer 0xba12b0 calls 0xba1190 on each entry, which destroys the window's children
    recursively and removes it from its parent. So the button is destroyed (deferred), not
    hidden. Our port hides it, which shows the same; it stays wired to `system_help_requested`,
    harmless while nothing shows it again;
  - walks rows 0-4, and moves each mapped button to (window x + 0x1f, window y + 0x3a + 0x22 per
    button already placed) with slot 39, then shows it (0x6f67d3..0x6f68a6);
  - resizes, each keeping its width (slot 21 at 0x6f68bf / 0x6f68d4 / 0x6f68e7): the tile (ID 5)
    to 0x1c per button, the inner frame (ID 6) to 15 + 0x22 per button, and the window to 0x3c +
    0x26 per button.

  The stack slots were followed through every push in objdump. With four buttons:
  - Option, Help, Restart and Quit sit at y 58, 92, 126 and 160;
  - the frame is 180x151 and the tile 148x112;
  - the window is **214x212**, not the entry's 214x245.

  `HudPanels._layout_system_window` does the same. The inner frame is rebuilt from its own def at
  the new height (`ControlDef.with_rect`), and the window through `HudWindow.set_registry_size`,
  which is the resize slot's relayout.
- **Help's caption.** The entry's Text is `UIIT_STT_GAMEEVENTGUIDE` under `#ifdef
  RENEWAL_NEWBIE_SUPPORT` and `UIIT_STT_HELP` otherwise. Both keys are in the exe, as UTF-16, and
  which branch this build takes is not read. The window shows this project's own documents, so it
  keeps "Help" (`HelpWindow.REGISTRY`, `"caption": false`). Its frame and size are unconditional.
  The body placement is `help_window.gd`'s own code, as before, and it grows with the window.
- **World map.** `HudWorldmap` built the registry frame itself. It now uses
  `HudWindow._add_registry_frame`, the one path every registry window takes, and so gets
  CIFMainFrame's caption (y 12, was 18), close (y 10, was 12) and drag strip. Its own
  `_gui_input`, which dragged by `mframe_wnd_`'s 68-pixel top (a number chosen from the art), is
  removed. CIFWorldMap is a CIFMainFrame whose Create calls 0x816f80 first (0x6964e9).
- **Community: open.** GDR_COMMUNITY is built by `CGInterface`, but round 2 found this client
  never loads `ifcommunity.txt`: its Create (0x707af0) loads no layout, and players see
  `CNIFCommunityWnd`. Putting ifcommunity's panes inside GDR_COMMUNITY's frame would present a
  composition the client never makes. This stays with the community item (the live `.2dt`
  windows).
- **Store: open.** GDR_STORE has four `#ifdef` variants, 254x317 / 317 / 360 / 370 by
  `RENEWAL_SHOP_SYSTEM` and `RESTORE_SOLDITEM_INSHOP`, and the define set cannot be read (round 2:
  the define table at 0xeed4e0 is never visibly filled). Neither store class fetches the buyback
  controls: CIFStore 0x6cf5a0 and CIFStoreForPackage 0x6d2c70 fetch only 11, 12 and 14, and the
  whole range 0x6ce000-0x6d6000 fetches only 0xb, 0xc, 0xe, 0x15, 0x16 and 0x31. So no class code
  picks a branch. The one hint points the other way from our layout choice. The layout read with
  nothing defined (the project's choice, `PANEL_DEFINES`) puts Repair / Repair all at y 332-356,
  below a 317 frame. The review found those two are outside every `#ifdef` in `ifstore.txt`, so
  every define set puts them there, not only ours. `UIIT_MSG_CANNOT_BUYBACK_ITEM_SELL` is in the exe (UTF-16, VA 0xda4018), and
  `CIFStoreForPackage::vslot_028` (0x6d4d10) uses it at 0x6d4ec3, which suggests the buyback feature is built in.
  That is not proof of the window's branch, so the store is not framed.
- **Alchemy: open.** GDR_ALCHEMYBOX is a `CIFAlchemyBox`, a plain `CIFWnd` drawing
  `alcm_window_1.ddj` (376x152), not a CIFMainFrame. Its Create (0x722770, the push at 0x7227aa) loads
  `resinfo\ifnewalchemybox.txt` (0xdb2818), not ifalchemybox.txt, which is not in the exe.
  That layout places `GDR_ALCHEMYBOX_ELEMENT_MANUFACTURING`, a `CIFAlchemyProcess` on
  `alcm_window_experiment.ddj`, at 0,150,376,228. `CIFAlchemyProcess::Create` (0x724ac0) loads
  ifalchemyprocess.txt, the layout our alchemy panel builds, into itself. Enchant and reinforce
  windows sit at the same rect, with code-built tabs. It is a different assembly, and the
  default tab was not read. `CNIFAlchemyWnd` also exists.

- **HudWindow's self-framed chrome comes from a layout this client never loads.** TITLE_TEXT_Y 18,

## The character, inventory, skill, action, party and academy windows are one framed window with a pane per tab, as the client builds them (round 587)

Client only. Nothing on the wire changes and the server is unchanged. This is item 2 of the GUI
audit's open list (the non-registry outer frame) and item 3 (inventory docking). Before it, the
six windows were separate self-framed windows: HudWindow floated ifalchemybox.txt's caption and
close button over each one's authored art (the audit's CHROME findings), and `dock_companion`
put the equipment frame beside the bag at x 176, y 0, unjoined. Every value below was read from
`sro_client.exe` (md5 `2a5794b72c90908d945be8b3f3f2edd4`; the decompile in `/var/tmp/decomp_client`,
checked against the linear `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm`) or measured in the archive's layouts or the
audit's node dump. Labels: **read** (the binary, at the cited address), **measured** (counted in
data or a dump), **inferred** (a conclusion from read or measured facts, with its basis). Nothing
was decided from a picture.

### Premise, re-verified

| Claim | Label | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C, I and S open `IFMainPopup` | read | `0x79ace0`, `0x79b020`, `0x79ae00` each read CGInterface's `+0x728` and call its slot 23 (ShowWindow) and `0x6a1f70` with 0x4b, 0x46 and 0x49. The dispatcher `0x780610` reaches them for command codes 0x43, 0x49 and 0x53 (its tables `0x780e48`/`0x780e00` and `0x780e90`). |
| `+0x728` is GDR_MAINPOPUP | read / measured | CGInterface fetches ID 0x19 into it (0x78ca87) and hides it (0x78cac8). `ginterface.txt`'s GDR_MAINPOPUP is `CIFMainPopup`, ID 25, `595,262,388,408`, `interface\frame\mframe_wnd_`, Text empty, outside every `#ifdef` (measured in the archive's copy, md5 `fce2ab6a…`). |
| GDR_QUEST and GDR_EQUIPMENT are declared in ifmainpopup.txt | measured | Both are in its Create section (IDs 76 and 71), with GDR_INVENTORY (70), GDR_PARTY (72), GDR_SKILL (73), GDR_ACTION (74), GDR_PLAYERINFO (75) and, under `APPLY_MENTOR_SYSTEM`, GDR_APPRENTICESHIP (77). |
| CIFMainPopup is a CIFMainFrame and loads ifmainpopup.txt | read | RTTI chain `CIFMainPopup : CIFMainFrame : CIFFrame : …`. Create `0x6a2560` calls `0x816f80` (CIFMainFrame's chrome, round 586) at 0x6a2598, pushes `0xda693c` (ASCII `resinfo\ifmainpopup.txt`; the decompile misrenders it as wide) at 0x6a25a3, and builds "Create" with itself as the parent (`push esi` 0x6a25af, builder 0x6a25d6). |

### The tab selector 0x6a1f70 (read in the asm)

It hides every pane (0x6a1c70), reads the window's rect (0xb8f420: x, y, w, h) and the display
mode's +0x24, then switches on the tab code through its table 0x6a236c (codes 0x46..0x4d):

| Code | +0x7fc | Caption (slot 45) | Panes shown | Tile | Window x |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x4b | 0 | UIIT_STT_CHARACTER | PLAYERINFO | hidden | 0x50 |
| 0x46 | 1 | UIIT_STT_INVENTORY | INVENTORY, EQUIPMENT | shown at (x+0xbd, y+0x44), 9x0x124 | W − w − 0x50 |
| 0x49 | 2 | UIIT_STT_SKILL | SKILL | hidden | W − w − 0x50 |
| 0x4a | 3 | UIIT_STT_ACTION | ACTION | shown at (x+0x28, y+0x9a), 0x134x0x7c | W − w − 0x50 |
| 0x48 | 4 | UIIT_STT_PARTY | PARTY | hidden | W − w − 0x50 |
| 0x4c | 5 | UIIT_STT_QUEST | QUEST | hidden | 0x50 |
| 0x4d | 6 | UIIT_CTL_TC_TRAININGCAMP | APPRENTICESHIP | shown, then hidden | 0x50 |
| 0x47 | — | — | — (the table's default) | — | — |

The window moves with slot 0x98 to (that x, its own y) and then calls its slot 20. The caption
strings are UTF-16 at 0xd96794, 0xd9676c, 0xd9674c, 0xd9672c, 0xd941fc, 0xd9670c and 0xd96344.
The tile's rects relative to the window are **(189, 68, 9, 292)** for the inventory tab, the
strip between the bag (13..189) and the equipment frame (198..376), and **(40, 154, 308, 124)**
for the action tab, which is its authored rect. The asm's stack offsets were followed through
each push (the rect is at `[esp+0x70]` before the pushes). `W` is the display mode's +0x24. That
+0x24 is the width is **inferred** from a centring routine that halves +0x24 for x and +0x28 for
y (0x4f8de3, 0x4f8dfc). The window's starting y is its registry rect's (262); nothing else was
found to move it.

`CIFMainPopup::vslot_023` (ShowWindow, 0x6a2390): showing re-selects the tab stored at +0x7fc;
hiding hides all eight panes. The constructor (0x6a1bc0) clears +0x7fc, so the first tab is the
character's.

### The keys (read)

The dispatcher `0x780610` translates a key to a command code (0x778310) and switches on it; with
the default bindings (the 33 virtual-key codes at 0x7778be) the codes are the letters'. Through its
tables (0x780e48 / 0x780e00 for 0x09..0x50, 0x780e90 for 0x52..0x59) it reaches: A (0x41)
0x79d5b0 (0x4a), C (0x43) 0x79ace0 (0x4b), I (0x49) 0x79b020 (0x46), L (0x4c) 0x79b0b0 (0x4d),
P (0x50) 0x79ae90 (0x48), S (0x53) 0x79ae00 (0x49). The underbar menu's dispatcher (0x60cd4c)
calls the same six. Each one does the same thing: if the popup is
visible and its own pane is visible (0x6a1cf0), it hides the popup. Otherwise it shows the popup
(which re-selects the current tab), selects its own tab unless its pane is already showing
(A selects unconditionally), and calls 0x79a7e0 on the popup (not read; we raise the window).
P and L also call 0x8cbac0 with their code (not read). The equipment toggle 0x79ad70 checks the
inventory pane and selects 0x46. No code reference to its address was found in the asm, and a
whole-file search for the dword 0x0079ad70 finds none in the data either (review of round 587), and
O is not a default binding. **Q is not a tab:** code 0x51 goes to 0x7990e0, which toggles CGInterface's window 0x4c,
the window game start builds from `res_ui\questlist.2dt` if absent (0x787024 -> push 0xdb9144 ->
0x469140). The popup's quest pane is reachable only through button 15, which Create hides.

**Our keys stay as they were:** C, I, K (skill: S walks backwards here), A, P, L, and O for the
equipment, which lands on the inventory tab.

### What is built

- `HudMainPopup` (new, `client/scripts/ui/hud/hud_main_popup.gd`) builds the popup through the
  shared registry path (`HudWindow.build` with `GDR_MAINPOPUP`, round 586): the 388x408
  `mframe_wnd_` frame, CIFMainFrame's caption (10, 12, 367), drag strip and close button
  (362, 10). ifmainpopup.txt is read with `APPLY_MENTOR_SYSTEM`. Each hosted pane's own layout is
  built into its pane control at the pane's origin, with the extra sections the old windows
  composed (skill's MainSkillWnd, the academy's NotifySubBox and NotifyContents). The seven
  buttons and ID 4 are hidden at build. All panes are hidden until a tab shows them.

  in `textuisystem.txt`: Character, Inventory, Skill, Action, Party, Academy), tile, and the
  window's x.

  (level, current and next EXP, stat points, Str, Int, HP and MP with their gauges, the four
  attack and defence rows, the two "+" buttons) is in it at the same rect as in ifplayerinfo.txt

+0x380, 4 (COMMONENEMY) -> +0x374 and 100 (the buff viewer) -> +0x388, and hides all five

(0x699166..0x699180). The close button (ID 11) is not fetched here. The select function moves it
to (window x + 0xb0, window y + 9) each time it shows a monster or a player (0x699658..0x699684),
which is its authored (176, 9). **Misread, corrected in round 592:** it then moves the button by
(+0x28, 0) before any class test (0x699686..0x69969b), so it sits at (216, 9). In the branches for
other object classes it moves it to x + 0xd8, which is also 216 (0x699c4b, 0x699cfc, 0x699dbc,

### The defines

`iftargetwindow.txt` has the four kind pieces in two `#ifdef UI_UPDATE_2009_FIRST` branches (236
wide, or 196 wide), and the fortress piece under `#ifdef APPLY_SIEGE_FORTRESS_SYSTEM`. The iftw_*
files branch on UI_UPDATE_2009_FIRST for their name rows (34,10,170,12, or 34,10,137,12 and
42,10,122,12). **The define set is one global map (read):** 0xeed4e0's only reader is 0x5004a0,
whose only caller is the parser's IFTVariable (0xb37aeb). So every layout is parsed under the same
set. **UI_UPDATE_2009_FIRST is in it (inferred, round 585):** CIFChatViewer::Create fetches ID 42,
which ifchatviewer.txt declares only under that define, and dereferences it with no null check
(0x7abc91 -> `mov edx,[eax]` at 0x7abc9c, re-read this round). **APPLY_SIEGE_FORTRESS_SYSTEM is in
it (inferred):** CIFTargetWindow::Create fetches ID 8, declared only under it, and calls through
it with no null check (0x699177). So the container is read with both, and the kinds' insides with
UI_UPDATE_2009_FIRST.

**Counter-evidence, measured.** In the 2009 branch two of the four pieces do not match their
atlas regions. `window_all.ddj` is 1024x512 (measured). The common enemy's region is 236 x 35.99
(its UV span; x 741, y 453): its art is opaque in rows 453..488 and transparent from row 489 down, so it is
drawn into a 51-tall rect. The job player's region is the #else branch's 196-wide one (x 543,
y 210), for a 236-wide rect. The special mob (236x78) and player (236x35) pieces match exactly,
and every #else piece matches its rect. The branch follows the define reading above, not this
data. HudTarget logs both mismatches (`HudTarget: … piece is … but authored …`).

### Found, not changed: which window a monster shows

HudTarget shows the common-enemy window for rarity 0 and the special-mob one otherwise. The asm
says otherwise. The select function (0x699540) tests the target's class. Its first test (0x6996a0)
is against the descriptor 0xef1a84. The object factory 0x9c1fa0 gives that descriptor to an object
whose type bits are TypeID1 1, TypeID2 2, TypeID3 1 (characterdata cols 9-11, as round 589 says),
i.e. a monster (read; the TypeID reading of
those bit fields is inferred). In that branch the rarity byte (+0x7ac) selects through the table
0x69a2d0. Every case (0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8) shows **+0x380, the special-mob window**, and calls
the rank-icon function 0x69b4c0 on it. Case 2 shows nothing. The common-enemy window (+0x374) is
shown only in two other class branches: descriptor 0xeef6f0 at 0x699ad2, and one case of 0xef1ac4
at 0x699c8e. So a normal monster shows the 236x78 special-mob window with the "normal" rank icon,
which is what `rank_icon_path`'s rarity-0 entry exists for.
This round was scoped to the container, so the rule is unchanged and the doubt is written into
HudTarget's header. It matters more now: a rarity-0 monster draws the 2009 common-enemy piece,
whose 36-tall art is stretched to 51 (above).

## A monster's target window is the one the client picks for its rarity (round 589)

Client only. Nothing on the wire changes and the server is unchanged. Round 588 found that
HudTarget's rule (common-enemy window for rarity 0, special-mob otherwise) contradicts the asm,
and it left the rule in place. Since that round, the rule also drew the 2009 common-enemy piece's
236 x 35.99 art stretched into its 51-tall rect for every normal monster. This round makes the
selection follow the client. Labels as before: **read**, **measured**, **inferred**.

### The class branches of CIFTargetWindow's select function (0x699540, read in the asm)

It hides every kind (0x699584..0x6995e2) and finds the object. If there is none, it stops. Then it
shows the window (0x699607), moves the close button to (x+0xb0, y+9) and then by (+0x28, 0)
(round 592). It then tests the object's
class with IsKindOf (0xb94b90) against five runtime-class descriptors, in this order.
**The descriptor names are read, not inferred:** each descriptor is built by a static initialiser
that passes the class name. For CICMonster, 0xd76490..0xd764b0 pushes 0xde281c (`"CICMonster"`),
then `mov ecx,0xef1a84`, then calls 0xb9c9c0.

| Descriptor | Class (its init string) | Factory's TypeID test (0x9c1fa0) | What the select function shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0xef1a84 | CICMonster (0xde281c) | bionic, 1/2/1 | the rarity table below |
| 0xeef6f0 | CICCos (0xde2234) | 1/2/3 (0x504f20) | **common enemy** (+0x374, ID 4), gem `tw_gem_animal.ddj` (0x699a55..0x699b6c) |
| 0xef1ac4 | CICNPC (0xde2a18) | 1/2/2 (0x69a3f0) | fortress piece (ID 8) for TypeID 1/2/4 with TypeID4 4, 1 or 3 (0x564ad0, 0x564a90, 0x564b10) -- 1/2/4 is what the factory gives CICGuard (0xeef710, 0x564a60), so CICGuard reaches this IsKindOf test as a CICNPC (inferred); otherwise **common enemy**, gem `tw_gem_player.ddj` (0x699c8e..0x699d3a) |
| 0xef1bc0 | CICUser (0xde305c) | bionic, 1/1 | player window (ID 0) if its slot 43 (`+0xac`) returns 4, else job player (ID 1) (0x699e0b..). What slot 43 returns was not read. |
| 0xee774c | CICATStruct (0xd87088) | 1/2/5 (0x52dc00) | fortress piece for TypeID4 6 (0x564b50) or 1/2/4/3 (0x564b10); otherwise **common enemy**, gem `tw_gem_normal.ddj` (0x69a0df..) |

The factory's other descriptors are not tested by name here: CICMonsterNPC 0xee77ac, CIItem
0xef1c28, CITeleportGate 0xef1dac and CIEventRuntimeObj 0xee77d8. Whether any of them derives from
a tested class (CICMonsterNPC from CICMonster, say) was not read. The TypeID reading of the factory's bit tests is **inferred**. The
tests themselves are read, and the class names confirm them. The bits are bionic (bit 1),
TypeID1 (bits 2-4), TypeID2 (bits 5-6), TypeID3 (bits 7-10) and TypeID4 (bits 11-15), the
characterdata columns 8-12. A correction to round 588: the common-enemy window is shown at a
**third** site, 0x69a0df (CICATStruct), as well as 0x699ad2 and 0x699c8e. The earlier grep had
been cut off by `head`.

The cases differ in the HP scale they pass to slot 39 (`+0x9c`), and every one that shows the

3 in characterdata_40000 (round 592; which one the client keeps was not read). **No monster has

unreachable with this archive, and is implemented only because the table says so.

## The target window sits centred at the top of the screen, where the client puts it (round 590)

Client only. World3D placed the target window at the registry's (442, 10), kept as an offset from
the centre line of a 1024-wide layout. The client does not leave it there.

### Read (0x699540's tail, 0x69a161..0x69a180)

```
69a161: call 0x4f9cd0          ; the display mode
69a166: mov  eax,[eax+0x24]    ; its width
69a169: sub  eax,[esp+0x24]    ; minus w
69a16f: sar  eax,1
69a171: push 0x7               ; y
69a177: push eax               ; x
69a178: mov  eax,[edx+0x98]    ; slot 0x98 (move) on the window itself (ecx = esi)
```

- **The window moves itself**, to x = (W − w) >> 1, y = 7, every time the select function shows a
  target. Read.
- **`w` is the shown piece's width, not the window's own.** Each branch reads the piece it showed
  into the same stack rect with 0xb8f420, which stores x, y, w, h: the special mob at 0x6999b1, the
  common enemy at 0x699b51, and the player pieces at 0x699e3e and 0x699e64, all `lea …,[esp+0x1c]`.
  `[esp+0x24]` is that rect's third field. The window's own rect is the registry's 10x10. Read.
- `W` is the display mode's +0x24. That it is the screen width is **inferred**, as in round 587:
  a centring routine halves +0x24 for x and +0x28 for y (0x4f8de3, 0x4f8dfc).
- **A rarity-2 monster**, which shows no piece, reaches the formula without anything writing that
  rect, so its x is not defined by anything read. This window then stays where it was. The archive
  has no such monster (round 589).

### What is built

- `HudTarget.place()` puts the window at `(floor((W − w) / 2), 7)`. `W` is the viewport's width in
  the UI's own units, which is what the F3 UI scale changes; `w` is the shown piece's width. It runs
  on every `show_target` and whenever the viewport changes size. The client re-runs its formula on
  every selection and has no resize of ours to follow.
- World3D's registry-offset block is removed, and the window is no longer anchored at the centre
  line. A grep found nothing else that read the target's position or `HudTarget.REGISTRY_NAME`,
  so that constant is removed too. `hud_click_routing_test` and `npc_service_reader_test` give the
  window their own rect.

| Window | UI scale | Logical width | Placed at |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1152x648 (the project's default) | 1.0 | 1152 | (458, 7) |
| 1920x1080 | 1.0 | 1920 | (842, 7) |
| 1366x768 | 1.5 | 910 | (337, 7) |
| resized to 1600x900, no new target | 1.0 | 1600 | (682, 7) |

The 236x78 piece fits in all of these. It would overflow only below a logical width of 236.

## The main window stays on screen at every window size and UI scale (round 591)

Client only. These are the review findings for round 587, fixed on top of rounds 588-590.

### 1. The main popup is held inside the viewport (our deviation)

Round 587 placed the popup the way the client's selector does, with nothing more: x at W − 468
(right-hand tabs) or 80, and y fixed at the registry's 262. The client never runs at our logical
sizes. The project sets no window size, so the default is 1152x648 (the reviewer measured
`root.size` on the box), and the F3 UI scale (0.5–3.0) divides the window. At y 262 the 408-tall
window needs a logical height of 670, so it overflowed at 1152x648 (by 22), at 1366x768 above
scale ~1.15 and at 1920x1080 above ~1.61. Either x needs a width of 468. Before round 587 the
windows were centred and always fitted.

`HudMainPopup.keep_on_screen()` now clamps the window into the viewport, x and y, pulling it to
the top or left edge when it cannot fit. It runs after every tab selection (so on every open and
tab switch) and whenever the viewport resizes. **This is our deviation, labelled so in the code;
the client does not do it.** (The first version of this round clamped the drawn position and
kept it, so a clamped y never returned to 262; round 592 keeps the wanted position apart.)

The target window gets the same clamp (`HudTarget.place`). For it the clamp changes nothing unless
the logical viewport is narrower than 236 or shorter than 85: the piece is centred, so it fits
whenever it can. At 600x400 and scale 3.0 (200 logical) it was at x −18.

Measured in the test: at 1152x648 the popup is at (684, 240) on the right-hand tabs and (80, 240)
on character and academy. At 1366x768 with scale 1.5 (910x512 logical) it is at (442, 104) and
(80, 104). Opened at 1920x1080 and resized to 1152x648, it is pulled in to (764, 104).

## The target window's close button, health bar and rank row sit where the client puts them (round 592)

Client only. This round fixes the review findings for rounds 588-591: three misreads in functions
those rounds cite as read, a count, two labelling nits, and the popup's clamp. Each was
re-verified in the asm before it was changed. I agree with all of them.

### 1. The close button is at (216, 9) (read)

The select function (0x699540) moves ID 11 to (x + 0xb0, y + 9) at 0x699658..0x699684, as round
588 said. It then does, before any class test:

```
699686: push 0x0
699688: push 0x28
69968a: push 0x1
69968c: push 0xb
69968e: lea  ecx,[esi+0x1bc]
699694: call 0x8b51f0        ; fetch ID 11 -- ret 0x8 (0x8b523d), so 0x28 and 0 stay pushed
699699: mov  ecx,eax
69969b: call 0xb90db0        ; mov/mov/mov/mov, jmp 0xb90c60
```

0xb90c60 does `add [esi+0x40],ebp` (dx, the first argument, 0x28) and `add [esi+0x44],eax` (dy,
0), then walks the children with itself (0xb90caa). That is MoveBy(dx, dy). So the button sits at
(216, 9) for every target. The NPC and structure branches' absolute `x + 0xd8` is 216 too. Round
588 stopped reading at the first move. `HudTarget` now places it at `CLOSE_BUTTON_AT` (216, 9) and
settles it there.

### 2. The rank rows are moved before the rarity switch (read)

0x69b4c0 reads the special-mob piece's own rect (0xb8f420 at 0x69b52a, into [esp+0x34]). Then:

- The rank icon (ID 3) moves to (x + 0x55, y + 0x36) = **(85, 54)** (0x69b52f..0x69b55a).
- The rank text (+0x378, which is ID 2 in CIFTargetWindowSpecialMob::Create) moves to
  (x + 0x69, y + 0x38) = **(105, 56)** (0x69b55c..0x69b57a).

The layout has (65, 54) and (85, 56), which is what we drew. For a party monster (+0x7ad == 1,
tested at 0x69b834) whose rarity is not 0 (`cmp [ebp+0x7ac],bl; je` at 0x69b890),
0x69b890..0x69b98d re-centres the rank row by the text's width (0x8b2f20) and moves the icon by
(−20, 0) (0xb90db0 at 0x69b988). The server sends no party flag, so that path is open along with
"(Party)".

### 3. The special-mob HP gauge is 208x4 (read)

CIFTargetWindowSpecialMob::Create (0x69b410) fetches ID 1 into +0x374 and, at
0x69b495..0x69b4a7, does `push 4; push 0xd0; call [vtbl+0x54]` (slot 21, SetSize). That is 208x4,
not the layout's 168x4. Measured in window_all.ddj: the 2009 special-mob piece's gauge trough
(rows 37-41) is dark from x ~15 to x 221, with its border at 222, so 14 + 208 = 222. The common enemy's Create (0x69aaa0) resizes nothing. Only the special mob's gauge changes.

The class code widens the special-mob rows by exactly the 40 pixels between the #else branch's
196-wide pieces and the 2009 branch's 236:

| What | Width |
|---|---|
| gauge | 168 -> 208 (+40) |

### 5. Rarity 7 renames the target (read)

At 0x6997b9..0x699834, for rarity 7, the name is rebuilt:

- 0x8c9c30 resolves `UIIT_STT_MOB_STRONG`.
- 0x50e300 appends `L" "` (0xe19330, the bytes `20 00 00 00`).
- 0x541210 appends the name.

The result replaces the name that 0x69b380 then sets. So a rarity-7 monster reads
"Elite <name>" in the archive's English. `HudTarget.monster_name` does this. If the text table
cannot resolve the key, the plain name is shown; that fallback is ours.

### 6. Counts

ID 38210 (MOB_SD_OSIRIS_3) is in two files, as rarity 8 in characterdata_39000 and as rarity 3 in
characterdata_40000. It is the only CICMonster ID whose repeated rows differ (measured: of the
IDs in more than one file, only 38210 and 61183 NPC_SOSUN differ at all). So rarity 3 is 812 and
8 is 82 if the first file's row wins, or 813 and 81 if the last wins. Which one the client keeps
was not read. Both are stated in round 589, and rarity 2 is 0 either way.

### 8. The main popup's clamp no longer sticks (our deviation, fixed)

Round 591 clamped the drawn position and kept it. After a clamp at 1366x768 x1.5 and a resize
back to 1920x1080, the popup stayed at y 104, and every tab then opened there. `HudMainPopup` now
keeps `wanted` apart:

- the selector's x;
- y from the registry's 262, or wherever the player last dragged it (a new `HudWindow.dragged`
  signal).

`keep_on_screen` draws `wanted` clamped. The clamp never feeds back. Round 591's reason ("the way
the client keeps a y the player dragged to") is withdrawn in that entry.

## The bag stays beside a shop or storage through a window resize (round 593)

Client only. A regression from round 592, found in review. `open_shop` and `open_storage` open the
bag (the main popup's inventory tab) and pair it with the vendor window. The vendor window goes at
(W/2 − its width − 8, centred) and the bag at (W/2 + 8, centred). The bag's position was written
directly, bypassing the popup's `wanted` position. `keep_on_screen()` rebuilds from `wanted`, so
the first `size_changed` threw the pairing away. Measured by the reviewer: at 76d8d23 the bag was
paired at (968, 336) and still there after a resize to 1900x1070; at 8805abb it jumped to
(1452, 112).

**Fix.** `HudMainPopup.place_at(pos)` sets `wanted` and clamps. `HudPanels.place_window(window,
pos)` routes a placement through it when the window is the popup, and sets `position` otherwise.
The shop and storage pairings use it. A grep for position writes in `hud_panels.gd` and
`World3D.gd` found one more on the popup: the QA panels hook's centring and tiling. That now uses
`place_window` too. Every other write is to a child control or a non-popup window. `HudWindow`'s
own drag writes `position` and then emits `dragged`, which round 592 already feeds into `wanted`.

**Also in this round (review nits):**

- `hud_target_layout_test.gd`'s comment named the authored 176,9. It now says 216,9 and why.
- Round 592's party path is gated on rarity as well: `+0x7ad == 1` (0x69b834) **and** rarity ≠ 0
  (`cmp [ebp+0x7ac],bl; je` at 0x69b890). That entry is corrected.
- Rounds 588-592 recorded `check` as 293 scripts. The lane (`/opt/srrevamp-client-popup`) also held
  the scratch audit tool `tools/zz_popup_audit.gd`, which is not in the repo, so the count was one
  too many. With it removed, `check` prints 292. Those entries are corrected.
- **Open, recorded:** `GDR_TWSM_TEXT_LEV` is authored 168 wide. At the x 105 the client moves it to,
  it reaches 273 in the 236-wide piece. The audit reports it as OUTSIDE. The width is the layout's
  (predates this round); whether the client clips the text there was not read.
